006c4fee-9275-57c3-b485-c14cd8a5f41c.title: [L705] User queue text and whole pending-order representations impose independent capacity gates
006c4fee-9275-57c3-b485-c14cd8a5f41c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L705.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/workbench/inputs.rs:5-8,22-29,80-86,103-115,240-249,285-301`; `src/wire/workbench_inputs.rs:26-51,148-160`; `src/workbench/intent.rs:18-31,92-115` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Each user input revision is capped at 8,192 UTF-8 bytes; queue pages are 32 rows with exact revision/total coverage. Order/dependency lists use at most 65,535 exact IDs; wire reads raw u16 count into Vec capacity without the generic negotiated collection check. Reorder names the complete pending set. Queue acceptance/correction and explicit execution are separate typed operations; archive/pin metadata do not themselves cancel execution or erase history.
- Consequence: Long daily-driving instructions fail as malformed input despite larger task-string limits elsewhere. Pending-set growth can block a complete reorder and produce frame/allocation pressure; paging queue history alone does not solve whole-order mutation. These are byte/cardinality gates, not elapsed sessions.
- Repair direction: Retain exact immutable inputs while supporting larger text through durable artifacts/chunks and indexed order mutations; preserve explicit holds, dependency checks and execution authority. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

009aa021-26d4-5296-90cc-0d189d15d1d9.title: [L356] E1 harness textual identities and paths have fixed portable-shape and byte limits
009aa021-26d4-5296-90cc-0d189d15d1d9.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L356.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/domain/identity.rs:7-47`, `src/domain/value.rs:5-10,22-42,62-82,102-118,138-179,192-225`.
- Behavior: component IDs are limited to 128 ASCII bytes with an alphanumeric first character and only alphanumerics, dot, underscore or hyphen afterward. Owner strings are at most 256 bytes, provenance 4,096 bytes, media type 255 visible-ASCII bytes. Paths are at most 4,096 bytes, 256 segments, 255 bytes per segment and enforce Windows device-name/trailing-dot/trailing-space restrictions on every platform; backslash and colon are forbidden. Sources must be below `.peritus-harness/components/`; targets cannot name control metadata at any segment.
- Consequence: valid host-platform filenames or longer provenance can fail harness declaration before execution. Root containment and protected metadata are authority/integrity boundaries distinct from representational byte limits; fixed portability rules are a product policy, not a timer. Later manifest loading and materialization callers remain under review.
- Repair direction: represent native filesystem identities losslessly with explicit portability compatibility, and externalize long provenance to digest-bound content. Keep no-follow containment and control-root protection. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

00bb66b5-7a4c-5845-82b2-77e57224948d.title: [L569] Linux activation consumes its status owner before a blocking observation
00bb66b5-7a4c-5845-82b2-77e57224948d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L569.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-linux/src/exec_status.rs:23-66`; `src/session.rs:219-257`; `src/native/helper.rs:115-125,248-281` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Activation takes the execution-status owner and removes its protected launch handle before reading the status stream. The read waits for EOF or the oversized-record limit and has no cancellation path. Even a complete fixed-size failure record still needs stream completion. Empty EOF is interpreted as success. Helper manifest and protected-payload reads are also blocking.
- Consequence: A stalled writer can hang activation, while an observation error leaves the same activation without the handle needed to retry it. Removing timeouts alone does not repair this ownership gap.
- Repair direction: Use a framed, cancellable activation handshake with durable ownership and an explicit execution-success acknowledgment. Commit the lifecycle transition and consumption of attachment handles together.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

00fc867b-547f-5733-9d51-5724ae2fd241.title: [L241] TUI cleanup uses nested fixed eight-second deadlines; reconnect retains the durable session
00fc867b-547f-5733-9d51-5724ae2fd241.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L241.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/client.rs:20-21,123-173,220-237`; `runtime.rs:35-36,181-197,271-276`; `runtime/connection.rs:36-53,101-122`; `model.rs:421-445,480-491,519-560`.
- ClientSession orderly close has a fixed **8-second absolute deadline** for queue admission, writer acknowledgement and writer join. Socket shutdown also has an **8-second** timeout. Runtime connection close wraps both pending-outbox drain and ClientSession close in another **8-second** grace, so remaining cleanup time can be shorter than an inner allowance. Expiry aborts/drops connection IO ownership; it can leave final detach/unsubscribe frames undelivered. These are client cleanup limits, not inference termination.
- Same-process reconnect asks for **model.retained_session()**, then falls back to the configured session. The model retains the session across disconnect and clears protocol/pending request observations while preserving recovery/drafts through their separate paths. Ordinary cleanup sends CancelSubscription and DetachTerminal; it does not issue a product-run cancellation in this inspected function.
- Prior ClientSession close is awaited before new connection negotiation, with its errors ignored by the reconnect attempt. Handshake itself has no elapsed deadline and is polled beside UI input; existing fixtures assert stalled handshakes/writers still allow quit. Product-mode reconnect exits to the launcher for daemon recovery, whose reopen selection remains a separate pending caller read. **All runtime/client sources and connection fixtures fully read; tests not run.** No existing-session failure was repaired during this audit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0103847f-ef5f-5ff7-be02-17ca6e5d3fef.title: [L369] E1 loader enforces aggregate payload capacity after reading all component bytes
0103847f-ef5f-5ff7-be02-17ca6e5d3fef.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L369.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/manifest/document.rs:66-79`, `src/manifest/loader.rs:61-81`, `src/manifest/loader.rs:228-263`; graph aggregate validation and compiled ceilings in L355.
- Behavior: parsing validates each declaration but does not construct the checked graph. `load_harness` reads and hashes every declared payload into a BTreeMap; only the separate subsequent `LoadedHarness::check` validates graph relationships and the aggregate materialized-byte limit. Under compiled bounds, 1,024 individually valid 8-MiB payloads can be read before the 8-MiB aggregate rejection. No cumulative loader byte budget or streaming frontier bounds that work. Exact size/digest checks are useful integrity protections but occur on the full allocated payload.
- Consequence: an input that is certain to exceed aggregate policy can consume substantial synchronous I/O, hashing, and memory before rejection. The roughly 8-GiB upper combination follows the per-component and count bounds; it is not a measured allocation or installed-run diagnosis. Existing C1 or host restrictions may reject earlier. This is late resource validation, not a new timer.
- Repair direction: validate declaration totals and the graph before payload reads, then stream checked artifacts with bounded resident memory and resumable progress. Keep complete digest and inventory verification. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

010aa687-6485-5028-be5d-5834a5f93572.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L375.

Large caller-admissible knowledge graphs can consume substantial CPU and appear stalled; this is an unmeasured source-derived risk, not a demonstrated live loop or a synthetic timer. Fixed structural loop bounds are not arbitrary timeout policies.
- Repair direction: merge canonical source/identity sets or build indexed lookups once, traverse actual dependency edges, and retain progress across host scheduling boundaries. Preserve exact digest and transitive invalidation semantics. No tests run.

034681b8-5b39-586f-8dee-8c78763b4e66.title: [L276] Native child retry recovery only recognizes the most recent committed command and repeatedly replays full history
034681b8-5b39-586f-8dee-8c78763b4e66.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L276.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/authority/owner/orchestrator.rs:48-71`; `children/collaboration.rs:187-201,222-265`; `children/scheduler.rs:132-175`; `children/gates_review.rs:214-257`.
- Exact D2/D3 retry helpers inspect only events.split_last. If a command already committed but a later child event exists before recovery, the helper reports stale fence instead of resolving the earlier exact command identity. Immediate lost-ack retries can succeed; progress after the commit creates another admission barrier. Caller/concurrency qualification is still pending.
- Child admission replays the complete current child, then commit helpers reload/rebuild it; retry may replay the complete predecessor prefix again. E0 settlement independently replays full current history and the publication prefix. Per-directive work therefore grows with retained history while holding the sole authority owner (L274).
- The child effect commits before separate E0/outbox settlement. Interruption between these steps requires immutable exact-command recovery across both owners; merely acknowledging a new lease cannot prove a second effect is safe. **Complete implementation read; no interleaved later-event/lost-ack execution or growth benchmark performed.** Fully read D2/D3 child tests retry each command immediately after restart, before any later successor exists; the later-event exact retry barrier is outside their cases.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

04060ce4-3887-5fa0-a41f-2aeefeedbd2e.title: [L422] E2 exact durable retry depends on the current checkpoint and the original claim fence
04060ce4-3887-5fa0-a41f-2aeefeedbd2e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L422.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-debugger/src/aggregate/reducer.rs:99-137`, `src/durability/commit.rs:81-120,196-244`, `src/durability/commit/claim.rs:65-77,126-139` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Pure reduction checks the latest state fence and terminal status before doing work. The commit layer correctly resolves an existing exact request before current-head checks, but only returns its batch when the current checkpoint is the exact successor; an advanced checkpoint returns ReplayAggregate. Claimed-start and settlement request digests include the C0 claim fence, so a newly reclaimed fence is a different exact request even with the original transition identities.
- Consequence: A generic retry that simply reconstructs the original transition from current state, or repeats it under a replacement claim, cannot transparently recover the original result. Recovery must first resolve the original operation and distinguish durable completion from still-owned work. This is a required recovery contract, not evidence that replay errors delete context; returning replay for an advanced checkpoint is explicit and preferable to falsely returning the older state.
- Repair direction: Retain the original request/claim receipt and authoritative outcome separately from current state. Resume from the latest reconstructed state while preserving historical completed-operation recognition across claim replacement. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

048d5d17-e80f-55d2-91eb-99a3fa77a8b7.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L540.

Per-connection accounting mutates before the shared total charge, so total rejection can leave the local account charged for a chunk never forwarded. Aggregate budget is lifetime state with no refill. Discarded redirect bodies also consume it.
- Consequence: A byte-limit error can occur after an upstream request has already triggered an effect or after a success header was sent. Retrying that generic connection failure cannot by itself prove safe replay. Configured byte counts mix forwarded control bytes, discarded bodies and reserved/unforwarded chunks. These are not execution timers but can stop useful work.
- Repair direction: Reserve/resolve exact transmission accounting before effects and preserve uncertainty for requests whose remote outcome is unknown. Separate user-selected network budget from observational counters and connection backpressure. No tests run.

04ee510f-af8d-575a-a37b-61a1a01d5e5d.title: [L329] D0 cannot redrive its pending provider envelope after a failed durable commit
04ee510f-af8d-575a-a37b-61a1a01d5e5d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L329.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/runtime/driver.rs:423-474`; `src/runtime/model.rs:155-177,181-225`; `src/runtime/durability.rs:131-192` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** drive_model_once always begins with model.pull_one. After a reducer/projection/journal failure the existing envelope remains pending, as intended for commit-before-ack safety. But pull_one rejects any pending envelope, and the driver provides no branch that retries committing that retained envelope before another pull.
- **Consequence:** Even a definitely uncommitted transient journal failure leaves the in-memory driver unable to redrive the same observation: the next step returns PendingEnvelope before reduction or append. The caller can cancel and rebuild from durable state, but this discards the uncommitted local envelope and depends on provider-specific exact restoration. The same trap applies to capsule or reducer-limit rejection while an envelope is retained. This undermines the documented pending-envelope durability boundary without an elapsed timer.
- **Repair direction:** Treat pending-observation admission as its own durable retry state. Retry the exact immutable envelope/command until its commit outcome is resolved, then acknowledge once, and only afterward allow another provider pull. Preserve the same stream/context across transient storage failure.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete source call chain; no storage failure injected. Current runtime-driver tests exercise normal acknowledgement, duplicate semantics, protocol failure and successful exact restart, but not retry of an uncommitted pending-envelope commit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0701f92a-2a08-5c4a-96cd-b7558111f32f.description:

It also rebuilds the normalized provider prefix and later replays that prefix again on exact resume. Every live provider envelope preview clones the current C5 ResponseReducer before acknowledging the same envelope into the original reducer. D0 cloning/hashing happens synchronously in these APIs.
- **Consequence:** Large accumulated response items and long event chains increase work before control returns; repeated cloning of a growing response can produce quadratic cumulative copying. Removing only count ceilings does not provide daily-driving responsiveness or a bounded recovery frontier. This is a possible stall mechanism, not an elapsed deadline or measured performance claim.
- **Repair direction:** Preserve an authenticated incremental replay frontier and indexed/paged events, verify only the required suffix, and preview new envelope admission without cloning all prior response material. Keep commit-before-ack truth and responsive control admission.

077eb83c-5ec0-5c35-a50d-0cfbd07b3c1c.title: [L609] Windows manifest encoding and transport disagree at their maximum size
077eb83c-5ec0-5c35-a50d-0cfbd07b3c1c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L609.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/manifest.rs:17-19,33-47,125-146,193-211`; `src/manifest/codec.rs:26-33,64-81,148-153,339-364`; `src/manifest/codec/scalars.rs:92-103`; `src/process.rs:14,297-316`; `src/secret.rs:10,80-95`; `src/process/profile.rs:7,56-66` in the same crate.
- Behavior: The codec accepts a frame up to four MiB and then appends a 32-byte checksum; direct decode accepts four MiB plus checksum. Framed helper transport rejects anything over four MiB including checksum, so the last 32 bytes of the codec's accepted frame capacity cannot be transported. Arguments/environment cap at 4,096 entries, strings at one MiB; environment names additionally cap at 32,767 bytes. Target inherited handles and secret collections each cap at 64; AppContainer names at 128 ASCII bytes, SID text at 184 bytes. Environment alias checks sort by case-sensitive ordering before adjacent case-insensitive comparison. Codec errors discard the dimension/capacity cause. Framed reads block synchronously without cancellation.
- Consequence: Near-boundary valid encoded manifests can fail the actual helper path; capacity and alias checks are inconsistent across representations. These are finite schema/transport gates, not elapsed-time limits.
- Repair direction: Define a single complete-frame capacity including checksums, enforce all selected platform capacities before consumption, preserve dimension-specific errors, and use one global case-normalized environment identity.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

07ed22ce-1c09-581d-b7be-1a32f7f2e296.title: [L083] Command caller applies fixed resource, output, and shutdown policies
07ed22ce-1c09-581d-b7be-1a32f7f2e296.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L083.

- `command_runtime/plan.rs:26-31,109-136` selects **8 MiB output/artifact allowance**, **16 KiB model output fields**, **64 KiB stdin chunks**, **16 MiB cumulative stdin**, **12 GiB memory**, **50 GiB disk**, **4,096 processes**, and **8,192 file descriptors**. Process CPU time is selected wall time multiplied by **64**, and absent when wall time is absent. Actual enforcement and parameter-field definitions are being read.
- Output overflow requests ContinueIncomplete rather than automatic termination (`115-124`). This means missing output evidence remains possible even if the command continues; the supervisor continues reading but retains only bytes within the per-stream and shared spool allowances (`supervisor/io.rs:244-259`). Later bytes are counted as dropped and never enter the displayed window; no output-limit cancellation is requested under this caller policy (`205-220`).
- `DeadlinePolicy::new` keeps ordinary wall time optional, but selects **500 ms graceful shutdown** and **5,000 ms reap** (`170-171`). These are cancellation/termination completion policies, not established deadlines on ordinary successful execution.
- `peritus-tool-router/src/execution.rs:140-144` confirms the unselected wall deadline is ignored for elapsed-time checks. A changed authority epoch still cancels. The placeholder logical tick 21 in the compiled call is therefore not a one-millisecond timeout when no timeout was selected.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

086e32f3-0eda-5fac-8108-d1b071fedd98.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L208.

Native runtime declarations pass through their runtime configuration constructor; profile state/resume transformation remains pending there. Tool router limits are derived from configured workers/authority queue and can introduce further narrower checks.

Treat current provider/profile changes as explicit compatible successor bindings while retaining logical context and unresolved obligations; do not silently bypass revision fences.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete bridge/canonical/restore reads, followed by all role constructors and policy tables. RoleProfile is currently deterministic from ActorRole. 09db7df8-72a7-5758-9bc6-bf4461159f29.title: [L218] Codex decoding caps raw events, event size and completed assistant messages, with closed event kinds
09db7df8-72a7-5758-9bc6-bf4461159f29.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L218.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/runtime/output.rs:18-20,199-229,256-304,308-343`; `output/selection.rs:15-36`; `output/failure.rs:7-50`.
- Native JSONL accepts at most **100,000 nonempty raw lines**, **4 MiB per line** and **1,024 completed agent messages**. Raw lines count before byte-identical deduplication, so replayed duplicates consume the event ceiling. The line limit is narrower than the protocol's 16 MiB public text limit and includes escaped JSON framing; total transport output is separately 16 MiB (L210/L211).
- Only thread.started/turn.started/known item lifecycle/turn.completed/error/turn.failed are accepted; unknown event or item kinds fail the whole turn. A nonduplicate event after terminal completion also fails. Protocol drift or nonessential new native notifications can therefore block inference completion rather than being retained as opaque observations. Native host effects remain prohibited and must not be accepted as ordinary notifications.
- With an authoritative final-response file, its trimmed contents must equal the last agent message, and the first decodable nonempty host-tool proposal is the suspension boundary. Without the final file, exactly one agent message is required. The production caller also requires final-file read success before admitting a turn, so decoder fallback alone does not supply recovery from a missing final file.
- Fixed typed codes/English substrings classify capacity/rate/quota/context failures; L214 records their retry categories. **Entire decoder/selection/failure files read; boundary/forward-event cases not run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0a49584d-95cd-59a1-a5ef-caac8016a24f.title: [L402] B0 pause loses the fixer phase and excludes pending/reviewing runs from session pause
0a49584d-95cd-59a1-a5ef-caac8016a24f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L402.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-kernel/src/reducer/run.rs:85-106`, `src/reducer/attempt.rs:97-120`, `src/reducer/attempt.rs:123-146`, `src/reducer/turn.rs:32-50`, `src/reducer/session.rs:18-30`, `src/reducer/session.rs:46-56`, `tests/transition_matrix.rs:95-113`, `tests/transition_matrix.rs:326-355`.
- Behavior: PauseRun allows Running or Fixing but stores only Paused. ResumeRun always restores Running. A run/attempt pair in Fixing therefore becomes Running/Fixing after pause/resume; ResumeAttempt requires Fixing/Fixing, StartTurn requires an Active attempt, SubmitAttempt also requires Active, and StartAttempt rejects while the current attempt remains bound. FailAttempt can abandon the attempt and allow a new one, but normal resumption of the same fixer attempt is unavailable. The tests cover Running pause/resume and direct Fixing resume separately, not this composition. Pending and Reviewing runs cannot pause, and any unpaused live run prevents PauseSession.
- Consequence: pausing ordinary fixer work can strand the current attempt behind mutually incompatible phase guards. Pausing review/pending work also fails at the control boundary. This is a source-derived reachable transition sequence, not an executed reproduction or a diagnosis of the installed UI lockup. The kernel has no process suspension or provider-session deletion.
- Repair direction: preserve an explicit resume phase and checked parent/child continuation state, including pending and reviewing phases. Restore the exact legal workflow after resume; verify composed pause/resume paths across phases. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Candidate identity checking is necessary integrity, not a synthetic limiter.
- Repair direction: Stream stable run-history pages and route candidate execution through a durable process owner with explicit cancellation/reconciliation. Carry candidate identity/expected operation generation in exact mutation requests rather than relying on a pre-request check. No tests run.

Fixed frame and nested limits still bound the formats; this is not an unbounded-parser claim or a measured explanation of the current lockup. No benchmark run.

0ad9b08a-65ea-5766-b757-8815da1291da.title: [L284] Scheduler replay reuse covers one aggregate and persistence recovery loses actionable error distinctions
0ad9b08a-65ea-5766-b757-8815da1291da.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L284.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/session.rs:15-19,35-50,65-88`; `durability.rs`; `durability/binding.rs`.
- A session caches exactly one aggregate. Switching runs, reopening the connection, an external commit, or any other append attempt invalidates reuse and requires observe_replay plus complete scheduler replay/checkpoint verification. Any failure discards the cache; exact committed-command resolution also returns no successor observation, causing the next access to replay again. This session is a journal cache, not the provider's native context window.
- A command's bound payload or complete-state overflow is classified through binding_error as **Journal/Quarantine**. Generic journal errors become **ReplayAggregate**, losing distinctions such as Busy versus corruption at this boundary. These are recovery/blocker classifications, not elapsed work deadlines.
- commit_transition resolves an exact committed command before checking the current head, but its helper still loads the current checkpoint. If it has advanced beyond that receipt, it returns an aggregate-advanced replay error instead of that helper returning the historical success. Application-ledger resolution can return the original batch directly; the callers therefore have different recovery contracts.
- The stored domain request digest is SHA256 of the exact encoded scheduler command bytes, matching the application admission digest. Binding verification is separate; no digest mismatch is asserted here. **Complete durability, binding, cache and schema policy read; no performance or failure-injection test executed.**

- Additional complete test evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/tests/versioned_durability.rs:134-139` explicitly expects an already committed genesis exact retry to fail after aggregate advancement with `Journal / ReplayAggregate`; this is an existing enforced expectation, not solely an untested source inference.

0aea9a98-4f97-5ce2-9d8d-d0e2087a64e5.title: [L816] Browser console interruption shares an unresolved input queue
0aea9a98-4f97-5ce2-9d8d-d0e2087a64e5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L816.

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/components/Console.svelte:1-41`; process-local gateway console and output limits in L808.
- Behavior: Console input, including Ctrl-C bytes, is chained behind previous input promises. The input field clears before acknowledgement without a durable original. Terminal scrollback is 4000 lines. A new component starts reading at offset zero, and each next read waits for the previous request before applying its 250-ms or 1800-ms cadence.
- Consequence: An unresolved input request can prevent the later interrupt from reaching the process. Browser history and the gateway's 1-MiB output ring are separate eviction boundaries; the 64-KiB page and polling cadence can lose output when production outruns retrieval. Closing a panel does not transfer native process ownership or preserve its output. Cadences are not execution deadlines.
- Repair direction: Give interruption an independent owner/control path, retain input effect receipts, and use durable output with acknowledged offsets rather than relying on process-local rings and browser scrollback. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Authenticate replay/checkpoint equivalence without rebuilding every old prefix for each command, and run persistence work through an owner that can still service control requests. 0cd35e25-ab79-54f4-a217-e9fae1540e46.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L317.

0d0d00d5-22ef-5644-9b7b-8c309ea54f01.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L078.

Only the first literal occurrence in each artifact determines the preview (`122-124`). Pagination/explicit offsets allow further reads but do not enumerate all matching occurrences.
- Packing reserves worst-case escaped expansion at **six output bytes per source byte**, plus metadata/cursor overhead (`167-185`). A nominal 16 KiB page therefore returns substantially less source text. If even metadata or the next full entry cannot fit, it returns a rejection requiring a larger page (`128-141,240-244`). These policies can amplify repeated reads; exact archived evidence remains retained.

0e78d96c-098d-5844-bd14-daabf54c276e.title: [L181] Restart invalidates execution-qualified candidates without comparing current execution facts
0e78d96c-098d-5844-bd14-daabf54c276e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L181.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/recovery.rs:17-98,109-178`.
- Startup reconciliation examines terminal, uncommitted, undiscarded candidates. It re-observes repository and source digests, but **any retained execution_digest being Some is itself sufficient to mark the candidate stale**, even when those other digests match. No current execution-context comparison appears here.
- Reconciliation preserves historical evidence and exported patches, advances the checkpoint identity and marks qualification for reacquisition. A qualified but uncommitted candidate can therefore lose actionable status simply through restart. This is a freshness policy rather than elapsed expiration; an actual change in observed execution dependencies must be distinguished from an unobserved assumption.
- Missing configuration or inaccessible candidate facts marks actions unavailable and requests workspace access restoration; it does not discard the evidence. **Complete source read; repeated gate execution after a real restart not reproduced.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0e85c494-ffd5-5940-a329-9f2d1c8f56c8.title: [L302] Collaboration confuses message identity order with causal order, rejecting valid successors or saving an invalid chain
0e85c494-ffd5-5940-a329-9f2d1c8f56c8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L302.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-collaboration/src/state/mutation.rs:30-37`; `reducer/apply.rs:196-220`; `message.rs:48-65`; `state/validation.rs:21-38`; `wire/mod.rs:357-383`; `wire/state.rs:105-141`; `durability.rs:59-80,124-145,234-240`.
- Messages are retained sorted by **message ID**. SendMessage gathers that order, derives expected ordinal from the count, and chooses task_messages.last() as the required predecessor. It never verifies that selected predecessor has ordinal=expected-1. Restart validation requires exactly that causal ordinal relationship.
- Source-derived sequence: message A has ordinal 1 and a greater ID than later message B, whose ordinal 2 correctly names A. A third message at ordinal 3 correctly naming B is rejected because admission selects A as the greatest ID. Naming A instead passes admission even though A has ordinal 1; that accepted successor can encode/commit but fails restart validation because 1+1 != 3.
- Stable IDs are opaque identities, not required monotonic timestamps. This is an ordering-model blocker and another accepted-state/decoder disagreement. Repair should retain/derive a checked per-task causal frontier, independent of identity sort order, and enforce the same relationship before acceptance and at restart. **Complete admission, insertion, constructor, wire, persistence and decoder chain read; no executable reproduction claimed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0ec6db9d-86b8-5289-ba07-efe481b90349.title: [L590] macOS manifests can encode a body that their decoder rejects
0ec6db9d-86b8-5289-ba07-efe481b90349.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L590.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-macos/src/canonical.rs:5-7,44-48,75-84,131-137`; `src/manifest.rs:24-29,290-329`; `src/manifest/codec.rs:43-58` in the same crate.
- Behavior: The canonical writer and manifest frame permit up to 512 KiB. The body is enveloped using `Writer::bytes`, which does not impose the 256 KiB string/byte-field limit. The decoder reads that entire body through `Reader::bytes`, which rejects anything above 256 KiB. Fields and collections separately have 256 KiB and 4,096-item limits.
- Consequence: A successfully constructed, checksummed manifest with a body above 256 KiB can fail in the helper decoder despite remaining within its declared frame bound. A near-maximum profile or combined ordinary arguments/environment can reach the mismatch. This is source-derived; no executable reproduction was run.
- Repair direction: Give opaque envelope bodies their own symmetric encode/decode bound, preflight the complete native representation, and qualify the exact boundary through the real helper before consuming authorization.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0f1530ef-b69c-5f0f-bb1f-63a49b3470a7.title: [L610] Windows kill-on-close jobs tie target lifetime to the helper owner
0f1530ef-b69c-5f0f-bb1f-63a49b3470a7.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L610.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/process.rs:80-105`; `src/native/job.rs:20-58,65-74`; `src/native/mod.rs:21-41`; `src/native/launch.rs:91-127` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Every Job Object is unnamed, kill-on-close, and owned in helper activation state. It installs finite active-process and memory limits plus an optional CPU limit; CPU zero correctly omits `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_TIME`. CPU milliseconds must fit signed 64-bit 100-nanosecond representation. The helper creates the target suspended, assigns it to that job, resumes, and waits indefinitely for root completion. Target/job identity and ownership are not made durable by these native routines.
- Consequence: Helper owner death or final job-handle closure kills the target tree, so an otherwise persistent logical session cannot survive that ownership loss. The infinite wait is not a synthetic run deadline; the persistence blocker is owner lifetime. Representation overflow can reject a very large explicit CPU budget.
- Repair direction: Keep native containment ownership in a durable supervisor with explicit adoption/handoff and independently inspectable job identity; preserve no-CPU-deadline semantics while negotiating representable explicit budgets.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

0f50f468-e595-5983-a00f-40f7192bd82f.title: [L174] SQLite qualification fixes file size, workspace shape, and repeatability policy
0f50f468-e595-5983-a00f-40f7192bd82f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L174.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/gates/sqlite_migration.rs:8,27-66,76-101`.
- SQL files are capped at **16 MiB** and read fully as UTF-8. Qualification always starts with an in-memory database, requires `schema.sql` and exactly the conventional `migration.sql`, then executes the migration **twice** against the same database. A valid one-time migration such as CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS fails the second pass; the inline test explicitly demands that failure.
- Optional `postcheck.sql` and `rollback.sql` are executed afterward. Query rows from postcheck are not interpreted as assertions. Foreign-key violations fail after each migration and rollback; no generic transaction, interruption/progress hook, or caller-selected repeatability policy appears here.
- The size and filename/repeatability constraints are hard-coded gate admission policies, not elapsed deadlines. Whether idempotence is required must come from the requested task rather than the generic SQLite project kind. **Complete source and tests read; host selection and affected real tasks not exercised.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

10ade4b6-ba15-564a-9c94-3fc5c50adf29.title: [L488] Google HTTP recovery drains complete rejected bodies and can lose typed failures behind retry-policy errors
10ade4b6-ba15-564a-9c94-3fc5c50adf29.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L488.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-google/src/client.rs:65-171`, `src/client.rs:176-188`, `src/client.rs:280-358` in the same crate; provider-core retry limits are covered by L207/L228.
- Behavior: each submission clones the full encoded request and accumulates bytes, but policy admission occurs only after failure. For non-200 status the adapter waits until body EOF, then classifies quota/status and plans retry. Retry-After accepts unsigned decimal seconds with at most three fractional digits; invalid/date forms disappear. A retained delay outside the configured policy can return an error before the constructed typed failure is published.
- Consequence: a stalled error body delays decisive failure/recovery without a timer, while optional delay parsing or policy failure can obscure the original status. Raising deadlines does not resolve these ownership/state gaps; fixed finite caller policies still limit attempts/elapsed/bytes. This audit does not identify the currently installed Google policy or claim a measured stalled connection.
- Repair direction: make header-derived failure state observable immediately, gather bounded optional body facts without blocking ownership transfer, admit retries before resubmission, and preserve failure identity when delay policy stops work. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

10c0ec72-eff9-54da-bddd-dbf1ae2b70e3.title: [L163] Review comments accept 8 KiB of text but their mandatory prompt wrapper must fit the same 8 KiB
10c0ec72-eff9-54da-bddd-dbf1ae2b70e3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L163.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/review.rs:17,219-228,257-267`; `control/review/ledger.rs:48-76,79-106,229-274`.
- **Limits/enforcement:** Review comments use ControlText<8192> and paths have a 4,096-byte lossy-display bound. Adding/rebinding a comment then adds action instructions, exact run/workspace IDs, five SHA-256 identities, path, target, and line ranges, and constructs another ControlText<8192> from the entire wrapper plus comment. An otherwise-valid 8,192-byte comment therefore cannot be added or rebound; long paths consume still more of the undocumented effective comment allowance. No dynamic allowance, separate structured identity channel, or precise effective-limit diagnostic is present.
- **Failure/recovery:** Whole transition rejects before publication; message/path history remains preserved. 112057e8-f832-5204-84dc-5d346187b4e4.title: [L453] An accepted out-of-range probability threshold cannot survive F0 wire decoding
112057e8-f832-5204-84dc-5d346187b4e4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L453.

119cd067-e0f9-5ab3-baeb-321470c91ce9.title: [L799] Attachment upload offsets are acknowledgement-driven but discarded on reconnect
119cd067-e0f9-5ab3-baeb-321470c91ce9.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L799.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/images/upload.rs:1-201`, `images/page.rs:1-121`, and `files/import.rs:1-300`, all completely read, together with the attachment parents in L798.
- Behavior: The UI reads selected content into memory, uploads at most 64 KiB per chunk (also respecting negotiated capacity), and advances only after the matching transfer/step acknowledgement. Upload identity, bytes, and next offset live in WorkbenchUi. Interrupt handlers take/drop the upload and request state on disconnect; reconnect asks the user to explicitly preview again rather than querying a persisted accepted offset. A missing ACK remains behind the global workbench pending gate in L789. Attachment histories use pages rather than an execution lifetime limit.
- Consequence: A transfer interruption can force another whole read/upload with fresh identities and can strand unrelated controls until the pending ownership changes. Chunking here does not establish resumable transfer after UI/daemon replacement. There is no default per-upload time deadline to remove.
- Repair direction: Persist transfer identity/digest and acknowledged offsets, query host settlement after reconnect, and resume/cancel that exact transfer before allocating a replacement. Allow unrelated observation/control channels to progress independently.

12a0bbbc-4f01-5431-907c-117cf2f68eb5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L416.

Complete canonical manifest bytes are allocated and hashed after selection.
- Consequence: shrinking a query or tightening its selected-event ceiling does not bound upstream indexing, frame checks or candidate allocations. A single malformed same-session observation outside the requested filters can block otherwise valid diagnosis. Potential costs scale with total journal/trace history, subject count and artifact references; no benchmark, installed lockup or corrupted production trace is claimed. Exact provenance checks are necessary, but their scheduling and scope remain significant for daily diagnosis.
- Repair direction: use verified indexed/ranged upstream selection with bounded incremental work, validate required provenance as evidence is admitted, and distinguish a source-integrity fault from an unrelated incomplete trace outside the query. 12c5b6a8-4977-5971-82a1-5f504f109d89.title: [L443] F0 silently evicts rollback targets from the long-lived production pointer
12c5b6a8-4977-5971-82a1-5f504f109d89.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L443.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/pointer/reducer.rs:161-184,239-243,245-255,272-300,313-319`, `src/pointer/rollback.rs:156-176`, `src/pointer/state.rs:206-210`, `src/limits.rs:22-33` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Each activation appends a history record; when the retained history length equals activation_history, append_history removes index zero first. The compiled maximum is 256 and a caller may tighten it to 1. RollbackProposal and both rollback preparation/activation require the target activation to remain in that suffix. With limit=1, even the immediately previous activation is absent after a new activation. No pointer command expands the window or loads an older target from immutable journal history.
- Consequence: Authorized rollback becomes impossible through the normal F0 pointer contract solely because enough later activations occurred. The authoritative journal may retain every event; this is checkpoint-target eviction, not deletion of evidence or model session context. The pointer continues promoting rather than halting at capacity, so the blocker is historical reachability rather than a promotion-count ceiling.
- Repair direction: Resolve rollback targets from durable immutable activation history with exact provenance and compatibility checks. Bound the hot projection/cache independently of target eligibility and preserve stable target identity across checkpoint compaction. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Equal activity revisions preserve the first encountered candidate, so selection depends on page ordering when revisions tie.

That is useful preservation, but not evidence of durable client draft storage across process exit. **All three implementation files fully read; server prompt replay and library ordering remain pending.**

164d4db4-800f-5867-9ebb-28f4250bab5e.title: [L418] E2 restart advertises an already-started attempt resume that its executor cannot perform
164d4db4-800f-5867-9ebb-28f4250bab5e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L418.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-debugger/src/runtime/recovery.rs:43-69`, `src/runtime/model.rs:75-117`, `src/runtime/mod.rs:11-20`, `src/model/mod.rs:1-11`, `src/aggregate/reducer/apply/model.rs:48-68`, `src/aggregate/reducer/apply.rs:69-132`, `src/aggregate/command.rs:20-123` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Recovery selects `ResumeModelAttempt` for a durable ModelRunning job with an available directive. The exported executor requires ModelPending, then unconditionally commits MarkModelAttemptStarted; the reducer also only accepts that start in ModelPending. No separate resume executor or lifecycle command is exported in the read modules.
- Consequence: Feeding the recommended recovery action back into the ordinary executor fails binding before provider I/O. 170cdbf2-3977-5250-be6d-ccfea38172f4.title: [L322] Legacy deterministic compaction retains an unbounded prompt lineage until it stops shrinking
170cdbf2-3977-5250-be6d-ccfea38172f4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L322.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/developer/context.rs:16-19,41-105,129-157,233-322`; `src/developer/context_encoding.rs:7-26,62-111`; `src/developer/semantic.rs:28-61,101-133`; `src/developer/context_port.rs:195-233` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** Legacy deterministic compaction preserves one text/tool-call/tool-result summary line per old block, with text previews 256 characters and tool previews 512. Recompacting a prior summary copies all prior_lineage, user_text, assistant_text, tool_call and tool_result lines into the next summary, then adds another lineage digest. There is no retirement or bounded external index for those lines. Candidate construction stops at the first noncompactable exchange rather than selecting later independent complete exchanges.
- **Consequence:** Although each initial replacement can reduce full output, repeated long work grows a minimum retained summary proportional to all historical tool calls. compact_once returns None when the replacement cannot shrink its candidate, and prepare_messages then eventually rejects the request when the accumulated summary plus protected inputs/tools exceeds input capacity. The eight-message preference can fall back to zero recent messages, but cannot solve this retained-lineage growth or a noncompactable leading exchange. Compaction source count is additionally limited to u16.
- **Repair direction:** Store exact lineage and old observations in a durable paged index, retain a bounded prompt frontier selected for current work, and retrieve omitted evidence under its stable identity. Preserve governing inputs and complete protocol obligations; make recovery from a full view an explicit selection operation rather than ending the logical task.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete source inspection. Host-owned local context bypasses both legacy compaction paths; semantic compaction can shrink to a model-authored checkpoint when explicitly enabled. This finding applies to deterministic legacy/fallback selection, not every production request, and is separate from local-memory limits L058-L079.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

17fe8ac0-1786-5593-ad92-4eb93386b8b9.title: [L341] Run settlement makes user wait and recovery immutable terminal decisions
17fe8ac0-1786-5593-ad92-4eb93386b8b9.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L341.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-run-settlement/src/cause.rs:9-33`; `src/disposition.rs:9-21`; `src/reducer.rs:21-33,47-64,67-91`; `src/settlement.rs:24-42,62-78`; `src/verified.rs:154-165`; `tests/reducer.rs:195-239,242-281`.
- **Blocker:** settle stores one terminal decision for every cause, including UserWait, Recovery, Provider, Context and Deadline. After that, both observe and settle reject AlreadySettled; there is no answer/reconcile/resume transition on that reducer. A qualified candidate is retained but WaitingForUser and RecoveryRequired explicitly override Accepted. Deadline here is only a descriptive cause supplied by callers; this crate has no clock, timeout, TTL or deadline enforcement.
- **Consequence:** Recoverable waiting/reconciliation cannot be represented as continued activity of the same settlement reducer. A host must create/reconstruct another unsettled reducer, carry forward the checkpoint and retain the enclosing logical execution separately. The candidate remains available and the original observation is not deleted. Whether a host does that correctly is a caller responsibility, so the domain alone does not prove session destruction.
- **Repair direction:** Distinguish immutable delivery/settlement observations from the durable logical run's resumable lifecycle. User answers and resolved recovery should advance that logical execution without losing context, candidate obligations or historical truth; exactly-once final completion should apply at the actual final boundary.
- **Evidence scope:** All sixteen crate files read. Existing tests explicitly preserve the candidate under wait/recovery and reject post-terminal updates, but do not reopen such a reducer. Tests/proofs were not executed. Source checks allow qualification to decrease and retain/reconcile provenance; these are evidence correctness rules, not arbitrary lifetime quotas.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

1a10cab1-9c42-575e-9f05-25eb002aab26.title: [L398] B2 treats superseded or unnecessary authority facts as current acceptance failures
1a10cab1-9c42-575e-9f05-25eb002aab26.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L398.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-quality-policy/src/evaluator/authority.rs:18-32`, `src/evaluator/authority.rs:173-304`, `src/evaluator/authority/supplied.rs:15-53`, `src/evaluator/authority/waiver.rs:17-67`, `src/evaluator/authority/waiver.rs:101-117`, `src/evaluator/authority/blockers.rs:31-96`, `tests/cases/authority.rs:192-228`, `tests/cases/authority.rs:322-396`, `tests/cases/waiver_semantics.rs:142-181`.
- Behavior: every supplied current waiver is validated, including waivers for findings below the blocking threshold. A waiver retained after its finding becomes resolved is rejected as AlreadyResolved. Every current approval is also checked for an expected subject; an acceptance approval where approval is not required, or an approval for a waiver no longer valid for the current finding, becomes an UnexpectedApproval failure. The low-severity tests explicitly reject invalid waivers/approvals without an UnwaivedBlocker; resolved-finding rejection is covered among the waiver scenarios. There is no inactive/superseded authority-fact representation in this input aggregate.
- Consequence: retaining previously relevant authority facts alongside current resolved findings can prevent acceptance even though that finding no longer needs a waiver. This is an integration-sensitive current-set boundary, not evidence that historical authorizations should silently override an active denial or forbidden waiver. The pure evaluator neither persists nor deletes sessions, sets timers, or proves the installed lockup's cause.
- Repair direction: preserve the immutable authority history and derive an explicit current projection with supersession and finding-resolution semantics. Validate active decisions and disclose contradictory facts; distinguish historical approvals from approval requirements that must actually be satisfied. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

1a304872-a253-544a-a963-ee506e8a9d30.title: [L233] Migration ownership has immediate contention rejection, and SQL validation uses broad lexical restrictions
1a304872-a253-544a-a963-ee506e8a9d30.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L233.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-migrations/src/engine.rs:115-152`; `src/config.rs`; `src/descriptor.rs`; `src/verified.rs`; `src/registry/validation.rs`; `src/error.rs`.
- Opening an engine takes an immediate exclusive **try_lock** on the backup-directory migration-owner.lock; a concurrent owner is rejected with Io/Retry and there is no wait in this path. Different databases using the same backup directory share that lock. SQLite's default busy wait is **5 seconds**, separately configurable including zero; it is a storage lock wait, not an inference/session lifetime.
- Migration source is capped at **4 MiB**, release labels at **128 printable ASCII bytes**, and versions at positive representable SQLite integers. SQL is split into uppercase lexical tokens and rejected for BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/ATTACH/DETACH/VACUUM anywhere in the text, including comments or string literals. This can reject safe future migration source unrelated to actual transaction control. The two currently compiled SQL sources do not establish that such a false positive occurs in installed use.
- Applied history must match every contiguous compiled version, source digest and release; newer schemas and reverse migrations are rejected. Those compatibility and transaction ownership invariants must not be confused with arbitrary source bounds or lexical false positives. The README still describes a one-version registry whereas source/tests contain two versions. **All migration implementation, metadata and SQL sources fully read; no new validation/lock test run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

1ac22fac-f48e-50b1-9d90-f4076d28d545.description:

1ae46c72-0073-5544-ae01-1a4a8635dcf6.title: [L176] Deterministic output gates turn limited language heuristics into hard delivery requirements
1ae46c72-0073-5544-ae01-1a4a8635dcf6.description:

- Output recognition only considers the previous **12 words** in a clause, negation within **2 words** before the output verb, and naming nouns within **6 words**. Single-file recognition uses a **6-word** verb window and a **4-word** negation window. These fixed language windows can miss long instructions or negate them incorrectly; gate failures are then decisive rather than advisory.
- Extraction splits every line on whitespace, including quoted paths containing spaces. Parsing strips terminal periods and delimiter punctuation, ignores paths containing *, $, = or unresolved placeholder brackets, requires absolute paths to be under the exact root, and recognizes a fixed English verb/noun/conditional vocabulary. These rules are interpretation constraints, not filesystem capacity or user-selected limits.
- Presence checks treat any symlink_metadata success as present without establishing file kind. Chronological reduction understands explicit removal and recreation, alternatives, and output-list indentation, but the single-file flag is true if any historical line matches; there is no later explicit relaxation of that flag in this implementation. Supersession depends on the supplied task history and remains to be traced.
- Preserve actual user requirements and path authority. A structured current contract should determine hard delivery gates; heuristic interpretation uncertainty should be recoverable rather than inventing obligations. **All implementation files and contextual-language tests read; untested edge-case risks, not demonstrated failures.**

1bd2df76-6aa4-5dff-8223-eacee95824e2.title: [L482] Anthropic streaming has a fixed 4096-entry deduplication ceiling and derived identities can exceed the protocol width
1bd2df76-6aa4-5dff-8223-eacee95824e2.description:

Derived item ids append a colon and decimal block index to a response id accepted at the same maximum width. Content, tool-buffer and reasoning-fragment constructors hardcode production protocol limits; replay wrappers are serialized before fragment admission.

A response id near the accepted width can fail only when its first item is normalized. Independent fragment/wrapper ceilings and synchronous whole allocations remain after elapsed deadlines are removed. No live provider boundary or installed-run reproduction is claimed.
- Repair direction: retain bounded deduplication with an explicit replay horizon or durable index, make identity derivation fit by construction, and thread one negotiated resource policy through framing, normalization, replay and reduction. Keep capacity handling recoverable without replacing it with another arbitrary timer. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

1bf2f3e6-c6c1-5477-9778-59d75c06364b.title: [L499] OpenAI stream indexing and whole-fragment assembly retain hidden bounds
1bf2f3e6-c6c1-5477-9778-59d75c06364b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L499.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/stream/state.rs:71-85,103-126`; `src/stream/decode.rs:11-64,125-143`; `src/stream/output.rs:11-66,117-179,197-249,274-356`; `src/stream/terminal.rs:170-201` in the same crate; previously read provider-core tool/structured-output healing bounds.
- Behavior: sequence zero and reordering are rejected, identical seen-sequence digests are retained for duplicate suppression, and positive gaps are accepted without detecting omitted events. Unknown correctness-critical events/items fail closed. Content indices are flattened as output_index times 65536 plus content_index without restricting the latter below 65536; overflow rejects large indices and different coordinate pairs can collide. Nonzero content parts append an identifier suffix under the same ItemId width bound. Tool arguments remain buffered until finalized, structured text is withheld until whole-value completion, and finalized text/arguments must exactly match retained deltas. Item closure scans all parts; seen sequence/item/part history remains for the whole stream. Usage input plus output must equal total when all three are present.
- Consequence: legal-width source identities can overflow after local suffixing; flattening can collide; missing sequence events may be detected only through downstream state failure. General output bounds do not remove the narrower whole-value/fragment/argument limits, synchronous copies/parsing, or growing history scans already recorded for healing. No provider claim that zero/gaps are valid is inferred here.
- Repair direction: define explicit provider sequence semantics, preserve collision-free tuple coordinates and bounded identifier derivation, publish meaningful buffered progress, and make assembly limits compatible with the normalized protocol and durable resume state. No tests run.

1c961e20-873c-558d-8da4-ae1b5abe95a5.title: [L144] Managed capture requires a complete representable Git snapshot and waits synchronously for helper processes
1c961e20-873c-558d-8da4-ae1b5abe95a5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L144.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/candidate/managed.rs:51-103,106-148,152-208`; `candidate/managed/capture.rs:22-123,127-205`; `capture/directories.rs:7-70`.
- **Blockers/enforcement:** All Git path bytes must decode as UTF-8; relative paths cannot contain `.git` components or non-normal path components. Every baseline object must be a 40- or 64-character hexadecimal Git ID, and file modes are restricted to regular/executable files, symlinks, or gitlinks. A single non-file/non-directory/non-symlink candidate, unreadable metadata, corrupt nested HEAD, or incomplete hash result aborts the whole capture. Nested repositories are captured recursively. No file-byte/count ceiling or recursion-depth ceiling exists here; 128-path hashing chunks are batching, not a total limit.
- **Progress/recovery behavior:** Fingerprint, changed-path, and patch operations recapture the full baseline using synchronous Git children. Helper stdout/stderr and input vectors are buffered in full, with no cancellation/progress observer in this layer. 1d1be852-35f0-56fc-bc66-dfe85f4c728f.title: [L343] C6 optional expiry is immutable across review; freshness crosses an epoch barrier
1d1be852-35f0-56fc-bc66-dfe85f4c728f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L343.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-memory/src/record.rs:52-100`, `src/record/transitions.rs:22-55,90-129,131-167`, `src/retrieval/filter.rs:39-58,73-85,89-105`, `src/retrieval/ranking.rs:94-124`, `tests/retrieval_matrix.rs:153-175,223-265`, `tests/lifecycle_matrix.rs:93-109`.
- Behavior: caller-supplied optional logical expiry excludes a record at `expiry <= query observation`. Review and explicit quarantine release preserve that original expiry; this API exposes no renewal/removal. Explicit Expired/Superseded states cannot reopen. Optional review-age policy rejects missing review or **any different logical epoch**, even without elapsed ticks exceeding the configured age. Confidence, accepted claim type, required features, supporting evidence, role visibility and optional negative/contradiction thresholds are additional eligibility barriers. A zero signal threshold can exclude even a zero negative ratio. Recency also falls to zero after 10,000 ticks or in another epoch, but is a ranking component rather than a standalone expiry.
- Consequence: renewed evidence/review alone cannot restore eligibility after a previously supplied expiry. An epoch change makes all prior-epoch reviews stale whenever age policy is enabled. None expiry/age is supported; there is no wall-clock timer, mandatory default TTL, or physical session deletion in this crate. Logical expiry can require a replacement memory identity or caller reconstruction even while the claim remains useful.
- Repair direction: distinguish explicit semantic invalidation from elapsed-time freshness; make accepted refresh/replacement policy explicit and preserve stable lineage and provenance. Persistent working context should not expire just because an observation clock changed. Scope: source-confirmed conditional behavior; caller policy/default selection and installed impact not established here. Existing tests inspected, not run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

1d5342a0-e55e-4413-b2dd-ad4438934bc7.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L003.

- `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench/checkpoints/capture.rs:246-254` reads each whole file with `peritus_patch::MAX_FILE_BYTES`, then maps **every** inspection error to `ControlError::StaleRevision`.

Sealing failures also stop with a durable-recording error. `peritus-product-runner/src/execution/checkpoint.rs:89-133` now verifies the observer forwards BeforeMutation to that ConversationView hook; `turn.rs:280-291` installs it on writer/fixer tools, and `executor.rs:243-257` rejects failed preflight before dispatch. 42bcef03-27c2-41fe-98fa-1e71200e3727.content:
Systemic repair plan for L003: checkpoint storage must be independent of patch-command payload admission.

The causal coupling is in peritus-daemon checkpoint capture and the product-runner BeforeMutation observer: a recoverable file-size/storage failure becomes StaleRevision and prevents command dispatch. A checkpoint is an immutable recoverable workspace snapshot; a patch is an authorized mutation transaction. They need separate representations and admission rules.

Change capture to stream file content into chunked immutable artifacts and persist a manifest of exact path, kind, content digest, revision and ownership. Align automatic capture, manual capture, sealing, writable fork validation and rewind with that snapshot contract. Preflight must confirm a restorable snapshot before permitting the mutation. Restore large snapshots through one durable transaction with recoverable progress, not unrelated partial patches. A real storage shortage enters an observable recoverable wait under the same task and native-session identity. Return typed storage, contention, stale-preimage and integrity failures; only actual revision mismatch is StaleRevision.

Preserve protected paths, canonical path identity, symlink/ancestor checks, exact preimages, explicit user cancellation and exactly-once effect receipts. Already accepted checkpoint evidence cannot be invalidated by a newer admission policy. Retain old manifest decoders; publish a versioned manifest/artifact representation atomically, verify its recovery roots before switching writers, and keep the prior generation readable during rollback. Coordinate L006, L010, L013 and L020 so capture never promises a restore that downstream encoding cannot perform.

Acceptance requires automatic capture and command execution with files just above 8 MiB; manual capture and restoration across more than 1,024 paths and an aggregate above 8 MiB; fault injection during chunk write, manifest publication and restore; exact saved-workspace restoration after reopen; and retained task/native-thread identity. Changing a preimage, introducing a protected path or an unsafe ancestor must still reject the mutation. Existing small snapshots and commands must retain their behavior. Read the remaining callers and run applicable ordinary and formal checks on the final migration; no source-only plan guarantees nonregression before those checks.

1deab1f1-3a9f-51d1-abfe-80627cf1865b.title: [L465] C5 exponential retry backoff can wrap to zero despite a positive minimum
1deab1f1-3a9f-51d1-abfe-80627cf1865b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L465.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/retry.rs:192-197,208-217`.
- Behavior: the exponential delay uses checked_shl with a shift already clamped to 63. checked_shl rejects an out-of-range shift count, but does not detect discarded high bits. Thus its unwrap_or(u64::MAX) does not protect arithmetic overflow in these allowed shifts. With base_delay_millis 100, attempt 63 or greater, no Retry-After and zero jitter, the shifted value is zero and the calculated delay is zero despite validation requiring a positive base.
- Consequence: a caller permitting enough safe retries can lose all backoff and repeatedly resubmit immediately. This is a reachable source-level planner defect; currently audited production layers with smaller retry counts do not establish that the live session reached this case. Removing those count limits without fixing the arithmetic would expose it more broadly.
- Repair direction: calculate exponential growth with saturating multiplication or an explicit overflow predicate, then apply the intended delay policy. Preserve nonzero scheduled waits and cancellation across long recovery sequences. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

1e3d5807-f11d-522f-b9d6-e46fb857cdf2.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L223.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/reducer/stream.rs:43-83,101-113,175-198`; `reducer/events.rs:46-67,88-109,166-183`; `reducer/terminal.rs:73-90,100-149`; production bounds in L017.

Item assemblies remain in the map after completion, so the item count is cumulative for the response.

These are closed acceptance policies, not provider session duration limits.

Exact sequence/identity/explicit completion checks prevent duplicate or incomplete tool admission and should be distinguished from arbitrary ancillary/count ceilings. **All four reducer implementation files fully read; no response-limit edge cases run.**

1fda0f55-5264-5fe3-bfa1-7e6665e41cab.title: [L419] E2 collapses permanent provider failures into retries and records zero failed-attempt usage
1fda0f55-5264-5fe3-bfa1-7e6665e41cab.description:

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-debugger/src/model/runner.rs:73-197`, `src/runtime/model.rs:211-231`, `src/aggregate/reducer/apply/model.rs:131-161`, `src/aggregate/types/model.rs:20-102` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Profile validation, provider start, and provider pull failures are normalized to ModelProtocol with Retry using their display text. Durable normalization then calls all such failures MalformedStream and records event_count and total_tokens as zero, even if a stream already emitted events/usage. Retry policy requires finite positive attempts (type ceiling 32, plan admission additionally constrained by L415's default 8); exhaustion returns the job to deterministic report preparation. Frozen model ceilings are checked separately for each result/failure, without cumulative failed-attempt usage.
- Consequence: Unsupported configuration or other permanent provider failures can repeatedly submit the same request until the synthetic attempt ceiling instead of explaining the correction required. Distinct transport/profile failures and consumed failed-attempt usage disappear from the durable record; quota decisions and diagnosis cannot use accurate aggregate consumption. Model-budget/invalid-proposal failures are intentionally nonretryable, and exhausting optional model work does not itself delete the run context or forbid deterministic reporting.
- Repair direction: Preserve typed provider failure, recovery certainty, continuation, and observed usage through failure settlement. Retry only failures whose recovery can change the outcome, with an explicit user policy for stopping, and account consumption across attempts without conflating protection with task termination. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

20a50119-6b79-5936-9ff7-c4f66d339890.title: [L726] A new terminal attachment must replay its whole history into a smaller pending queue

20ab4104-29c9-5280-b157-a7bdae34bca2.title: [L195] Guidance identities accumulate in a single 16 MiB catalog, including forgotten records
20ab4104-29c9-5280-b157-a7bdae34bca2.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L195.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_control/guidance.rs:24-25,79-108,153-219,244-343`.
- Guidance storage uses schema version **1** and the journal's **16 MiB** maximum state size. Saving inserts an identity into a sorted catalog; forgetting writes a content-free slot and tombstone but does not remove the identity. Each subsequent mutation clones and rewrites that entire catalog through bounded StateInstall admission.
- The identity count therefore has a lifetime encoded-size ceiling. Forgetting cannot shrink this catalog, and once it cannot be installed, even another forget/revise/pin/scope mutation needs the same oversized catalog write. No catalog segmentation, paging, metadata retirement or version migration appears in this file. Per-guidance content/rendering limits and stored codec details remain to be inspected.
- Canonical storage, monotonic revisions, tombstone dominance and refusal to reactivate forgotten guidance are integrity requirements, not session expiration. Catalog replay rejects unsupported schema/noncanonical state; error mapping turns LimitExceeded into Capacity and most other application validation errors into InvalidInput.
- **Complete source read; capacity failure not reproduced.** The 16 MiB threshold is encoded bytes, not a measured maximum guidance count.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

225a0b86-77fe-5b82-9036-2abce802d21a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L521.

Applying each observation clones the current complete span map for failure atomicity. Observations retain both the decoded domain value and canonical frame bytes; event identities and spans are not retired. Projection encoding and invariant hashing copy the entire accumulated projection. Single-trace recovery loads the complete chain; all-trace recovery integrity-exports the entire journal.

There is no incremental projection cursor, chunked recovery, cancellation or progress callback in these paths. This is complexity derived from the code, not measured latency. Keeping sessions persistent will expose growing history rather than eliminating this cost.
- Repair direction: Maintain a durable validated projection head and apply only journal suffixes, use narrowly staged mutations for failure atomicity, and preserve resumable replay progress. Exact committed-command replay already resolves before history replay and should remain idempotent. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L363.

23497d7a-7835-5f1e-afc9-e915fb93ed87.title: [L309] Every E0 directive requires a finite immutable delivery-attempt allowance
23497d7a-7835-5f1e-afc9-e915fb93ed87.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L309.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/directive.rs:171-219,318-345,366-385`; `src/reducer/apply/directives.rs:15-42`; `src/runtime/driver.rs:78-106`; `src/runtime/recovery.rs:109-149`; `src/durability.rs:278-299`; `src/durability/acknowledgement.rs:74-94`.
- **Limiter:** A directive's `maximum_deliveries` is a positive `u16` (1 through 65,535), fixed in the durable payload. `mark_published` consumes the allowance before the external publisher is invoked. Reaching the count returns `LimitExceeded / NeedsHuman`. There is no unlimited value, reset/replenishment command, or replace-pending operation. The first publication also passes this finite allowance to C0's independently counted outbox delivery attempts (see L251/L264/L265).
- **Consequence:** Transient delivery failures and restart boundaries can consume a finite retry policy while the same exact work remains unfinished. Recovery can classify a Published-but-Absent destination as Deliverable even though a new E0 publication is forbidden by its remaining allowance; a terminal/failed delivery is not automatically recorded by this helper. E0 publication and C0 claim counts are separate, so this does not establish that a crash before the first effect necessarily prevents the existing outbox row's first delivery.
- **Repair direction:** Keep exact stable effect identity and reconciliation, but make stopping after transient delivery failures an explicit optional policy. Persist delivery outcomes separately from publication intent, and coordinate E0 recovery with C0's remaining authoritative delivery state rather than classifying deliverability without checking it.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete directive, driver, durability and recovery source inspection; no exhausted outbox was executed during this audit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

246d1953-ddb5-5a97-bb95-e3bea963da2d.title: [L391] Primitive capability names have a compiled 128-byte ASCII grammar boundary
246d1953-ddb5-5a97-bb95-e3bea963da2d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L391.

The approval rendering field cap in L385 is larger than the accepted capability name.

24ca3c2b-58bf-5cc6-b9f8-4f743959fd20.title: [L796] Goal drafting is local and goal controls inherit the global read fence
24ca3c2b-58bf-5cc6-b9f8-4f743959fd20.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L796.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/goal.rs:1-282`, `goal/draft.rs:1-161`, and `goal/refresh.rs:1-31`, all completely read.
- Behavior: Objectives and graphical criterion descriptions are limited to 8,192 bytes. An unconfirmed draft resides only in WorkbenchUi, permits one optional graphical criterion, and always includes the existing mandatory runner-acceptance criterion. Confirming first saves the exact objective in the brief, then starts the goal after a separately correlated brief refresh. Pause/resume refuse to send while any global workbench request or unresolved command is pending; missing goal inspection asks the user to repeat the control after reading. Mandatory acceptance criteria describe completion authority; they are distinct from a synthetic lifetime cap. A native-context recovery guarantee still requires the durable execution-owner work recorded earlier.
- Repair direction: Make explicit goal controls independently admissible against the exact goal identity, persist unconfirmed/partially confirmed user intent, and settle staged brief/goal admission durably. Keep user confirmation, safe-boundary pause semantics, and exact criterion identity.
