258bdf92-c897-51e0-b2e5-3556e401b00a.title: [L470] Compatible API defaults retain finite retry and private production capacities
258bdf92-c897-51e0-b2e5-3556e401b00a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L470.

No installed compatible-route failure reproduced.

26601576-590d-59ed-a265-2b8983e992f2.title: [L364] E1 recovery repeatedly rebuilds complete history and re-encodes state
26601576-590d-59ed-a265-2b8983e992f2.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L364.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/durability/recovery.rs:42-54,83-129`, `src/wire/event.rs:58-75`, `src/aggregate/reducer.rs:58-89,159-237`, `src/aggregate/state.rs:168-203`, `src/domain/history.rs:108-157,292-318`, `src/replay.rs:54-65`, `src/projection.rs:29-40`.

Every reducer decision clones retained state and hashes its complete canonical identity, including sorted complete history. Projection rebuild/repair also replays from genesis.
- Consequence: recovery and ongoing mutation cost grows with all retained revisions/plans/receipts/diagnostics rather than the current change. This is synchronous whole-prefix work, with no internal yield/cancellation boundary. It is a source-grounded performance risk, not a measured explanation of the live lockup or an artificial timeout.
- Repair direction: validate durable indexed segments once, resume from a checked frontier and contiguous suffix, reuse immutable objects, and compute incremental exact state certificates. Preserve independent validation without discarding state or restarting lineage. Runtime entry points remain under review; no tests or timing measurements run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

272e2696-4c52-5ed4-abee-eff02adddba6.title: [L511] Plugin failed-state handling and queued authority cannot support durable recovery
272e2696-4c52-5ed4-abee-eff02adddba6.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L511.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/host.rs:126-135,210-273,290-305,314-357`; `src/transport.rs:58-64,97-142,165-169`; `src/quota.rs:21-32` in the same crate.
- Behavior: all exchanges serialize through one transaction mutex despite higher concurrent-request quotas. Invocation lifecycle/authority/quota checks happen before queueing and are not rechecked after acquiring that mutex. Any exchange error, including a pre-cancelled token or request-encoding error before submission, marks the whole instance Failed; those paths need not terminate its process. Failed instances remain in the map and block start until stop removes them. Some invalid invocation status responses instead return RestartPlugin while leaving the lifecycle Ready. Registry, counters, transport handles, and lifecycle state have no persistence/reattachment API; process drop kills the child. Kill/wait errors are discarded.
- Consequence: cancellation of unsent work can disable the entire plugin, queued work can proceed using stale lifecycle/authority observations, and requested restart is not a direct available transition. Losing the host loses the process/context and evidence needed to distinguish completed effects. Higher admission concurrency does not create parallel wire progress.
- Repair direction: bind dispatch to fresh authority after admission, distinguish unsent cancellation from failed/possibly accepted execution, align recovery disposition with actual transitions, and journal invocation/instance identity with explicit reconnect or reconciliation semantics. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

274d1729-c83f-52c4-b2ee-f71617c29900.title: [L508] Plugin SDK identity and diagnostic restrictions include another Unicode panic path
274d1729-c83f-52c4-b2ee-f71617c29900.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L508.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-sdk/src/identity.rs:20-23,57-84,121-129,187-204`; `src/manifest.rs:55-70,278-289,362-391,485-500`; `src/error.rs:34-40`; `src/manifest/wire.rs:94-131`; `src/protocol.rs:22-38,113-125` in the same crate.

Entrypoints have a 512-byte safe relative path, at most 64 arguments, and 4096 bytes per argument without NUL. Capabilities must be strictly sorted/unique with at most 256 declarations. An indefinitely blocked output sink is a progress blocker with no synthetic time limit involved. A cursor gap is terminal here rather than an explicit snapshot/replay transition. This is source-derived behavior, not a reproduction of the user's running TUI.
- Repair direction: Give subscriptions and effect requests persistent identity/cursor receipts, reconnect/reconcile them without redispatching effects, and separate output backpressure from connection liveness. Bound file ingestion before allocating it and preserve typed recovery information. No tests run.

2821142e-9374-5df0-bc7f-e094b722791d.title: [L161] A historical fork with a pinned queued input fails its own child-state validation

Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L161.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/record/seed.rs:31-53`; `control/inputs/transition.rs:10-18`; `control/context.rs:119-127`; child creation `control/record/transition.rs:94-106,57-58`; aggregate validation `control/record/projection.rs:206-210`.
- **Blocker/enforcement:** Historical seed generation converts queued inputs to Held so a child cannot silently inherit pending execution. It clones the source context-preference ledger unchanged, including exact input pins. Pins require Queued or Incorporated state. Installing such a seed in the child and validating it therefore rejects a queued input's retained pin as InvalidInput. A valid source conversation can generate a seed that cannot become a valid fork.

The root cause is incompatible transformations of queue lifecycle and context treatment, not missing deadline configuration. No automatic reconciliation preserves the pin's historical meaning in the child here.
- **Classification:** Source-confirmed fork/context lifecycle blocker; no runtime reproduction claimed. Independent child execution authority must remain separate while copied public context becomes internally valid.

2942d1e2-111f-5b5f-b76c-14da38046e29.title: [L650] Quality parsing depends on volatile event delivery rather than complete published artifacts
2942d1e2-111f-5b5f-b76c-14da38046e29.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L650.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/execution/active.rs:20-63,83-93,116-127,143-177,216-235`; `src/parser.rs:25-70`; `src/observation.rs:104-139`.
- Behavior: Selected parsers accumulate stdout/terminal bytes solely from process events in 256-event polls. Any sequence gap (including non-output events) or parser-buffer overflow permanently marks parsing incomplete. Complete output artifacts are published afterward, but the parser does not reopen those artifacts to recover missing bytes. The cursor, definition, parser buffer, flags, owner, and result are local memory. recover merely polls that same live object; there is no reconstruction/adoption constructor. With OutputParser::None the parser returns NotRequested immediately, while infrastructure/output completeness is still independently required.
- Consequence: A lagging consumer can classify a correct check as InvalidResult despite complete recoverable output, and replacing the quality execution object cannot reconnect its parsing context. Complete evidence must remain required; the blocker is the delivery-dependent way it is obtained.
- Repair direction: Parse content-addressed complete output or persist a resumable parser cursor/state, and implement durable same-operation owner/result adoption. Preserve failure on actually incomplete or invalid output.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

2a52df1b-186c-5f7c-a7e1-f5102beee11a.title: [L160] Clearing a goal cancels its record but does not permit a new goal in the same conversation through these controls
2a52df1b-186c-5f7c-a7e1-f5102beee11a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L160.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/record/transition/goal.rs:71-100,219-264`; previously read goal lifecycle L031-L034.
- **Blockers/enforcement:** StartExecution rejects archived conversations, any existing execution, zero run ID, or an empty eligible pending input view. StartGoal rejects ANY existing goal record and requires exact equality with the current brief objective before starting execution. ClearGoal invokes `goal.cancel` rather than removing the goal/execution bindings; this module exposes no transition that clears either retained binding. Therefore a fresh StartGoal/StartExecution after cancellation is refused by these controls, even though the cancelled evidence is correctly retained.
- **Recovery distinction:** Existing execution/goal continuation has separate controls, and caller/UI behavior has not yet been traced. This finding does not assert all follow-up messages fail; it identifies the explicit new-run/new-goal path and its lack of a successor lineage transition. Fork/new conversation may provide an alternate path, but should not be assumed equivalent to continuing the user's session/context.

2b095b4a-7410-5654-a261-8a695ec23b92.title: [L348] B1 validates all retained accounting history on every transition and query
2b095b4a-7410-5654-a261-8a695ec23b92.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L348.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-budget/src/transition.rs:89-112,149-192,254-265,297-308`, `src/state.rs:216-247,307-313`, `src/transition/validation/accounts.rs:55-115`, `src/transition/validation/reservations.rs:24-100`, `src/transition/validation/structure.rs:25-46,94-118`, `src/transition/validation/refinement.rs:60-64,113-119,157-161`, `src/transition/lifecycle/retry.rs:29-105`.
- Behavior: each transition validates the complete input, copies all accounts and reservation tombstones, validates the complete output, and checks immutable/monotonic prefixes plus ancestor propagation. Even a checked single-account or single-reservation query revalidates the entire ledger. Each reservation performs earlier-prefix uniqueness and exact-action retry-history scans; each account recomputes child and operation-reservation sums. Closed accounts and settled/cancelled reservations remain in the vectors; shrinking them violates refinement. The closed command vocabulary has no retirement/checkpoint-fold command.
- Consequence: reservation validation alone is quadratic in retained reservation count per query/transition; repeated operations over growing history can produce cumulative cubic validation work. There is no async yield/cancellation contract inside this pure synchronous call. It can delay whichever host lane invokes it, including observation or cancellation commands that also pay validation costs. This is a source-level complexity finding, not a measured live-session latency diagnosis or a claim that a numeric work-count cap exists here.
- Repair direction: retain immutable receipts outside the active accounting frontier; verify incremental updates and ancestor balances, maintain identity/action indexes, and separate full-history validation from ordinary control admission. Preserve accounting integrity and old exact replay through durable indexed receipts. Scope: the complete 123-file budget crate, including proof modules and tests, is now read; no benchmark/test execution.


Additional source evidence: `src/accounting_prefix_model.rs:54-96,207-246` contains ordinary executable `fn` witnesses that recursively walk the remaining account/reservation suffix; the five-axis wrappers repeat that walk. `src/accounting_model.rs:257-345` and `src/accounting_model/aggregation.rs:16-78` add full-account recursive contribution witnesses to lineage charging. These are included by `src/lib.rs:11-12`, unlike erased `spec fn`/`proof fn` definitions. They add source-level recursion and traversal pressure; optimized release cost and stack behavior have not been measured, so no particular production stall or stack threshold is claimed. Account-count traversal fuel is a structural termination witness, not a configured daily-driving deadline.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

2d24e7f6-75ce-51c8-8d4a-cd4fb9b8fe8f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L388.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-policy/src/evaluation_predicates.rs:11-72`, `src/ceiling.rs:75-79`, `src/evaluation_constraints.rs:173-203`, `src/evaluation.rs:192-218`, `tests/cases/constraints_approval.rs:76-137`, `tests/cases/constraints_approval.rs:293-320`, `tests/cases/reference_model.rs:38-57`.
- Behavior: coverage uses a union of grants, but effective validity and use limits intersect every grant whose identity and any requested permission match. Grant applicability has no observed-time condition. Already complete coverage does not stop additional grants from tightening the whole scope. One expired matching grant remains effective even if another grant supplies valid current coverage. Cross-epoch and disjoint-window grants are admitted as canonical inputs, then produce whole-request semantic denial during evaluation.
- Consequence: retaining an old overlapping grant alongside its intended successor can make fresh authorization remain Expired or EmptyConstraintIntersection. Reauthorization against the same definition does not change that result, and restriction-only amendments preserve the ceiling as described in L386. Tests explicitly require all-applicable intersection, including contradictory epochs; this is current contract behavior, not a claim that the installed daemon has rotated grants this way or that the reducer itself loops.
- Repair direction: distinguish explicit restrictive constraints from alternative or superseded grants in the authority model. Select or retire grants through a reviewed successor-authority transition, retain history as evidence, and report the exact blocking grant/window. Preserve deliberate security restrictions while making renewal possible without replacing a session. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

2d62f08d-4c47-55b9-93a7-5dfa45315a03.title: [L618] Windows helper narrows target status and hides post-activation failure causes
2d62f08d-4c47-55b9-93a7-5dfa45315a03.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L618.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/native/launch.rs:108-127`; `src/helper_process.rs:9-13,34-44`; `src/runner.rs:139-168` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Native target exit is read as unsigned 32-bit then clamped to signed-32-bit maximum; helper entry converts the resulting signed value to unsigned eight-bit ExitCode, replacing values outside 0-255 with generic failure. Post-activation target execution/observation errors are replaced by reserved TargetCreate. Phase-aware classification correctly preserves the reserved numeric range when activation has been observed, but cannot restore discarded wide status or failure causes.
- Consequence: Windows target errors and platform exception values can lose their original identity, undermining root-cause diagnosis and recovery selection. Actual target status publication is constrained by the helper's artificial eight-bit representation rather than the native Windows status width.
- Repair direction: Carry exact native target termination and structured post-activation failures through the authenticated status channel and journal independently of helper process exit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

3120378a-a23e-5b6a-b1f3-7650f830420f.title: [L277] An interrupted command between durable admission and dispatch is permanently rejected on exact retry
3120378a-a23e-5b6a-b1f3-7650f830420f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L277.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/command/service.rs:44-108`; `authority/owner/storage.rs:17-42`; `command/service_tests.rs:131-216`; `startup/recovery.rs:10-60`.
- submit performs admission, domain dispatch, and terminal settlement as separate awaited owner messages. Interruption after admission can leave Pending with no domain commit. Existing Pending/Indeterminate never goes back to dispatch: it calls reconcile_command, whose DefinitelyAbsent branch durably rejects the command as **UnsupportedFamily**, irrespective of the actual submitted family.
- Every dispatch Err also tries to mark Indeterminate and ignores any settlement error. A definitely-uncommitted retryable storage failure can therefore enter the same terminal rejection path on retry. The immutable idempotency key then retains that rejection; submitting exact intent again cannot perform the intended work.
- This gate confuses definitely absent with unsupported and has no admitted-intent resume path. Repair must persist enough exact intent and ownership to resume/reject truthfully under the same identity, while resolving committed effects first. Changing session/window or command identity is not an equivalent repair.
- The complete service tests preseed a domain commit before application admission and cover historical v1 committed recovery. They do not exercise the admission-before-dispatch interruption. The subsequently fully read black-box `tests/daemon_conformance_support/session/indeterminate.rs:33-94` explicitly seeds an uncommitted Indeterminate command and requires UnsupportedFamily plus durable Rejected after restart. The conformance expectation therefore codifies this no-work recovery outcome; it must change with the lifecycle contract. The complete startup recovery implementation uses the same permanent UnsupportedFamily rejection before intake for every DefinitelyAbsent request. Scheduler durability has now been fully read and uses SHA256 of the exact encoded command bytes, matching the application ledger; no scheduler digest mismatch was found. The other domain adapters remain to be traced. **Complete service, owner and startup reconciliation read; no crash/failure reproduction run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

31c11fbe-5dbc-58e0-b406-ce5eb7b6b1cb.title: [L564] Linux cgroups impose a fixed CPU throttle alongside configured resource limits
31c11fbe-5dbc-58e0-b406-ce5eb7b6b1cb.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L564.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-linux/src/cgroup.rs:90-143`; `src/native/rlimit.rs:1-35`; `src/descriptor.rs:105-154` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Every prepared cgroup receives `cpu.max = 100000 100000`, regardless of the requested CPU-time budget. Preparation requires delegation of CPU, memory, and process controllers together. Native rlimits separately impose configured address-space, file-size, file-descriptor, process, and CPU bounds; a zero CPU duration skips that rlimit.
- Consequence: An untimed execution can still be throttled to one CPU. Missing any required controller rejects preparation. The disk allocation is applied as a per-file `RLIMIT_FSIZE`, which does not enforce the aggregate disk meaning of that allocation. These are source properties, not measurements of the installed daemon.
- Repair direction: Represent CPU bandwidth separately from CPU duration and allow an explicitly unbounded bandwidth policy. Require only the controls necessary for the authorized plan, preserving containment. Give aggregate disk accounting its own enforcement and recovery semantics.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

327a2b4b-41b7-54ab-94ad-011e5d88925e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L091.

Observation handles alone cannot preserve ownership across daemon loss. Crash-watchdog/recovery behavior remains under review.

Recovery needs evidence-based ownership reconciliation and a durable policy for continued authorized work; automatic duplicate execution is not safe merely because a limiter is unwanted. Ordinary FailWork with Retryable also becomes terminal Exhausted at the immutable bound; otherwise it releases to RetryPending, and RetryWork requires that phase plus attempt room. **Complete work definition, phase, terminal, dispatch, retry/failure mutation and single-reservation loss classification/release read; batch loss and effect-shell recovery callers pending.**

33919718-7569-5cc7-9cc0-73216dd0fa30.title: [L420] E2 retry eligibility is persisted as a bare clock tick without epoch or bounded-delay proof
33919718-7569-5cc7-9cc0-73216dd0fa30.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L420.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-debugger/src/aggregate/types/model.rs:73-102,298-400`, `src/runtime/model.rs:150-187`, `src/aggregate/reducer/apply/model.rs:48-68,164-187`, `src/aggregate/command.rs:240-256`, `src/model/runner.rs:73-167` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Retry scheduling requires delay_ticks > 0 and <= the immutable maximum, then stores now_tick + delay_ticks as a u64 not-before tick. The aggregate only checks a positive not-before tick and next attempt identity, so direct command admission cannot validate the runtime's delay ceiling. Start compares caller start ticks to the saved tick. No epoch, tick unit, origin, rebase transition, or elapsed-time clock is carried by these records. The runner and durable attempt executor read here have no E2 wall-time watchdog; the compiled 24-hour resource label in L415 is not enforced by these paths.
- Consequence: If a caller changes/reset its tick origin while retaining the job, an old pending eligibility tick can block a restarted attempt until the new clock catches up. Actual caller clock behavior is not established here. Conversely, the reducer can admit an arbitrarily distant positive retry tick despite a smaller frozen delay policy. The positive delay/finite attempt policy cannot be amended on the job, while provider hangs depend on the provider's cancellation responsiveness. Do not describe the 24-hour label as an observed running deadline.
- Repair direction: Bind scheduling to an explicit durable clock contract with epoch handling, and validate the same scheduling policy at every admission boundary. Make backoff and stopping an explicit user policy while preserving job/context identity. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

33eaa4c1-073f-5456-9b34-f39135b2908a.title: [L802] Some display bounds can hide recovery details or omit wide characters
33eaa4c1-073f-5456-9b34-f39135b2908a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L802.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/render/prompts.rs:1-141`, `chat/transcript.rs:134-170`, `status.rs:1-82`, `tabs.rs:1-81`, and `chat/status.rs:1-51`, all completely read; additional content renderers in this batch completely read.
- Behavior: Prompt scrolling uses u16 offsets and saturates its maximum at 65,535 wrapped rows, unlike the workbench inspector's usize row slicing. Transcript wrapping skips a grapheme whose cell width exceeds the available width; at width one a wide character can disappear from visible/copyable rows. General status uses a single unwrapped line, while chat uses two unwrapped lines, so long recovery messages are clipped by terminal width. RecoveryRequired always advertises `/retry` without consulting the operation's legal-control set; the control handler can then refuse that action. Queue previews disclose their three-line/160-character truncation and offer exact full-text inspection, while briefs disclose the existing eight-proposal/8,192-byte exclusions. These are presentation/input-access boundaries, not execution deadlines.
- Consequence: A narrow display can obscure the cause/action needed to leave a blocked state, and sufficiently long valid prompt projections would outgrow the scroll representation. A displayed retry hint does not prove that a recovery transition is legal or executable. None of these findings establishes the current live lockup by itself.
- Repair direction: Use addressable row paging/usize navigation, preserve indivisible wide graphemes through resizing, and derive visible recovery actions from the same legal-control/reconciliation state as dispatch. Keep exact authority IDs and distinguish observed accounting from unavailable provider counters.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

34691ec1-f89d-5d55-8142-140d74664895.title: [L670] Optional startup update discovery remains on the critical launch path without cancellation or durable download continuation
34691ec1-f89d-5d55-8142-140d74664895.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L670.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/app.rs:72-79`; `src/update.rs:13-44,85-118`; `src/update/release.rs:57-83`; `src/update/download.rs:15-107,125-172`; `src/update/install.rs:9-78,90-120`; `src/update/process.rs:18-108`.
- Behavior: Default-on cached release discovery is awaited before workspace/provider setup or TUI entry. The six-hour interval suppresses update polling; it does not expire sessions. HTTP clients configure no explicit timeout/cancellation here; release/checksum bodies are read completely before the 64-KiB/exact-hex check. Archives stream with a 1-GiB cap, but retry deletes the same release staging directory rather than resuming and has no update lock. Extraction/native install/version check explicitly pass None to the optional-deadline process helper. Its stdout drains with bounded retention but joins until EOF; a descendant holding the pipe can prevent return. Windows defers update into an untracked helper that waits for the parent PID and verifies only the CLI version.
- Consequence: An optional network operation or helper can hold up daily startup, and interrupted/repeated updates lose download progress or collide in staging. The source contains no active synthetic default updater execution timer; removing timers does not provide UI responsiveness, cancellation, or durable continuation automatically. Platform/architecture and exact release-tag admission remain separate packaging gates.
- Repair direction: Run optional discovery outside launch-critical work under a cancellable owner, persist resumable download/install receipts, coordinate staging ownership, and verify completion of the complete installed application/daemon pair.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

349759b7-037f-504f-9524-3a94cd71be71.title: [L806] Web stop shares the send wait, while supposedly observational recovery can start execution
349759b7-037f-504f-9524-3a94cd71be71.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L806.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/api.rs:100-168,181-214`; `src/operations.rs:13-60`, `src/daemon/chat.rs:35-65,67-201`, `src/daemon/receipts.rs:66-115,139-177,223-251` in that crate.
- Behavior: send, control and model settings take the same conversation mutex for the entire awaited request pipeline. A missing reply holds it indefinitely; stop waits behind send. GET operation observation invokes recover_send, which drives create/queue/start/continuation and can retransmit an exact domain command. Observation does not take the operation/conversation guards used by mutations; manual acknowledgement calls observation first.
- Consequence: a stalled submission can prevent cancellation through the same UI, and polling or review of an uncertain operation can cause execution rather than merely report its disposition. Concurrent recovery observes may race. Exact domain identities reduce duplicate effects but do not make this a read-only operation or prove native ownership recovery. Removing a timer alone leaves the shared-control blocker.
- Repair direction: give controls and receipt inspection independent access to the owning operation, make observation read-only, and route explicitly authorized resume through serialized durable operation state. Preserve unknown-effect and exact-command fences.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

34b9ac54-db16-5932-8e1b-d4b6ba798e81.title: [L258] Durable sessions have no age limit, but closing is irreversible and command recovery has no continuation cursor
34b9ac54-db16-5932-8e1b-d4b6ba798e81.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L258.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/application/session_store.rs`; `application/session_types.rs`; `application/command_store.rs:169-199`; `application/command_types.rs`.
- The session store contains **no TTL, session-count ceiling or age retirement**. It keeps the same SessionId across explicit protocol-negotiation updates. Active→Draining→Closed is monotonic and Closed cannot be reopened through this adapter. Transport loss must therefore remain separate from durable session closure (the inspected daemon disconnect path does preserve this separation, L236).
- Opening an existing session requires exact actor/authority/created/protocol/version facts. Protocol refresh must use observe_application_session_negotiation, which updates metadata in place rather than opening a new identity. The lifecycle advance checks the old state in a separate read, then UPDATEs only by session_id; concurrent independent connections could defeat the advertised monotonic check unless callers serialize them. Actual concurrent production use is not established here.
- Unsettled-command recovery returns **1..4096** rows ordered by command_id without a cursor/offset. This is not a 4096-command lifetime quota, but a still-unresolved first page cannot be bypassed to enumerate later rows through this method. One malformed row fails the entire batch. Pending/Indeterminate commands are durable with no elapsed auto-settlement; completion/rejection requires exact receipts. **All session/principal/command implementation files fully read; startup recovery callers and paging behavior partly covered elsewhere.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

351c6e2a-6c12-53e0-ae74-e19199171dc4.title: [L334] D1 full checkpoints impose a cumulative evidence-size ceiling below advertised per-gate maxima
351c6e2a-6c12-53e0-ae74-e19199171dc4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L334.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-gates/src/wire/state.rs:51-83,152-187,268-287`; `src/wire/mod.rs:252-280`; `src/canonical.rs:25-69`; `src/durability.rs:159-170,214-237`; `src/evidence/receipt.rs:91-119`; `src/descriptor.rs:16-24`.
- **Blocker:** Every transition encodes one complete GateStateFrame under production codec limits: 16 MiB frame, with sixteen bytes of frame overhead. Passed gates retain full publication requirements, admitted evidence mappings and artifact metadata. No completed-gate receipt retirement, external receipt reference or whole-state capacity proof is applied by the reducer before progress.
- **Bound analysis:** Each requirement is written once as a 32-byte declaration and again in a 104-byte admitted mapping. The individual advertised maxima of 1,024 gates and 1,024 requirements per gate therefore allow 136 MiB of those fields alone, before slots, attempts, artifacts and headers. This arithmetic describes the D1 representation mismatch; no maximally populated B2 contract or large passing fixture was built in this audit.
- **Consequence:** Any otherwise admissible successor above the frame ceiling fails with Codec/Quarantine before C0 append. In-memory authority remains at the old state, so preserving the same candidate cannot complete further evidence publication through this representation. Earlier successful checks remain durable, and cancellation may still be representable; this is not a claim that every control command fails at the same threshold.
- **Repair direction:** Use bounded current frontier plus exact immutable receipt references and independently paged records. Validate representation admission before effects and preserve post-effect observations separately from presentation/cumulative checkpoint capacity.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

35fefe1c-2525-54ea-a32f-7bab52b2b993.title: [L389] Policy evaluation repeatedly scans canonical sets and recurses over unbounded input collections
35fefe1c-2525-54ea-a32f-7bab52b2b993.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L389.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-policy/src/scope.rs:303-350`, `src/scope_selector.rs:120-140`, `src/scope_selector/containment.rs:100-250`, `src/evaluation_predicates.rs:11-95`, `src/operation.rs:208-288`, `src/operation_access.rs:28-75`, `src/operation_risks.rs:70-138`, `src/operation_risk_fold.rs:61-113`.
- Behavior: canonical permission membership scans the whole vector without stopping when sorted order has passed the target; subset and selector checks repeat that lookup for each input value. Coverage scans grants separately for each requested permission. Operation validation performs a fresh recursive registry lookup per permission, and risk derivation repeats those searches for each of ten risk categories. Executable denial/coverage/operation helpers recurse with depth proportional to grant, rule, permission or descriptor counts. The pure constructors do not impose independent count caps on those collections.
- Consequence: equally growing permission sets already give quadratic subset/matching work, and growing permission/registry inputs multiply lookup cost. Deep recursive helpers depend on the build's stack behavior rather than an iterative implementation. This is source-grounded workload and stack-growth potential; no benchmark, stack overflow, installed input scale or live lockup has been demonstrated. Mathematical spec functions and proof blocks are distinct from the executable helpers cited here; six policy tiers and ten risk variants are enum cardinalities, not daily quotas.
- Repair direction: use merge walks, exact indexed or binary lookups, and iterative scans while retaining the verified ordering and exact-pair contracts. Avoid solving the scalability problem by adding a small lifetime quota or timer; isolate expensive evaluation from control responsiveness. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

366a538f-406f-5695-85f8-a5573da0c2ac.title: [L196] Guidance paging follows full replay, and all eligible guidance must fit a 64 KiB request block
366a538f-406f-5695-85f8-a5573da0c2ac.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L196.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_control/storage/guidance.rs:52-98,116-144`; `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/workbench/memory.rs:16-23`; `memory/render.rs:61-129,183-192`.
- Inspection allocates and validates every catalog identity before scope/forgotten filtering and before returning a **32-row page**. Missing/corrupt state for an invisible or forgotten record aborts the query; changing the page offset cannot avoid it. Row totals/offsets are u32/usize checked, while actor/workspace authorization is required.
- Future-request capture similarly rebuilds all catalog rows, filters eligible active guidance and renders all selected records. Exact rendered text, provenance framing and escapes must fit **64 KiB**; overflow fails the entire render and the daemon maps that failure to InvalidInput. Pinning affects ordering, not selection or size. There is no overflow selection/compaction branch in these files. The declaration's comment mentions a row limit for rendering, but the renderer itself enforces bytes rather than the inspection page's 32-row count.
- Each guidance text is limited to **8 KiB**, each forget reason to **1 KiB** (also L156); newline, tab, quote and backslash escaping can expand accepted raw text. Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L658.

User-input/cancellation admission does not require signed authority time. Necessary explicit authority validity must not become automatic loss of conversation or native model context; renewal/reissue handling remains pending.
- **Complete prompt broker, authority target/restoration, clock, authentication and tests read; tests not run.** Errors preserve capacity versus stale authority versus invalid authentication categories, but these functions do not themselves renew a challenge.

3aa2fc20-2eb1-599a-ac3b-47abb262a34c.title: [L568] Linux capability probing can block indefinitely before execution is prepared
3aa2fc20-2eb1-599a-ac3b-47abb262a34c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L568.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-linux/src/backend.rs:27-33`; `src/preparation.rs:83-96`; `src/probe.rs:108-117,305-347`; `src/descriptor.rs:105-154` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Backend creation and authorized preparation run native probes. Probe commands use blocking `Command::output`; diagnostic truncation occurs after all output has been collected. Proxy connection probing is blocking. Executable hashing checks a 128 MiB metadata size and then reads the whole file without a read-time bound or cancellation. Baseline admission also requires PTY capability even for pipe-based commands.
- Consequence: A hanging probe can lock preparation indefinitely without a synthetic deadline being involved. A growing executable can exceed the pre-read size check. Unneeded PTY failure or a changed probe digest can reject an otherwise usable plan.
- Repair direction: Make probing cancellable, stream bounded diagnostics and hashes, and bind capability requirements to the requested execution. Preserve exact integrity checks while giving probe changes a supported reconciliation path.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

3d61f536-be63-56b2-8295-75045745e41d.title: [L360] E1 full diagnostic history prevents terminal failure or conflict settlement
3d61f536-be63-56b2-8295-75045745e41d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L360.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/aggregate/reducer/settlement.rs:101-123`, `src/aggregate/reducer.rs:195-236`, `src/aggregate/command.rs:36-81`, `src/domain/limits.rs:36`, `src/materialization/failure.rs:35-57`, `src/materialization/failure.rs:91-105`.
- Behavior: recording a materialization failure or reconciling a conflict removes pending work only in a cloned candidate state, then rejects if 1,024 retained failures (or a tightened maximum) already exist. The rejected transition leaves the original pending plan intact. The entire closed command vocabulary has receipt retirement but no failure retirement, diagnostic rollover, or limit amendment. Successful settlement separately rejects a full hot receipt map, but can recover by explicitly retiring a settled receipt first.
- Consequence: diagnostic capacity can block recording a true terminal failure and preserve a pending plan that blocks later plans for the same workspace. No cancellation command provides an alternate cleanup path within this aggregate. 3dd0ec14-b291-55aa-8710-d6e168dc73a1.title: [L795] Queue reorder requires every pending ID but the composer cannot hold the largest valid order
3dd0ec14-b291-55aa-8710-d6e168dc73a1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L795.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/queue.rs:1-257`, `library.rs:1-133`, and `fork.rs:1-106`, completely read; larger fixed queue/domain bounds in L705 and composer bound in L784.
- Behavior: Reorder accepts one textual list containing all pending 32-hex IDs and constructs the whole vector before the input-order validator. The protocol admits up to 65,535 IDs, requiring about 2.16 MiB of textual identifiers and separators, beyond the 1 MiB composer task bound. Queue text itself remains capped at 8,192 bytes. Paged row selection preserves exact input revision/identity, and aggregate refresh does not reinterpret an old row against a reordered list. Library navigation is paged; fork requires exact checkpoint references and truncates only the generated title at a UTF-8 boundary.
- Consequence: The UI cannot express a valid maximum-size reorder even though the underlying order type accepts it. Page sizes/title presentation do not end execution. Immutable row/checkpoint/workspace checks are authority boundaries, not synthetic runtime ceilings.
- Repair direction: Represent reorder as durable incremental moves or an uploaded/reference-backed exact order, with a revision fence and completion receipt. Retain identity-based selection and independently progressing page reads.

3e100cb5-a5cf-56c6-b568-e9bd016a6976.title: [L611] Windows ConPTY control workers have detached and blocking ownership
3e100cb5-a5cf-56c6-b568-e9bd016a6976.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L611.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/native/handle.rs:40-66,69-164`.
- Behavior: Terminal dimensions are accepted as unsigned 16-bit earlier but converted to signed 16-bit during native activation. Input and control thread join handles are immediately discarded. Input relay and signal control hold the same writer mutex across blocking write/flush; close-input control needs that mutex. Read errors, malformed controls, resize failure and write failure silently stop workers. Terminal destruction closes the console without joining those workers.
- Consequence: Backpressure can prevent control and input-close progress, and a worker can silently disappear without a session failure observation. Native teardown cannot establish worker quiescence from retained joins; late console controls can race owner destruction. The 8,192-byte relay chunk is a throughput choice, not a lifetime quota.
- Repair direction: Retain and supervise workers, interrupt blocked I/O through explicit cancellation, serialize console lifetime and controls, and validate native terminal dimensions before consuming execution authority.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

3ef6cb65-0edc-5585-ad4c-eafbf72fd8bf.title: [L534] Managed networking requires finite connection and owner lifetimes
3ef6cb65-0edc-5585-ad4c-eafbf72fd8bf.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L534.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/plan.rs:34-90`, `src/accounting.rs:44-98`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:92-148`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:19-27`, `src/proxy/connect.rs:28-33`, `src/canonical.rs:8-59`.
- Behavior: NetworkBounds requires positive connection duration and a positive proxy-owner duration at least as large, plus positive per-connection bytes and aggregate bytes at least as large. There is no None/unlimited mode. The owner stops accepting once elapsed time reaches total_millis, cancels workers and revokes its configured credential. Workers and upstream sockets install mandatory connection_millis read/write/connect timeouts and enforce elapsed connection accounting. Other ceilings are 1..1,024 accepted connections, 1..maximum_connections concurrent workers, 4..65,536 retained observations and 256 bytes..1 MiB headers. Canonical plans have a fixed 2 MiB bound checked after complete allocation.
- Consequence: Long-running authorized network work is terminated by a synthetic lifetime even when making progress. Persistent process/session ownership does not remove these separate proxy deadlines. This crate exposes caller-selected values, not the actual installed caller values; native sandbox callers still require complete reading. Plan bytes bind these values and currently provide no widening/renewal operation.
- Repair direction: Model absent execution deadlines directly, separate transport cancellation/progress from explicit authority expiry, and preserve recoverable quota/backpressure state. Do not substitute a very large integer for an unlimited lifecycle. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

3f0289b4-e455-58a4-89bd-c714cc13e70b.title: [L407] B3 agent DTO constructors check only opaque payload capacity before admitting complete records
3f0289b4-e455-58a4-89bd-c714cc13e70b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L407.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-protocol/src/agent/wire.rs:12-25`, `src/agent/command.rs:113-144`, `src/agent/command.rs:209-225`, `src/agent/event.rs:115-146`, `src/agent/event.rs:211-227`, `src/agent/state.rs:149-187`, `src/agent/state.rs:277-298`, `tests/agent.rs:148-165`, `tests/fixtures/v1/agent-command.bin` (complete 315-byte inspection).
- Behavior: new() validates the opaque bytes using a temporary writer containing only that length-prefixed field, then retains metadata and the payload. Full command/event/state encoding adds identities, revision, phases, counters, digest claims and frame overhead later. For example, a source-derived command with the golden fixture's field shapes and a 900-byte payload can pass the isolated check under frame 1,024 / payload 1,008 / opaque 1,000 limits, while its complete frame is 1,199 bytes and cannot encode under the same limits. The existing constructor test covers opaque excess, not metadata overhead. Hashing separately allocates a domain-prefixed copy of the payload; constructor validation also creates a serialized copy.
- Consequence: successful construction does not establish complete-frame representability, even when callers use the same explicit limits afterward. A caller that treats new() as pre-admission wire validation can encounter a later capacity failure. No effect dispatch/commit ordering or installed failure is established solely by these inert DTO files. The production opaque and frame bounds themselves were already recorded in L009.
- Repair direction: validate complete canonical records before durable/effect admission, with one shared size calculation or checked full encoding and structured capacity errors. Avoid redundant complete payload copies where streaming hashing/encoding can preserve exact semantics. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4125beff-0748-530a-8936-036f4fe5b159.title: [L582] A dirty Git workspace can lose the only object needed to finalize its candidate
4125beff-0748-530a-8936-036f4fe5b159.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L582.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-workspace/src/mutation.rs:13-20,60-65,111-119`; `src/candidate.rs:64-75,282-302`; `src/rollback.rs:99-100`; `src/gateway.rs:50-70`; `src/reconcile.rs:233-250` in the same crate.
- Behavior: A successful patch leaves the workspace dirty and returns a private-field `MutationOutcome`. Candidate creation requires that outcome and the dirty condition. Patch application and rollback require the clean condition. Restart reconciliation can classify a restored workspace dirty, but these APIs do not reconstruct or decode the required mutation outcome from its durable patch/action metadata.
- Consequence: After losing the in-memory outcome, the target API has no supported candidate-finalization path for the successfully applied patch. A known dirty workspace also cannot invoke rollback through this gateway. Exact dirtiness is correctly reported, but continuation remains unavailable here.
- Repair direction: Persist and restore the exact mutation outcome and candidate obligation. Admit independently authorized rollback/reconciliation from known dirty state with explicit preimages and lineage checks, instead of requiring the clean state that the repair is meant to establish.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

416eb039-1811-5b81-85e7-03d6cbccde9a.title: [L387] Policy clock-epoch recovery guidance cannot repair the retained authority floor
416eb039-1811-5b81-85e7-03d6cbccde9a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L387.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-policy/src/time.rs:52-137`, `src/capability_use_model.rs:63-95`, `src/capability_failure.rs:10-138`, `src/failure/metadata.rs:36-48`, `src/decision.rs:16-58`.
- Behavior: a clock-epoch mismatch is classified as Reobserve. The authority state and capability preserve their original epoch on failure, and subsequent observations must still use that exact epoch. Reobserving a new epoch cannot advance or rebind either value. A same-epoch regression can recover by obtaining a tick at or beyond the retained floor, but changing epochs is a different operation. The failed capability-use result retains the unchanged capability and error, while the owned use request is not included in that result.
- Consequence: a generic handler that follows Reobserve against a clock whose epoch has changed can repeat the identical rejection indefinitely. The pure crate has no internal retry loop or session teardown, and an actual installed clock change remains to be established. Callers must separately retain pending action intent and distinguish clock catch-up from obtaining fresh authority; otherwise recovery lacks the request that failed.
- Repair direction: classify epoch change separately and route it to an explicit successor-authority transition with preserved pending action identity. Keep clock regression checks, avoid silently accepting a new epoch as existing authority, and return or durably retain the exact rejected request for recovery. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

42057b18-7280-5ea7-bb5b-38680e3ef957.title: [L314] E0 exact committed retries still depend on the latest checkpoint
42057b18-7280-5ea7-bb5b-38680e3ef957.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L314.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/durability.rs:94-104,230-276,369-381`; `src/integration_tests/durability.rs:16-39,134-153`; `src/runtime/driver.rs:84-106`; `src/reducer.rs:155-175`.
- **Blocker:** C0 can resolve the exact command digest and original event, but E0 also requires the current checkpoint to equal that command's original successor. If later work advanced the same run, the exact committed retry returns StaleState/Replay rather than its historical committed receipt. This is safer than the scheduler/collaboration adapters' quarantine classification (L284/L306), but still requires a separate caller recovery path. The driver itself attempts reduction before command resolution, so resubmitting an already consumed command at its current successor fails the reducer fence first.
- **Consequence:** A delayed acknowledgment or retried request cannot be treated as successful from this API alone after progress. Blindly reissuing a new command to work around it risks duplicating semantics; blindly returning the failure can strand a caller even though its work committed. Underlying journal failures are collapsed into static External/Replay messages, losing the distinct journal recovery action.
- **Repair direction:** Resolve exact historical command receipts independently of the mutable current checkpoint. Reconcile the driver's current state separately and preserve typed journal failure/recovery evidence. Do not weaken identity/digest conflict checks.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete adapter/driver/tests inspection. Tests retry immediately before advancing/reopening; no delayed retry after a later commit or caller stall was executed.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4265b31b-dc52-5c35-9e61-832378afd2d6.title: [L291] Removing scheduler workers does not free registration capacity, and drain/terminal lifecycles have no reopening path
4265b31b-dc52-5c35-9e61-832378afd2d6.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L291.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/reducer/apply/worker_control.rs:9-34,68-83`; `worker.rs:107-141`; `state/mutation/scheduler_phase.rs`; `reducer/apply/control/finalization.rs:129-198`.
- Registration compares the **entire retained worker vector** with the immutable worker limit (compiled maximum **4,096**). RemoveWorker only sets Removed; it deletes no record. A removed identity cannot be restored Available or registered again, and it still consumes retention. Repeated replacement workers can exhaust registration even with no live ownership.
- Worker concurrency must be **1..active_reservations**, execution classes are nonempty/canonical among five supported classes, and resource dimension/capacity checks are finite. Descriptor fields have no update command; quiescent Lost/Draining workers can return Available only before removal.
- DrainScheduler closes new work and worker admission. Pause/Resume can preserve or return to Draining, but there is no Undrain. Freshly constructing an entirely new authorized policy is distinct from the restricted amendment API.

467a4695-11b7-5e68-9513-fdce257127b1.title: [L664] Immutable launcher snapshots can repeatedly replace the same shared daemon
467a4695-11b7-5e68-9513-fdce257127b1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L664.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/app.rs:77-116`; `src/daemon.rs:145-190,198-233,281-341`; `src/bootstrap/configuration.rs:73-87,354-368`.
- Behavior: Each launch retains one PreparedProduct/configuration snapshot throughout its recovery loop. The endpoint is derived from the stable installation/store identity. ensure_ready shuts down a reachable daemon whenever the applied marker differs from that snapshot's configuration path or the current daemon-file hash. It does not refresh/adopt current product configuration or negotiate the running daemon's actual generation. The marker is truncated/rewritten after endpoint reachability, contains a configuration path rather than configuration-content hash, and is not tied to an authenticated daemon process instance.
- Consequence: If two live launcher windows hold different configuration generations, each can replace the shared daemon when its TUI reconnects, producing repeat shutdown/reconnect cycles and repeated pressure on runtime/context recovery. A missing/partial marker can also trigger replacement. This is a source-derived causal scenario, not an observed reproduction of the user's current lockup.
- Repair direction: Give shared-daemon configuration reconciliation one durable owner, negotiate/adopt a compatible current generation, and coordinate required replacement with retained active-run/context ownership. A reconnecting presentation client must not repeatedly impose a stale configuration snapshot.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

46992279-83bc-5ddb-9f40-1833df28b0c4.title: [L149] Incomplete or changed discard preparation blocks restart cleanup with no repair operation in this module
46992279-83bc-5ddb-9f40-1833df28b0c4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L149.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/candidate/managed/transaction/owned.rs:52-75,92-168,176-235,244-303`; `transaction/mod.rs:95-109,200-232`; preparation callers `restore/sources.rs:93-118` and `restore/prepared.rs:200-229`.
- **Blockers/enforcement:** Restart checks EVERY recorded staging asset before cleaning any of them. Assets require an exact 90-byte ownership nonce, expected names/ancestors, a closed set of leaf filenames, and a matching sealed directory digest once payload leaves exist. A crash after writing a payload but before persisting its seal leaves `sealed=None`; the next cleanup rejects that asset as incomplete or changed. A foreign entry, changed marker/parent, or replaced Git lock similarly blocks the entire retry. The owner-file lock uses immediate `try_lock`, with no queue/retry here. Marker reading takes 257 bytes for identity checking, not a source-file limit.
- **Recovery distinction:** Preserving foreign or uncertain data is necessary; deleting it would violate ownership. However, this module exposes inspect/execute/prepare, without an explicit path to preserve an uncertain asset separately and then resume recovery. Whether callers expose such resolution remains pending. Test-only publication barriers are compiled out of shipped builds and are not runtime synthetic deadlines.
- **Classification:** Persistent recovery dead-end candidate, rooted in state/ownership transitions rather than an elapsed timeout. The unsealed crash interval is source-confirmed; the crash tests are now fully read, not run. `transaction/tests/crash.rs:33-40,74-96` kills at Prepared and each completed publication barrier, after preparation seals are recorded; it does not inject a kill between payload write and seal save. `transaction/tests.rs:194-208` confirms uncertain/replaced staging is preserved and refuses execution.

47065019-87de-5a1a-b1e7-b44bd777ef22.title: [L167] Unknown receipt format versions are silently skipped during replay
47065019-87de-5a1a-b1e7-b44bd777ef22.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L167.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/developer_tools/receipt/codec.rs:24-81`; `receipt/storage.rs:107-148`.
- The decoder accepts an integer version and known record shape. Storage validates and retains only version 1 records, while advancing past records of every other version without an incompatibility fence. A compatible-shaped record from an unsupported version therefore contributes no remembered effect; a later admission can treat its ordinal as unseen.
- This is a persistence compatibility defect rather than a timeout. Unknown formats should retain an explicit incompatible state or migrate with preserved effect identity. The loader also truncates a genuinely incomplete trailing frame to the last complete offset, but rejects an oversized length prefix before determining whether its body is complete.
- **Source-confirmed; unsupported-version replay and damaged-prefix recovery have not been reproduced in this audit.**

Encoding writes the complete pending map. Decoding rejects it above that receipt-history limit. Commit encodes the candidate checkpoint without decoding it first.

- Repair direction: ensure admitted state remains reconstructible; separate pending admission from receipt-retention policy and negotiate host capacity without invalidating durable work. Retain independent pending records rather than a complete map inside one checkpoint. Migrate reducer, decoder, commit validation, and recovery together.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

473306b7-880e-5f7f-ad0e-f2c3b01cef63.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L651.

Finalization takes the process owner before wait_and_publish, parser classification, result structure, timing, artifact references, and terminal-envelope creation. Only a fully built ToolResult is cached. Publication can return retained C2 terminal facts, but there is no durable local owner/result handoff for a later error. A subsequent poll/recover can encounter quality-owner-missing rather than recover the finished result or retry artifact publication. The capacity boundary and restart gap were inspected, not experimentally reproduced.
- Repair direction: Persist terminal facts and publication receipts before consuming ownership; reserve metadata capacity or account artifacts independently, and make final result assembly/publication retryable without rerunning the check.

47e5938f-adcd-5518-83e3-9ef37bf05504.title: [L295] A late start acknowledgment can erase a requested cancellation, outside the existing non-resurrection proof
47e5938f-adcd-5518-83e3-9ef37bf05504.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L295.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/reducer/apply/cancellation/update.rs:198-232`; `update/activity.rs:10-38`; `state/mutation/reservation_command.rs:42-67`; `state/mutation/acknowledge_start.rs:125-221`; `work_update/apply_at.rs:70-75`; `cancellation/non_resurrection.rs:74-123`.
- Source-traced sequence: DispatchNext creates an unstarted Reserved reservation. CancelWork sets its work to **Cancelling** while retaining that reservation and started=false. AcknowledgeStart checks only that the live reservation is not started, marks it started, and unconditionally sets the work to **Running**. No old-phase admission rejects Cancelling on that path.
- pending_directives then stops emitting its cancellation, because the work is Running. A subsequent newly fenced CompleteWork can be accepted as success. Cancellation intent is represented only by the overwritten phase; the described path can lose the user's requested stop.
- The existing non-resurrection theorem composes Cancel, **late CompleteWork**, AcknowledgeCancellation, then CompleteWork. Its premises exclude AcknowledgeStart between cancellation and completion. Complete graph tests likewise do not exercise this race. Proven field/ownership invariants are narrower than the required monotonic cancellation contract.
- The subsequently read `verified/reservations/readiness/phase.rs:15-18` permits Cancelling with either start bit. `readiness/start.rs:33-58` requires an unstarted reservation but does not require a Reserved predecessor, then specifies a Running successor. Thus the actual start preservation theorem can prove its current ownership relation even while accepting the cancellation reversal. `tests/cancellation_tree.rs:384-394` checks only late success around cancellation acknowledgment. `tests/queue_recovery.rs:152-224` reuses the queue pressure released by Cancelling and then loses the worker; it does not test late start acknowledgment after that reuse.
- Repair must preserve cancellation intent across every late acknowledgment/recovery transition, while accepting truthful owner evidence and retaining exact dispatch identity. **Complete admission/mutation chain and relevant proof scope read; no executable race reproduction or live-instance attribution claimed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4882caea-5e1e-50ee-90d0-6c4806c63d38.title: [L666] Product-state fallback can leave the next generation permanently occupied by corruption
4882caea-5e1e-50ee-90d0-6c4806c63d38.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L666.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/persistence.rs:26-51,54-116,119-159,161-178,235-248`; `src/bootstrap.rs:44-49,71-98,179-198`.
- Behavior: Startup scans/sorts all generation files and falls back from invalid newer payloads to the newest valid state. It does not quarantine or reserve past those rejected generation numbers. A later change increments the recovered state by one; commit refuses an existing final filename with different bytes. Thus valid generation N plus corrupt N+1 permits fallback but blocks the next changed state at N+1. The recovery test uses a far-future corrupt generation and only reloads, so it avoids this immediate-successor collision. Pending publication is removed/restarted; mutable recovery files are replaced by truncating the final file in place. All generation files are retained, with unbounded reads/scans and no content-size check at this boundary.
- Consequence: Apparent fallback recovery can strand provider/workspace/bootstrap changes indefinitely. Interrupted mutable registration/settings replacement can leave a malformed final artifact. These are source-derived recoverability gaps; no corruption was injected into live product state.
- Repair direction: Allocate a new durable generation past every observed/reserved generation or quarantine conflicting candidates with explicit provenance, prove the next save after fallback, and atomically replace recovery files with synchronized receipts.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

499e7390-40a6-557d-978f-b95e87e2acde.title: [L580] A failed workspace action-marker write can poison later opens
499e7390-40a6-557d-978f-b95e87e2acde.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L580.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-workspace/src/consumption.rs:79-126,139-154,167-180,221-246`; `src/writable.rs:65-67`; `src/folder_mutation.rs:110-111,221-233` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Action markers are created exclusively at their final names, then written and synchronized. Errors leave the path in place; the in-memory map is updated only after success. Restore reads each entire file before checking its exact fixed size, and one malformed, inaccessible, misnamed, or mismatched marker rejects the complete revision ledger.
- Consequence: A partial write can make an exact retry appear already consumed and prevent later workspace opens. A complete write followed by synchronization failure is also an ambiguous committed effect without a reconciliation result. Oversized corrupt marker files are fully allocated before rejection.
- Repair direction: Persist a recoverable marker state machine with atomic bounded writes, reconcile exact interrupted writes, and retain the difference between absent, in-flight, and completed actions. Bound reads before allocation and isolate corruption without fabricating completion.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

49ee1e12-f56f-52c6-927e-55e83fc180ac.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L285.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/runtime.rs:226-286,289-383`; `state.rs:131-136`.

This is a source-level starvation condition; the actual effect-shell caller must be traced to determine whether it rotates independently or guarantees timely acknowledgment.
- This function has no elapsed acknowledgment timer, worker-liveness check or independent cancellation capacity. Repair should make progress and cancellation delivery explicit without forfeiting idempotent dispatch identity. **Complete directive implementation and ordering declaration read; production poll caller and concurrency reproduction pending.**

4a56210d-85c3-535f-bc86-bb3fb455a7d1.title: [L357] E1 feature lists can pass construction and encoding but fail canonical reconstruction
4a56210d-85c3-535f-bc86-bb3fb455a7d1.description:

Canonical encoding writes complete feature lists. Both declaration and graph decoders reject a feature list longer than `max_dependency_edges`, even though feature requirements are not dependency edges. Feature text separately has a fixed 128-byte lowercase ASCII limit.

A dependency-edge quota must not silently govern an unrelated feature list at restart. Round-trip admissibility is a prerequisite for publishing durable state; migrate wire and caller checks together.

- Persistence trace: `src/durability/commit.rs:107-126,140-185`, `src/wire/state.rs:17-18,56-66`, `src/wire/event.rs:35-51,58-75`, `src/durability/recovery.rs:91-114` encode and publish the supplied checked transition without an admission round-trip; first restore decodes the nested graph and fails. Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L310.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/command/records.rs:63-114`; `src/state.rs:60-86`; `src/reducer/apply/acceptance.rs:150-180`; `src/reducer/apply.rs:29-41`; `src/reducer/apply/directives.rs:78-91,96-108`; `src/runtime/recovery.rs:36-62`; `src/integration_tests/cancellation.rs:14-97`.
- **Blocker:** Genesis WriterPending has no active children. An empty child-head reconciliation is legal, so Pause commits it. Resume checks that paused and active child lists match (both empty), restores Active(WriterPending), and retains `paused_reconciliation`. The dispatch guard then admits only resume publications, acknowledgments, or Cancel. ResumeChildren requires an active paused destination; none exists. Only its acknowledgment clears the reconciliation, and none can be created.
- **Consequence:** The source-derived legal sequence Start -> Pause(empty heads) -> Resume(same heads) permanently blocks StartWriter and normal lifecycle commands. The user can cancel the run, but cannot continue it in the same aggregate. The same empty-child issue applies to other phases before child activation. This is a state-transition defect and does not require a timeout, workload saturation, or a failed provider.
- **Repair direction:** Complete the resume barrier immediately when no children require resumption. Define the barrier by remaining durable child acknowledgments and prove that every admitted paused state has a resumable successor, including zero children and a pending publication. Preserve exact child ownership and do not silently discard active work.
- **Evidence scope:** Source-derived transition trace, not an executed regression test or live diagnosis. The fully read cancellation test activates three child domains before Pause and clears the flag through their acknowledgments; it does not cover Pause/Resume at genesis.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4b1ac926-fcea-52c4-a727-0f2974444585.title: [L372] S1 snapshot admission conflates stable section identity order with dependency order
4b1ac926-fcea-52c4-a727-0f2974444585.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L372.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-run-knowledge/src/snapshot.rs:138-190`, `src/snapshot/validation.rs:115-143`, `src/snapshot/validation.rs:146-224`, `src/identity.rs:11-75`, `tests/topology.rs:60-71`, `tests/topology.rs:97-113`, `src/model/topology.rs:109-139`.
- Behavior: snapshot sections must be strictly increasing by their opaque sixteen-byte section IDs, and each dependency must occur before its consumer in that same vector. The IDs have no declared topological meaning. Thus a consumer with ID 4 depending on section ID 5 is rejected in ID order as a forward dependency; reversing those two sections is rejected as noncanonical order. The graph can be acyclic and still have no admissible representation with those stable IDs.
- Consequence: callers must assign or replace identities to satisfy an incidental storage order, or lose a valid grounded knowledge graph. This is a structural admission blocker rather than a time limit or session deletion. The tests explicitly require forward-dependency and descending-ID rejection. The example is derived from complete source; those tests were read, not executed.
- Repair direction: keep canonical identity order for storage and equality, compute dependency traversal separately, and reject actual missing dependencies/cycles. Coordinate runtime validation and its formal model; retain identity and lineage checks. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4b25f9e9-e2d8-5b81-a7f5-893bfd8a48c3.title: [L210] Generic provider subprocess overflow kills the invocation, including stderr-only overflow
4b25f9e9-e2d8-5b81-a7f5-893bfd8a48c3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L210.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/process.rs:17-19,92-102,130-168`; `process/tokio_transport.rs:29-83,136-239,253-256`; `process_containment.rs:14-38`.
- Generic ProcessRequest admits at most **256 arguments / 2 MiB total argument bytes / 128 environment removals / 128 bytes per environment name**, plus the selected stdin cap. The Tokio transport reads all stdout/stderr into memory and errors as soon as either crosses its total byte cap. With L209 defaults, **64 KiB of diagnostic stderr alone** suffices to fail the invocation and trigger child termination even if stdout remains valid. This is effect termination, not display truncation.
- Stdout journaling writes and syncs each accepted read chunk (buffer **8 KiB**, not a total cap). The overflowing chunk is rejected before journaling, and stderr has no journal here. Cancellation, selected timeout, stdin/output/journal IO errors all terminate the child. Both production native adapters were subsequently confirmed to use this transport (L211/L213), so overflow termination applies to those routes.
- Termination targets the direct child and awaits child.wait without a cleanup bound. Linux configuration creates a process group but uses a direct-child parent-death SIGKILL and kill_on_drop; this code does not terminate/join the whole group or adopt it on restart. A surviving descendant holding a pipe can also delay EOF after child exit. These are ownership/completion risks requiring reproduction, distinct from preserving the durable provider context identity.
- **Entire request/transport/containment implementation read; no overflow or descendant-EOF case run.** Canonical executable pinning and environment/argv integrity remain necessary checks.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4c1035c1-e219-5067-98ba-c51aae52e229.title: [L556] Sandbox time limits are optional but six resource dimensions still require finite bounds
4c1035c1-e219-5067-98ba-c51aae52e229.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L556.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox/src/resource.rs:53-147`, `src/resource.rs:150-201`, `src/process_policy.rs:5-14`, `src/process_policy.rs:65-92`, `src/terminal.rs:152-176`, `src/terminal.rs:267-291`, `src/reference/session.rs:160-184`.
- Behavior: `with_optional_time` represents absent wall and CPU bounds as zero on the canonical wire and skips their finite comparison. Memory, disk, output, handles, processes and concurrency still require positive finite quantities. Process policy separately requires a finite simultaneous process maximum and a denied/bounded descendant allowance. Terminal output also requires a positive finite byte budget. The reference usage API only adds usage in all dimensions; it has no release/decrement or gauge update for simultaneous resources. Untimed counters still reject arithmetic overflow. Reference accounting enforces contract limits rather than the smaller requirements.
- Consequence: Removing timers does not remove output/storage/capacity ceilings. Treating a simultaneous handle/process/slot count as cumulative charging would eventually exhaust a continuing session, although native callers must be inspected before asserting they use that reference pattern. The optional-time implementation is an existing repair and must not be mislabeled as a mandatory execution deadline.
- Repair direction: Preserve explicit absence of time bounds, give other policy budgets an intentional unlimited representation where authorized, and separate lifetime consumption from current/peak resource measurements with correct release and durable accounting.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.
