4c720477-a78e-5123-bb44-d6ee73ec4ed6.title: [L347] B1 equal usage with new evidence can reject the final report
4c720477-a78e-5123-bb44-d6ee73ec4ed6.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L347.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-budget/src/transition/reconciliation/observation.rs:115-158,204-238`, `src/transition/reconciliation/observation/terminal/replay.rs:50-81`, `src/failure.rs:143-161`.
- Behavior: when an active reservation already has usage evidence, **equal** cumulative amounts with a different evidence digest return BindingMismatch before the reducer considers Interim versus Final. A final report with unchanged usage but a distinct final-event digest is therefore rejected, leaving the reservation active and its unused ceiling reserved. Any downward component is separately rejected as NonmonotonicObservation. After terminal settlement only the exact stored raw report, finality and evidence replay is accepted.
- Consequence: a provider/host that naturally binds evidence to each observation event must reuse the previous evidence digest or choose full-ceiling settlement to close unchanged usage. BindingMismatch is labeled Terminal even though the external work may have completed. This can strand accounting/retry admission if the caller lacks an explicit alternate reconciliation path. The crate README states same-evidence replay as an intended invariant; the problem is conflating an unchanged measurement with an exact event replay when finality advances.
- Repair direction: model event identity, measurement high-water and lifecycle finality separately; allow a correctly correlated later final observation to finalize without charging the same usage twice, while retaining both evidence bindings. Scope: direct source consequence; host evidence construction not established here, no final-report reproduction run.

- Test evidence update: `tests/model.rs:28-97` and `tests/retry.rs:69-110` deliberately reject unchanged interim usage with new evidence. `tests/ledger.rs:122-129` and `tests/lifecycle_reference.rs:139-155` use increased final usage; they do not cover unchanged-usage finality advancement. `tests/generated.rs:11-14,77-89` runs 4 x 64 x 24 **interim** samples. These are qualification bounds, not installed quotas; tests inspected, not run.



Formal-contract evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-budget/src/reachability/guards/outcomes.rs:36-53` requires absent/unchanged evidence when cumulative usage is unchanged even for a final report. `src/reachability/rejections/reservation.rs:65-90` specifies the same `BindingMismatch` without a finality exception. Repair therefore needs coordinated runtime, guard, rejection-model, and regression-fixture changes; the restriction is not an undocumented runtime-only branch. All budget crate files have now been read completely, with no alternate refill, reopen, root un-fault, or same-usage/new-evidence finality path found.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4cc4f4da-1624-5f08-95cc-e2d1645cf3f3.title: [L105] Tool terminal/progress construction can fail after an effect because of rendering and output totals
4cc4f4da-1624-5f08-95cc-e2d1645cf3f3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L105.

- `result.rs:327-351` adds **all referenced artifact sizes plus canonical structured-result bytes**, then refuses the terminal envelope if that sum exceeds the call output allowance. Human/model renderings, progress count, and artifact count are separately checked. The allowance therefore includes result metadata as well as the underlying archived command bytes; concrete adapter behavior is being followed.
- `identity.rs:6-8,20-22,141-158` hard-caps all BoundedText at **16 KiB**, implementation identity at **256 bytes**, and idempotency keys at **128 bytes**. BoundedText rejects empty text and NUL rather than truncating; descriptor model/human ceilings cannot widen this type's maximum.
- `progress.rs:48-56` rejects sequence at or above selected progress count, oversized rendering, or changed authority epoch. This is total invocation progress admission, not a rolling telemetry window; actual adapters determine whether exhaustion terminates or drops updates. The shell adapter suppresses updates once its 4096-event ceiling is reached and marks progress truncated; it does not cancel the process (`peritus-tools-shell/src/execution/active.rs:111-119`). Resource samples consume this same allowance (`execution/progress.rs:67-73`).
- Protocol diagnostics separately cap paths at **8 KiB** (truncate with a suffix) and static details at **4 KiB** (replace oversized detail), potentially hiding exact nested causes (`error.rs:117-138`). Caller-defined transport limits are enforced by envelope parsing; protocol version is currently exactly one (`envelope.rs:25-37`).
- Artifact references disallow zero-byte objects (`artifact.rs:67-74`) and require exact invocation provenance at result construction. Zero output belongs in structured output through this protocol. These are representation/provenance restrictions, distinct from artificial elapsed deadlines.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4eb071e6-bece-5f10-a7da-280c9c5a4697.title: [L216] Claude completion admission depends on exact native fields and a lexical prose classifier
4eb071e6-bece-5f10-a7da-280c9c5a4697.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L216.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-anthropic/src/runtime/output.rs:35-78,81-110,113-151,160-183`; `runtime/output/completion.rs:5-66`.
- Tool-free native public prose is admitted only with exact type=result/subtype=success/stop_reason=end_turn/terminal_reason=completed, is_error false, **num_turns exactly 1**, empty permission_denials, no queued/subagent/deferred/local-command activity and a matching optional origin. A complete response lacking one required field falls through to private-envelope decoding and can become Incomplete/Malformed rather than a public answer.
- Except for Markdown headed with **1-6 leading # characters**, any line starting with JSON/array/fence or prose containing tool_calls, content plus a brace, or a colon before a bracket is treated as a private candidate. Legitimate tool-free prose with code/examples can therefore be rejected by transport-shape policy. Preventing accidental tool execution is necessary; conflating visible prose with the private envelope is a separate acceptance heuristic needing edge tests.
- Reported error classification uses a fixed English substring list for auth/capacity/context/model failures. Native error_max_turns/error_max_budget_usd/error_max_structured_output_retries are recognized terminal error subtypes; those names describe upstream-reported limits and are not new Peritus duration defaults. The capacity decoder confirms the source of L213's Never retry mapping.
- Entire transport JSON is validated with production CanonicalJson bounds before result classification; tool proposal count is capped by the request maximum, exact catalog names required, content nonempty/no NUL. Bounded healing is restricted to private envelopes. **Both decoder files fully read; missing-field/prose-classifier cases not run and upstream version compatibility unverified.**

4ec0ed1b-b446-56dd-b087-2b91fe44f151.title: [L353] C6 compaction cannot replace required sources and requires an already selected source set
4ec0ed1b-b446-56dd-b087-2b91fe44f151.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L353.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-context/src/compaction/validation.rs:108-129,131-141,155-182,204-233`, `src/compaction/replacement.rs:119-128,206-260`, `src/compaction.rs:181-267`.
- Behavior: validation accepts only source ranges whose complete nodes already appear in the supplied plan, rejects protected content and mixed context classes, retains complete source nodes in validation evidence, and requires a strict token reduction. It marks every required root or required dependency as required, including an otherwise optional source selected for a required root. Atomic replacement then rejects all such required sources with `RequiredCompactionSource`. Validation alone can produce evidence that replacement refuses. Source ranges are audit lineage, not a partial live-node replacement.
- Consequence: this replacement path cannot recover a required closure that exceeds L350: it needs a preexisting selected source set and refuses to replace its required members. Omitted large optional nodes also cannot enter this compaction path from the same plan. This does not establish that every caller lacks another recovery path. Protection and authority rules preserve important semantics; removing them indiscriminately would lose required content rather than repair continuity.
- Repair direction: separate immutable required evidence and original source references from their bounded render representation. Permit checked derived views while retaining durable originals, authority boundaries, required obligations, and exact lineage. Provide a capacity-recovery entry point that can inspect durable sources beyond the currently selected model view. Replacement graph/dependency implementation and tests remain under review; no tests run.

- Test-source corroboration: `tests/compaction_matrix.rs:221-244,380-401` explicitly expects omitted sources to fail validation, while required sources pass validation and then fail replacement. All compaction implementation/model/test files are now completely read; no other replacement recovery entry point exists within this crate. No tests run.

4ee506f0-c9bc-5cb8-b924-e023690b0ef4.title: [L429] E3 campaigns require six positive finite resource ceilings and a finite retry policy
4ee506f0-c9bc-5cb8-b924-e023690b0ef4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L429.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/limits.rs:5-81`, `src/profile/policy.rs:23-69,127-171`, `src/profile/binding.rs:250-330`, `src/dataset/manifest.rs:30-65`, `src/accounting/ledger.rs:60-100` in the same crate.
- Behavior: EvaluationLimits requires positive values no higher than compiled tasks 2,048, rollouts 16,384, attempts per rollout 16, bootstrap replicates 100,000, pass@k values 32, and complete state bytes 16 MiB. Production defaults reduce attempts to 8, bootstrap to 10,000, and pass@k count to 16. Retry policy requires a positive finite attempt maximum within the limit; ledger overage reports Terminal. A profile's selected tasks × two arms × rollouts per task must fit its frozen rollout ceiling. Dataset tasks must fit their construction limit. Metric policy requires at least one positive canonical k and bootstrap replicate, and only confidence 950,000 millionths is supported.
- Consequence: Callers cannot request an unlimited campaign/retry history or larger workload through these APIs, and receive ReduceScope or terminal accounting errors instead of lossless batching. The confidence constant is a supported statistical-method contract, not a running deadline. These are evaluation-specific source limits; ordinary installed agent runs are not shown to execute through E3 by this inspection.
- Repair direction: Make workload/retry stopping explicit user policy and page durable task/rollout/attempt storage. Keep statistical methods versioned and their supported confidence parameters explicit rather than confusing them with task longevity. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

4f3805fc-7027-5e6e-9559-ff0fa53d706f.title: [L746] Export retries treat an existing path as an immutable result without verifying its bytes
4f3805fc-7027-5e6e-9559-ff0fa53d706f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L746.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/deliverable.rs:36-52,185-204,238-283`; `src/product_run/persistence/deliverable.rs:7-48` in the same crate.
- Behavior: saved export/repeated-action eligibility tests only nonempty export_path and is_file. Export writes a whole patch to a fixed per-run .patch.new path, syncs it and renames to the fixed .patch destination; Unix syncs the directory, while this path has no equivalent Windows directory sync. Persisted deliverables store the path but no export digest.
- Consequence: an externally changed file can satisfy the existing-result check, and path existence alone does not identify the original immutable export. Late publication/projection failure remains recoverable only through the saved path/current run state, rather than a verified export receipt. Fixed output publication can replace earlier bytes before the run record is updated.

4f8f71a1-0491-5b9f-a0a5-53c0a0e21e21.title: [L243] A subscription gap has no TUI snapshot-recovery transition
4f8f71a1-0491-5b9f-a0a5-53c0a0e21e21.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L243.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/protocol.rs:12-51,188-198`; `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/interaction.rs`; daemon subscription handling recorded in L239.
- On SubscriptionGap the TUI emits a notice and returns no recovery effect. The server has entered SnapshotRequired, so ordinary event pumping cannot continue. The TUI subscription Resume command does not perform the required snapshot transition. Reconnect constructs another subscription from the retained last_cursor; the gap response does not replace that cursor with a recovered snapshot position. This can strand the display and reproduce the same gap on reconnect.
- This is a missing state/recovery transition, not justification for a new elapsed timeout. The repair must bind snapshot recovery to the same durable session and then resume from the snapshot cursor. The inspected journal query uses actual MIN/MAX positions; its 4096 bound is a query-page limit, not evidence of automatic deletion after 4096 events (L247).
- Separately, the TUI retains at most **4096 display events**, removes their dedup identities on eviction, and shows previews of **240 input bytes** (escaped display text can be longer). Notices retain a **4096-byte prefix** and expire after **24 UI ticks** (about six seconds at the runtime's 250 ms cadence). Those presentation limits do not terminate the product run, but a disappearing notice can hide the reason the display remains stalled. **Complete client protocol and interaction files read; runtime reproduction not performed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

513d8140-354a-55ff-a982-ff20ba89bf15.title: [L337] D1 exact retry requires current successor state and restart requires an external exact plan
513d8140-354a-55ff-a982-ff20ba89bf15.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L337.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-gates/src/durability.rs:79-95,159-181,240-287`; `src/durability/lifecycle.rs:65-126`; `src/engine.rs:216-224,231-257`; `src/event.rs:14-19`; `src/state.rs:227-240`.
- **Blocker:** Durable genesis contains the snapshot binding; state contains the plan digest and cap, but GateEngine::resume still requires the original GatePlan supplied externally. Lower commit resolution requires the latest checkpoint to equal the old command's exact successor; later legitimate progress returns ReplayAggregate. Plan-free lifecycle retry recognizes only the latest event. GateEngine::commit first reduces against its current local state, so repeating an already acknowledged old command hits stale fences before lower receipt resolution.
- **Consequence:** Recovery depends on reconstructing the exact historical plan, and delayed duplicate delivery cannot simply return its historical success receipt after progress. D1 deliberately returns replay rather than declaring the advanced aggregate corrupt; callers still need that recovery path. Other host records may supply the plan, so this is not proof that all installed restarts lose it.
- **Repair direction:** Store/version the authoritative plan or an exact reconstructable plan artifact and resolve historical command outcomes independently of current-head admission. Refresh current authority after resolution without creating a second effect permit.
- **Evidence scope:** Full durability/lifecycle/engine reads. No ambiguous commit failure, delayed delivery or missing-plan fixture was run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

515eb153-80a6-5c47-938c-7fc7c8e79baf.title: [L146] Discard holds Git locks across restoration and can wait indefinitely without a control channel
515eb153-80a6-5c47-938c-7fc7c8e79baf.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L146.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/candidate/managed/head/prepared.rs:69-132,142-198`; `head.rs:37-118`; `restore.rs:24-57,109-159,183-219`; `recovery.rs:52-105`.
- **Blockers/enforcement:** HEAD preparation starts a synchronous `git update-ref --stdin` transaction and waits for exact `start: ok`, `prepare: ok`, and `commit: ok` lines. Its locks remain held through source/index restoration. Neither these reads nor child waits have cancellation or reattachment here; Drop closes stdin and then synchronously waits too. Failure diagnostics read at most 8,192 stderr bytes without a truncation marker. Symbolic HEAD restoration requires an ordinary HEAD file, exclusive HEAD.lock, unchanged observed HEAD, and a fresh absent restored-branch name.
- **Recovery constraints:** Preflight verifies all required source/index blobs and nested repositories before restoration. New repository recovery uses filesystem rename into the owner's `.git/peritus/discarded` directory; a cross-filesystem rename or denied permission fails instead of falling back to a copy. Windows symlink restoration accepts only UTF-8 file-link targets and requires OS support/permission. These environment constraints can block discard, with retained paths included in relevant errors.
- **Persistence distinction:** Recovery directories and displaced commit refs are deliberately retained; branches are not rewritten. There is no elapsed expiry or automatic cleanup of archived repositories here. Retained-repository consumers are fully read: `retention/store.rs:18-68,139-187` requires the correct SHA-1/SHA-256 store and an exact source-tree/index manifest match; `retention/restore.rs:91-115,165-251` explicitly refuses cross-filesystem reconstruction on Unix and preserves recreated destinations. Transactional restart consumers are being read next.
- **Classification:** Synchronous process-control gaps and authority/environment fences. No proposed repair should reintroduce an arbitrary kill timer to mask them. Source confirmed, not a demonstrated live lockup.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

517a05c4-822b-53ce-a411-f9e59a5b0657.title: [L267] Full journal integrity forbids prefix retention and revalidates every historical state value
517a05c4-822b-53ce-a411-f9e59a5b0657.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L267.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/integrity.rs:127-163`; `integrity/scan.rs:17-72`; `integrity/validation.rs`; `integrity/artifacts.rs`; `hash_chain.rs:85-103`.
- The complete integrity scan requires COUNT(events) == MAX(global_position), then exact global positions **1..last**. Removing any old prefix as retention is corrupt under this contract. The 4096 global-window query size is therefore not an automatic retention policy. Complete history is durable here, but no authenticated retired-prefix/checkpoint contract exists in this scan.
- Scan loads every immutable event and aggregate head into memory, then independently resolves every command, loading its event range again. It restores and hashes **every historical state revision**, not only latest values, before comparing the complete latest-history catalog with the current catalog. Cost grows with total retained session/command history and sum of complete historical value sizes. integrity_scan returns only a summary but still constructs the same full IntegrityExport internally.
- Artifact validation checks all artifact_references for missing/unfinalized/quarantined content **before filtering journal-owned rows**. A bad reference owned by another subsystem can therefore fail the whole journal scan. Any bad old history row also aborts it; daemon startup's before-IPC dependency was already recorded in L198.
- journal_head_hash converts aggregate count to **u32 with expect**, so an unrepresentable count would panic rather than produce a typed error. This is a theoretical representation boundary, not an ordinary short work quota; no such large store was constructed.
- Repair must make verification incremental and preserve exact durable identity/history while scoping damaged-owner recovery. Simply deleting old rows violates today's integrity contract; simply removing memory/time bounds does not remove repeated full-history work. **All integrity implementation and hash files fully read; no storage/performance/recovery test run.** `sqlite/history/tests.rs:288-320` verifies physical allocation below half logical history for 1024 growing values, then runs a full integrity scan; it checks deduplication savings, not reopening/verification latency as history grows. Recovery tests explicitly reject deletion of an old state revision.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

519c1861-653f-581b-b413-68a2902486a0.title: [L492] Anthropic and Google reuse one provider frame identity for multiple normalized events, causing C5 to discard required semantics as duplicates
519c1861-653f-581b-b413-68a2902486a0.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L492.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-anthropic/src/stream/state.rs:108-124`, `src/stream/state.rs:191-216`, `src/stream/message.rs:33-42`; `crates/model/peritus-provider-google/src/stream/state.rs:81-120`, `src/stream/interactions.rs:142-163`, `src/stream/interactions.rs:322-335`, `fixtures/v1/interactions_success.sse:19-21`, `fixtures/v1/interactions_tool_thinking.sse:21-39`; `crates/model/peritus-model-protocol/src/reducer/stream.rs:51-83`, `src/reducer/stream.rs:152-172`, `src/reducer/events.rs:146-183`, `src/reducer/terminal.rs:73-90`.
- Behavior: all semantic events expanded from a provider frame inherit the same SSE id and raw digest. C5 records the first and treats subsequent matching ids/digests with the next local sequence as duplicates, advancing sequence but skipping application. Google tool step start therefore keeps ItemStarted and discards ToolCallStarted; later arguments have no registered call. An identified Google completion frame starts with Usage, so its cache/Finish/ResponseCompleted events are skipped. Anthropic start metadata/usage expanded under one id is similarly discarded. Compatible explicitly binds identity only to its first expanded event, demonstrating a different contract.
- Consequence: provider-frame identity and normalized-event identity are conflated. An otherwise valid stream can fail tool assembly or finish EOF as incomplete; metadata/accounting can disappear. The Google corpus already includes these identified frames, but the adapter qualification collects raw normalized events rather than applying C5 reduction. This is a cross-module source diagnosis, not a test run or proof of the current native executable lockup.
- Repair direction: deduplicate provider frames once before expansion; give normalized children stable distinct identities or bind provider identity only to the first child under an explicit shared contract. Qualify the complete adapter-to-reducer-to-next-request path. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

51f4b58c-4650-5645-a89f-8f343b21a756.title: [L242] TUI send-queue exhaustion forces disconnect and drops the remaining transport outbox
51f4b58c-4650-5645-a89f-8f343b21a756.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L242.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/runtime/connection/outbox.rs:7-28,36-50`; `runtime/connection.rs:36-38,96-99,125-156`; `runtime.rs:266-269`; `client.rs:95-102,110-120,184-217`.
- The runtime outbox retains **128 pending frames plus one active send**; the independently owned client writer channel holds **256 commands**. Input and client-observation channels hold **128 / 512** entries. These are fixed capacities, with no reservation for heartbeat replies or cleanup in the inspected FIFO structures.
- A push beyond the pending ceiling returns Task; runtime immediately routes that error through sent, which resets the outbox, drops the ClientSession and marks the model disconnected. All remaining transport frames are discarded together. Draft/receipt recovery must distinguish definitely unsent frames from those already queued/written; that model recovery is still being traced. Capacity exhaustion is escalated from one rejected submission to loss of the whole connection.
- Reader observations await the shared event channel, and writer error reporting uses that same channel. A stalled main reducer can therefore delay receiving/replying to heartbeat events under the server cutoff. Actual responsiveness fixtures cover a small filled writer setup, not the 128-frame overflow or prolonged event-channel saturation. **Entire outbox, runtime wiring, IO tasks and fixtures fully read; tests not executed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

51ffd7fa-1be8-5f52-a09f-3ba120d6c202.title: [L704] Context inspection has fixed source-size and sealed-message ordinal gates
51ffd7fa-1be8-5f52-a09f-3ba120d6c202.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L704.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/workbench/context.rs:11-12,41-50,174-196,202-217,246-264,300-342`; `src/wire/workbench_context.rs:87-137`; `src/workbench/context/tests.rs:28-89` in the same crate.

Empty files are allowed but other zero-byte sources are rejected. Wire checks page count before allocating.

A sealed request manifest is not proof that a provider context window was restored. Pagination/revision checks protect honest coverage and should be retained.
- Repair direction: Let metadata describe larger durable sources without requiring them to fit model input; use wide indexed positions and bind native restoration separately. No tests run.

520a8050-37ad-5645-a621-6d102f151715.title: [L525] Git command byte ceilings fail whole operations and do not bound their duration
520a8050-37ad-5645-a621-6d102f151715.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L525.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/command.rs:12-13`, `src/command.rs:108-137`, `src/command.rs:213-249`, `src/repository.rs:118-125`, `src/error.rs:6-7`.
- Behavior: Every subprocess has a mandatory positive stdout ceiling, default 16 MiB and hard maximum 64 MiB. Stderr is capped at the smaller of that ceiling and 16 KiB, then a failed-command diagnostic retains at most 4,096 bytes. Reader threads keep draining to EOF after detecting overflow. The owner waits for process exit, then joins the stdin writer and both readers, before returning an error for excess output. The overflow error has Quarantine recovery guidance even when the command exited successfully.
- Consequence: A large status/diff/worktree/config response or noisy stderr can reject a completed operation. Output retention is bounded, but execution and pipe completion are not: no cancellation channel, process ownership handoff or continuation exists here. Reader/writer failure is observed after the blocking process wait and can strand that wait if a pipe stops being drained. There is no production elapsed timer in this adapter.
- Repair direction: Treat observation size as paged or streamed data and retain exact completion identity for mutating operations. Provide cancellation and pipe/process supervision through owned execution, without replacing this gap with an arbitrary wall deadline. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

52bf82e0-a4c3-5529-8664-dc634b509757.title: [L543] Inherited listener handoff assumes a complete record from a stream read
52bf82e0-a4c3-5529-8664-dc634b509757.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L543.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/inherited.rs:159-197`, `src/proxy/inherited.rs:200-283`.
- Behavior: A Unix stream channel sends a fixed record plus one SCM_RIGHTS descriptor. Receive requires one recvmsg to return exactly the complete record bytes and exactly one descriptor; a short stream delivery is rejected and received descriptors are closed. It does not retain a partial record for continuation. The receiver polls nonblocking every five milliseconds and observes explicit cancellation; proxy lifetime timing begins only after the listener is received and owner::run starts.
- Consequence: Stream segmentation is represented as an invalid handoff rather than resumable framing. A slow handoff has no implicit timer in this layer, which is consistent with explicit cancellation, but the returned endpoint remains absent until successful framing. Five-millisecond polling is cadence, not a session deadline.
- Repair direction: Define descriptor-bound stream framing with retained partial bytes or use a matching message-oriented channel contract. Preserve exact descriptor count, loopback and close-on-exec validation. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

54e1fcf7-d4cf-5f38-aeb2-80218e532192.title: [L298] Dependency refresh finishes synchronously by repeatedly rescanning all retained work
54e1fcf7-d4cf-5f38-aeb2-80218e532192.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L298.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/state/mutation.rs:263-398`; `state/mutation/dependency_action.rs:159-246`; `dependency_round.rs:242-383`; `dependency_round/apply.rs:195-280`; `dependency_measure.rs:16-95,225-261`; `state/lookup.rs:116-199`; `reducer.rs:70-82`. Owner serialization is traced in L274.
- **Mechanism:** every ordinary command invokes dependency refresh. A round scans the entire retained work vector, looks up each dependency of WaitingDependencies/Queued records by binary search, collects all changes from the pre-round snapshot, then applies them synchronously. It repeats until a fixed point. The two-halves remaining counter derives from a decreasing natural measure of existing records; this is a termination witness, not an arbitrary timer or turn allowance, and valid-state proofs establish completion rather than silently leaving dependency work unfinished.
- **Daily-driving effect:** terminal records remain in the scanned vector. A failure cascading through a dependency chain advances only one edge per snapshot round and can require a number of full-history scans proportional to chain depth. Source loops therefore permit quadratic retained-record visitation for a long chain, with additional dependency lookup and mutation costs. There is no yield, incremental dependency index, or persisted progress boundary inside refresh. A serialized authority owner can delay unrelated control work while computing an accepted transition. No latency benchmark or live-lockup attribution is claimed.
- **Ontological repair requirement:** preserve complete dependency truth with indexed affected-node propagation and a responsive ownership boundary. Do not remove the structural termination reasoning as if it were a synthetic daily quota; remove whole-history work from routine control admission, and qualify long-history cancellation/status responsiveness independently of proof-only termination.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

558470aa-1767-55ce-97e5-7963db85fb3e.title: [L190] Preview terminal input requires Network permission even for local interaction
558470aa-1767-55ce-97e5-7963db85fb3e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L190.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/workbench/launch/terminal.rs:24-34`; `launch/process.rs:24-46`.
- A conversation-owned preview terminal requires **Read, Write, Process and Network** capabilities before input, without inspecting whether the specific launch/input needs network. This can block ordinary local interactive input when Network is revoked. Terminal attachment separately requires Read and an exact live preview handle.
- Launch environment values must exist as valid Unicode in the daemon environment; missing/non-Unicode requested variables become MissingRequiredFeature. The launch forwards the profile's optional wall limit unchanged; `None` remains untimed.
- Permission fences remain authoritative. Local operation without Network should be admitted only when the actual process gateway can enforce denied networking, as the developer-command tests demonstrate for their path; unrestricted terminal input must not silently widen authority. **Complete source read; preview command permission selection and network-denial behavior not exercised.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5641a4ac-9344-529e-8395-9451528c9073.title: [L695] Default protocol recovery advice does not establish safe restoration of the original operation
5641a4ac-9344-529e-8395-9451528c9073.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L695.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/error/code.rs:176-214,260-270`; `src/error/mod.rs:133-241` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Default retry classes recommend reconnecting for session mismatches, submitting new requests for idempotency conflicts, and recovery for idempotency capacity. Human explanations suggest waiting or restarting for capacity, restarting artifact transfers, and reattaching or starting a new terminal. No default code selects SameRequest or Never. These are classifications and prose, not implementations of receipt lookup or owner restoration. In L685, changing request/correlation IDs changes the command digest even with the same idempotency key; in L686, pure capacity has no automatic retirement or spill.
- Consequence: Generic restart/new-request advice can leave the original effect or native process unresolved, and restart does not necessarily retire durable capacity. The error taxonomy cannot certify that repeating an operation is safe or that reconnecting restores its provider context. This is a source finding, not a measured restart failure.

569363fb-fc6d-5177-a660-1002c24dc3bc.title: [L515] Failed telemetry export batches are rebuilt rather than pinned for retry
569363fb-fc6d-5177-a660-1002c24dc3bc.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L515.

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/export/pump.rs:83-109`, `src/buffer/state.rs:105-186`, `src/export/types.rs`, `tests/buffering_export.rs:42-63`.
- Behavior: A pump reads a fresh prefix of the current queue for every flush. It does not retain the exact previously failed batch. Enqueue after a failure can extend a partially full batch; DropOldest can evict records in the failed batch. Batch identity includes record sequence/content, so these changes produce a different batch identity. Exact acknowledgements are checked before retirement, which is a necessary integrity guard.
- Consequence: The stated exact-batch retry behavior is not preserved across intervening enqueue. If remote acceptance happened before acknowledgement loss, rebuilding a different batch cannot by itself establish idempotent batch retry. Event-level downstream deduplication may compensate, but is not proved here. The test retries a full two-record batch without interleaved enqueue.
- Repair direction: Persist a pending export batch and its acknowledgement identity until resolved, and define how overflow interacts with records already in flight. Test acknowledgement loss plus interleaved enqueue and overflow. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

57b752b7-a5fb-507c-aa94-52d63381be9e.title: [L244] Prompt and terminal capacities differ across UI, wire and ownership layers
57b752b7-a5fb-507c-aa94-52d63381be9e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L244.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/interaction/prompts.rs`; `model/interaction/terminal.rs`; `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/wire/prompt.rs`; `src/schema/fields/flows/prompt_terminal/prompt.rs`.
- Ordinary prompt answers are checked against the codec's **1 MiB string** ceiling. Signed Base64 answers are decoded before the check and compared with the larger whole-frame bound even though the wire's opaque signed-decision field is limited to **8 MiB**. A narrower broker answer constraint can still reject a UI-admitted answer. Prompt wire/schema also allow **64 choices**, **65535 constraints**, and **1 MiB choice/text fields**. The editor's own input capacity remains to be traced before claiming the maximum practical answer size.
- One unresolved PendingTerminalAttach suppresses another attach until a response or disconnect. Terminal input is bounded to **64 KiB per chunk** and resize to **4096 columns / 256 rows**. These are transfer/display bounds, not a command lifetime. Cancellation is gated by a current live input-capture binding; a client that lost the attachment cannot use this UI path to cancel the old process until it can recover a valid attachment.
- The ownership check must remain exact; recovery should reacquire or expose authorized control of the same terminal, rather than inventing a new process or treating loss of display attachment as process completion. **All named files fully read; terminal registry callers and editor capacity remain pending.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

588f9d45-0f2f-5903-bb22-5580ec42f5ee.title: [L379] B1 expired-claim recovery guidance does not name the required fencing transition
588f9d45-0f2f-5903-bb22-5580ec42f5ee.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L379.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-leases/tests/failure_contract.rs:40`, `crates/state/peritus-leases/src/failure.rs:166-191`, `src/transition/authority.rs:54-66`, `src/transition/lifecycle.rs:178-183`, `src/transition/fencing/expiry.rs:55-74`, `src/transition/authority.rs:78-81`.
- Behavior: `ClaimExpired` is classified only as `Reauthorize`. Renew/use both reject the expired active lease before policy intersection; consuming a fresh policy capability cannot change that expired lease. Expiry requires an explicit fence followed by correlated reconciliation, or release with exact quiescence can make the next generation available. An accepted lease use is also limited by the earlier of lease expiry and policy validity, not lease duration alone.
- Consequence: a generic recovery dispatcher following the advertised class can repeatedly reauthorize and hit the same lease expiry without advancing lease recovery. This is a misleading recovery contract, not proof that a particular installed dispatcher loops. Rejections preserve the unchanged aggregate and attempted use command, so the data needed for proper recovery is not discarded here.
- Repair direction: return typed lease-recovery work that distinguishes policy refresh from expired-holder fencing/reconciliation, and retain the pending command/session context while resolving it. Removing a run deadline must not leave an unreported policy/lease expiry behind. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

596742c8-57df-5108-ba47-c82f34839450.title: [L537] Connection duration accounting uses different origins for different phases
596742c8-57df-5108-ba47-c82f34839450.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L537.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/worker.rs:41-67`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:91-118`, `src/proxy/connect.rs:104-172`, `src/accounting.rs:92-98`.
- Behavior: HTTP elapsed accounting starts after the entire client request header is read. DNS and connect occur before the next elapsed check, and upstream response-head reads do not consult that clock. CONNECT starts a new Instant separately inside each upload/download relay, excluding its earlier header/resolve/connect phases. Per-read/write socket timeouts reuse the complete connection duration. Elapsed accounting rejects strictly greater-than duration while owner lifetime stops at greater-than-or-equal.
- Consequence: The mandatory connection duration is neither a consistent whole-connection limit nor reliable cancellation. It can terminate a progressing transfer yet exclude expensive startup/header phases. A timer field is not evidence of a complete recovery contract.
- Repair direction: Remove implicit execution lifetimes and define observable phase progress and ownership cancellation consistently. If a user explicitly selects a deadline, represent its origin and scope once rather than restarting it per phase. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5999ad18-6462-5ec9-99ed-1a2546095f55.title: [L471] Compatible profiles exclude all provider-side continuation and several unused capabilities
5999ad18-6462-5ec9-99ed-1a2546095f55.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L471.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-compatible/src/profile.rs:224-257,260-271`, `src/request/validation.rs:15-45`, `src/request.rs:29-37`, `src/request/responses.rs:21-24` in the same crate.
- Behavior: every compatible profile must use stateless replay, Unsupported resume, best-effort local cancellation, provider-enforced output and declared streaming. Any Unknown capability anywhere in the profile is rejected, as is any supported capability without a mapped implementation even if the current request does not use it. Requests reject every continuation, storage/background setting, cache setting, reasoning control, audio/document and unresolved media. Only Draft202012 schemas are accepted; a parallel-call count narrower than the negotiated count is rejected because the wire maps a boolean only. Responses additionally rejects seed/stops.
- Consequence: this adapter cannot reconnect an interrupted provider response at an exact cursor. Persistent local conversation replay is still possible; stateless provider invocation alone does not mean that the local session is ephemeral. Availability depends on the exact adapter contract, and removing these checks alone cannot invent provider resume guarantees. Whole-profile unknown rejection can prevent a supported basic request until its profile is normalized.
- Repair direction: preserve exact local history and unresolved invocation identity independently of provider state; represent supported capabilities and their required operations per invocation. Add reviewed provider-side resume implementations where available, and retain explicit unsupported recovery rather than silently replacing the context. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5a9482eb-f8e3-50b5-98b3-668fe1b15698.title: [L548] Failed file staging and destructor cleanup can lose ownership of secret artifacts
5a9482eb-f8e3-50b5-98b3-668fe1b15698.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L548.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/delivery.rs:178-205`, `src/delivery.rs:229-285`.
- Behavior: Staging creates a lease-named file exclusively, writes and syncs it, then adds it to the session only on success. If write or sync fails, an attempted removal error is ignored, leaving a possible partial file outside the artifact list. A later exact retry encounters the existing name. Explicit release retains failed removals for retry, but Drop discards release errors and destroys the owner object.
- Consequence: A partial artifact can survive without a retryable ownership record; process teardown can discard the only cleanup state. A finite lease does not solve this recovery gap. No injected filesystem failure or crash was executed during this audit.
- Repair direction: Journal ownership before creating artifacts, preserve cleanup failures durably, and reconcile exact existing artifacts on recovery and retry. Retain explicit idempotent release and restrictive file permissions.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5ad8e00c-fcf6-5f42-9f3e-c51c47d95dae.title: [L426] E2 supported observations are rejected by five English substring heuristics
5ad8e00c-fcf6-5f42-9f3e-c51c47d95dae.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L426.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-debugger/src/report/claim.rs:56-79`, `src/causal/candidate.rs:17-37` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Observation construction lowercases text and rejects it if it contains ` might `, ` likely `, ` probably `, ` recommend`, or ` should ` anywhere. It does not inspect quoted source text or the actual proposition. Statements also have a hard 4,096 UTF-8-byte ceiling, nonempty requirement, and control-character restrictions.
- Consequence: An exact supported observation quoting a source such as a message containing “should” can be refused as supposedly inferential despite its citation. Conversely, a wording without those five substrings can pass regardless of its semantics. The byte/control bounds are serialization/display constraints; the substring rule is an additional synthetic admission blocker for diagnostic prose, not an execution timeout.
- Repair direction: Encode the observation/inference distinction through typed evidence obligations and provenance rather than English word matching. Store complete supported statements with bounded display pages. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5aeb1f8e-8fcf-5046-97b5-a807b60a745e.title: [L368] E1 component inventory imposes an undocumented directory-to-file ratio ceiling
5aeb1f8e-8fcf-5046-97b5-a807b60a745e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L368.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/manifest/inventory.rs:24-50`, `src/manifest/loader.rs:200-225`; portable source-path depth rules in L356.
- Behavior: inventory counts every descendant directory and file and rejects once their total exceeds eight times the configured component count. This is separate from the declared-file/component ceiling. It uses `UnsafeEntry` even for ordinary no-follow directories. Tightening components to one makes a single valid component nested more than eight entries below the root fail inventory although its source path passes the domain's much larger depth bound. Empty directories count too. Listing is complete per directory before that global check; there is no continuation cursor.
- Consequence: harmless directory organization can block loading an otherwise valid manifest. This is a synthetic structural quota, not evidence of an unsafe entry or elapsed timeout. The default 1,024-component policy permits 8,192 descendant entries; it has no unbounded alternative under the current policy API.
- Repair direction: traverse a durable/paged inventory with explicit resource accounting and separate safety violations from capacity. Directory batching should not permanently invalidate a legitimate component set. Preserve no-follow, exact declared inventory, and path confinement. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5bfc7c9f-84e5-52a5-bdc9-991404f93bb8.title: [L436] E3 committed-command replay fails after the aggregate advances and binds effect retries to a claim fence
5bfc7c9f-84e5-52a5-bdc9-991404f93bb8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L436.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/aggregate/reducer.rs:96-123`, `src/durability/commit.rs:96-119,363-420` in the same crate.
- Behavior: The pure reducer requires the latest predecessor before deciding a command. C0 commit resolution runs before current-head validation, but resolve_existing still requires the current checkpoint to equal the old command's exact successor. After a later command advances the state, the old committed receipt produces Recovery/Quarantine. Claimed and settlement request digests also include the outbox fence; reclaiming the same message changes the digest for the same command identity.
- Consequence: An exact successful command can cease to be retryable after unrelated progress, and an effect retry under a new owner fence can conflict unless the caller retains and reconciles the original receipt and identities. This can obstruct reconnection without any actual context expiration. Immediate duplicate retries may work; this finding concerns later-state replay and reclaimed claims.
- Repair direction: Resolve durable command/effect receipts independently of the current successor checkpoint, then load the latest state. Distinguish logical effect identity from delivery ownership while preserving stale-owner rejection. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5c287225-829f-553a-aa03-07e87dce6871.title: [L312] Unrelated E0 resources reuse artifact and directive caps, and full history has a byte ceiling
5c287225-829f-553a-aa03-07e87dce6871.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L312.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/candidate.rs:99-122,203-227`; `src/handoff.rs:205-235,320-359`; `src/ownership.rs:105-135`; `src/canonical/wire/observation/agent.rs:39-76`; `src/wire/state.rs:238-311,323-388`; `src/durability.rs:74-87`.
- **Limiter:** `artifact_references` (at most 1,024) caps producer principals and paired ancestry digests as well as each handoff's artifact inputs, evidence inputs, and blocking findings. Reviewer pool size uses `child_directives` (at most 4,096). The agent observation decoder separately uses the compiled artifact ceiling for fixer responses. Complete state retains duplicated current candidate/cycle, historical candidates/cycles, embedded candidates in every handoff, observations and used commands under a mandatory actual encoded payload bound of at most 16 MiB minus header; event payloads have the same ceiling. Used commands have an additional 65,535-item limit. Six child-kind entries correspond to the closed domain enum, not a configurable work limit.
- **Consequence:** Reducing one supposedly independent resource policy can reject a different valid input (for example producer provenance or a reviewer pool). Accumulated truthful history can prevent every next event/control checkpoint from fitting even when active work and the named count budgets have room. Byte enforcement occurs before the journal append, so this path does not establish the accepted-unreadable checkpoint defect documented in L297/L301.
- **Repair direction:** Separate resource admission from complete lifetime evidence. Give each real active resource its own policy and represent provenance/history through digest-bound paged records rather than rejecting full aggregates at an arbitrary total byte count. Keep canonical ordering and complete finding/provenance coverage.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete constructor, codec and persistence inspection; no large-history fixture was executed.

5c7b8afe-20df-5442-8973-5d44f7bc56b3.title: [L504] MCP strict protocol and post-result serialization bounds can terminate a usable connection
5c7b8afe-20df-5442-8973-5d44f7bc56b3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L504.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-mcp/src/protocol.rs:7-8,19-29,60-225`; `src/jsonrpc.rs:26-79`; `src/server.rs:97-108,317-354,378-436,467-509`; `src/framing.rs:7-42,45-67`; `src/bridge.rs:93-167` in the same crate.
- Behavior: only protocol version 2025-06-18 is admitted; DTOs reject unknown fields. Client/server identities are nonempty and at most 128 bytes, instructions at most 16 KiB, tool/prompt names at most 128 bytes without controls, and resource URI at most 4096 bytes. Requests and responses must fit the same configured message limit. A whole bridge result is converted/serialized before response-size rejection, which fails the writer rather than returning a per-request bounded result. Public resource/prompt projection DTOs described as bounded do not enforce per-field bounds. List pagination first obtains the entire bridge collection, then slices it using an unversioned numeric offset into the current collection.
- Consequence: richer protocol metadata can be rejected; a successful large resource/tool result can close response delivery after the operation has already completed. Count pagination does not bound page bytes or avoid full collection allocation, and concurrent collection changes can skip/repeat entries. These format/version/resource boundaries are distinct from local deadlines.
- Repair direction: negotiate supported protocol versions, preserve forward-compatible metadata where safe, enforce projection limits before effect/whole allocation, page at the authority source with a stable snapshot cursor, and return bounded per-request failures without taking down the writer. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5cb72961-67d4-57c8-9f83-8fe672ac81e7.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L565.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-linux/src/cgroup.rs:11-12,129-143,176-242`; `src/preparation.rs:284-328` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Cleanup issues `cgroup.kill` when available, polls population, and returns a retry error after three seconds. Drop ignores that error. Failed installation ignores removal errors before a handle is returned. Existence checks can interpret inaccessible metadata as absence, and population parsing treats a missing or malformed populated field as unpopulated. Higher-level process error mapping collapses detailed cleanup causes into supervisor failures.
- Consequence: A synthetic cutoff can leave a populated leaf after the in-memory owner disappears. Partial preparation can leave a leaf that the next installation rejects as already existing. Ambiguous observations can also be mistaken for completed cleanup.
- Repair direction: Persist the exact cleanup obligation before side effects and retain it until verified reconciliation succeeds. Treat inaccessible or malformed kernel state as indeterminate. Use progress notifications and explicit cancellation instead of abandoning ownership after a timer.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5ce7ed24-b9e4-5544-9bcc-a9ca070eca01.title: [L535] Proxy acceptance quota counts rejected connections and never refills
5ce7ed24-b9e4-5544-9bcc-a9ca070eca01.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L535.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/owner.rs:103-136`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:38-74`, `src/proxy/mod.rs:143-147`.
- Behavior: The owner increments accepted before checking worker capacity or its lifetime connection allowance. Every busy response, malformed/unauthenticated request and failed worker launch therefore consumes connection allowance. Completed workers release concurrency slots but never replenish accepted. After the allowance is exceeded, all new sockets receive 503 while the listener keeps running until cancellation or owner expiry. Observations retain the earliest fixed number and drop every later record; no drain or rotation API releases capacity, and snapshots clone the complete retained vector.
- Consequence: Retry on a temporary busy response can permanently exhaust the proxy's lifetime admission quota. Waiting for workers does not restore admission. Later failure/closure/release diagnostics may be lost once the observation log fills. These count barriers are independent of the elapsed limits.
- Repair direction: Separate socket acceptance, rejected admission, active concurrency and authorized lifetime usage. Provide durable progress/backpressure and rotating observational storage instead of an unrecoverable counter ceiling. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5d7acbbd-0ad6-56b8-b137-5a20149d857b.title: [L265] One unsupported destination or exhausted message can force the whole daemon read-only
5d7acbbd-0ad6-56b8-b137-5a20149d857b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L265.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/outbox/claims.rs`; `outbox/router.rs:52-88`; `outbox/handlers.rs`; `outbox/claims/orchestrator.rs`; `outbox/pump.rs:88-104`.
- Claimed destinations are a closed inventory of **14**. The router also has a caller-configured maximum and requires unique handlers. Production children cover four destinations; the complete durable port adds ten. An out-of-inventory destination or known destination without a configured handler is Unsupported/Operator; a malformed known claim is CorruptState/ReadOnly.
- On a delivery error, reaching max_attempts or receiving CorrectRequest/ReadOnly/Operator calls enter_read_only for the **entire daemon**, then ends the pump. There is no per-message dead-letter/recovery state in this dispatcher. A single route/config/version mismatch or exhausted row can therefore block unrelated daily work.
- The E0 decoder binds directive.maximum_deliveries exactly to the durable row's max_attempts. Their numerical equality is necessary integrity; the producer-selected finite attempt count and scoped recovery policy still need tracing. Native handlers await durable owning-API settlement and return false; false means already settled, not permission to skip settlement. **All router/handler/claim implementations fully read; producer attempt policy remains pending; normal startup port selection is now confirmed in L269.**

5dc4e8d9-8e7d-5879-b8a6-ebe565b9c55b.title: [L444] F0 phase progression prevents admitting later diagnosis, variants or replacement evaluations
5dc4e8d9-8e7d-5879-b8a6-ebe565b9c55b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L444.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/campaign/reducer/transition.rs:70-183,185-205`, `src/campaign/reducer/transition/collection.rs:35-60`, `src/campaign/command.rs:14-76`, `src/campaign/state.rs:13-45` in the same crate.
- Behavior: SubmitDiagnosis is only legal in BaselineRunning/Diagnosing; the first manifest moves to Proposing. AdmitVariant is only legal in Proposing; the first evaluation moves to VariantsRunning. The first attribution moves to Attributing, where more evaluations are illegal. An evaluation is keyed solely by variant identity and an existing key is rejected even when a later report supersedes the earlier observation. There is no paused state, phase rollback, evidence replacement or scope-amendment command. Cancellation remains legal from nonterminal phases, unlike E3's late-analysis restriction.
- Consequence: Interleaving discovery, evaluation and attribution or obtaining corrected evidence can require a successor campaign even when the same baseline/candidate work is still useful. A single permanently unevaluated admitted variant also blocks RecordSelection, which requires an assessment for every variant. This is a source-derived lifecycle constraint, not proof of context loss or permission to bypass promotion review.
- Repair direction: Define durable per-variant/evidence lifecycle and explicit supersession rather than one global phase that closes all earlier admission. Preserve immutable snapshots and completed work when extending or repairing campaign scope. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5e183789-bf37-5307-a842-6bc54c224a0b.title: [L396] B2 canonical snapshots couple identity order to cycle order and disallow repeated finding/approval history
5e183789-bf37-5307-a842-6bc54c224a0b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L396.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-quality-policy/src/evidence/reviews.rs:49-103`, `src/evidence/ordering.rs:13-33`, `src/evidence/authority.rs:41-69`, `src/canonical/collections.rs:45-65`, `src/review.rs:122-132`, `tests/cases/construction.rs:29-82`, `tests/cases/canonicality.rs:166-214`, `crates/foundation/peritus-spec/src/contract/validation.rs:227-231`.
- Behavior: reviews must simultaneously increase by every byte of ReviewCycleId and by positive u16 cycle ordinal. Two reviewer observations cannot share one ordinal, so this model consumes one cycle for each reviewer rather than representing several reviewers in one cycle. A legitimate chronological pair whose IDs sort in reverse cannot be made canonical merely by reordering it: one ordering fails the ID check and the other fails the ordinal check. All finding IDs must be globally unique across reviews, even if two independent reviewers report the same finding with identical disposition/digest. Gate IDs are unique across the entire gate snapshot, and semantic approval subjects are unique across the entire approval snapshot, without including revision in those identity keys. Tests explicitly enforce duplicate finding, duplicate ordinal, descending ordinal, and repeated approval-subject rejection.
- Consequence: this is a current-snapshot representation, not an appendable multi-revision attempt/review/approval history. Feeding retained historical facts directly into it can reject them before acceptance is evaluated; honest corroboration of one stable finding also requires caller-side normalization or distinct finding identities. Simultaneous independence/quorum cannot be represented using a shared cycle ordinal, explaining the quorum<=cycle-limit coupling in L393. The installed ID generation and normalization paths remain to be traced; no live UUID-order failure is claimed.
- Repair direction: keep stable identities separate from chronology, retain multi-observer finding provenance and disposition revisions explicitly, and derive a checked current acceptance projection from durable history. Preserve contradiction detection and independent-review counting; do not delete history or forge fresh identities solely to appease canonical order. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5e24989a-2caf-5807-88b4-75ab4f2c7c2a.title: [L623] Evidence work repeats synchronous whole-history and artifact verification without a resumable work owner
5e24989a-2caf-5807-88b4-75ab4f2c7c2a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L623.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-evidence/src/admission.rs:35-75,93-127`; `src/sqlite/store.rs:81-104,196-216,274-289`; `src/bundle/plan.rs:125-177,206-238`; `src/bundle/assemble.rs:80-119`; `src/bundle/verify.rs:145-168,278-284` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Admission scans the checked export's artifact references and verifies artifact bytes before recognizing an exact retry. Bundle planning reloads records for freshness, verifies duplicate artifact references before deduplication, and linearly searches records for each frame. Assembly verifies each artifact again and then hashes its stream; offline verification similarly matches each frame against the full record list. The Read/Write interfaces provide no cancellation or durable cursor, and final EOF validation can block on a still-open stream.
- Consequence: Growing history and repeated retries can spend substantial time reading and hashing while producing no new durable result. EOF can wait indefinitely; this is an unowned blocking operation, not an artificial session deadline.
- Repair direction: Bind verified content to immutable digests and one transaction snapshot, index frames and artifact references, recognize durable retries before redundant work when safe, and persist cancellable phase/cursor progress. Source review only; no tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5e2e0150-4861-5397-acec-64df9a940e82.title: [L652] Quality timeout/cancel/recovery classification can contradict its own decoder and remove recovery
5e2e0150-4861-5397-acec-64df9a940e82.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L652.

Terminal failure construction separately gives TimedOut, Cancelled, or RecoveryIndeterminate disposition precedence. Process SelectBackend is also collapsed into reauthorization rather than retaining backend-selection guidance.
- Consequence: The adapter can manufacture an envelope its own consumer rejects, obscuring the original interruption and disabling the recovery route that the terminal initially carried. Removing default timers alone cannot repair cancellation/restart behavior.
- Repair direction: Derive structured outcome and terminal failure from one consistent classification, retain causal parsing/exit facts separately, and preserve the required recovery owner/route. Add producer-to-decoder cases for interrupted parsers.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5e34bd9e-ddd9-5686-9939-81374807ae7e.title: [L255] Valid Git quoted paths and long source lines can disable the entire structured diff
5e34bd9e-ddd9-5686-9939-81374807ae7e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L255.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/workbench/review/parser.rs:30-69,202-238`; `workbench/review/diff.rs:58-63,88-101`; `workbench/review/anchor.rs`.
- A diff header is accepted only by finding the literal delimiter ` b/`; +++/--- paths require an unquoted a/ or b/ prefix. There is no Git C-quoted path decoder. A valid quoted Git header (for example a path containing a tab or a non-ASCII filename under default Git quoting) can therefore fail the entire structured parse rather than remain accessible through a decoded exact anchor.
- Each line and hunk header uses MAX_PRODUCT_DETAIL_BYTES (**64 KiB**) and each line rejects controls other than tab. A single larger minified/source line rejects the whole structured object. Hunk start/count fields are **u32** and reject a positive count at line zero or an entirely empty range. These are syntax/display representation gates, not elapsed deadlines.
- Source tests cover ordinary unquoted paths, digest changes, traversal, and a small wire roundtrip; they do not demonstrate large-line, quoted-path or collection-bound behavior. A repair should preserve exact path/content identity while providing decoding and page/range access. **All six review source/test files fully read; no test executed.**

Full command/envelope frames use the production codec; the combined capsule must also fit the durable state bound. Kernel commits accept exactly one matching event and store one immutable capsule per event. Version/kind/phase/role inventories are closed.

The digest serializes every accumulated run, attempt, turn, action, review, and waiver each time. With a growing aggregate, cumulative replay work can grow quadratically; there is no resumable checkpoint or paged recovery path in this adapter.

No elapsed deadline or session expiry is imposed here, but permanent dependence on every old input and repeated complete-state work are daily-driving recovery risks.
- Expiry instants, remaining-use limits, and the five budget dimensions are serialized as authority facts; these files choose no short default. **Complete kernel persistence/recovery implementation read; no growth benchmark or damaged-input execution performed.**

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/telemetry/runtime.rs:21-63`; `src/telemetry/local_file.rs:13,21-75,79-110,118-138,156-169` in the same crate.
- Behavior: open recovers all trace records, projects them, restores eight retained checkpoints, and rebuilds a 4,096-item DropOldest buffer with 128-item batches before flushing synchronously. The exporter rejects a directory above 65,536 entries; its count includes non-batches and quarantined temporaries. Quarantine renames incomplete files but does not remove them; byte quota eviction selects only batch-prefixed files. Windows directory sync is inert.
- Consequence: retained non-batch/incomplete entries can exhaust admission regardless of remaining byte quota. Export/recovery I/O can block open and propagates Worker/Retry errors rather than providing an independent unavailable-observation mode. Fixed dropping and checkpoint retention need explicit gap accounting; they are not execution timers. Existing-file reads verify size first but then read to EOF without a read cap.
- Repair direction: recover and compact spool entries with explicit durable export/gap receipts; make telemetry failure observable without silently losing primary work progress. Page trace recovery and keep filesystem I/O off progress-critical paths. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

6009e476-6dce-54c7-910e-ae8fe2d5aeb7.title: [L669] Provider setup can disable durable routes on transient status failure and block even offline startup
6009e476-6dce-54c7-910e-ae8fe2d5aeb7.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L669.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-launcher/src/provider_setup.rs:24-31,91-153,184-234,237-287`; `src/provider_setup/models.rs:65-127`; `src/provider_setup/connection.rs:6-76`; `src/provider_setup/direct.rs:21-42`.
- Behavior: Every ordinary launch synchronously probes both account tools before checking prior setup/offline choices. NeedsAttention follows sign-in repair; declining or failing to restore readiness removes the route from the persisted enabled set and can choose another default/disable failover. A thrown login error instead exits startup. Retained model IDs are reused, and catalog failure permits an explicit manual model ID. Direct credentials are stored before the multi-provider selection is committed; cancelling later setup/test/publication has no enclosing credential-publication receipt. Settings remove replaced credentials even while old immutable configurations remain. Connection testing joins a blocking worker and has no caller cancellation handle.
- Consequence: A slow unused account probe can block direct-only/offline launch. Temporary status failure can become a durable route/configuration change, feeding the shared-daemon replacement behavior in L664. Deleting an old key can prevent continuation of older route generations; cancelled setup can leave an unpublished key reference. Explicit failover consent and manual model selection are legitimate user choices, not synthetic deadlines.
- Repair direction: Separate observed health from retained route intent; allow presentation/offline launch independently of optional probes, persist exact setup/publication ownership, and retain credential references while active durable generations require them.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

60f77db6-2697-505b-9d54-48d83a440bf4.title: [L495] OpenAI background response registration silently stops after 4096 identities
60f77db6-2697-505b-9d54-48d83a440bf4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L495.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/stream/terminal.rs:28-36`; `src/client.rs:65-115,283-302`; `src/client/cancel.rs:93-127` in the same crate.
- Behavior: a newly created background response is inserted into a process-local set only while its length is below 4096. Reaching the bound produces no failure or warning. Completion does not retire identities; successful confirmed cancellation removes one. Persisted-continuation restoration inserts identities through a separate path without this bound. New client/model composition resets the set.
- Consequence: later background responses can run successfully but become locally ineligible for exact resume or confirmed cancellation. The inconsistent restoration path also means the numeric cap is not a consistent resource bound. This is a lifetime registration limiter, not a session TTL.
- Repair direction: replace the ephemeral admission cache with durable response records and explicit active/terminal lifecycle reconciliation; capacity pressure must not silently revoke an already accepted response's resume/cancellation rights. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

61d9897d-351f-5296-b52e-0e1e0165cb18.title: [L509] Plugin host lifetime quota can be exhausted by rejected work
61d9897d-351f-5296-b52e-0e1e0165cb18.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L509.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/quota.rs:16-55`; `src/host.rs:153-175,230-266,407-421`; `src/authority.rs:106-133`; `src/transport.rs:145-162` in the same crate.
- Behavior: lifetime usage increments before concurrent admission. A concurrency rejection refunds the active count but not lifetime usage. Successful completion releases only active capacity; lifetime count never refills within an instance. Exhaustion is labelled RetryLater although waiting cannot restore it. Mandatory manifest/host invocation duration drives a Tokio response-read timeout. The authority grant must carry a nonzero deadline and is forwarded to the plugin, but the host neither checks it against a clock nor uses it to narrow the invocation timeout. Host configuration/narrowed quotas are not validated on construction/start.
- Consequence: bursts of rejected work can permanently disable an otherwise idle plugin. Zero host ceilings can produce immediate failures despite positive manifest quotas. A compulsory local duration survives the product's earlier deadline removals, while the separate purported authority deadline is not enforced consistently. No numeric production host defaults are inferred from the five-second/16-request test fixture.
- Repair direction: make lifetime usage recoverable or explicitly unlimited, account only admitted effects and refund rejected reservations, represent untimed invocation policy end to end, and validate explicit authority/capacity semantics consistently. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

62d76711-b08a-5f50-aca0-ddb1049e38de.title: [L787] The composer accepts a larger draft than durable chat admission can represent
62d76711-b08a-5f50-aca0-ddb1049e38de.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L787.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/conversation.rs:1-338` and `sessions.rs:1-147`, completely read; task-sized editing gate in L784.
- Behavior: Normal chat admission converts the entire draft to `WorkbenchInputText` and rejects anything outside 1–8,192 bytes. The composer instead permits `MAX_PRODUCT_TASK_BYTES`. Sending then stages creation, queue admission, execution discovery/start, and continuation through separate receipts. New titles are derived from at most 64 characters; explicit session titles and literal searches are capped at 256 bytes, and library requests ask for 64 rows with pagination. An archived session requires explicit unarchive. The continuation command has no independent operation identity, as recorded in L716.
- Consequence: A valid editable draft can become unsendable at Enter. A queued input can survive while later execution admission fails or remains unresolved; the UI cannot infer that receipt acceptance means the original native window was recovered. Title/search page capacities differ from execution budgets and authority checks must remain explicit.
- Repair direction: Unify the editable/admitted input contract using durable referenced text, and make queue-to-execution continuation an idempotent operation with a recoverable worker identity. Preserve archive, workspace, and user-stop authority.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.
