631634bc-9665-5f42-baa2-2ca115aab67d.title: [L612] Windows secret reader rejects material exactly at its advertised one-MiB boundary
631634bc-9665-5f42-baa2-2ca115aab67d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L612.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/native/secret.rs:16-17,29-80,93-123`; `src/channels.rs:155-184` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Protected secret reading checks `len == 1,048,576` before attempting the EOF read. Exactly one MiB is therefore rejected even if the next read would prove EOF. Reads are synchronous with no cancellation and close the inherited source handle before returning the read outcome. Environment delivery requires UTF-8. File delivery uses ordinary `fs::write`, allowing create/truncate and retaining no exact file-cleanup owner in staged secrets, whose state contains only environment entries.
- Consequence: Material at the declared maximum fails activation; a partial read cannot retry the closed source. File creation/write failure can leave material whose cleanup is not represented by this helper staging owner. Surrounding session teardown is being inspected separately. These are capacity and staged-effect problems, not timeouts.
- Repair direction: Read at most maximum plus one byte with an explicit length/EOF contract, preserve ownership through fallible staging, and retain exact private-file cleanup obligations through helper and session recovery.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

656d342c-1208-5200-9d56-a028e417d5b4.title: [L620] Evidence storage retains a five-second contention timer and fixed SQLite representation bounds
656d342c-1208-5200-9d56-a028e417d5b4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L620.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-evidence/src/sqlite/store.rs:23-64`; `src/sqlite/connection.rs:7-44`; `src/sqlite/row.rs:158-173`; `src/error.rs:81-94` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Default options install a five-second SQLite busy timeout. The API requires a Duration rather than an explicit wait-until-canceled policy. Connection setup also fixes SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH at 32 MiB and disables attached databases; journal positions must fit positive SQLite INTEGER. Busy and locked failures preserve their source and return Retry, but this crate supplies no persistent wait/retry owner.
- Consequence: Ordinary database contention can interrupt evidence work at an artificial elapsed-time threshold. Integer, attachment, and row-size restrictions are storage/protocol constraints, not run deadlines; removing the timeout must not erase their error distinctions.
- Repair direction: Carry cancellation and a durable contention continuation through the storage owner; separate optional operational waiting policy from schema representability. Source review only; no tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

6584acd7-e633-53fb-8d88-4e5b9af89cad.title: [L335] D1 progress and recovery synchronously copy complete state and replay complete history
6584acd7-e633-53fb-8d88-4e5b9af89cad.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L335.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-gates/src/reducer.rs:58-85,88-113,120-143`; `src/canonical.rs:11-79`; `src/durability.rs:79-95,295-345`; `src/durability/lifecycle.rs:24-61`; `src/engine/publication.rs:57-85`; `src/wire/state.rs:51-87`.
- **Blocker:** Each accepted command clones and hashes every retained slot, receipt and consumed execution/action identity, then constructs and encodes another full checkpoint. Resume loads every aggregate record and semantically reduces every event from genesis. Each evidence publication independently reloads all records to locate one authoritative result. Plan-free pause/resume still loads the complete event collection and checkpoint.
- **Consequence:** Growing attempt/evidence history increases synchronous CPU, allocation and database work for progress and controls. Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L378.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-leases/src/transition/lifecycle.rs:65-78`, `src/transition/validation.rs:147-152`, `src/transition/fencing.rs:123-133`, `src/transition/reconciliation.rs:245-261`, `src/transition/fencing_apply.rs:135-168`.
- Behavior: Available acquisition requires the stored authority epoch and monotonic tick floor. The explicit clock-discontinuity reducer requires Active, so it cannot rebind an Available aggregate after a changed epoch. A Reconciling aggregate can reset its epoch only when its original cause was ClockDiscontinuity; expiry, holder loss, release, and revocation reconciliation reject a later epoch change even with a safe correlated observation. Quarantined has no recovery command (L377).
- Consequence: a durable lease with no active holder, or one already being reconciled, can lose all continuation paths after an authority-clock restart/change. This is a source-derived phase/clock contract gap; these files do not establish which installed host changes epochs on restart. Same-epoch regression may become usable if time catches up, whereas a different epoch cannot pass ordinary comparison.
- Repair direction: represent clock rebinding as a durable command permitted in safe nonactive phases and during pending reconciliation, preserving generation/correlation rather than reminting identities or bypassing quiescence. Coordinate formal phase/clock invariants. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

66bfc2de-dded-5d7c-931f-c12af50de2e5.title: [L256] Lossless history is durable, but installation and replay repeatedly traverse complete state/history
66bfc2de-dded-5d7c-931f-c12af50de2e5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L256.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/sqlite/history.rs`; `sqlite/history/node.rs`; `sqlite/query/state.rs`; `sqlite/query/aggregate.rs`.
- History has **512-byte leaves**, **fanout 16**, maximum tree **level four**, and a logical value maximum of **16 MiB**. The leaf size is not an independent lifetime quota. At the 16 MiB value limit, installation visits 32768 leaf chunks plus their internal nodes. Every existing node is read and checked on each visit; content-addressed reuse avoids duplicate inserts but does not skip the full traversal.
- Historical reads reconstruct the entire logical value and validate every visited node and producer event. Aggregate replay loads and validates every retained event through the exact head into a Vec. These adapters choose no elapsed timeout, but increasing session/state history entails synchronous work proportional to full retained data; they expose no incremental/page recovery for these operations.
- Missing/damaged nodes, mismatched hashes, or absent producing events abort the requested history/replay. This is necessary integrity enforcement; daily-driving repair needs durable incremental verification and scoped recovery without turning one corrupted history row into an unexplained fresh context. Current callers and cross-subsystem failure consequences are tracked separately (including L198). **All named implementation files fully read; no timing benchmark or recovery reproduction performed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

66c5cfe5-5380-53a9-aece-9121d351dffe.title: [L207] Provider retry policy forbids more than 16 attempts and rejects long Retry-After observations
66c5cfe5-5380-53a9-aece-9121d351dffe.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L207.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/retry.rs:9-11,97-125,146-187,281-296,332-362`; daemon caller in L205.
- RetryPolicy constructors impose at most **16 attempts**, a maximum backoff of **24 hours**, positive base delay/cumulative bytes and at most **1 GiB cumulative transfer**. An optional selected elapsed bound still exists; without_deadline omits only that bound. Attempt and cumulative-byte exhaustion stop otherwise legal recovery.
- The daemon Anthropic/Google policy selects **3 attempts / 64 MiB cumulative bytes / 2-second maximum delay and Retry-After**. A Retry-After observation above that selected maximum is rejected as InvalidRetry rather than honored or converted to a longer wait. An observation beyond the byte/attempt/selected elapsed ceiling similarly errors before action planning. Actual HTTP Retry-After producer/adapter behavior remains pending.
- Backoff uses deterministic **0.5-1.5 jitter** capped to max_delay; it is a delay, not a session timeout. Fresh retries after ambiguous acceptance and partial streams require exact idempotency/resume protection, respectively. Those restrictions protect against duplicate provider actions and must remain distinct from synthetic recovery exhaustion.
- **Entire policy implementation read; no long Retry-After or reconnect test run.** This closes the previously unknown 64 MiB/delay argument semantics in L205.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

688649e8-eff9-5a52-a351-63e64a6ff036.title: [L390] Policy can create an approval challenge whose approval window has already expired
688649e8-eff9-5a52-a351-63e64a6ff036.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L390.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-policy/src/evaluation.rs:192-234`, `src/evaluation_approval_result.rs:54-76`, `src/rule.rs:237-297`, `tests/support/reference.rs:159-190`, `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/request.rs:187-236`, `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/request.rs:333-360`, `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/authentication.rs:151-161`, `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/authentication.rs:251-267`.
- Behavior: evaluation checks the observed tick against the effective capability scope, then only checks that approval validity has a nonempty intersection with that scope. It does not check that the observed tick lies inside the resulting approval window before returning ApprovalRequired. The approval-request constructor checks collection bounds and computes its digest without rejecting a challenge whose requirement expired before evaluated_at. Authentication later requires the requirement window to contain its observation.
- Consequence: for example, effective scope [5,90), approval requirement [0,20), and evaluation at tick 30 produce a challenge with approval window [5,20) and retained time floor 30. It can be packaged as a request, but no nonregressing same-epoch approval observation can satisfy it. Fresh user approval cannot repair this request. The independent scalar reference model repeats the missing temporal check, and the completely read policy test suite exercises empty intersections and scope expiry rather than this nonempty-but-already-expired challenge. This example is derived from the executable branches, not an executed reproduction or a claim about current prompt production.
- Repair direction: validate approval eligibility at challenge construction, represent future validity as a resumable wait where applicable, and route expired requirements to an explicit refreshed-authority path that retains action/session identity. Do not present an impossible approval prompt or retry it unchanged. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

68c9b9ee-7a29-56fe-b320-5d2cbe77b8f4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L554.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-patch/src/transaction/apply.rs:150-171`, `src/transaction/apply.rs:188-210`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:34-85`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:102-146`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:189-228`, `src/transaction/filesystem.rs:295-347`, `src/transaction/roots.rs:41-72`, `src/line_endings.rs:25-80`.
- Behavior: Targets above the shared production file bound cannot be exactly observed for a patch. Symlinks, special nodes and nested repositories are rejected. Non-Unix executable-mode patches are rejected before staging. Same-device root validation is implemented on Unix; other platforms accept that check unconditionally and can fail later during rename. Full file reads/hashes, repeated pre/post/rollback observations, directory discovery, normalization, writes and synchronization run synchronously without cancellation or a progress cursor.
- Consequence: This path has no synthetic wall-clock deadline, but blocked filesystem I/O cannot be canceled through the API and an accepted multi-file operation has no incremental recovery progress interface. File-size and platform representation limits can prevent legitimate edits. Exact preimage checks, disjoint roots and unsafe-target rejection protect mutation integrity and must remain effective when limits change.
- Repair direction: Support scalable exact observation and durable incremental progress, expose cancellable host operations, and validate native volume/mode capabilities before effects rather than treating unsupported checks as successful.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

693a1427-c736-5a8d-9e86-59420d7d9877.title: [L546] Redaction fingerprint construction expands the entire secret before applying its count limit
693a1427-c736-5a8d-9e86-59420d7d9877.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L546.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/material.rs:8-22`, `src/fingerprint.rs:51-75`, `src/fingerprint.rs:80-89`, `src/fingerprint.rs:116-133`.
- Behavior: Material accepts up to one MiB. Redaction construction hashes every sliding fragment of length four through 64, collects all hashes, sorts and deduplicates them, then rejects more than 65,536 unique fingerprints. For a one-MiB input, this constructs 63,961,124 fingerprint entries before deduplication. Each hash builds another temporary byte vector. Matching scans the fingerprint vector synchronously.
- Consequence: An input allowed by the material boundary can incur tens of millions of allocations and hashes, substantial memory use and sorting before a later rejection. No cancellation or progress boundary is provided. The expansion is derived from the loops, not a measured stress run.
- Repair direction: Define a redaction representation and algorithm whose construction and matching costs are bounded by the accepted material size; reject unsupported inputs before expansion or process them incrementally with cancellation. Preserve the security purpose of redaction.

6a6d17a6-2aa6-5914-9c72-e9ebb63fc03c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L538.

- Behavior: System resolution revalidates every returned address and fails the whole result if any answer is denied. Connect sorts admitted addresses and tries only the first, with no attempt at the remaining admitted answers when that address fails. Matching reconstructs/clones the complete network rule contract for each request and resolved IP. UDP requirements are rejected because no exact datagram relay is implemented; managed requests support TCP only. Special-address and explicit-deny checks are retained security boundaries.
- Consequence: A mixed answer set or an unavailable first admitted address can block a destination even when another authorized answer is reachable. This is a compatibility/recovery limitation, not a reason to remove destination authorization. Repeated contract reconstruction adds synchronous work; no measured bottleneck is claimed.
- Repair direction: Preserve deny precedence and special-address authority while defining selection among independently admitted addresses and cancellable connection attempts. Supply an explicitly admitted datagram path where required. No tests run.

Remove a mandatory iteration cutoff for ordinary driving; if an explicitly authorized quota applies, expose its reason and a durable continuation/amendment path. No tests run.

6d176d0f-f9e0-5fb1-89f0-e2d3d44df11a.title: [L660] Account status can block foreground setup and misclassify infrastructure failure as sign-out
6d176d0f-f9e0-5fb1-89f0-e2d3d44df11a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L660.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-provider-onboarding/src/account.rs:14,55-76,84-115,164-177,180-229`; `src/account/windows_tests.rs:18-99`.
- Behavior: Account status uses synchronous Command::output with no local cancellation/progress surface and only checks the 64-KiB stdout/stderr cap after collecting both complete streams. Catalog observation probes Codex then Claude sequentially. Any unsuccessful status exit is SignedOut; launch failure, oversized output, or malformed Claude JSON becomes NeedsAttention without its actual diagnostic. Successful interactive login synchronously repeats status. Windows uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW and a Claude title opt-out; its regression exercises console isolation with a ten-second transport fixture.
- Consequence: A hanging/noisy status command can hold up the calling UI despite the nominal output bound, and an infrastructure failure can send the user through unnecessary login again. These observations do not justify adding a synthetic session deadline. The Windows ten seconds are fixture values.
- Repair direction: Make status discovery cancellable/asynchronous with incremental retention and explicit unknown/infrastructure outcomes, preserving credential-safe causal diagnostics and the existing console isolation.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

6d3cedca-f9c0-5017-b482-ca58f096ab94.title: [L430] E3 execution requires a wall deadline and has no untimed representation
6d3cedca-f9c0-5017-b482-ca58f096ab94.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L430.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/profile/binding.rs:98-168,195-218,222-330`, `src/execution/directive.rs:35-67,149-183`, `src/execution/port.rs:56-129` in the same crate.
- Behavior: ExecutionBinding stores deadline_micros as u64 and rejects zero, along with zero concurrency. The positive deadline participates in its immutable digest and is copied into both candidate and evaluator stage directives. There is no None/Untimed variant. The E3 execution wrapper itself runs synchronous external ports and does not measure elapsed time or install a watchdog; enforcing the requested deadline is delegated to runtime composition.

The read source proves the mandatory contract but does not establish which external owner enforces it, what value an installed evaluator uses, or that it caused the current session timeout. Concurrency's u16 width is a physical scalar constraint, separate from the positive-only policy.
- Repair direction: Represent an explicit optional user deadline separately from process ownership, cancellation, isolation, and measured elapsed usage, and propagate untimed execution consistently through both stages and their canonical identities. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

6d3d9ff7-5906-51be-9810-40da2a35eca0.title: [L438] E3 repeatedly copies and replays the complete campaign instead of resuming bounded work
6d3d9ff7-5906-51be-9810-40da2a35eca0.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L438.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/aggregate/reducer.rs:22-30,69-93,172`, `src/aggregate/state.rs:115-117,185-195,346-418`, `src/durability/replay.rs:36-48,76-101`, `src/wire/event.rs:52-70`, `src/wire/state.rs:15-18,55-66`, `src/durability/commit.rs:82-94`, `src/runtime/publication.rs:87-88` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Every transition clones and canonically hashes the complete rollout map and retained batch artifacts. C0 loading activates each frame through apply_event and then applies it again; rebuild replays the entire history again. State frames clone and nest the entire canonical checkpoint under production byte bounds. rollouts() creates a complete Vec even when recovery only needs an any() probe. Publication exports the complete journal for evidence admission. These synchronous paths expose no cancellation/progress probe.
- Consequence: At R retained rollouts and E events, transition/recovery work includes O(E*R) full-state copying/hashing after the plan is populated, with repeated replay passes and full-history allocation. Larger profiles can spend increasing time rereading/rebuilding rather than executing new work. Nested codec limits can reject a full checkpoint even if individual components fit. This is source-level cost analysis, not a benchmark or attribution of the live session's loop.
- Repair direction: Preserve immutable history while making validated checkpoints and effect receipts support incremental recovery, streaming projections and bounded resumable analysis. Keep cancellation/status independent of full-campaign serialization. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

6e3a1049-b625-5fa8-8898-0baa7bdf2410.title: [L800] Caption edits unnecessarily invalidate file previews, and multiline captions are rejected
6e3a1049-b625-5fa8-8898-0baa7bdf2410.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L800.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/files/keys.rs:1-126`, `files.rs:161-295`, `files/import.rs:71-94,222-279`, and `images/editor.rs:1-97`, all completely read.
- Behavior: File field editing calls `discard_preview` after every editor key, including caption changes and cursor movement. A user who previews first, then enters the required caption, must preview/read again before confirmation. Image caption editing does not discard its byte preview. Both caption editors reject every Unicode control character on paste, including newline/tab, despite WorkbenchInputText supporting ordinary multiline text and the README promising multiline captions. Field limits are 4,096 path bytes, 80 file-range bytes, and 8,192 caption bytes. File preview/read acceptance checks destination and path but does not compare the current range/refresh draft to the request's range/refresh when an already-issued reply arrives.
- Consequence: The file workflow can induce repeated reads without acceptance and can reject a normal pasted multiline instruction. An old range reply can become available after the range draft changed, although confirmation still carries the preview's exact original request. This is a UI state/consent mismatch, not a provider execution timeout.
- Repair direction: Keep byte-preview consent stable across caption/cursor edits, allow inert newline/tab in caption text, and correlate incoming previews with the full current source/range/mode generation. Repreview only when bytes, selection, or authoritative provider binding changes.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

6ed37dab-2fda-581b-a58d-a7b2c04d8cf4.title: [L362] E1 sixteen-MiB policy is narrowed by nested eight-MiB codec fields
6ed37dab-2fda-581b-a58d-a7b2c04d8cf4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L362.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/aggregate/command.rs:170-183,263-269`, `src/aggregate/state.rs:139-145,173-203`, `src/wire/state.rs:52-66`, `src/wire/command.rs:97-109`, `src/wire/event.rs:94-112`, `src/durability/commit.rs:113-126,344-374`; production codec bounds previously completely read under L009.
- Behavior: E1's compiled event and state capacities are 16 MiB, but canonical production encoding caps one opaque field at 8 MiB. Complete history is one state field, the full state identity is another opaque field, and the complete canonical state is wrapped in another field for family 81. Command/event semantic data is similarly one opaque field. Capacity errors from these encoding paths are classified as `Quarantine`, before the explicit E1 length checker can return a recoverable configured-limit rejection.
- Consequence: durable mutation or settlement can stop below advertised E1 capacities, and a proposed allocation failure can receive an integrity-quarantine disposition. Retirement shrinks hot receipt content, but adds permanent retired receipt IDs; that set is subject to the production 65,535-item collection ceiling and whole-state bytes. There is no retirement-ID rollover command in the fully read aggregate vocabulary.
- Repair direction: align domain admission, canonical transport and durable checkpoint representation. Use separately addressed history/plan/receipt segments and small frontier checkpoints; represent recoverable capacity pressure separately from corrupted durable input. Exact binding and malformed-input rejection remain necessary. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

70168ce9-f55d-5cb9-809b-21798ef4c444.title: [L046] In-place scope journal has a lifetime byte ceiling and strict torn-record barrier
70168ce9-f55d-5cb9-809b-21798ef4c444.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L046.

- `workspace_delivery/scope.rs:14-15,86-102,165-215` limits the append-only scope evidence journal to **64 MiB** and each record to **512 KiB**. Enrollment fails when the next record crosses the total ceiling. A torn/non-newline/oversized record, wrong schema/scope, or duplicate path rejects the whole load.
- Every paths/enroll/changed-paths/diff query loads that journal; changed paths additionally stamp every enrolled path. There is no journal rotation, chunked state migration, or torn-tail reconciliation in this file. Other recovery implementations are pending before claiming none exist.
- File previews stop at **16 KiB** and rendered diffs at **512 KiB** (lines 122-153,260-279). Exact hashing streams whole files with an 8,192-byte buffer and has no source byte ceiling in this implementation; a buffer size is not a file limit.
- Nonempty directories cannot be scope declarations (lines 243-248); effects therefore require explicit file paths rather than directory inventories. New read enrollment can fail for journal/schema corruption before the read tool dispatches (L043).

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7183cded-1ee6-5ab3-9fa7-2e997a03d202.title: [L798] Attachment previews select launcher role defaults instead of the active conversation's provider
7183cded-1ee6-5ab3-9fa7-2e997a03d202.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L798.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/images.rs:1-245`, `files.rs:1-341`, and `files/import.rs:1-300`, all completely read; `src/model/chat.rs:278-284` and binding/receipt callers already fully read.
- Behavior: Image reads, workspace-file previews, external-text imports, and their confirmation checks take the writer profile from `ProductUi::providers`, which represents the launcher's next-run role selection. Ordinary chat uses `chat_providers`, which first prefers the selected run snapshot's actual providers. Attachment model choice is separately taken from `chat.models.writer`. Thus opening an existing conversation with a different provider can pair its model with the launcher's default profile for preview/consent. The exact consent checks themselves are necessary; their source of identity must be corrected. This source-derived mismatch was not reproduced against the installed daemon.
- Repair direction: Resolve provider/model selection through the same exact conversation/run binding used for chat, and invalidate a preview only when that authoritative binding changes. Keep byte digest, workspace, model, and user-confirmation identity together.

71b8b1e6-3922-5c31-8356-fa2869888985.title: [L346] B1 one reservation overrun permanently faults the entire ancestor lineage
71b8b1e6-3922-5c31-8356-fa2869888985.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L346.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-budget/src/transition/reconciliation/observation.rs:94-103,115-151,204-218`, `src/transition/reconciliation/observation/terminal.rs:151-182,232-233`, `src/transition/accounting/fault.rs:78-110`, `src/state.rs:23-34`, `src/transition/reconciliation/finalization.rs:174-225,236-271`, `src/transition/reconciliation/finalization/cancellation.rs:112-154`, `src/command/vocabulary.rs:18-41`.
- Behavior: any cumulative usage dimension above the immutable **operation reservation** consumes the remaining reserved ceiling, stores the raw report, marks the reservation OverrunFaulted, and faults its account plus every ancestor through the root. This occurs even if total root capacity would otherwise be available. There is no reservation enlargement, corrected-overrun reconciliation, or account recovery command. Both exact full-ceiling settlement and ambiguous settlement consume all outstanding reservation; later accurate final usage is not accepted in those terminal phases. Cancelling Held releases the reservation but keeps the precharged attempt; active effects must settle through the other paths.
- Consequence: one under-estimated operation or erroneous usage report can permanently deny new work to sibling accounts through the shared faulted root. Recovery of a truthful later usage report cannot undo that fault in this model. This is an accounting/lifecycle barrier, not a timer implemented here. Existing active reservations can still be reconciled: there is no general require-open check on settlement, so this finding does not claim cancellation/cleanup is blocked solely by exhausted amounts.
- Repair direction: persist raw observations and resource incidents separately from logical run termination, admit truthful corrections with exact monotonic accounting rules, and make any spending stop an explicit resumable policy decision scoped to its owner. Do not silently turn a per-operation estimate miss into permanent whole-run loss. Scope: source-confirmed domain behavior; installed incident and tests not reproduced in this read-only audit.

- Test evidence update: `tests/ledger.rs:245-289` uses root tokens 20 and child reservation 10, reports 11, asserts **both child and root Faulted**, and rejects later root work despite remaining root capacity. This is an existing source fixture, not a fresh execution.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

This is independent of an elapsed horizon and can drive repeated rejections or prevent automatic recovery. Actual HTTP-date/provider behavior was not queried; this is a parser/policy finding from source.
- Repair direction: retain provider scheduling data with explicit units/parse status, support its documented forms, and schedule cancellable recovery without throwing away the normalized rejection when local policy cannot schedule it. No tests run.

72de9c8b-ee52-58e1-a0a1-f3f7b496e1ba.title: [L251] Outbox attempts cannot be unlimited, and exhaustion invalidates a still-valid final lease
72de9c8b-ee52-58e1-a0a1-f3f7b496e1ba.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L251.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/outbox.rs:5-8,63-79,107-132`; `sqlite/outbox_store.rs:19-50,60-105,113-163`.
- Each message requires a positive **u16 max_attempts** with no unlimited representation, an ASCII-graphic destination of **1..512 bytes**, and a payload at most **16 MiB**. Claim time and lease_until are caller-supplied positive increasing ticks; these files choose no wall-clock lease duration.
- Before selecting a new claim, the UPDATE changes **every Pending or Claimed row with attempts >= max_attempts to Exhausted**, without checking whether a Claimed row's lease has expired. A row reaches that attempt count when the final claim is issued. Any subsequent claim can therefore exhaust it while its last worker still holds a valid lease. The worker's exact acknowledgment then fails StaleHead because state is no longer Claimed.
- There is no reopen/requeue path in this complete adapter. Exhaustion can become permanent loss of delivery rather than an explicit recoverable outcome. A repair must distinguish an active final claim from an expired failed attempt and preserve durable delivery identity/fencing. The direct acknowledgment helper also treats an already Acknowledged row as idempotent without comparing the supplied old fence, while append-bound acknowledgments require a current exact claim; that contract difference needs caller review. **Both files fully read; production producer/dispatcher selected attempts and lease cadence remain pending.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7461303b-b05f-5cf1-af46-5119b91428ae.title: [L753] Accepted review feedback can lose its execution handoff and exact retry does not restore it
7461303b-b05f-5cf1-af46-5119b91428ae.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L753.

- Behavior: the ordinary command commits AddReview/RebindReview to C0, then calls resume_feedback only for a fresh accepted receipt. An exact retry returns the existing C0 receipt early and never retries that handoff. A failed save can leave an in-memory queued projection without a spawned owner. Starting feedback also resets aggregate progress rather than retaining the prior attempt base.
- Repair direction: persist a resumable feedback-execution handoff with the original command identity, reconcile it on both fresh and duplicate receipt paths, and commit/rollback the run transition before spawning. Retain explicit feedback modes and current-candidate checks. No tests run.

75884c13-2a1d-5021-970a-01abef84788d.title: [L628] Projection installation compares generation ownership but does not check that its candidate still represents the current journal
75884c13-2a1d-5021-970a-01abef84788d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L628.

- Behavior: Atomic install validates the candidate's own payload digest/count and compares only the caller's expected active generation. It checks no authoritative current journal position/head in the install transaction. A journal advance without a competing projection install leaves that CAS unchanged, so an older candidate can still become active; a later startup then asks for another genesis rebuild. All old generation payloads remain in SQLite, with no garbage-collection operation in this crate. Identical valid bindings are reused and a stale generation CAS rolls back atomically.
- Consequence: Busy active journals can repeatedly obsolete expensive rebuilds without a suffix catch-up plan. Repeated changed bindings retain complete duplicate derived payloads and grow disk usage. This is a consistency/work-amplification gap; no installed recurrence is claimed.
- Repair direction: Compare the candidate's authoritative journal binding at activation or atomically catch up to a verified suffix; retain the old active generation until success and reclaim only unreferenced derived generations under an explicit retention owner. Source review only; no tests run.

75f7241d-5e45-5546-9c54-da3a46694938.title: [L649] Hidden quality rendering truncation and progress caps can turn successful work into incomplete evidence
75f7241d-5e45-5546-9c54-da3a46694938.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L649.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/render.rs:9-39`; `src/execution/active.rs:18,76-100,129-140`; `src/execution/terminal.rs:35-78,82-105`; `src/result.rs:237-265,280-324`.
- Behavior: Output rendering escapes the full retained byte slice before limiting it. Its shared text helper silently truncates at 16 KiB, below the advertised 32-KiB rendering limit. An escaped output between 16 and 32 KiB is returned with Complete metadata despite that additional truncation; a larger chosen tail is truncated again at its end. Progress above the selected event count is discarded and marked progress_truncated. The quality decoder considers that flag incomplete evidence even if the process, complete artifacts, output parser, and success predicate passed, changing a success into IncompleteEvidence with fresh-action reauthorization guidance.
- Consequence: Model/human output can be misleadingly labeled complete, and a long successful check can be blocked solely by an informational progress count. The renderer also spends memory/time constructing bytes it will discard. These conclusions are source-derived, not an executed large-output check.
- Repair direction: Render only the requested window with accurate truncation metadata; make progress pagination/loss distinct from result evidence completeness so progress capacity cannot invalidate a proven successful execution.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

76b0589a-16a2-59dc-9167-7e48b6bdf979.title: [L226] Anthropic HTTP Retry-After above two seconds becomes InvalidRetry instead of a deferred retry
76b0589a-16a2-59dc-9167-7e48b6bdf979.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L226.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-anthropic/src/client.rs:97-111,140-173,324-345`; `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/retry.rs:146-187`; daemon-selected policy L205/L207.
- Anthropic reads the first Retry-After header as decimal seconds with at most **three fractional digits**, converts it to milliseconds and passes it unmodified into RetryPolicy. A valid value such as **3 seconds** exceeds the daemon's selected **2-second maximum** and plan returns InvalidRetry, propagated before a normalized RateLimited terminal is returned. This closes the concrete production producer/caller chain for L207; Google remains separately pending.
- Date-shaped values, surrounding whitespace or longer fractions do not parse in this helper, so the requested delay is omitted. Adapter status/content-type grammar is also closed: success requires exact **HTTP 200** plus text/event-stream; status 409/500/504/529 is transient, other server statuses follow the nonretryable default mapping.
- Retry accounting increments only the encoded request body for each submission, with **3 attempts / 64 MiB** selected; response/error bytes are not added here. The policy is consulted after failure, not as pre-submission admission, so it is a recovery ceiling rather than an all-transfer quota. Error bodies are fully drained/buffered under the HTTP **256 MiB** maximum before classification; an error-drain failure propagates before the useful status failure is emitted.
- **Complete client/config/error/client-tests source read; no long-delay reproduction or error-drain test run.** Existing tests exercise Retry-After zero, not this two-second rejection. Exact ambiguous-acceptance restrictions remain necessary to prevent duplicate provider submission.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

793f681c-e00a-55af-babb-646034762cc4.title: [L292] Bypass aging is a priority class, not a guarantee of dispatch at the configured bypass count
793f681c-e00a-55af-babb-646034762cc4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L292.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/selection/scan/work.rs:19-42,163-240`; `selection/model.rs:185-221`; `reducer/apply/dispatch.rs:91-107,145-159`; `selection/{scan,capacity}.rs`.
- Feasible bypass counters saturate at the immutable bound (at most **32,767**). Crossing it makes an item aged, which precedes unaged items. **Two aged items still compare priority before enqueue ordinal**. A lower-priority aged item can therefore be bypassed again by higher-priority aged work; the configured value is not an absolute maximum number of bypasses.
- Selection scans all retained work and picks the first feasible worker in canonical identity order. There is no worker rotation. Each feasibility call recomputes global/per-worker resource sums and concurrency counts; dispatch then rescans all work for feasible bypass updates, with a further work lookup per item. Gate and requirement evaluation repeatedly matches observations to definitions and scans observations again for each definition. Category coverage repeatedly crosses required categories and reviews. The ghost/spec recursive models do not themselves execute; fixed-size identifier/digest comparisons also do not imply input-sized recursion. No runtime latency, stack failure, or installed incident was measured. Apart from the separately recorded ordinal limits, no additional vector-length quota is established here.
- Repair direction: build validated indexes and cached current matches once, retain explicit semantic checks, and reuse them for coverage, independence and authority evaluation. Preserve canonical serialization independently from lookup layout. No tests run.

79cfbfda-a653-554f-8106-54b38105ef75.title: [L162] Attachment count limits can block releasing held inputs, while pin overrides use a different selection path
79cfbfda-a653-554f-8106-54b38105ef75.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L162.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/images.rs:193-208,249-315`; `control/images/metadata.rs:22-41`; `control/images/tests.rs:69-131`; file equivalent `control/files/ledger.rs:152-177`; effective selection `control/record/projection.rs:79-116`; related L126/L128/L154.
- **Limits/enforcement:** Whole-record image validation counts every selected attachment whose caption is incorporated or eligible pending, capped at 16 images / 12 MiB aggregate, with 4 MiB encoded / 8,192 side / 16 Mi pixels / 64 frames per image. A user can attach another image while an earlier caption is Held, but releasing that caption is then refused Capacity. File selections analogously cap 32 references / 512 KiB; these checks run on unrelated whole-record transitions too. Deselected/held history remains archived rather than freeing retained-record bytes.
- **Selection mismatch:** The lower image/file ledger counts only `selected=true`. Conversation-level effective selection can additionally include `selected=false` sources when explicitly Pinned and omit Excluded sources. The record's attachment-size validation uses the lower ledger, not that effective selection. Thus pin overrides can admit an effective set beyond the ledger's checked selection, while excluded-but-selected sources can still consume its allowance. Final host/provider admission handling remains pending; this is a confirmed discrepancy, not a claimed unchecked provider request.
- **Classification:** Product-selected admission ceilings and inconsistent preference accounting, separate from image decoding integrity and actual provider capacity. Tests above are fully read, not executed. Synthetic limits can obstruct queue lifecycle even with durable history intact.

79fc9687-0389-5066-8bed-5f92a04f632f.title: [L227] Provider catalog discovery fails entire results at fixed page, byte, frame and entry ceilings
79fc9687-0389-5066-8bed-5f92a04f632f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L227.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/catalog.rs:17-18,42-48`; `catalog/http.rs:12-14,61-90,104-149`; `catalog/runtime.rs:12-13,118-133,141-167,179-193,206-233`; `catalog/parse.rs:8-54,61-68`.
- HTTP discovery is capped at **16 pages / 4 MiB per page / 16 MiB total / 4,096 models**, with cursor at most **4,096 bytes** and each display label at most **512 bytes**. Native catalog queries also allow **16 Codex pages** and **4,096 accumulated entries / 4 MiB per frame / 16 MiB total**, plus at most **64 frames while waiting for each response** or Claude initialization. More harmless native notifications can exhaust that waiting-frame count before the matching response arrives.
- A single malformed entry/label, conflicting HTTP duplicate metadata, oversized response or exhausted page/frame count rejects the entire discovery result rather than yielding usable pages and a continuation. Claude model initialization requires the exact nested models field. Missing optional token/tool metadata stays unknown; no fabricated fallback model list is inserted. Explicit model selection remains available through adapter APIs; UI dependence on successful discovery still needs caller closure.
- Native discovery uses a fresh temporary directory for a **metadata-only subprocess**, then kills/waits for it after the query. This is not ephemeral inference context or a model-run timeout. No selected query elapsed deadline appears here; kill/wait cleanup is unbounded. Same-origin pagination and repeated-cursor detection protect credentials/progress and should remain separate from fixed catalog exhaustion.
- A selected model derives a new immutable profile ID from original profile/revision/model and resets profile revision to **1**, preserving route limits/capabilities but demoting model-specific provenance to Profiled. This also selects another native namespace (L215). **All four catalog files fully read; no large catalog/notification test run.**

7b5a7b8c-1ae3-52b1-a6b3-5532021fdb13.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L182.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/lifecycle.rs:20-71`.
- The caller supplies a shutdown timeout, applied separately to every drained task. The timeout result is ignored, and this method contains no explicit abort-and-join or native-owner reconciliation after an expired wait. It then marks an originally interrupted non-user-cancelled run RecoveryRequired unless its phase is Complete, and ignores persistence errors during these status updates.
- This timeout is a shutdown coordination allowance, **not an ordinary active session lifetime**. The defect risk is interpreting a failed join as settled ownership: the subsequent projection can offer unknown-outcome acknowledgement based on terminal phase, while this method has not established that the original effect owner is inactive.
- Cancellation is requested before joins. Whether a particular tool can outlive that request depends on its owner/cancellation implementation and the daemon shutdown caller. **Source-confirmed missing join-result handling; active-effect race is an inference requiring reproduction and caller tracing.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7b883a36-9562-5ebc-a27a-56d1a30b12e8.title: [L528] Structured Git diff and history have additional fixed, nonpaged observation ceilings
7b883a36-9562-5ebc-a27a-56d1a30b12e8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L528.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/diff.rs:12-15`, `src/diff.rs:65-82`, `src/diff.rs:141-187`, `src/diff.rs:201-225`, `src/history.rs:12-13`, `src/history.rs:55-68`, `src/history.rs:109-129`, `src/history.rs:140-183`.

Both complete Git outputs are collected before smaller request bounds are checked; all split name-status fields are collected before count validation. Every selected subject must be UTF-8, at most 4,096 bytes, and each author timestamp must parse as u64; one incompatible commit rejects the complete history observation.

A finite history result does not communicate whether more history exists; caller-guided traversal must reconstruct that separately. Per-request bounds do not prevent generating a larger response first. Byte, entry, subject and representation limits are distinct from execution deadlines.
- Repair direction: Add exact commit/path continuation and artifact-backed or streamed patch data, with explicit complete/incomplete observations and per-entry diagnostic handling. Preserve immutable commit-pair identity. No tests run.

7c3f9584-61b7-5a09-b45b-23367a28355e.title: [L857] Installed service templates impose restart and stop limits
7c3f9584-61b7-5a09-b45b-23367a28355e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L857.

- Source: `packaging/linux/peritus.service:4-13`; `packaging/windows/Peritus.Task.xml.in:20-47`; `packaging/macos/com.corvidae.peritus.plist.in:14-22`.
- Linux permits **five starts within 300 seconds**, restarts failures after **five seconds**, and sets a **40-second stop timeout** with mixed kill mode. Windows has no total execution-time limit (`PT0S`), but allows only **five failure restarts** at five-second intervals and permits hard termination. macOS throttles relaunch to **five seconds** and restarts unsuccessful exits.
- Daily-driving consequence: Linux and Windows can exhaust automatic recovery after repeated daemon failures, leaving reconnection dependent on external intervention. Stop deadlines can also interrupt graceful recovery. These are checked-in templates; installation of these registrations on the original live instance has not been established.
- Repair direction: preserve daemon and task identity through recoverable failures, remove fixed restart exhaustion, and coordinate shutdown with durable recovery receipts. No service or process was changed.

7c50397e-e06f-5f6b-8e02-1844d48c8862.title: [L303] Production framing imposes a hidden 65,535-command lifetime on collaboration, including cancellation and acknowledgments
7c50397e-e06f-5f6b-8e02-1844d48c8862.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L303.

- Source: `crates/foundation/peritus-codec/src/limits.rs:22-28`; `writer.rs:118-125,142-152`; `message.rs:33-39`; `crates/orchestration/peritus-collaboration/src/state/mutation.rs:80-89`; `wire/state.rs:52-64,116-123`; `durability.rs:64-72,263-269`; `command.rs:12-106`.
- Collaboration advertises messages<=262,144 and state<=64 MiB minus 16, and its state decoder's local command bound is tasks + 2*messages + 65,535. But every durable frame uses CodecLimits::PRODUCTION: **16 MiB complete frame** and **65,535 items in any collection**. The shared writer rejects a complete used_commands vector at 65,536.
- Every accepted command adds one retained ID; no command retires them. Once 65,535 IDs are committed, any additional command requires a 65,536-item state collection, including CancelTask, AcknowledgeCancellation, AcknowledgeMessage, Pause/Resume or Finalize. Canonical state encoding fails before append and maps the capacity failure to Codec/Quarantine. Actual frame size may block earlier; advertised larger message/state ceilings do not remove this hidden cap.
- Repair must decouple live control/state from lifetime receipt history with a versioned durable frontier and exact retry guarantees, and reconcile aggregate limits with protocol storage. Reserving more IDs or enlarging one quota postpones the same lifetime failure. **Complete framing and commit chain read; no 65K saturation run executed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7c614c8b-af19-5e12-8cb3-9e5c2a690d58.title: [L157] Request capture checks full reply history before exclusions or compacted replacements
7c614c8b-af19-5e12-8cb3-9e5c2a690d58.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L157.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/inputs/capture.rs:105-162,165-211`; caller `control/record/projection.rs:129-167`; public-reply ceiling `control/reply.rs:23-32`.
- **Limits/enforcement:** `capture_with_reply_view` first renders ALL incorporated user inputs and eligible pending instructions against MAX_REQUEST_CONTEXT_BYTES (16 MiB via `control.rs:65-66`). It then sums EVERY supplied reply's ORIGINAL byte length plus 32 bytes, and refuses Capacity if that total exceeds the same fixed ceiling. This precheck happens BEFORE excluding replies, omitting trailing replies, or substituting compacted source handles. Brief and file context add their own checks against this ceiling afterward. Each reply separately permits at most 1 MiB and cannot be empty.
- **Failure/recovery:** A conversation can stop admitting requests because original history exceeds the limit even when its actual compacted/excluded next view would fit. User-input history is always rendered and cannot be excluded through context preferences. Local provider-context compaction does not bypass this upstream control capture. The exact host-supplied reply-map retention/selection policy remains to be read; the check is confirmed for all entries supplied, not an assumption that every historical artifact always enters this map.
- **Classification:** Synthetic context admission ceiling and ordering defect that can defeat intended history compaction. Source-confirmed, not a live-size reproduction. Repair must retain immutable history while admitting an appropriate provider view, not delete or expire the conversation.

- Production caller traced: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_control/inputs.rs:156-180` first captures eligibility using empty reply text, selects only eligible replies, then rejects **the sum of their original immutable byte lengths plus framing and the eligibility capture** above 16 MiB before loading the text and applying the real capture. Excluded and trailing replies are filtered here, so this is not an all-history reply charge in that caller. **Compacted replacements do not reduce the original-byte charge**, confirming the compaction/admission mismatch on the production path. Images/files are checked again after effective pin/selection resolution (L162), preventing those overrides from producing an unbounded provider request.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7c92ec4b-f134-5581-99de-69357a4a425e.title: [L797] Restore recovery receipts release the UI's exact-operation retry record
7c92ec4b-f134-5581-99de-69357a4a425e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L797.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench/checkpoints.rs:1-290`, `checkpoints/receipts.rs:1-161`, `memory.rs:1-279`, `permissions.rs:1-158`, and `init.rs:1-137`, all completely read.
- Behavior: Checkpoint/restore matching retains exact operation, checkpoint, destination, revision, and original command. Rewind refresh obtains a fresh snapshot and builds another inspectable preview, unlike compaction in L794. After any matching restore receipt, including RecoveryRequired, `clear_checkpoint_command` takes the unresolved command; the UI clears the rewind request/preview and retains only the restore receipt with instructions to inspect recovery. `/sessions retry` can no longer replay that removed original command through this record. Checkpoint names are capped at 256 bytes. Guidance mutations select only an active ID in the current page and fence both record/dependency/conversation revisions. Permissions intersect immutable host authority, and init requires exact equality to the reviewed proposal.
- Consequence: Durable server history survives, but client retry ownership ends before restore recovery is settled. An operator receives an instruction rather than an executable reconciliation transition. Guidance paging and permission/proposal checks protect user scope and should remain; none of these files adds an execution timer.
- Repair direction: Retain a durable recovery operation until the restore transaction settles, expose its actual reconciliation action, and distinguish accepted recovery state from completed effect. Preserve exact preimages, proposal consent, forget semantics, and host authority.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7ce1dd5c-61ce-5b47-a935-3118f3268e32.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L743.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/interaction/presentation.rs:45-82`; `src/product_run/interaction/tool_activity.rs:18-71`; `src/product_run/interaction/tool_activity/display.rs:4-64,102-142`; `src/product_run/interaction/narration.rs:22-68`; `src/product_run/progress.rs:97-222` in the same crate.
- Behavior: completed JSON envelopes render whole strings and then truncate via the activity byte budget; tool previews parse full JSON, redact recognizable credentials and retain bounded head/tail text. Tool completion pairs with one volatile pending_tool by name/sequence, and takes that pending record even on a name mismatch. Waiting notices update one existing status entry rather than counting elapsed time toward failure. Progress counters saturate and elapsed/quiet values are observational, not cancellation triggers.
- Consequence: presentation expansion can cut a finding or run instruction despite exact lower-layer traces remaining elsewhere. Parallel/mismatched completion notices lose their prior public pending association, though they do not grant success authority. Removing timer language would not repair missing output continuation; conversely these elapsed counters do not need removal as execution deadlines.
- Repair direction: make display truncation explicit with exact trace/source links and paged full content; key pending tool observations by durable invocation identity. Preserve privacy redaction, typed settlement authority, and nonfatal liveness updates. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7cf6ea42-13ec-5d34-94fc-0cbad6727013.title: [L635] Filesystem traversal/search loses progress at bounds and silently excludes some search scope
7cf6ea42-13ec-5d34-94fc-0cbad6727013.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L635.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-fs/src/read.rs:239-324,327-365,377-395`; `tests/filesystem_tools.rs:50-60`.
- Behavior: Traversal materializes the entire selected subtree and returns an error at the next entry beyond the bound, discarding observed entries. It stops recursing at maximum_depth without a scope-truncated marker. Search first performs that whole walk, reads each eligible file, ignores binary and over-per-file-bound files, and only accounts UTF-8 bytes after the read. Total-byte or match overflow returns an error and discards all matches, with no continuation cursor. Preview text always contains the first UTF-8-safe 512 bytes of the line, even when the match occurs later. Case-insensitivity is ASCII-only. One no-follow symlink inspection failure rejects the entire traversal, as the test explicitly expects.
- Consequence: Broad code exploration may repeatedly redo the same reads instead of obtaining the next page; a no-match success does not establish absence in skipped/deeper files. The 64 MiB scanned-text allowance does not bound bytes read from binary files. Rejecting traversal/special nodes is an integrity boundary, but whole-job failure is a separate recovery choice.
- Repair direction: Return a truthful scope/skip summary and digest-bound continuation with retained partial results; budget actual I/O before reading and center match previews on the hit. Preserve no-follow guarantees while making unrelated unsafe entries separately reportable. Source review only; no tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7d145c05-237b-5625-990d-b4c29c05ac76.title: [L744] Deliverable controls hold the global run lock through unowned synchronous Git and file operations
7d145c05-237b-5625-990d-b4c29c05ac76.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L744.

Committed export and commit helpers use std::process::Command output with whole stdout/stderr capture and no C2 owner/cancellation handle here. Git hooks/signers run inside that synchronous call. Recovery matching hashes the whole saved patch and candidate source to EOF.
- Consequence: a blocked Git hook, signer, child or file operation can prevent record access/control for unrelated runs. Unbounded wall time permits the wait but does not provide progress, cancellation or native adoption. Whole output capture can grow before any public diagnostic bound applies. These are conditional source-derived blockers, not a measured live hang.
- Repair direction: retain a durable explicit deliverable-operation owner and native effect receipt, perform cancellable observation outside shared locks, and publish a fenced result only after reconciliation. Stream output/hashing with progress and exact ranges. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7b71a5cb-12e5-4ee4-aa4d-9190ba6471b9.content: OS cause reproduced directly: run33 of the separate OS-cause experiment exited101 because std::process::Command::output on a just-copied auth fake returned Os code26 / ExecutableFileBusy / Text file busy (/tmp/peritus-issue825-os-cause-33.log); the failed run is retained and the loop stopped. Source fs::copy creates executable writers while other fixture threads fork; Linux fork can inherit those writers until exec closes them, so parent copy completion is insufficient to ensure the inode has no writer. The manual execve ETXTBSY and fork descriptor inheritance contracts support this mechanism (https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html and https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fork.2.html). Repair the fixture owner by hard-linking the immutable built binary in private directories on the same artifact filesystem; no executable-copy writer, fork mutex, sleep, retry or deadline change. Deterministic Linux regression holds a writer on a legacy copy, observes ExecutableFileBusy, then verifies the new immutable alias has the Cargo artifact device/inode and executes the real auth rejection while that writer remains live; after dropping the writer the legacy copy executes too. Cleanup removes only the private alias and retains the source artifact. Native Windows/macOS qualification must confirm alias naming and filesystem semantics. Source-parent tempdirs avoid an actual cross-device failure here: /tmp and the Cargo cache are different filesystems. Historical discarded auth predicate cannot be retroactively recovered; new spawn/trace defects have concrete reproduction and root repair.

7dd507bb-eab4-5ec6-bc61-49787abc5ad5.title: [L807] Web attachments are accepted at sizes that the durable message cannot send
7dd507bb-eab4-5ec6-bc61-49787abc5ad5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L807.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/files/attachments.rs:28-111`; `src/daemon/chat.rs:14-33` in that crate.
- Behavior: staging accepts text snapshots up to 48 KiB and up to 16 selections; its error promises a 64 KiB combined message limit. Sending embeds all selected content and metadata as JSON, then rejects the complete message above 8 KiB. A separate 256 MiB retained-attachment metadata quota has no removal action in the fully read API dispatcher; deleting bytes alone does not remove the metadata sum.
- Consequence: valid staged attachments, including a single large snapshot, become unsendable; encoding/metadata further reduce usable text capacity. Normal repeated attachment use can reach a permanent cache-admission blocker. Exact source/session/digest checks are integrity requirements, not synthetic lifecycle limits.
- Repair direction: use durable attachment handles and chunked source admission consistently with the daemon, disclose the actual assembled capacity before accepting selections, and provide explicit durable snapshot removal/storage reconciliation.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7f587220-cc63-57cf-a26d-22de72209b77.title: [L648] Quality discovery can reject the whole catalog and consume its retry inputs
7f587220-cc63-57cf-a26d-22de72209b77.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L648.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-quality/src/discovery.rs:18,63-121`; `src/discovery/cargo.rs:7-34`; `src/discovery/just.rs:9-59`; `src/dispatcher/discover.rs:87-119,123-173`.
- Behavior: Discovery reads only root Cargo.toml and Justfile/justfile, each at most 1 MiB. Just scanning rejects more than 16,384 lines or 1,024 recipe names; it recognizes simple public zero-argument-looking headers, not the complete Just grammar. Every valid TOML table creates four all-targets/all-features Cargo checks. Duplicate names across explicit definitions, Cargo, or both Justfile spellings reject the whole catalog. The dispatcher takes its explicit vector before inspection and emits every complete check in one production JSON value; it retains the catalog only after terminal envelope success. That envelope has no cursor/artifact fallback and fewer allowed members than a 1,024-entry catalog needs.
- Consequence: A large or colliding surface can block even otherwise valid explicit checks, and retrying the same dispatcher sees consumed input. Unsupported discovery syntax is silently absent. Catalog shape/size failure is classified Protocol/Never rather than exposing the inspection/parser cause or a resumable result.
- Repair direction: Preserve explicit catalog availability and discovery diagnostics, reconcile names deliberately, use actual tool metadata for discovery, and serve large immutable catalogs in resumable pages before consuming retry ownership.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

7f5e28e0-35ea-58c7-bbcb-e785c337f7d9.title: [L253] Editor limits preserve rejected drafts, but signed-approval capacity is checked against the wrong layer
7f5e28e0-35ea-58c7-bbcb-e785c337f7d9.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L253.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/editor/input.rs:16-39`; `model/editor.rs:48-68,146-177`; `terminal/line_input.rs:19-62`; prompt limits in L244.
- Message/review editors use MAX_WORKBENCH_INPUT_BYTES (**8192**), process-ID drafts **256 bytes**, and ordinary prompt answers the codec string ceiling (**1 MiB**). Signed-approval paste uses **ceil(max_frame_bytes / 3) × 4** Base64 characters, approximately **22 MiB** for a 16 MiB codec frame, although the signed wire field is opaque **8 MiB**. This admits much larger text/decoded data than the request can serialize; it is a layer mismatch rather than a native-context limit.
- Editor paste removes control characters except newline/tab and rejects an oversized insertion while retaining the prior text. Pending editor drafts are kept in in-memory maps/queues; disconnect restores them with an ambiguity warning, not automatic replay. This is not durable client draft persistence across process termination.
- Pipe text must be strictly smaller than maximum_chunk_bytes to reserve the terminating newline. While awaiting acknowledgment, keyboard/paste editing is disabled. Oversized pipe paste is silently ignored. The model exposes no timed pending reset in these files; the acknowledgment/disconnect lifecycle must carry the same input identity and avoid an indefinite editing lock. **All four implementation files fully read; inline pipe tests read, not run.**

801f2975-5f4b-5b22-8719-fc0299fc38f1.title: [L394] Acceptance graph construction and its executable certificate use cubic scans and input-sized recursion
801f2975-5f4b-5b22-8719-fc0299fc38f1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L394.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-spec/src/gate.rs:222-260`, `src/gate.rs:308-364`, `src/gate_model.rs:71-131`, `src/gate_model.rs:144-225`, `src/gate_model.rs:250-328`, `src/gate_model.rs:349-361`, `src/gate_model/canonical.rs:30-48`, `src/gate_model/canonical.rs:68-135`, `src/contract/validation.rs:12-49`, `src/contract/validation.rs:111-183`.
- Behavior: GateGraph::new repeatedly scans canonical definitions from position zero for each selected gate; contains_gate scans the accumulated order. Even N independent gates in ascending order cause roughly the sum over i of the sum over j<=i of j comparisons, hence cubic growth. The constructor then runs a separate ordinary-Rust execution_order_is_valid certificate: uniqueness and declaration checks repeat linear searches, and canonical execution repeats first-eligible scans with full-order searches. These are executable fn bodies, distinct from erased spec/proof code. Search, uniqueness, dependency, definition-order, and canonical-order routines recurse to collection length, with no independent graph-size bound in the pure spec constructors. Cross-contract evidence validation also scans complete declarations once or twice for every gate-evidence edge, and scans gates/categories for evidence producers.
- Consequence: large valid contracts can spend substantial synchronous CPU time constructing/rechecking an unchanged certificate, while stack usage can grow with graph/order/dependency size. That can resemble a stall despite the absence of a wall deadline. These are source-derived growth and stack risks, not measured performance, reproduced stack overflow, or proof of the installed lockup. Small three-node graph tests cover order/cycles, not large-input responsiveness.
- Repair direction: construct indexed adjacency, indegrees, identity-to-position maps and a canonical eligible queue once; refine iterative executable checks against the same proof relation, without repeating full graph construction. Index cross-component evidence declarations and preserve immutable certificates. Do not solve responsiveness by adding a timeout or silently dropping gates. No tests run.

80a39ee4-47f9-5715-8e9c-64024e4fcabe.description:

Preserve explicit authority while repairing recognition or traversal restrictions. **Full source and inline test read; not exercised.**

80cdf3c8-7131-5fb6-9031-9b8f0fb58763.title: [L152] Trace append has no size limit but local-context recovery refuses traces above 1 GiB
80cdf3c8-7131-5fb6-9031-9b8f0fb58763.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L152.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/trace.rs:207-215`; `trace/local_memory.rs:59-65,76-131`; related torn-tail behavior L060.
- **Limits/enforcement:** The trace writer continually appends complete provider/tool/checkpoint records without checking total size. Local-memory observation replay refuses the entire trace once file length exceeds 1 GiB and refuses each scoped-tool frame above 64 MiB. These checks occur before selecting the requested scope; scoped frames for other scopes are also deserialized and version/sequence checked first. Schema version must equal 1, invocation/sequence must be nonzero, and records reject unknown fields; reconstructed arguments/output must meet production canonical-JSON bounds.
- **Failure/recovery:** A run can write successfully for a long time and then become unrecoverable through this reader after restart. Traces are shared across records/scopes at this path, so unrelated retained history contributes to the total limit. The reader returns torn-tail presence and requires append work to stop pending recovery; it does not repair that tail. There is no rotation, indexed scope seek, paging, compatible migration, or configurable growth policy in these files.
- **Classification:** Fixed recovery-only storage limits create a persistence mismatch. Genuine malformed/torn data needs safe recovery, while ordinary retained growth should not invalidate the session. Source confirmed; no 1 GiB reproduction or live causal attribution claimed.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

813b4cb8-6e01-5051-82ed-ed51333e9e2b.title: [L616] Windows managed networking adds a five-second native transaction wait and ephemeral filter ownership
813b4cb8-6e01-5051-82ed-ed51333e9e2b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L616.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/native/wfp.rs:38-75,78-140,262-265,324-330`; `src/network_filter.rs:22-40,53-60`; `src/network.rs:23-42`; `src/native/wfp/keys.rs:18-36` in the same crate.
- Behavior: WFP sessions set `txnWaitTimeoutInMSec` to 5,000, use dynamic nonpersistent ownership, and permit only IPv4 loopback TCP. Public route construction accepts loopback IPv6, which fails later during native installation. Probe installs a disabled block but does not exercise actual permitted connections or both enabled block filters. Filters select package SID rather than one process; no per-run AppContainer uniqueness check occurs here. Explicit release retains a failed engine close for retry, while drop ignores failure. Calls are synchronous and underlying BFE statuses become generic errors.
- Consequence: The fixed five-second field is a native transaction wait policy, not an execution lifetime; these routines do not start a WFP transaction, so deadline activation is not established by this read. Dynamic filters cannot be adopted from this owner record after restart. Route-family mismatch fails after earlier allocation. Shared package identities require concurrent-run qualification rather than assuming process-specific filtering.
- Repair direction: Align route negotiation with native IPv4 support before consumption, remove an unjustified fixed transaction-wait policy or make selected native semantics explicit, and keep filter ownership durable with exact package isolation and connection-level qualification.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

81f4e533-016b-57b7-a187-a311bf91d83b.title: [L296] Scheduler ingress can durably accept state that its own restart decoder rejects
81f4e533-016b-57b7-a187-a311bf91d83b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L296.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/wire/command.rs:212-223`, `wire/domain.rs`, `wire/records.rs`, `wire/state.rs:102-210`; `command.rs:231-253`; `reducer/apply/worker_control.rs:9-34`, `reducer/apply/admission.rs:42-73`; `reducer.rs:63-82`; `durability.rs:123-207,309-338`, `durability/binding.rs:7-35`, `durability/semantics.rs:10-48`.
- **Mechanism:** wire commands construct worker descriptors and work specifications with compiled production maxima. The authoritative aggregate may bind smaller limits. Worker registration rechecks capacity and retained-worker count but omits descriptor concurrency against the aggregate reservation limit. Work admission checks retention, queue, revision, capacity, dependency identities, parent and supporting worker, but omits the specification attempt ceiling and dependency count against aggregate limits. Typed `from_state` commands also accept an already constructed kind without rebinding those values. Reduction does not validate the complete successor; encoding and commit check schema, cross-record fences and actual byte sizes, not inert-state validity. Checkpoint decoding later constructs descriptors/specifications using the actual aggregate limits and rejects the persisted records.
- **Concrete source traces:** an aggregate with reservation limit 1 can accept a production-valid worker with concurrency 2 when capacity and remaining checks fit. An aggregate with attempt limit 1 can accept a production-valid work specification with maximum attempts 2. A dependency ceiling of 1 can similarly be bypassed by a specification containing 2 existing dependencies, when the other admission requirements fit. These accepted records can be stored, then fail checkpoint decoding on replay/restart. This is not a claim that resource dimensions escape global capacity checks.
- **Daily-driving effect:** a successful command can leave an aggregate that cannot reopen; the durability codec maps decode failure to Quarantine. 83b8d8ac-c814-584c-8481-9706d648f3ae.title: [L636] Filesystem result windows expose only the first 500 items and can still fail the canonical JSON ceiling
83b8d8ac-c814-584c-8481-9706d648f3ae.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L636.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-fs/src/render.rs:10-11,59-111,118-147,188-226,243-261`; `src/dispatcher.rs:273-309`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/limits.rs:20-55`; `src/schema/canonical.rs:81-90,209-231,239-289` in the protocol crate.

Oversized output becomes a generic protocol failure rather than an artifact or smaller recoverable page. Integer renderings saturate at i64::MAX rather than preserving larger exact u64 values.
- Consequence: Accepted read/traversal input can perform all its work and still return no usable result. Repeating the same request cannot expose item 501 or a too-large encoded file. Whether downstream model context includes the structured payload remains a composition question; the summary rendering alone does not contain file contents.
- Repair direction: Plan byte-sized pages against actual serialized limits, include a continuation/artifact digest, preserve exact numeric encodings, and verify downstream content delivery end to end. Source review only; no tests run.

84c5cd6b-7d43-52d8-afa6-be328e918d4d.description:
