85e210a8-121c-51fa-9839-84376eb34247.title: [L344] C6 index retrieval still scans and copies the whole view synchronously
85e210a8-121c-51fa-9839-84376eb34247.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L344.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-memory/src/index/types.rs:113-122,149-159`, `src/index/rebuild.rs:126-155,173-285`, `src/index/canonical.rs:17-50,281-286`, `src/retrieval/plan.rs:181-238,240-271,301-328`, `src/retrieval/output.rs:287-309`.
- Behavior: index rebuild cross-checks every tombstone against every input revision, scans tombstones for each latest record, clones each retained record, inserts posting groups through linear scans, and copies the entire canonical content/metadata into a new byte vector before hashing. Retrieval ignores those posting lists, scans the complete active view, insertion-sorts identities and ranks, and validates tombstones pairwise. These operations are synchronous and expose no cancellation/yield/paging contract.
- Consequence: growing memory causes repeated full-view work and potentially quadratic ordering/replay work despite the index abstraction. That can delay the host lane that calls it; it is a structural responsiveness concern, **not** a measured explanation of the live lockup. The fixed 4,096 cap bounds this implementation by rejecting larger inputs rather than making persistent growth resumable.
- Repair direction: incremental verified index maintenance, indexed candidate selection with global deterministic merging, streaming digests, and a cancellation-responsive host execution lane. Scope: full crate including tests read; no latency benchmark or installed-run reproduction during this audit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

868e3530-983d-5e90-9a4f-e9e43110bb66.title: [L823] Settings save can overwrite edits made while the request is unresolved
868e3530-983d-5e90-9a4f-e9e43110bb66.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L823.

- Evidence: `webui/src/lib/components/Settings.svelte:6-14`, `19-33`.
- Behavior: Saving disables only the Save button. Preference controls, view switching, import, and Reset remain active. A successful awaited response replaces ui.preferences, ui.config, and the editor source, even when newer edits were made during that request. Reset can submit another mutation while an earlier save remains unresolved. Import reads the whole selected file before gateway admission.

8691cf26-9cf5-5b18-af45-3e0a7b8542da.title: [L237] Connection capacity can be occupied by uncancellable hello reads or stalled serial writes
8691cf26-9cf5-5b18-af45-3e0a7b8542da.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L237.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/ipc/server.rs:41-65,79-106,122-127`; `session/connection.rs:40-46,119-131,163-204`; `ipc/frame.rs:64-104,141-153`; configured connection ceilings L202.
- The server retains a permit for each connection until run_connection returns, and pauses acceptance when all permits are held. Before entering its stop-aware action selector, each connection awaits its initial ClientHello read, authority establishment and ServerHello write without selecting the stop channel. An authenticated peer that keeps a partial/empty hello open can therefore retain a slot and prevent the server's final join from completing after stop.
- After negotiation, request handlers and event pumps are awaited serially. Complete frame write_all/flush also awaits without selecting stop or inbound control. A client that stops reading can hold this task in a write, preventing it from processing queued heartbeat replies, cancellation, or shutdown. Removing elapsed timers alone does not repair ownership or make cancellation observable during these waits.
- Frame reads **do** retain partial header/payload progress when cancelled; header-declared lengths are checked before allocation under the negotiated codec limit. Those integrity/allocation checks are separate from the lifecycle issue. The listener's **100 ms** retry delay prevents resource-error log spinning and is not a session timeout. **Server, connection, framing and cancellation tests fully read; no stalled-peer test run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

87566473-ee5e-59eb-a234-b7210b563793.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L111.

- `crates/tools/peritus-tool-router/src/router.rs:272-333` removes an active entry, invokes poll/control/cancel, and converts **any** `DispatchFailure` into a terminal result. It completes the replay record and does not return the active owner, even if the error came from a rejected control request rather than process termination.
- The shell maps C2 `CorrectRequest` (including a full 64-entry control queue, L092) to Failed/Execution/NewAction/Reauthorize (`peritus-tools-shell/src/execution/failure.rs:12-19`). Dropping the still-owned process initiates cancellation and join (L091). A transient backpressure error can therefore cancel the command and prevent further control of the original invocation.
- If normalization itself fails (for example invalid cross-epoch timing), the replay record is marked indeterminate and the active entry is also dropped. Explicit recovery likewise removes ownership on a lost/error observation (`router.rs:228-268`). Identity fences are necessary, but these failure paths do not preserve a recoverable owner or separate control rejection from terminal execution truth.

88547246-4934-5fa0-9026-6dd6c515276a.title: [L395] B2 acceptance refuses successful observations beyond the finite completion counters
88547246-4934-5fa0-9026-6dd6c515276a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L395.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-quality-policy/src/ordinal.rs:11-98`, `src/evaluator.rs:130-148`, `src/evaluator/gates.rs:173-189`, `src/evaluator/reviews.rs:192-205`, `src/decision.rs:90-122`, `tests/cases/completion_limits.rs:16-123`.
- Behavior: one-based gate attempts and review-cycle ordinals are positive u16 values. The evaluator copies mandatory contract maxima (L393) into the decision, rejects any current passing gate with attempt>max_gate_attempts, and rejects any current review with cycle_ordinal>max_review_cycles. Equality at the configured ceiling is accepted. Tests explicitly require passing attempt 3/failed acceptance at 4, and acceptable cycle 4/failed acceptance at 5; u16::MAX is the greatest representable ordinal and is tested as valid at a matching maximum.
- Consequence: work can execute and pass its actual success rule yet fail acceptance solely because a synthetic attempt/cycle counter is exceeded. Setting only wall timeout None does not change this result. This crate has no timer, persistence, lifecycle mutation, or context deletion; the pure failure can be reevaluated with another contract/evidence set. Existing orchestration consumers determine whether they convert it into an irreversible run state. Failed gate observations are already nonpassing independently of their ordinal; this additional limit check specifically rejects successful gate results.
- Repair direction: make execution-count budgets optional explicit policy, use wide checked sequence identity independently of budget enforcement, and support budget adjustment while retaining durable run/context identity and exact successful evidence. Keep actual gate predicates, reviewer independence, and authority checks. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

89ac30b7-4dbe-5cb2-ac96-e9f07c773738.title: [L479] Compatible streams can hide a known malformed suffix behind an already queued completion
89ac30b7-4dbe-5cb2-ac96-e9f07c773738.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L479.

- Behavior: a parsed chunk is processed synchronously and terminal events are queued immediately. A later data frame in that same parsed batch is rejected because terminal is already set, but the failure is appended after the queued completion. The owned stream returns the completion and permanently stops pulling at its first terminal event. A later network chunk is not read once the adapter is terminal either.
- Consequence: the adapter can already know about malformed data yet report successful completion to its caller. This is an ownership and terminal-publication error, not a missing timeout. The result also depends on where transport chunks divide frames. No live reproduction or test execution is claimed.
- Repair direction: define a consistent logical terminal boundary and validate already parsed input before publishing its one terminal outcome. Do not leave a known failure behind a terminal that prevents its delivery; do not wait indefinitely for transport EOF to finalize a legitimately completed response. Add chunk-partition regressions when repair is authorized.

89b69d04-c251-5ba8-add3-40cb22b9bfa3.description:

8a6b4892-b9a3-5917-8c25-7a44939b91cd.title: [L155] Public-reply compaction has fixed source/focus/replacement bounds and can reject a valid focus
8a6b4892-b9a3-5917-8c25-7a44939b91cd.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L155.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/control/compaction.rs:16-17,95-145,149-172,176-206,211-265`.
- **Limits/enforcement:** Focus and structural replacement each allow 1,024 bytes, while every replacement also adds a fixed source-identity/digest/size explanation and focus wrapper. A focus valid at the input limit cannot fit the replacement limit. Such a reply is silently skipped; if no replacement remains, compaction returns InvalidInput. At most 65,535 source/replacement entries are accepted. Each source passes a C6 graph configured with four nodes, 1 MiB content, two dependencies, and two visibility roles; oversize source content becomes generic InvalidInput rather than a size-specific diagnostic, though the PublicReplyReference constructor independently already restricts supported replies to 1 MiB (`control/reply.rs:29-30`). Tokens are estimated as ceil(bytes/4), with a minimum of one.
- **Failure/recovery:** Replacement must be strictly smaller than original, exact digest/bytes must match, and entries cannot duplicate invocations. These identity/conservation checks are necessary. Exact reply artifacts remain retained; compaction changes only the active prompt view and does not shrink whole durable history. There is no split-source compaction or accommodation for a maximal otherwise-valid focus here.
- **Classification:** Product-selected compaction bounds and misleading error behavior; no elapsed timer or deletion expiry. Source confirmed, not reproduced in this audit. Automatic/caller selection remains under review.

8b4e583f-bf33-592a-b224-867b8932cfea.title: [L785] Chat progress is gated by volatile pending lookups and a missing binding can detach the run
8b4e583f-bf33-592a-b224-867b8932cfea.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L785.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat.rs:1-299`, `model/chat/binding.rs:1-145`, and `model/chat/commands.rs:1-218`, completely read.
- Behavior: A pending chat query, open, binding, or product-message binding suppresses all `poll_chat` work, including the goal poll. Submission and model changes wait for volatile mutation/binding bookkeeping. The first send on an unchecked saved run performs a binding lookup and requires the user to send again. If a run remains selected without a durable workbench destination after that path, sending clears the run/binding and asks for another Enter to start a new conversation. Binding depends on negotiated `WorkbenchRunBinding`. Opening another workspace also blocks on an unsent draft; active mode changes require an explicit stop. Command dispatch closes the file panel before it validates the command and generally leaves goal-inspection mode for unrelated commands.
- Consequence: A slow/unresolved lookup can suppress visible progress even though daemon work continues. The detach/new-conversation fallback can make an unavailable original destination look like ephemeral session behavior; it does not recover the original native context. Mutation serialization and exact workspace routing protect authority and need durable reconciliation rather than deletion. The current live session's lockup was not reproduced by this source read.
- Repair direction: Separate independent observation streams, preserve the original durable run/destination through lookup failure, and expose reconciliation state with a retry that retains identity. Trace pending-request expiration and reconnect ownership in the runtime and receipt handlers.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Boolean evidence obscures timeout versus unsupported behavior. These are source findings, not observed macOS execution results.
- Repair direction: Make probe cancellation explicit and duration optional, preserve typed probe failures and cleanup ownership, and qualify the actual selected deny-default policy and enforcement path rather than replacing missing evidence with optimistic booleans.

8c17a952-879b-562a-85ef-1ccc4245129c.title: [L709] File selection cannot address any source beyond 64 MiB and has a narrower import-label gate
8c17a952-879b-562a-85ef-1ccc4245129c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L709.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/workbench/files.rs:15-16,47-56,86-103`; `src/workbench/files/preview.rs:20-33,60-67,85-100`; `src/workbench/files/import.rs:21-29,60-71,102-114`; `src/wire/workbench_files.rs:18-24,66-82,119-135` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Selected UTF-8 text is limited to 256 KiB; complete source metadata is limited to 64 MiB, byte-range end is limited to 64 MiB, and line-range last is capped at 64 million. Consequently an explicit small range cannot represent a source larger than 64 MiB through this metadata. Workspace path/label permits 4,096 bytes while import requires at most 1,024. Model identifiers are at most 512 bytes. Empty file transfers/selections are allowed. Whole selection identities/digests and provider revision are confirmation-bound; external imported labels are not reopened as paths.
- Consequence: Large logs/generated files cannot be attached even as a small explicitly selected range, and valid workspace descriptors can fail after switching to import. These are fixed product representation policies rather than measured provider or storage capacity.
- Repair direction: Separate complete-source metadata/addressability from chosen model-input chunk size; provide scalable ranged selection and consistent inert labels while retaining authority/digest fences. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

8d875ee7-3abd-50a9-b245-7cf4ad3a1c04.title: [L406] B3 acceptance/amendment decode hard-codes production limits inside caller-selected codec limits
8d875ee7-3abd-50a9-b245-7cf4ad3a1c04.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L406.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-protocol/src/acceptance/contract.rs:117-140`, `src/acceptance/contract.rs:182-187`, `src/acceptance/contract.rs:229-250`, `src/policy/amendment.rs:61-76`, `src/policy/amendment.rs:104-109`, `src/policy/amendment.rs:145-159`, `crates/foundation/peritus-codec/src/limits.rs:20-49` (complete reread).
- Behavior: callers can construct explicit CodecLimits with larger values. AcceptanceContractDto and PolicyAmendmentDto decode their content under the reader's limits, then clone and convert using CodecLimits::PRODUCTION instead of those reader limits. Digest verification reserializes the whole content using the production 16 MiB frame / 65,535 item / 1 MiB string / 64 nesting ceilings. Any inner codec or domain failure is collapsed to InvalidDomainValue. Constructors, explicit try_into_domain and encode paths can use the caller-supplied larger limits.
- Consequence: selecting larger outer limits cannot extend these two decode families past the inner production ceilings; a collection accepted by the outer reader can fail reserialization under 65,535. Raising configured limits alone can therefore leave recovery/round-trip failure, with its limit-specific cause hidden. 8d92aba1-52f9-5eae-ab95-5e7a382ae409.description:

8e276769-3073-5466-a46a-9e3735c95f27.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L454.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/wire/campaign.rs:279-281,318-330`, `src/wire/pointer.rs:299-301,338-350`, `src/wire/semantic/campaign.rs:9-10,75-77`, `src/wire/semantic/state/campaign.rs:13-62`, `src/wire/semantic/state/pointer.rs:14-42`, `src/durability/campaign.rs:34-48`, `src/durability/pointer.rs:33-47` in the same crate; production codec limits in L009.
- Behavior: Inner semantic codecs hard-code CodecLimits::PRODUCTION. Checkpoints serialize all retained manifests, diagnoses, evaluation metrics, attributions, assessments or pointer history into one byte vector; the outer frame writes that vector as a single bytes field. Its eight-MiB opaque-field limit applies even though the whole-message ceiling is sixteen MiB. F0 has no independent state-size configuration or incremental checkpoint representation.
- Consequence: Individually valid additions within every F0 collection/text bound can still make the next complete checkpoint uncommittable. Cancel/fail also serializes retained state, so it does not provide a general size-reduction path. Expanding an outer caller codec cannot lift the hard-coded inner contract. This is a source-derived scaling ceiling, not evidence that an evolution checkpoint reached it in the live run.
- Repair direction: Persist immutable evidence once by verified reference and checkpoint a paged projection. Reserve reliable control/settlement operations independently of aggregate evidence volume while preserving exact provenance and replay integrity. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

8eb0d3f4-dafe-5d18-9d43-843afe9ebb1a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L745.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/deliverable/commit/attempt.rs:14-82`; `src/product_run/deliverable/commit.rs:22-112,146-178`; `src/product_run/deliverable/commit/handoff.rs:9-67` in the same crate.
- Behavior: the saved attempt contains workspace path, selected-path digest, candidate-source digest and patch digest; its decoder caps the sidecar at 64 KiB. Before commits change nested HEADs, the patch and run projection are persisted. Retry can reconcile changed repository context when source/patch still match. Each Git effect then runs synchronously, with HEAD resolved after completion; no expected per-repository parent/commit identity or started-child receipt is stored by this helper. Handoff clears resume when rebinding a changed repository context.
- Consequence: source proof meaningfully avoids redoing unrelated content changes, but a crash in a nested commit or after a hook effect lacks an exact native operation outcome in this sidecar. Retry has to inspect current Git state; a matching saved patch does not prove which original commit completed. The sidecar size bound is a representation limit, not execution expiry.
- Repair direction: persist per-repository effect intent, expected parent/tree and exact resolved commit identity, with crash reconciliation before further commits. Retain saved patches, source fencing and explicit user authorization rather than restarting an ambiguous effect. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

- Behavior: `/compact` builds its request from the retained conversation snapshot; `refresh_compaction` clones that exact stored request. On compaction inspection failure, the error handler clears the preview but leaves both request and conversation snapshot. Automatic checkpoints can advance the aggregate revision without a UI mutation receipt. General pre-command snapshot refresh handles checkpoint/rewind/fork and selected session metadata actions, but not compaction. Therefore pressing refresh can repeatedly query the same obsolete revision until the operator separately refreshes the conversation. Context/queue pages have explicit revision and offset validation, while brief edits require exact inspected proposal identity. Compaction focus is limited to 1,024 bytes and brief text to 8,192 bytes.
- Consequence: This is a state-refresh loop rather than an elapsed-time failure. Exact revision/consent checks prevent applying an obsolete preview and must remain. Context inspection displays metadata and does not reconnect a provider window.
- Repair direction: On an obsolete preview request, obtain a fresh aggregate snapshot, rebuild a newly inspectable preview, and require confirmation of that new preview. Preserve the original draft and source intent; do not replay a previously consented mutation against changed contents.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

8fa987d2-fa99-5d19-a602-9d9620ea5045.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L090.

90f8e1d0-74b0-56a4-bcb4-a331b7e79779.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L121.

- `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/gates.rs:72-142` launches external gate commands with synchronous `std::process::Command::output()`, rather than the owned C2/C4 command runtime. 915063ba-9169-57e6-a863-8281e16d9fd0.title: [L096] Structured command/environment admission has fixed size and portability restrictions
915063ba-9169-57e6-a863-8281e16d9fd0.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L096.

- `command.rs:5-8,29-53` caps executable text at **4,096 bytes**, each argument at **64 KiB**, argument count at **4,096**, and complete argv at **2 MiB**. These are application constructor limits, separate from the operating system's actual argv/environment limits. Empty executable/NUL checks are format constraints.
- `environment.rs:7-10,132-189` caps allowlisted/final variable count at **1,024**, names at **255 bytes**, each value at **64 KiB**, and aggregate environment at **2 MiB**. Names must follow a portable ASCII identifier grammar. Names are folded to uppercase for collisions on every platform, so differently cased Unix environment names cannot coexist through this representation.
- Non-Unicode allowlisted ambient values reject the entire environment (`147-151`). A non-Unicode canonical working directory also rejects execution (`working_directory.rs:55-60`); these portability restrictions can block otherwise representable native Unix paths/environments.
- Backend name/version tokens have a **128-byte ASCII-token** limit (`plan.rs:22,357-363`). `plan_canonical.rs:241-249` adds u32 representation limits for lengths but no independent total canonical-byte ceiling. Exact target/revision, selected backend enforcement, and policy projection checks are authority/integrity constraints rather than elapsed cutoffs.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9231726b-e75a-533b-9589-5191ad65bd9f.title: [L514] Telemetry queues impose finite item counts and bounded shutdown flushing
9231726b-e75a-533b-9589-5191ad65bd9f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L514.

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/buffer/mod.rs:17-55`, `src/buffer/state.rs:105-186`, `src/export/pump.rs:83-139`, `src/export/types.rs`.
- Behavior: Capacity and batch size are mandatory positive counts, capacity cannot exceed 1,000,000 items, and overflow can reject newest or drop oldest. There is no spill path or wait for capacity. Enqueue constructs the encoded prefix before rejecting a new record. Capacity counts records, not their encoded bytes. Shutdown attempts at most the caller-selected batch count and returns Pending with queued records retained when that count is exhausted. Export and exporter shutdown are synchronous calls without a cancellation channel.
- Consequence: These controls can discard or reject observational records and can stall an exporter caller indefinitely. A large record still has large memory cost inside a small item-count queue. This crate's documented observational role does not establish that these controls themselves cancel agent work; that requires caller evidence. No telemetry session TTL is introduced here.
- Repair direction: Separate loss policy, memory accounting, durable spill and explicit drain progress from agent execution authority. A finite flush count must preserve an actionable continuation. Synchronous exporters need an ownership and cancellation contract rather than an assumed timer guarantee. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

923a1d06-1487-57dc-865b-41b702df255b.title: [L238] Shutdown acknowledgement precedes queue admission, and reporting delivery can block
923a1d06-1487-57dc-865b-41b702df255b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L238.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/session/request.rs:318-349`; `session.rs:14-35`; `session/connection.rs:132-148,234-254`.
- Shutdown response construction and socket write occur **before** try_send admits the shutdown command. If the shared shutdown queue is full or unavailable, the peer can receive ShutdownAccepted and then lose the connection without its command being admitted. Queue capacity and durable/idempotent admission need to be distinguished from accepted work; acknowledgement must reflect the actual admission boundary.
- Each shutdown command owns an **8-event reporting channel**. Delivery awaits send and ignores its returned error. Relay awaits each event and each socket write; it exits only after ShutdownComplete or reports closure-before-completion. A nonreading peer can stop relay consumption and leave reporting delivery waiting when the channel fills. Actual teardown event count and delivery call placement still need caller verification before claiming a production capacity overflow.
- **Request dispatch, reporting channel and relay fully read.** No new shutdown/backpressure test run, and no daemon process was changed during this audit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

93355f12-a324-578d-9a08-d3387f745450.title: [L220] Native executable discovery stops at a nonexecutable file instead of trying later PATH entries
93355f12-a324-578d-9a08-d3387f745450.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L220.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/runtime/executable.rs:18-28`; `crates/model/peritus-provider-anthropic/src/runtime/executable.rs:18-28`; canonical pin validation in L210.
- Discovery tests is_file, then immediately returns pin for the first candidate. If that regular file is not executable, canonical pinning rejects it and later PATH entries are never considered. A stale or nonexecutable file earlier on PATH can therefore block an otherwise installed native provider, and daemon component construction can then fail globally (L208).
- Windows candidates include cmd/bat launchers; compatibility with direct process spawning remains unverified. Immutable exact executable pinning is necessary, but selecting only the first regular candidate is a separate discovery policy. **Both complete discovery implementations read; no PATH fixture or Windows launcher test run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

93c008a9-6542-53b7-85b5-506a8e7cc03d.title: [L069] Artifact recovery fences the store on missing bytes or malformed layout
93c008a9-6542-53b7-85b5-506a8e7cc03d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L069.

- `recovery.rs:108-199` materializes the complete durable inventory, verifies each recorded object, and scans both digest trees. Missing recorded bytes abort recovery (`157,174,309-314`); noncanonical names, nonregular entries, or unexpected temporary-directory contents also abort it (`231-291`). These are integrity barriers rather than synthetic runtime deadlines.
- An uncataloged object left after publication is quarantined on the first recovery and removed on the next (`179-199`). Cataloged corruption is marked and contained; some duplicate/missing corruption layouts still terminate recovery (`203-216`). Startup callers and operator repair affordances remain pending.
- `finalize.rs:52-98` independently rejects an artifact read above its caller-selected maximum and allocates the complete accepted artifact in memory. `hash_file` uses a 16 KiB streaming buffer without a total-size/time cap (`128-154`); the buffer is not a limiter.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

94cc7111-187d-5de5-8e85-94727655bff3.title: [L088] Durable process registry can block launch at 16,384 unsettled records
94cc7111-187d-5de5-8e85-94727655bff3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L088.

- `peritus-process/src/consumption.rs:34-35,132-141,180-198` retains at most **16,384 execution records**, trying to retire to **15,360** on startup or capacity pressure. If enough records cannot retire, opening the store or consuming a new execution identity fails with recovery-required state.
- Retirement requires both `ownership_settled` and an exactly matching claim/manifest (`consumption/retention.rs:27-33`), sorted by age. Completed phase alone does not qualify. Retirement deletes the claim, spool, and manifest (`registry_storage.rs:203-223`); no tombstone is written by that helper. Unlike L082, this registry does have an automatic retirement path, but it removes this layer's old identity/result record. Higher-level ordinal/replay safeguards must be assessed independently.
- Consumption is persisted before process creation. A subsequent spawn failure cannot simply reuse the already-consumed identity. Quiescence scans all retained manifests and refuses unresolved ownership or live phases (`quiescence.rs:114-142`); these are ownership-integrity barriers rather than ordinary wall deadlines.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

5addca21-c6dd-4a70-b33b-5a8bd6219343.author: 6ME5
5addca21-c6dd-4a70-b33b-5a8bd6219343.content: #187 code implemented; final-phase verification is deferred as requested. Removed the 16,384 open/consume admission ceilings and 15,360 retirement threshold. Replaced lifetime in-memory maps with a private SQLite projection rebuilt record-by-record from authoritative files, bounded cache and 256-record query pages. Settled results retire only after complete artifact publication, into checksum-bound immutable claim+terminal tombstones published and synced before active manifest/spool deletion; legacy fixed-size consumption claims remain to prevent downgrade identity reuse. Terminal lookup and complete quiescence/reconciliation include tombstones. Added streaming reconcile_with plus the collecting compatibility API. Ambiguous manifest publication re-observes canonical disk state; derived projection errors rebuild under the same owner on next use, retaining the prior frontier until replacement validates. Quarantine preserves consumed filename identities as indeterminate records. Optional retirement or scratch cleanup failures do not impose a new admission ceiling; scratch indexes have kernel-owned leases and only abandoned indexes can be reclaimed. Underlying new SQLite/IO errors retain source provenance via the #189 ProcessError API. Source/diff review only: no tests, builds, lint, formatting or codegen runners invoked. Issue remains open. Residual: startup rebuild reads historical files and the compatibility reconcile report collects all results; these are not yet performance-qualified.

95144790-1dc4-55db-bc6d-2702aa0d3a54.title: [L517] The newest telemetry checkpoint can block recovery despite retained older checkpoints
95144790-1dc4-55db-bc6d-2702aa0d3a54.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L517.

- Evidence: `crates/observe/peritus-telemetry/src/storage.rs:20-21`, `src/storage.rs:105-109`, `src/storage.rs:151-224`, `src/storage.rs:318-362`, `tests/checkpoint_recovery.rs:171-189`.
- Behavior: The store selects the highest checkpoint filename sequence and decodes only that file. A corrupt or incorrectly bound newest file fails loading without trying a retained older checkpoint. V1 checkpoints are rejected; V2 is an exact 152-byte format. Retention must be positive. Opening the store cleans matching temporary files under a single-owner assumption. Persisted identical checkpoints can retry finalization; mismatched content at the same sequence is rejected.
- Consequence: Retaining older valid checkpoints does not supply a usable recovery fallback on the newest-file failure path. Format, binding and checksum checks are integrity requirements; removing those checks would not repair recoverability. Windows directory syncing is a no-op in this implementation, so the Unix durability path cannot certify Windows power-loss behavior.
- Repair direction: Preserve quarantine diagnostics for a bad newest checkpoint while selecting an older verified checkpoint and replaying the journal suffix. Make format migration and ownership explicit. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

951596fb-3a0f-5f56-9bf8-f3b775dd0da2.title: [L308] E0 cleanup consumes the same exhaustible budgets as normal work
951596fb-3a0f-5f56-9bf8-f3b775dd0da2.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L308.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/reducer/apply/directives.rs:15-42,45-94,143-163`; `src/reducer/apply.rs:15-21`; `src/reducer/apply/acceptance.rs:183-230,232-301,304-330`; `src/state/counters.rs:61-81`; `src/state/mutation.rs:180-203`; `src/reducer.rs:155-175`; `src/state/validation.rs:122-145`.
- **Blocker:** Publishing a fresh child-cancel, pause, or resume directive increments the immutable child-directive counter. Cancellation reconciliation increments both cancellation-reconciliation and retained-observation counters. Every control command also appends a used command ID; the complete state requires at most 65,535 IDs. No capacity is reserved for settlement or control operations.
- **Consequence:** At the directive ceiling, Cancel may commit but its needed CancelChildren publication fails. At the observation or cancellation-reconciliation ceiling, truthful child settlement cannot be admitted, so active children remain authoritative and Finalize cannot close the run. Reject/Fail/Exhaust cannot bypass reconciliation once Cancelling. At the command-history ceiling, even a zero-work control successor is rejected by final state validation. This is an accounting dead end, not proof that a child failed or that the user's task ended.
- **Repair direction:** Give cancellation and authoritative settlement an independent durable path that remains admissible under workload backpressure. Store lifetime receipts in a versioned history rather than a bounded in-state vector. Preserve truthful child outcomes instead of skipping reconciliation or introducing another timer.
- **Evidence scope:** Source-derived boundary behavior; no saturated aggregate was executed and no live lockup is attributed to this finding yet.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_control/compaction.rs:13,37-98,126-148`.

Once complete, it always retains the **two most recent eligible unpinned replies** in full, preserves all pinned replies, and only compacts older eligible sources that the existing prompt-view reducer can save. This controls user-visible public-reply compaction; it is separate from the developer loop's local-context compactor.
- Eligibility itself requires successfully loading/validating the complete conversation and capturing mandatory inputs. Compaction cannot bypass a failure at those earlier history/request ceilings. Original source replies remain durable, and the production input caller still charges their original sizes (L157).
- Generation increments are checked u64 and preview counts checked u32; owner/workspace/revision checks are authority fences rather than artificial lifetimes. **Complete source read; host execution_complete producer and a stalled-run example remain pending.**

97a70cb8-6c45-5023-abb2-a40faad23449.title: [L092] Bounded control admission and synchronous stdin can obstruct cancellation and observation
97a70cb8-6c45-5023-abb2-a40faad23449.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L092.

- The supervisor control queue holds **64 messages**. All controls, including cancellation, use nonblocking `try_send`; a full queue returns an input error with CorrectRequest recovery (`control.rs:221-235`). There is no separate cancellation reservation in this queue.
- The **16 MiB cumulative stdin** ceiling is enforced inside the owner thread, after individual writes have been accepted into the control queue (`supervisor/io.rs:147-169`). Exceeding the cumulative limit errors the tick and enters supervisor-failure cleanup; it is not merely a rejected write returned synchronously to the sender.
- `write_all` and `flush` run synchronously on the supervisor thread (`159`). A process that stops reading its input can block resource sampling, output draining, signals, and cancellation on that owner. Control/output drains also run until their queues are empty (`99-136,192-229`), with no fairness budget in these routines. Windows native terminal controls likewise lock a shared writer and synchronously write/flush resize or graceful-stop frames (`native/windows_channel.rs:93-101`), adding a helper-reader stall path. These are source-derived stall paths, not yet live reproductions.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

97d36902-0a99-500f-9c2a-df54f6301864.title: [L315] E0 can commit a valid large D2 terminal observation that its own decoder rejects
97d36902-0a99-500f-9c2a-df54f6301864.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L315.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-review/src/limits.rs:56-86`; `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/child/review.rs:219-308`; `src/canonical/wire/observation/quality.rs:41-77,98-124`; `src/reducer/apply/role_cycle.rs:164-217`; `src/state/validation.rs:38-98,242-303`; `src/verified.rs:82-95`; `src/durability.rs:69-87,190-213,376-381`; `src/wire/state.rs:302-311` (remaining paths in the orchestrator crate).
- **Blocker:** D2 permits up to 65,535 findings. Its checked E0 adapter copies every unconserved finding into the observation without a 1,024 cap. E0 observation writing uses the shared production collection limit (65,535), but `read_review` and `read_review_fixer` impose `MAX_ARTIFACT_REFERENCES` (1,024). E0 state validation checks the review's run/binding/revision but not that decoder-specific finding ceiling.
- **Consequence:** Given a valid terminal D2 NeedsHuman/Failed/Cancelled observation with 1,025 sorted unconserved findings, the typed E0 reducer can admit it with no fixer handoff, retain it, and the durability API can encode/commit its event and checkpoint if their byte budgets fit. Reload rejects the event's 1,025-item finding vector as corrupt and returns Codec/Quarantine. A transport caller that decodes the command first instead rejects legitimate D2 truth before admission. NeedsFix cannot simply omit the excess findings because the fixer handoff must conserve the exact set and separately caps it at artifact_references.
- **Repair direction:** Make domain admission, encoding and decoding share a versioned admissibility contract. Represent large finding sets through paged digest-bound evidence rather than converting an artifact input ceiling into a finding ceiling. Prove that every accepted durable successor is decodable under its stored binding, including terminal non-success and cancellation truth.
- **Evidence scope:** Source-derived conditional counterexample with exact count mismatch; no large D2 fixture or poisoned SQLite journal was executed. This is the same accepted-versus-reload structural defect seen in L296/L297/L301, not an attribution of the live session's current failure.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

97f16741-6b83-5a79-9e7d-f14725857aa3.title: [L431] E3 blocking stage effects cannot observe cancellation through the execution-port contract
97f16741-6b83-5a79-9e7d-f14725857aa3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L431.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/execution/port.rs:12-36,56-129,132-165`, `src/execution/directive.rs:12-28,137-147`, `src/execution/observation.rs:11-51,249-260` in the same crate.
- Behavior: execute_rollout probes cancellation before candidate execution and again before evaluator execution. Each port call is synchronous and receives a directive without the CancellationProbe or a cancellation token. No probe is made after evaluator return before constructing its verdict. Required trace completeness and optional teardown completeness are validated after effects; invalid observations return Quarantine. Failed-stage observations retain only a class/digest/retryable flag, not resources consumed before failure.
- Consequence: E3 itself cannot interrupt a stuck stage through this trait, regardless of durable cancellation becoming true during the call. An external adapter could independently observe cancellation, so an inevitable hang is not claimed. Post-effect validation can leave the wrapper without a returned complete rollout record despite completed work, and failed-attempt consumption is unavailable through this failure type. The downstream reducer only admits SettleRollout in Running, so a late ordinary verdict cannot legally override Cancelling; explicit cancellation settlement is required (aggregate/reducer.rs:274-305). The blocker is interruptibility and retained partial observations, not cancellation dominance.
- Repair direction: Give effect ownership an interruptible, resumable contract carrying cancellation and exact stage/continuation identity. Retain partial outcomes and failed-stage resource observations before reconciliation or retry. No tests run.

985793ef-2dd3-53bb-a027-1a5a325bb084.title: [L371] S2 qualification repeats full path and alternative scans without a resumable work boundary
985793ef-2dd3-53bb-a027-1a5a325bb084.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L371.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-obligations/src/qualification/verdict.rs:203-232`, `src/evidence/binding.rs:205-243`, `src/qualification/evaluation/alternatives.rs:74-123`, `src/qualification/evaluation/alternatives.rs:147-233`, `src/qualification/evaluation/alternatives.rs:236-323`, `src/canonical/encode.rs:10-24`, `src/canonical/encode.rs:216-270`.
- Behavior: each mandatory path calls a fresh linear search from the beginning of the observed path vector, even though both identity sets are canonical. A requirement with P mandatory/observed paths therefore has quadratic path-comparison work. Alternative group collection uses linear membership tests; each group traverses the complete ledger and each distinct evaluated branch traverses it again. Total group/branch identities are bounded by ledger entries, so these outer traversals can add quadratic ledger work, not an independently multiplied cubic bound. Complete ledger canonicalization allocates and copies all retained clause/schema/path bytes into one vector before hashing; the 1,024 vector capacity is an initial allocation, not a byte ceiling.
- Consequence: synchronous qualification and canonicalization can do substantial work on large admissible inputs without yielding or retaining a progress frontier. Binary condition/evidence lookups and the linear schema subset matcher are real exceptions. This is a source-derived resource/progress risk, not a measured stall, a timer, or proof that the installed product uses alternative requirements. The earlier product caller creates Hard requirements and normally at most sixteen disjoint full clauses under its source cap.
- Repair direction: merge canonical path sets with cursors, index group/branch membership once, and stream canonical hashing without a second full ledger allocation. Preserve exact qualification semantics and use resumable traversal where host responsiveness requires it. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9a4ce769-4830-5519-b3cd-db6511351401.description:

Whether retained terminal work can be retired, and how each bound rejects normal work, are being traced in the reducers. Representation and resource constraints must not be silently treated as elapsed deadlines or fixed by losing run identity. **Complete limits, binding and append-schema policy read; admission/retirement callers pending.**

9a4f02f0-817f-5776-b2a2-2af3f00e8c79.title: [L358] E1 revision history has lifetime count and whole-snapshot byte exhaustion without retirement
9a4f02f0-817f-5776-b2a2-2af3f00e8c79.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L358.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/domain/history.rs:31-100,108-157,160-188,292-318`, `src/domain/revision.rs:54-64,284-297`, `src/domain/limits.rs:25-36`.
- Behavior: history retains every complete immutable revision, including branches, in one vector. The 10,000-revision compiled ceiling rejects the next append. Every append also serializes a sorted snapshot of all revisions, each containing its complete graph, and rejects it above the configured state bound (16 MiB compiled). A rejected append pops only the new revision. There is no retirement, rollover, paging, or limits-amendment method in the fully read history API.
- Consequence: evolution can stop at a lifetime revision count or combined metadata size even when each revision is valid and current materialization is small. Restore clones every encoded revision and rebuilds history through append, repeatedly re-encoding all prior revisions; lineage lookups are linear, ancestor traversal repeats them, and branch-tip queries scan all revision pairs. These synchronous growth risks are source-grounded; no installed timing or new runtime reproduction is claimed. Traversal bounded by retained history length is an integrity termination bound, distinct from the arbitrary 10,000 history ceiling.
- Repair direction: persist content-addressed revision objects and indexed append segments while keeping exact predecessor/protected-asset/rollback evidence. Checkpoint a durable frontier rather than all complete graph descriptions; permit indefinite history without resetting lineage identity. Aggregate/checkpoint enforcement and recovery callers remain under review.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9ab968d5-1db1-5647-bf68-2c13b2c8dca8.title: [L455] F0 repeats whole-state and whole-store work synchronously during attribution, commit and recovery
9ab968d5-1db1-5647-bf68-2c13b2c8dca8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L455.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-evolution/src/attribution/engine.rs:123-142`, `src/campaign/reducer/transition.rs:61-63`, `src/campaign/state.rs:260-288`, `src/durability/replay.rs:79-116,127-161`, `src/wire/campaign.rs:170-199,279-281,318-321`, `src/wire/pointer.rs:178-213,299-301,338-341`, `src/runtime/publication.rs:53-83` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Each task prediction performs an existence scan and another task/k scan through the complete pass-at-k vector. Transitions clone all nested prior campaign evidence and rebuild the collection digest. Commit prevalidates state encoding, clones it into a frame and encodes it again. Recovery loads all events, applies each reducer during frame checking and again in the replay loop, then decodes and compares the complete checkpoint. Every publication obtains a global journal integrity export and scans its artifact references before admitting evidence. These synchronous functions offer no cancellation/progress cursor.
- Consequence: Task attribution can cost O(predictions times task/k observations), and campaign replay repeatedly copies growing embedded evidence. Pointer history bounds cap its hot state but do not make the event journal finite. These are source-derived latency and memory-pressure risks; no benchmark, active-session stall or wall timeout is attributed to F0 here.
- Repair direction: Index task/k observations, reference immutable evidence, perform each checked reduction once and verify paged snapshots with authenticated replay cursors. Preserve integrity while providing resumable bounded work and observable progress. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9bc059ac-5f53-5036-a353-9aff8277cd52.title: [L366] E1 public rollback reason bypasses validation and can produce an unreadable durable plan
9bc059ac-5f53-5036-a353-9aff8277cd52.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L366.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/materialization/plan_model.rs:43-94`, `src/materialization/planner.rs:103-120`, `src/materialization/plan_codec.rs:63-79`, `src/materialization/plan_codec.rs:101-107`; persistence path in L357/L361.
- Behavior: the rollback helper and decoder require a nonempty reason with no control characters and at most 1,024 bytes. The public enum exposes its raw String field. The planner accepts that enum without revalidation and computes a valid plan identity by encoding the supplied string under the larger production string bound. Thus a directly constructed rollback with 1,025 ordinary ASCII bytes, an empty string, or controls can be built and encoded but cannot be decoded. The aggregate admits the private checked plan without decoding it, and the commit path publishes encoded checkpoint/event bytes without a round-trip check.
- Consequence: successful in-memory construction does not guarantee restart readability. This is a source-derived public-API counterexample, not an executed reproduction or a claim about the installed user's current run. A rollback narrative cap is not an elapsed deadline.
- Repair direction: make validated rollback text an opaque value, validate at every public construction boundary, and make encoder/admission/decoder acceptance agree before durability. Store longer narratives by artifact reference rather than invalidating recovery. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9d981a10-11ec-559b-9ca1-436d75290836.title: [L502] MCP finite admission and response backpressure can block cancellation notifications
9d981a10-11ec-559b-9ca1-436d75290836.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L502.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-mcp/src/server.rs:31-62,130-143,189-263,268-281,549-560`; `src/bridge.rs:225-269` in the same crate.
- Behavior: production limits are 2 MiB per message, 32 in-flight requests, and 128 entries per page; limits must be positive. Saturated admission immediately returns an internal error instead of queuing work. Responses share a bounded queue of the same request count. The input loop awaits sends of initialization, parse, duplicate-id, and overload responses. A slow writer/full response queue stops this loop from reading cancellation notifications. List bridge methods have no cancellation argument; other operations rely entirely on bridge cooperation without a cancellation select.
- Consequence: overload, repeated invalid input, or output backpressure can remove the responsiveness promised by the server comment, and hung list calls cannot be cancelled through the bridge contract. Increasing counts or adding a timeout does not repair the control-plane dependency. Positive-only validation also fails to check the semaphore's representable maximum before constructing it.
- Repair direction: give control notifications independent progress under response backpressure, define cancellation for every admitted method, and make admission/rejection recoverable with validated resource bounds. No installed MCP-server incident or test execution is claimed.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/authority/owner.rs:48-69`; `owner/handle.rs:117-124`; `owner/runtime.rs:24-369`; `owner/error.rs`.
- The owner has one bounded queue (**1..65,536** capacity; caller default in L202). Every facade call awaits queue space, then a oneshot reply. Status, read-only transition, transfer cancellation, draining, and Stop have no separate reserved admission or service lane.
- The owner processes one message fully before receiving another. Journal queries, full replay/reconstruction, hashing, artifact I/O, and dispatch are synchronous within that Tokio task. A slow or stuck operation delays diagnostics and cancellation for every client and can starve ordinary runtime workers. No elapsed cutoff exists here, but removing timeouts alone cannot repair that progress dependency.
- Dropping the caller's reply receiver does not withdraw an accepted message: reply ignores send failure after completing the work. Recovery must preserve/resolve command identity after caller loss. Busy/Storage is labeled Retry; the owner sends that result and continues, without retrying it itself.
- Session mutation and prompt registration/answers require global mutation readiness. Prompt status/correlations and retirement operate on the in-memory broker; the closed owner message inventory contains no durable outstanding-prompt enumeration/republication command. This closes L259's owner-interface trace, while producer republication remains pending.
- **Complete owner and facade source read; no head-of-queue stall or live lockup reproduction performed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9dd8d031-464f-5b08-81bf-e1385182e030.title: [L512] Plugin discovery cardinality and whole-catalog failure can block unrelated extensions
9dd8d031-464f-5b08-81bf-e1385182e030.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L512.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/discovery.rs:30-37,141-179,187-227,238-259`; `src/trust.rs:73-86`; `src/host.rs:136-155` in the same crate.
- Behavior: production discovery permits 16 roots, 256 plugin versions, 256 KiB manifests, and 512 MiB artifacts. It collects and sorts every immediate directory entry before filtering plugins, then synchronously reads/parses each manifest and hashes each accepted artifact in 64 KiB chunks. A root I/O error, invalid manifest, duplicate identity/version, or 257th plugin returns an error for the entire catalog; no partial usable catalog is returned. The host keeps an immutable discovery snapshot. Start trust checks stored discovery digests rather than re-reading the artifact bytes before launch.
- Consequence: one unrelated invalid/excess plugin can prevent obtaining any catalog; entry-count pagination/cancellation is absent and large discovery work is synchronous. Cached discovery/trust does not establish the current bytes at dispatch. Exact trust verification itself is an integrity boundary, not an artificial deadline to delete.
- Repair direction: expose per-plugin diagnostics and a recoverable catalog, perform bounded incremental discovery with stable current artifact identity, and retain explicit trust admission while removing unrelated catalog-wide blockers. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

The pre-activation absence branch can overstate cleanup of independently prepared proxy/secrets; activated absence can strand cleanup classification. No synthetic TTL is needed for these persistence failures.
- Repair direction: Persist an exact reconstructible owner record with native birth identities, each outstanding cleanup obligation, and independently inspectable resource state; add adoption and continued supervision transitions distinct from termination-only classification.

9f40fada-dae8-5976-a476-a19dbffe79e4.title: [L522] Trace causal contracts require the exact latest event and classify missing predecessors as terminal integrity
9f40fada-dae8-5976-a476-a19dbffe79e4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L522.

9f65a261-fa8d-59e4-ba9d-2bc93175a98d.title: [L510] Plugin cancellation and deadline handling can hang before termination
9f65a261-fa8d-59e4-ba9d-2bc93175a98d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L510.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-host/src/transport.rs:91-162,165-219`; `src/host.rs:230-266,314-332` in the same crate.
- Behavior: exchange first awaits a single transaction mutex, writes/flushed the complete request, and only then starts the cancellable response-read timeout. Queue wait and input writes have no cancellation select. On cancellation/timeout it awaits another full cancellation-frame write before termination. If the plugin has stopped reading stdin or the pipe is full, that write can wait indefinitely. Stop uses the same transaction and write path, so its shutdown timeout does not cover acquiring the transaction or sending shutdown.
- Consequence: local cancellation can be blocked by a different invocation, large input, or the attempt to deliver cancellation itself. Nominal invocation/startup/shutdown deadlines cover only response reads and cannot guarantee cleanup. Removing synthetic deadlines must be paired with interruptible ownership/control progress, not a blind deletion of the only eventual response exit.
- Repair direction: make queue/write/read ownership cancellation-aware, reserve a control path that cannot depend on the stalled plugin consuming stdin, and proceed with explicit termination/reconciliation when cooperative notification cannot progress. No tests run or hang reproduction claimed.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9f74da89-5d8d-5595-bb7a-19cbacdd4285.title: [L332] D1 immutable gate planning and attempt ceilings terminate retryable work
9f74da89-5d8d-5595-bb7a-19cbacdd4285.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L332.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-gates/src/descriptor.rs:16-24,108-139,161-167,248-252`; `src/reducer/apply.rs:90-118,177-219`; `src/state.rs:227-264`; `src/command.rs:22-77` (remaining paths in the gates crate).
- **Limits:** At most 1,024 gates, 1,024 direct dependencies per gate and 1,024 evidence requirements per gate. The product of declared gate count and immutable per-gate maximum attempts must fit 65,535 before any attempt begins. Per-slot attempts are u16 and remain consumed after recovery. Plan/state bind the maximum; the command vocabulary has no allowance amendment, replenishment or continuation successor.
- **Blocker:** Even infrastructure failure with FreshAction permission becomes Failed once attempts reach the maximum. SafeToRetry recovery also becomes Failed at the maximum. Remaining dependent gates then become Blocked and finalization produces a non-pass. Large plans are rejected on worst-case attempt accounting even if actual work would use fewer attempts. This is a lifetime work quota, not an elapsed-time requirement.
- **Deadline distinction:** B2 and C4 timeout declarations must match exactly, but the current declaration is optional and plan hashing encodes None; D1 does not itself require a positive wall timeout. The installed caller's choices remain separate findings.
- **Repair direction:** Separate logical gate obligation and recovery authority from finite per-dispatch attempt/accounting representations. Continue safe, authorized infrastructure recovery with preserved gate identity and history; expose any deliberate operator stopping policy instead of silently exhausting an immutable counter.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete plan/state/command/reducer reads. The embedded descriptor test explicitly rejects two gates with 32,768 attempts each. Tests were not executed; no installed trigger was generated.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

9fa03809-149d-5858-ae50-38cfd4dacd39.title: [L496] OpenAI terminal queue can hide malformed suffixes and defer local cancellation
9fa03809-149d-5858-ae50-38cfd4dacd39.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L496.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/stream.rs:104-152,183-198,230-275`; `src/stream/decode.rs:11-64`; `src/stream/terminal.rs:50-80` in the same crate; the previously read provider-core owned stream terminal boundary.
- Behavior: an entire parsed SSE batch is decoded before queued normalized events are returned. A malformed frame after a completion in that batch appends `ResponseFailed` behind the queued completion. The owned stream stops at its first terminal event. Pending events are also popped before the underlying body is asked to observe cancellation.
- Consequence: an already discovered suffix contradiction can be invisible to consumers, depending on transport chunk boundaries. Buffered events can continue to be delivered after local cancellation. This repeats the terminal-publication boundary problem recorded for the other adapters; it is not an idle timeout.
- Repair direction: validate the batch before publishing completion, define one consistent policy for contradictory terminal suffixes, and apply cancellation at the event-delivery boundary. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

a0ad88c4-b932-5990-9a0d-3165f120234c.title: [L494] OpenAI exact-resume cursor does not restore stream assembly state
a0ad88c4-b932-5990-9a0d-3165f120234c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L494.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/client.rs:103-115,257-302`; `src/request.rs:1-221`; `src/stream.rs:47-73`; `src/stream/state.rs:38-85`; `src/stream/decode.rs:109-120`; `src/stream/output.rs:117-176,197-249`; `src/stream/terminal.rs:155-167` in the same crate.
- Behavior: resume admission requires an observed/restored response identifier and sequence, and the request sends `starting_after`. Every resulting stream nevertheless starts local sequence zero and an empty `ResponseState`: no started response identity, last provider sequence, item/part map, tool input, or accumulated text. Restoring a persisted continuation adds only its response identifier to the admission set. Selecting a model composes a new client with a new admission set.
- Consequence: suffix events for a previously started response cannot pass lifecycle, item, part, or terminal validation unless the provider replays all prerequisite state. Replaying creation into a fresh decoder also does not establish continuity with the prior normalized reducer. This is an exact-resume contract gap in the direct Responses adapter, not a demonstrated cause of the installed native Codex lockup.
- Repair direction: persist and restore the decoder/reducer state and sequence boundary together, or explicitly reconcile a provider snapshot before admitting suffix events. Model selection and client reconstruction must retain the durable response authority. Verify disconnects inside text, reasoning, and tool arguments through the production reducer. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

a22cb379-7700-5f2d-9b56-0dbaa343f428.title: [L246] One outstanding observation can suppress later polling; recent-list replacement can lose an older selection
a22cb379-7700-5f2d-9b56-0dbaa343f428.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L246.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/product/observation.rs:53-101,104-126,141-151`; `model/product/interaction.rs`; `model/product.rs:263-279`.
- If any ProductQuery or ProductExactQuery remains pending, polling returns before requesting fresh product observations or a product interaction snapshot. There is no elapsed expiry in this path. Removing a timer without a recoverable, correlated query lifecycle leaves a stalled response capable of suppressing the display indefinitely while the connection still appears live. Response routing and transport-disconnect recovery are documented separately; the actual lost-response condition has not been reproduced.
- A recent-list response replaces the entire runs vector and retains settlements only for that vector. An exactly queried older run is inserted at index zero and becomes selected when absent. The complete render/product root saturates the content scroll maximum at **u16::MAX (65535 rows)**; wrapped content beyond that offset is inaccessible through this scroll projection without a separate paging path. **Complete product root, observation, composer, resume and interaction files read; no behavioral test executed.**

a31cc400-cf17-5509-94a3-c4943c4e7809.title: [L858] Upgrades use disposable rollback state and lack a durable session handoff
a31cc400-cf17-5509-94a3-c4943c4e7809.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L858.

- Evidence: full `packaging/linux/Upgrade-Peritus.sh`, `packaging/macos/Upgrade-Peritus.sh`, `packaging/windows/Upgrade-Peritus.ps1`; `packaging/linux/Install-Peritus.sh:83-98`; `packaging/macos/Install-Peritus.sh:36-45`; `packaging/windows/Install-Peritus.ps1:90-108`; `packaging/linux/Uninstall-Peritus.sh:17-44`.
- Behavior: all upgrades copy package files into a temporary backup, invoke the installer, then delete the backup on success or rollback handling. Linux suppresses restore-copy failures and still deletes the backup; macOS removes the application tree before restoring; Windows's finally block deletes backup even when restoration throws. These scripts have no persistent transaction journal, startup recovery, or provider/native session handoff. POSIX installers atomically publish individual files but neither coordinate a multi-file version transaction nor stop the running daemon; Windows installation force-stops matching installed processes first. Linux uninstall coordinates only its registered systemd service, then removes package files.
- Consequence: interruption outside trap/exception handling can leave a mixed installed generation, and failed rollback can erase the retained recovery source. Successful POSIX replacement can coexist with an older running executable; Windows replacement can interrupt active sessions without a checkpoint handshake. User data preservation messages do not demonstrate preservation of native ownership or the provider context window.
- Repair direction: persist installation generation and rollback receipts until recovery is verified, and coordinate upgrades through an exact-instance durable checkpoint/reconnect protocol. Preserve backup on failed restoration and resume interrupted publication instead of relying on disposable scope cleanup. Source inspection only; no upgrade, uninstall, or restart executed.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

a4858e8c-5048-599a-8852-cb9f35a7dcbc.title: [L304] Collaboration finalization can wait forever on a delivery, and subtree cancellation refuses an already-terminal root
a4858e8c-5048-599a-8852-cb9f35a7dcbc.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L304.

- Finalize requires every retained task terminal and every retained message acknowledged. Cancellation/abandonment/task completion does not settle message delivery; the vocabulary has no failed-delivery, delivery withdrawal, reconciliation or retirement command. An unavailable receiver can therefore keep the aggregate nonterminal indefinitely despite all task execution ending.
- CancelTask rejects a Terminal target **before** traversing its descendants, paralleling scheduler L294. A failed/abandoned parent, or an AnyRequired parent that already succeeded while another child remains live, cannot be used as the cancellation subtree root. Descendants require separate owner/ancestor-authorized cancellation commands, which themselves require active owner acknowledgment to finish.
- Waiting for truthful termination is distinct from an artificial timer; the blocker is a missing durable outcome/recovery path for unavailable delivery and already-ended parent ownership. Repair should model those outcomes explicitly while preserving truthful success and cancellation identity. **Complete domain state and command paths read; effect/runtime receiver recovery remains a separate caller audit, with no live attribution.**

- Behavior: ProxyRecoveryRecord is an in-memory checksummed value. This crate has no record encode/decode or attach/reopen operation that restores a ManagedProxy from it. classify accepts an observed owner and caller-supplied listener/worker facts; it does not inspect the recorded listener port, current plan or routing token. Absent listener/zero workers is AbsentClean only if released was already recorded; otherwise it is Mismatched. Live handles own process-local threads, cancellation tokens, sockets and non-clone routing material and cancel/join on Drop.
- Consequence: A checksum and LiveOwned classification do not establish exact live reattachment. A crash before recording released does not become a proven clean completion through this classifier. Higher native recovery adapters may provide observation/reconciliation and must be read before claiming a live failure. There is no durable same-context recovery implementation here.
- Repair direction: Bind recovery to real observed runtime identities and durable intent/completion, with explicit absent/unknown/replacement handling. Keep socket ownership distinct from provider context identity. No tests run.

a6002d2f-f8b5-560a-af15-1892d5b7b42d.title: [L147] Retained repository recovery depends on exact local metadata and has no migration or cancellation here
a6002d2f-f8b5-560a-af15-1892d5b7b42d.description:

Retained manifests reject unknown fields, source-tree/index mismatch, invalid modes/object/path IDs, a path serving as both file and directory, and file parents. Linked recovery requires its original administrative database to remain accessible through ordinary directory ancestors; it does not independently relocate or duplicate that shared database. Unsupported Git metadata node types, non-UTF-8 names, missing backups, or replaced parents abort reconstruction.
- **Persistence/work behavior:** Entire ref and reflog root sets are pinned and fetched locally; fetch explicitly disables automatic GC. Complete metadata trees are retained except object directories and specified transient lock files. No count, byte, depth, expiry, or cancellation bound exists in these retention functions; 64-root fetch batches are not a total limit. Whole JSON manifests and most helper outputs are buffered. All this work is synchronous and can delay recovery without progress events at this layer.
- **Classification:** Exact-identity/integrity fences and synchronous recovery gaps, distinct from synthetic workload caps. Durable retained data should support compatible evolution and explicit conflict resolution; there is no version migration or alternate linked-database recovery in these files. Fully read `tests/retained.rs:225-241` establishes the narrow legacy behavior: a baseline missing the optional retained property can restore an existing child, while deleted-child recovery fails without an independent backup. a616b86b-1375-5e89-b288-ad9b05287f1d.title: [L240] Shared clients have no default request deadline, but idle requests have no heartbeat owner
a616b86b-1375-5e89-b288-ad9b05287f1d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L240.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-app-client/src/timeout.rs`; `connection.rs:34-48,108-122,143-153`; `request.rs:28-74`; `events.rs:22-79,82-104`; `frame.rs:33-59,95-115`; CLI adapter `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/client.rs`.
- The shared client accepts **Option<Duration>**, with **None = no timeout**. A supplied duration covers the full connect/negotiation or request/write/control exchange; this layer selects no synthetic default, and explicit zero is not rejected. Event reads deliberately have no request deadline. The CLI adapter forwards these settings unchanged; option selection still needs the CLI caller reads.
- Heartbeats are replied to only during an active request or when an event consumer explicitly reads and responds. There is no idle background heartbeat task. Retaining an otherwise unused shared request connection therefore cannot keep it alive under the server's fixed cutoff (L236); a later reuse can also meet queued superseded nonces. The TUI uses its own independent reader/writer client, so this is not proof of that TUI taking the shared-client idle path.
- Any interrupted/failed exchange invalidates the client, requiring replacement and reconciliation of the original operation receipt. Client frame reads use per-call local buffers, so cancelled reads cannot safely continue on that stream; daemon frame reads retain progress instead. Native model context and durable IPC session identities are independent of this stream replacement. Reconnect explicitly supports requesting the original active session and rejects a different returned session.
- Windows named-pipe connect is a single open attempt; pipe-busy retry is absent here. Nonzero random transport IDs have a **4-attempt** all-zero retry ceiling, an exceptional identity-source bound rather than a daily work budget. **All eight shared-client source files and CLI adapter fully read; inline tests not run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

a64e058b-295a-594e-9ebf-31df9aca04ef.title: [L786] Selection overlays consume control keys, and model updates clear intent before send success
a64e058b-295a-594e-9ebf-31df9aca04ef.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L786.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/navigation.rs:1-258`, `model/chat/doctor.rs:1-99`, `model/chat/picker.rs:1-34`, `model/chat/models.rs:1-305`, `model/chat/models/effort.rs:1-92`, `model/chat/working.rs:1-70`, `model/chat/catalog.rs:1-214`, and `model/chat/catalog/entries.rs:1-264`, all completely read.
- Behavior: Terminal-selection mode handles every key before chat control routing and consumes it until Esc/F2 or paste restores live mode; Ctrl-R and normal quit/cancel keys therefore do not reach their usual handlers while it owns input. Clipboard copying has one pending operation per selection. Doctor and model discovery deduplicate pending reads, with Esc removing their local request tracking. Manual model IDs bypass catalog membership explicitly; effort choice does not require discovery. Saving model/effort clears the command and closes pickers before `request` can fail to send; a no-run selection exists only in the current UI model. The working indicator resets by busy period/run and only reports elapsed observation time, with no deadline or stop condition.
- Consequence: An input-owner mode can resemble an unresponsive UI; its release is a local mode transition, not provider reconnection. An offline/failed model update requires reconstructing the cleared intent, and process restart loses unsent UI-only selection. The busy timer is not an artificial execution limiter. No live UI or tests were exercised in this audit.
- Repair direction: Make input ownership and release continuously visible, preserve exact model-update intent until durable acknowledgement, and reconcile it through reconnect. Keep explicit manual-ID/command boundaries and observer-only elapsed accounting.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.
