a8700e44-572b-5dfa-9d32-953167b3a6e8.title: [L541] Proxy redirect and HTTP restrictions turn some normal responses into connection failure
a8700e44-572b-5dfa-9d32-953167b3a6e8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L541.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/proxy/http.rs:84-144`, `src/proxy/http.rs:185-207`, `src/proxy/http.rs:260-264`, `src/redirect.rs:15-54`, `src/redirect.rs:81-99`, `src/proxy/redirect_worker.rs:13-30`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:91-118`.
- Behavior: HTTP requests must use uppercase-letter methods and HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1; every request Transfer-Encoding is rejected, including chunked bodies. Only plain-HTTP absolute targets, origin form or CONNECT are supported. Headers are UTF-8, names at most 128 bytes, rewritten heads at most 1 MiB. Redirect targets are at most 8,192 bytes and the counter is u8 with no unbounded mode. Despite its documentation mentioning HTTPS, RedirectTarget::parse accepts only http://. The proxy always attempts to process a 3xx Location; RedirectMode::Deny returns an error rather than forwarding that response. Following also rejects body-bearing requests and methods other than GET/HEAD.
- Consequence: Ordinary HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, disabled internal following or redirected uploads can surface as EOF/failed connection instead of a response the client can handle. Named/header/count ceilings add compatibility barriers. Removing request framing validation indiscriminately would undermine protocol integrity.
- Repair direction: Forward ordinary redirect responses when internal following is disabled or unsupported, and define supported streaming/framing behavior explicitly. Preserve destination reauthorization for any internally followed successor. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L200.

Dispatch ownership is retained through result consumption to prevent duplicate execution.

These deadlines are shutdown-specific, not automatic worker session expiration. **5 ms** polling is an observation cadence.
- A shutdown with terminal observations is Unclean until those observations are externally settled, even when no task remains. The inspected daemon caller records their count rather than settling them in this method. General worker admission/result-draining callers remain pending.
- **Both files fully read; no queue-pressure or abort-resistant task reproduction.** These constructors reject larger/unbounded operational choices regardless of host capacity.

aa184d88-4bb4-5115-a10c-94de3d7eb9a1.title: [L526] Git repository admission excludes filter-configured repositories and non-UTF-8 roots
aa184d88-4bb4-5115-a10c-94de3d7eb9a1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L526.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/repository.rs:25-53`, `src/repository.rs:164-185`, `src/repository.rs:251-280`, `src/repository.rs:327-346`, `src/command.rs:77-101`, `src/command.rs:171-195`, `src/name.rs:5-32`, `src/baseline.rs:11-12`, `src/baseline.rs:78-91`.
- Behavior: Discovery defaults to requiring the exact root; a caller can explicitly allow descendants. Canonical root/Git/common paths must be UTF-8 and are all bound into repository identity. Any configured filter.*.clean, smudge or process key is rejected before protected operations, even if no selected path uses that filter. Hooks, global/system configuration, prompting, signing and repository-selection environment are disabled. Worktree names are at most 96 bytes from an ASCII alphanumeric/dash/underscore alphabet, with leading dash and git/peritus reserved; revision expressions are nonempty, non-option-like, control-free and at most 1,024 bytes.
- Consequence: Ordinary repositories using Git LFS or other external filters in local configuration are unsupported rather than executed under a supervised filter contract. Non-UTF-8 filesystem roots and broader worktree names are unsupported. Identity and option-injection protections are necessary; disabling unrelated programs does not itself establish a recoverable route for affected repositories. Fixed author dates are reproducibility metadata, not execution deadlines.
- Repair direction: Make unsupported repository features explicit before admitting work, and supply a supervised compatible filter path when needed. Preserve exact-root/repository identity and argument/environment protections. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

aa2cfabe-fbce-5696-8388-42e738efc331.title: [L217] HTTP stream framing enforces nonwidenable 8 MiB frame and 16 MiB pending-buffer limits
aa2cfabe-fbce-5696-8388-42e738efc331.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L217.

Comments are exposed without canceling inference; no idle/elapsed deadline is present. **All three framing files fully read; no new frame-boundary/performance test run.**

aabc5a5e-4ee0-59c0-a068-9ce100f58a8b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L562.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox/src/reference/mod.rs:132-155`, `src/reference/mod.rs:222-230`, `src/reference/session.rs:317-357`, `src/observation.rs:127-138`, `src/refinement.rs:10-32`.
- Behavior: The reference backend defaults to 4,096 retained observations, clamps this to the finite terminal event budget, and reserves five lifecycle events. Optional events are dropped with a counter; there is no drain/retirement API. Sequence and drop counts saturate. The public teardown helper returns complete from the first termination occurring before the first release in slice order without validating plan/backend identities, disposition or sequence. Proofs establish scalar compilation/admission conjunctions rather than resource release or liveness.
- Consequence: Long-running diagnostic detail disappears despite continued execution. A supplied mixed or failed observation stream can be classified complete by the helper. The capacity reservation correctly avoids terminating reference work solely because optional observations fill up; it must not be reported as an execution event-count deadline.
- Repair direction: Stream or retire acknowledged diagnostic observations while preserving lifecycle receipts, and require consistent identity, successful outcomes and valid ordering for teardown evidence.

aae80fb2-8c33-558b-8cdf-d26345e75204.title: [L805] Web operation capacity can be consumed forever by already reconciled transport children
aae80fb2-8c33-558b-8cdf-d26345e75204.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L805.

- Behavior: the ledger admits at most 4,096 records when no completed record is removable; completed eviction follows BTreeMap identity order. Generic postcondition recovery returns a successful observation and stores the parent result, but does not complete its native transport record. Those unresolved children are hidden from the pending-operation list and are removed only by manual review, which returns early if the parent already has a result. File saves bypass the admission guard by directly inserting records.
- Consequence: recoveries can accumulate invisible unresolved children until new actions are refused. Completed receipt eviction also removes the persisted deduplication basis for a previously used operation identity. A file-save bypass can enlarge a fully unresolved ledger further. These are count-based synthetic admission and retention bounds, not timeouts. Source-derived; not reproduced against the installed gateway.
- Repair direction: atomically settle parent and transport disposition on proved recovery, retain durable identity tombstones independent of display history, and separate paging/storage policy from action admission.

ab185691-eff6-51a1-953c-0a02f83e2385.title: [L723] Instance admission can misreport filesystem failures and strand temporary publication files
ab185691-eff6-51a1-953c-0a02f83e2385.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L723.

- Behavior: every failed `try_lock` becomes AlreadyRunning. Instance publication uses a PID-named `create_new` temporary file; this path has no stale-temp reconciliation. Windows removes the previous instance record before renaming the successor, and its directory-sync helper is inert.
- Consequence: a filesystem/locking failure can look like a live competing daemon; a crash-left temporary file can reject publication when its PID is reused. Windows publication can lose the prior birth record across the remove/rename interval. These are source-derived failure conditions, not a diagnosis of the running instance.
- Repair direction: distinguish lock contention from other failures; reconcile temporary publication against exact ownership facts; make record replacement recoverable. Retain exclusive state-root ownership and native process-birth verification. No tests run.

ab829f7f-d97c-54cd-810a-0500850e2a33.title: [L808] Web consoles are process-local and counted even after the CLI exits
ab829f7f-d97c-54cd-810a-0500850e2a33.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L808.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/terminal.rs:29-131`; `src/state.rs:55-62,114-120`, `src/consoles.rs:19-88`, `src/api.rs:307-310,357-389` in that crate.
- Behavior: the gateway stores only in-memory PTY owners and refuses the 25th console even if existing children have ended. Output beyond 1 MiB is discarded with an explicit lost-offset flag, delivered in 64 KiB pages. CLI arguments cap at 128 and 32,768 bytes each; terminal input caps at 65,536 bytes and geometry at 10–400 columns/2–200 rows. Drop kills and waits for the direct child synchronously, with no owned persistent adopt record or joined reader thread.
- Consequence: gateway exit discards console identities and output and terminates CLI children on ordinary Drop; a restarted gateway starts with an empty map. Finished consoles consume capacity until explicitly closed. A blocked input write or child wait can hold an async handler or the consoles map lock indefinitely. Retaining a map entry during one gateway lifetime is not persistent session ownership.
- Repair direction: separate display subscriptions from durable process ownership, persist console binding/output offsets with explicit close disposition, and make child/group lifecycle and input waits observable and cancelable without expiration.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ac6e33c0-ed5d-51bc-b62e-391a08605491.title: [L536] Proxy cancellation can block on unsupervised host calls and header reads
ac6e33c0-ed5d-51bc-b62e-391a08605491.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L536.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/resolution.rs:29-46`, `src/credential.rs:292-299`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:41-48`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:142-160`, `src/proxy/http.rs:246-258`, `src/proxy/mod.rs:153-188`, `src/proxy/owner.rs:106-145`.
- Behavior: DNS resolution and credential acquisition are synchronous trait calls without cancellation. Request/response header readers perform one-byte blocking read_exact calls without observing the cancellation token. Shutdown and Drop cancel the token, then synchronously join the owner and its workers. Socket timeouts apply to individual calls, not a cancellation wakeup; header bytes arriving before each read timeout can keep parsing alive after owner cancellation. The owner's accept error returns through ? before its cancel/join/revoke epilogue, dropping worker join handles rather than resolving them.
- Consequence: Mandatory time values do not prove that shutdown can recover: blocked DNS/provider calls and continued header reads can hold joins. Increasing the timeout also increases the time before some workers notice cancellation. The early-error path violates the documented complete-owned-join contract in this layer; no live reproduction is claimed.
- Repair direction: Supervise cancellable host operations and owned socket shutdown, keep teardown on every exit path, and persist unresolved ownership instead of either detaching it or imposing another arbitrary deadline. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ade7fa93-45d3-531a-8929-f9f4c616c671.title: [L213] Claude marks transient capacity refusal as Never retry and derives resume from a pre-spawn marker
ade7fa93-45d3-531a-8929-f9f4c616c671.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L213.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-anthropic/src/runtime/provider/result.rs:25-34,80-96`; `runtime/provider.rs:165-220,355-381`; `runtime/provider/session.rs:13-88`.
- A decoded Claude Capacity failure is TransientProvider and DefinitelyNotAccepted, but the common failure constructor gives every certainty except MaybeAccepted **Retryability::Never**. Thus an explicitly classified transient refusal does not offer the safe-new-request retry used by the Codex capacity path. Underlying capacity decoder and host interpretation need caller closure before a live outcome claim.
- Claude durably allocates an exact **36-character UUID** before inference, initially uses --session-id and later --resume. Its invocation-started marker is synchronized **before transport.run**, and existence alone changes later attempts to --resume. A definitely-absent spawn failure can therefore select resume for an identity not yet accepted by the native runtime; there is no native-existence/launch-phase reconciliation in this module. Actual CLI treatment of an absent UUID remains unverified.
- Session output must be one complete JSON value with the exact top-level session_id before result normalization. A missing identity in an otherwise actionable error response causes an earlier generic session/configuration failure, potentially hiding the typed capacity/context/model error. Exact UUID matching protects isolation; marker interpretation and classification order are separate recovery issues.
- Production uses the same Tokio ProcessTransport, so L210's 16 MiB stdout/64 KiB stderr termination applies here too. Authentication is an untimed 64 KiB-output subprocess on every start. **All provider/session/result code and inline exact-session test fully read; no absent-UUID or transient-capacity reconnect run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ae63d2f3-5afb-566f-95c8-487ec2c7f331.title: [L527] Git status rejects complete observations at fixed counts, paths and parser boundaries
ae63d2f3-5afb-566f-95c8-487ec2c7f331.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L527.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-git/src/status.rs:14-16`, `src/status.rs:262-319`, `src/status/porcelain.rs:15-55`, `src/status/porcelain.rs:261-277`.
- Behavior: Status collects all untracked files and matching ignored paths, including submodule state. Parsing admits at most 100,000 entries, 64 MiB total and 4,096 bytes per path; the command's default 16 MiB output ceiling applies first. Paths must be UTF-8, control-free canonical relative forms. Any unsupported header/record, unborn HEAD or excessive entry/path rejects the entire observation with Quarantine guidance. Status then runs write-tree and maps every unsuccessful status of that command to absent index_tree without distinguishing conflicts from other failures.
- Consequence: A large or unusual working tree has no status pagination route and can become quarantine-class failure. A legal Git filename containing a newline or non-UTF-8 bytes can also block observation. Ignored content is deliberately visible, but inclusion consumes the same finite observation capacity. An unavailable index tree does not communicate its underlying cause.
- Repair direction: Preserve safe raw-path identity independently of presentation, stream status with an exact observation boundary, and distinguish representational/capacity failures from repository corruption and actual index conflicts. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

aec31127-eb85-52cd-b5d5-98c04851cd0c.title: [L384] B1 encoding a request after authority-time advancement disagrees with its semantic digest
aec31127-eb85-52cd-b5d5-98c04851cd0c.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L384.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/digest.rs:313-316`, `src/codec/request.rs:29-31`, `src/codec/request.rs:53-68`, `src/state/resolve_helpers.rs:66-104`, `src/state.rs:187-188`, `src/state/use_reducers.rs:129-130`, `src/state/lifecycle.rs:136-139`, `src/request.rs:295-299`, `tests/codec.rs:35-49`.
- Behavior: the semantic request digest's field 18 uses immutable `challenge_epoch`/`challenge_tick_millis`. The canonical request encoder instead writes `request.authority_time()` into field 18, hashes the complete frame, and rejects when that hash differs from the stored semantic digest. Successful resolution, consumption, or expiration advances `authority_time` while explicitly preserving original challenge fields and digest. Once that floor differs from the challenge, encoding this otherwise valid request fails with RequestDigestMismatch. The decoder also reconstructs challenge and current floor from the same single field.
- Consequence: this public codec cannot persist/round-trip ordinary advanced request state. A caller that serializes the successor request for checkpoint/reconnect can hit a persistence blocker after a valid transition. The source explains the failure without a byte/quota excess; merely raising limits would not repair it. Installed C0 may persist original request plus transition journal instead, so this finding does not claim every installed approval commit fails. The codec test read covers a newly created request only; no tests were executed.
- Repair direction: define immutable signed challenge facts and mutable aggregate clock state as separate canonical fields/records, sharing the exact signed preimage encoder. Version decoding to preserve both and verify round trips after resolution, consumption, expiry, and replay without changing the original signed request digest.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

aed29396-08dd-5166-9833-cee253793794.title: [L367] E1 planner can admit more file operations than its C1 executor permits
aed29396-08dd-5166-9833-cee253793794.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L367.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-harness/src/materialization/planner.rs:38-83`, `src/materialization/planner.rs:93-101`, `src/materialization/executor.rs:158-201`, `src/runtime/driver.rs:136-153`, `src/runtime/driver.rs:181-212`; C1 bounds in L006 and E1 component bounds in L355.
- Behavior: the planner installs every declaration in the new graph and adds a delete for each prior owned file absent from that graph. It checks nonempty operations, path collisions, and installed-byte total but not C1's 1,024-operation ceiling. Two valid revisions with 1,024 disjoint small-file target paths can therefore produce 2,048 operations while satisfying E1's graph and byte bounds. The plan can commit before `PatchSet::new` rejects it during execution. The runtime classifies this as `PatchRejected` and attempts durable failure settlement; it does not divide the plan into work units.
- Consequence: an admissible revision replacement can deterministically fail materialization because of a downstream synthetic batch ceiling. Normal durable failure settlement clears pending work when failure capacity is available; L360 describes the additional settlement blocker. No example was executed, and target ownership/security checks must remain intact.
- Repair direction: plan against the exact effect representation, or use resumable bounded patch batches with durable progress and a complete ownership frontier. Operation-count batching must not impose a lifetime ceiling on a valid revision change. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

aee826dc-47f2-5158-850f-9fdb56b7762e.title: [L503] MCP task completion and disconnect handling lack active-session reconciliation
aee826dc-47f2-5158-850f-9fdb56b7762e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L503.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-mcp/src/server.rs:130-177,180-265`.
- Behavior: request tasks are added to a JoinSet and joined only after the input loop ends; completed tasks accumulate throughout a long-lived connection. Clean EOF does not signal cancellation or abort active requests before waiting for every task. Writer failures are not selected alongside the input loop. A panicked request skips active-map removal, while task errors/panics are observed only after EOF. The server context/lifecycle is process-local and initialization is permitted exactly once.
- Consequence: a disconnected client can leave shutdown waiting indefinitely on bridge work, an idle reader can delay detection of a failed writer, and a panicked request can leave its identifier permanently classified active on the surviving connection. Long-lived sessions retain completed-task bookkeeping. These are ownership/reconciliation gaps; the absence of an arbitrary deadline is not itself the defect.
- Repair direction: reap completions while serving, react to writer/disconnect events, clean active identifiers through owned guards, and reconcile admitted work with durable daemon session authority before closing or reconnecting. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

af267399-0daf-50af-8828-4fe7a3d83ec4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L478.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-compatible/src/hosted_reasoning.rs:28-87`, `src/stream/chat.rs:246-253`, `src/stream/chat/hosted.rs:125-155`, `src/stream/responses_state.rs:103-121` in the same crate.

These operations are synchronous with no cancellation/progress cursor.

Limits checked only after appending/serialization do not bound intermediate work to the stated final ceiling. This is source-derived scaling, not a benchmark or proof of the installed lockup.
- Repair direction: maintain indexed reasoning identities and incremental canonical size/digest state, stream completion fragments, and make large retained-output traversal resumable under owned cancellation. No tests run.

afba0790-cc43-5bb1-be08-659f88ff1b4a.title: [L336] D1 pause freezes effect observations and its effect shell is synchronous
afba0790-cc43-5bb1-be08-659f88ff1b4a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L336.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-gates/src/reducer/apply.rs:26-37,55-59,121-133,246-278`; `src/engine.rs:160-179,231-287,294-315`.
- **Blocker:** A paused run cannot record a result, classify recovery or publish evidence; only resuming/cancelling permits those observations again. GateEngine also refuses pause/resume and other commands while a local dispatch permit exists, except BeginCancellation. execute consumes that permit and calls a synchronous executor while mutably borrowing the engine; that call itself has no asynchronous control/cancellation parameter.
- **Consequence:** Pause is an observation-admission barrier as well as a new-work barrier. A terminal arriving while paused must be retained by an external caller until resume; no durable pending-observation queue exists here. A slow executor blocks this engine call unless its adapter supplies independent process control. This establishes the API constraint, not that every installed adapter lacks such control.
- **Repair direction:** Separate permission to start new work from permission to durably settle owned effects. Keep typed incoming observations and control responsiveness available while logical progress is paused, without weakening exact identity and authority checks.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

b0da721c-0eca-5f94-9b57-1ac6c3e84d89.title: [L674] CLI artifact transfers lose resumable progress and output replacement has a destructive failure gap
b0da721c-0eca-5f94-9b57-1ac6c3e84d89.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L674.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/artifact.rs:54-91,112-198,211-258,278-319,322-378,381-385`; `src/args/artifact.rs:74-105` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Download/upload allocate fresh transfer identities; chunk offsets, ordinals, digests, temporary filenames, and request identities live only in the invocation. Disconnect exits without reconciling the transfer. Receive errors remove the partial file and ignore removal errors; no remote cancellation is attempted. A publication error instead leaves an unrecorded part file. Upload hashes the entire input, reopens it, sends each chunk under a fresh request identity, and checks size only afterward; server digest verification remains necessary. Default upload chunk size is 64 KiB, constrained by the negotiated chunk maximum; these are transport framing bounds, not work TTLs. Forced output publication removes the previous output before fallible rename; non-force existence-check/rename is not an atomic no-replace operation, and directory sync is absent.
- Consequence: The resumable protocol cannot resume this CLI invocation without a retained transfer receipt; interruption repeats I/O and may strand server state. A rename failure after forced deletion can lose the user's previous output. Integrity checks on bytes and digest should remain; the missing persistent transfer/publication state is the blocker. Source-derived, no failure injected.
- Repair direction: Persist transfer/source digest/offset/temp publication state, reconcile an exact transfer after reconnect, and publish with atomic platform-appropriate replace/no-replace plus directory durability. Preserve partial verified data through recoverable failures. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

b1189c10-82cc-5795-9ee3-cbe4b86cf940.title: [L320] D0's durability boundary cannot return even an immediate exact committed retry
b1189c10-82cc-5795-9ee3-cbe4b86cf940.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L320.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/runtime/durability.rs:131-192`; `src/runtime/driver.rs:253-264,345-377` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** commit_agent_transition checks the current head against the command's predecessor before passing the command identity to C0 append. After that exact transition has committed, the head is its successor, so repeating the same immutable command/event/checkpoint fails BindingMismatch before C0 can resolve its prior receipt. There is no committed-command lookup here.
- **Consequence:** A lost response after successful append cannot be repaired by exact retry at this API, even without intervening progress. drive_once additionally reconstructs a fresh command against its current state for the supplied identity; repeating an identity after advancing changes its content and conflicts with the journal's original command binding. Callers must reload and independently determine what committed, but the error does not return the historical result.
- **Repair direction:** Resolve exact command content and its committed historical receipt before current-head admission. Return both the immutable prior outcome and an explicit current-state frontier, without replaying effects or installing an old checkpoint over later progress.
- **Evidence scope:** Source-derived immediate-retry behavior; no ambiguous commit injected. This is stricter than the latest-checkpoint-only retry restrictions already recorded for scheduler, collaboration and E0.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

b1a46624-1e80-5549-8f6f-cb5e9331f5a3.title: [L643] Git observation and rendering ceilings have no continuation protocol
b1a46624-1e80-5549-8f6f-cb5e9331f5a3.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L643.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-git/src/schemas.rs:9-24`; `src/input.rs:8-60,125-137`; `src/render.rs:14-16,30-140,146-200`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/result.rs:327-351` and the production JSON limits recorded in L636.
- Behavior: Git diff accepts at most 100,000 entries and 8 MiB of patch; history accepts at most 1,024 commits. The renderer then keeps the first 500 items, at most 32 parents per commit, and only the first 48 KiB of patch, with truncation flags but no next cursor or patch byte-range request. Rendering also has to fit the independent production JSON and prepared-call output bounds. Model/human renderings are summaries; fuller detail is in structured output.
- Consequence: A caller cannot page through a selected large result using this API. Long paths, subjects, or many-parent history can fail shared JSON construction rather than yielding a retrievable partial result. This is a source-derived composition gap, not a measured installed-session timeout or proof about downstream context delivery.
- Repair direction: Make complete immutable observations retrievable by cursor or artifact, with bounded individual pages and consistent envelope accounting. Preserve truthful completeness metadata without requiring callers to repeat the same prefix.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

- Behavior: Before staging a candidate or restoring a snapshot, a synchronous recursive filesystem scan counts every entry, rejecting the 200,001st. It skips descent into the root .git metadata, but does not honor Git ignore rules for other directories. Any nested entry named .git is unsupported, including initialized submodules or nested worktrees. The scan has no resumable cursor, progress or cancellation hook.

An initialized submodule is observable through status but its nested .git file blocks candidate creation/restoration. These are fixed compatibility and count barriers, not elapsed deadlines. Restoration subsequently uses read-tree followed by clean -fdx, so its effect contract also includes removing ignored/untracked content from that exact managed worktree.
- Repair direction: Define candidate content and protected nested repository handling explicitly, and preserve progress for large scans. Avoid turning ignored file volume into a permanent snapshot barrier. Restoration needs a durable planned effect and reconciliation, rather than weakening repository ownership protection. No tests run.

b515fb47-ecfb-58d4-bd9b-52e5ec088565.title: [L297] State-size admission runs before adding the accepted command to history
b515fb47-ecfb-58d4-bd9b-52e5ec088565.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L297.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/reducer.rs:42-47,70-82`; `state.rs:308-321`; `state/mutation/cursor.rs:28-51`; `state/validation.rs:9-23`; `limits.rs:163-210`; `wire/state.rs:102-210`; `durability.rs:123-207,309-338`.
- **Mechanism:** each used command contributes 16 bytes to the state estimate. Ordinary reduction checks the estimate after applying the semantic change but before advancing the cursor, which appends another command. There is no subsequent estimate/inert validation before encoding and append. Reload checks the estimate including the newly appended command, so an admitted successor can exceed its immutable bound by 16 bytes and be rejected on restart even when its actual encoded frame fits. Genesis checks after its first command is present, making the ordinary-command ordering inconsistent with genesis.
- **Concrete source arithmetic:** positive state bound 1,040 is permitted. Empty genesis has estimated size 1,024 + 16 = 1,040. A fresh PauseScheduler checks that unchanged estimate, succeeds, then appends a second command, producing estimate 1,056. With a small capacity vector the actual encoded state remains below 1,040, so the separate actual-byte commit gate does not repair the error. The restart estimate gate rejects it. This arithmetic follows the complete source; no executable test was run in this audit.
- **Daily-driving effect:** any accepted transition close to a configured estimate boundary can turn into a restart-time quarantine, including control commands meant to manage existing work. The broader lifetime growth and conservative rejection issues remain recorded in L286/L289.
- **Ontological repair requirement:** validate the final post-cursor successor once, using the same durable invariant and size contract as reopening. Remove heuristic lifetime ceilings from control admission as part of the separately authorized limiter repair; merely increasing the bound preserves this inconsistency.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

b7a881a6-26c2-5920-a3f3-24527bbac51e.title: [L498] OpenAI optional metadata and whole error bodies can block response classification
b7a881a6-26c2-5920-a3f3-24527bbac51e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L498.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/client.rs:212-257`; `src/client/response.rs:12-27`; `src/client/cancel.rs:38-89`; `src/stream/metadata.rs:21-35,47-96,173-250` in the same crate.
- Behavior: rejected requests and cancellation replies are read to EOF under the fixed response byte bound before status handling. Optional request identifiers over 512 bytes, numeric/reset/retry headers over 64 bytes, invalid UTF-8, or inconsistent rate windows raise local errors. Retry parsing accepts integer milliseconds/seconds up to one day, ignores other formats, and the default 2 s retry policy can reject otherwise parsed delays. Reset parsing accepts integer unit groups up to seven days; unsupported fractional forms are ignored. Successful SSE responses can be rejected by optional metadata parsing before a stream is handed to the caller.
- Consequence: a stalled error body delays a known status until cancellation, while optional observations or Retry-After policy errors can displace the useful provider failure or accepted response. Reset and Retry-After values are metadata/retry policy, not local session expiry timers.
- Repair direction: publish the known status/acceptance first, consume diagnostics incrementally, and isolate optional metadata errors from response correctness while honoring provider backoff without an arbitrary 2 s ceiling. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

b7fef9f6-f82a-5231-9d04-e183e87f957a.title: [L327] D0's fresh-start API can discard an exact provider-resume prefix before admission succeeds
b7fef9f6-f82a-5231-9d04-e183e87f957a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L327.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/runtime/driver.rs:389-420,491-547,642-677`; `src/runtime/model.rs:105-146`; `src/reducer.rs:256-267,382-406`; `src/state.rs:223-267` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** start_model_once clears model_prefix before computing the request fingerprint or committing ModelRequestStarted. It does not reject a pending ExactResume retry. Pure model start preserves the old cursor for that retry, but this API constructs ModelSession::start with a fresh empty C5 reducer instead of rebuilding the durable prefix. The separate restore_model_once requires that prefix to be nonempty.
- **Consequence:** Fingerprint, reduction or journal failure in a fresh-start attempt can erase the process's retained exact-resume prefix while leaving durable state unchanged, making the intended restore API unavailable until the whole driver is reloaded. If the exact retry takes this fresh-start route successfully, the pure old cursor and fresh normalized reducer disagree about the stream frontier; a correct same-stream continuation is not reconstructed. The API boundary relies on callers choosing the right path despite accepting the wrong one.
- **Repair direction:** Encode fresh versus exact-resume admission in separate checked state/capability types, build the candidate session prefix before committing, and clear/replace runtime prefix only after the selected transition succeeds. Keep the same durable provider cursor and logical context across failures.
- **Evidence scope:** Source-derived API misuse and failure-path counterexamples; no provider or journal failure injected. The exact restore path itself explicitly handles unsupported provider restoration and validates returned continuation identity.

- **Additional fully read fixture evidence:** tests/runtime_driver.rs:361-507 performs exact recovery through restore_model_once with a retained prefix and fresh retry budget. It does not exercise accidental fresh-start admission or prefix preservation after failed commit. No test was executed.

Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L106.

Shell terminal rendering includes every published stream artifact's full byte size plus mandatory nonempty structured metadata (`execution/terminal.rs:29-76,79-163`).

Output close to that size may also fail because no metadata headroom is reserved. This is a source-confirmed cross-layer mismatch; a runtime reproduction has not been run during the read-only audit.
- This defeats the intended truncation policy: the process continues while dropping excess bytes (L090), and the shell explicitly permits a successful exit with truncated output (`execution/terminal.rs:175-263,339-347`). The result constructor nevertheless returns `shell-result-envelope` after execution/publication. `execution/failure.rs:59-68` classifies this as Failed/Protocol/Never/None. The router turns it into a terminal failed envelope, completes replay state, and removes the active execution (`peritus-tool-router/src/router.rs:272-333`); normalization carries neither structured output nor artifact references (`normalization.rs:27-42`). Product projection then exposes failed status, empty streams, null exit code and unknown disposition (`peritus-product-runner/src/developer_tools/command_runtime/result.rs:26-81`). Thus successful command completion becomes a failed tool observation without its published output references. Whole-run continuation after this observation remains under examination.

bb01e378-9d2a-52bd-a08a-16ca3ebbbc45.title: [L345] B1 requires immutable finite budgets and cannot replenish consumed capacity
bb01e378-9d2a-52bd-a08a-16ca3ebbbc45.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L345.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-budget/src/limits.rs:8-20,115-137`, `src/amounts.rs:57-81`, `src/command/vocabulary.rs:18-41`, `src/transition/allocation/begin.rs:34-61,145-223`, `src/transition/lifecycle/retry.rs:29-107,127-147`, `src/transition/lifecycle/seal.rs:67-79`, `src/transition/lifecycle/close.rs:67-125,157-160,232-259` (all paths under the same crate).
- Limits: every account has finite u64 limits for model tokens, provider cost microunits, accountable active-effect milliseconds, attempts and retries. Zero is immediately exhausted; there is no Unlimited, amendment, top-up, unseal, or reopen command. Every new Begin charges exactly one attempt; a new reservation for an already retained exact action/revision must charge one retry and wait for all prior matching attempts to become terminal. Consumed amounts remain inclusive at every ancestor. Closing a child returns only unused delegation, not consumption or charged attempts.
- Consequence: once a root or immutable child consumes a dimension, ordinary settlement cannot replenish that consumption. `InsufficientBudget` says AfterAccountingChange, but no accounting transition can restore already consumed capacity; unused reservations/delegations can be released. A sealed account cannot resume new work. Per-operation reservation size can also deny work before actual usage reaches the account limit. Exact old Begin/allocation replay is resolved before new-work phase checks, a useful distinction from the broken latest-head-only replay paths recorded earlier.
- Repair direction: distinguish descriptive accounting from explicitly requested spending/resource constraints; support unlimited logical execution and durable authorized budget amendments without replacing execution/context identity. Preserve actual costs and exactly-once accounting. Scope: B1 API confirmed; this effect-free crate does not schedule a wall-clock kill, and host defaults/installed bindings require caller evidence. No tests run.

- Test evidence update: `tests/adversarial.rs:147-160` explicitly treats a zero root ceiling as valid but rejects the first attempt; `tests/retry.rs:12-50` exhausts two attempts/one retry. Small fixture values are not installed defaults. Tests read, not run.

- Repair direction: Permit streaming omission and digest computation independently of whole-payload allocation, and check domain counts before allocating decoded collections. Preserve vault binding checks. No tests run.

bfe52a52-0c3d-5242-abd8-7ce230dfc107.title: [L697] Pure terminal attachment state has no saved-position restoration or replay admission
bfe52a52-0c3d-5242-abd8-7ce230dfc107.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L697.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/terminal/state.rs:31-60,84-133,161-237`; `src/terminal/messages.rs:8-44,145-191,260-311`; `src/terminal/verified.rs:7-37,39-83`; `src/verified/mod.rs:226-277` in the same crate.
- Behavior: TerminalState creates Attached at sequence/offset zero. Output must match the exact next position; replayed output is rejected. Detach/cancel retain exact idempotent facts and permanently end the attachment; subsequent output and exit are rejected. There is no restore/reattach constructor in this state module. Exit requires the exact output fence; the positive-signal check rejects Signal(0) but accepts negative i32 signals. Separate generic verified terminal predicates use last-sequence-plus-one accounting, while this implementation carries next-sequence accounting directly.
- Consequence: Keeping a native process alive does not suffice to reconnect its observer; retained position and attachment disposition must be reconstructed through another layer. The arithmetic proofs do not certify persistence or adoption. Negative signal acceptance is a classification defect, not an execution deadline.
- Repair direction: Persist and reconcile observer positions and explicit attachment outcomes, define replay semantics without weakening exact process bindings, and align exit-domain validation. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

c078bb71-37d1-526d-bcbe-cc0389eed0c2.title: [L755] Improvement backfill is whole-history work and its evaluation prompt still prescribes a bounded budget
c078bb71-37d1-526d-bcbe-cc0389eed0c2.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L755.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/improvements.rs:14-75,83-134`; `src/product_run/improvements/store.rs:178-222,260-280`; `src/product_run/improvements/evaluation.rs:13-44,98-181,188-240` in the same crate.
- Behavior: every inbox action first loads the entire existing inbox and scans every same-workspace run under run/store locks. Candidate reads allocate complete SQLite JSON before checking MAX_STATE_BYTES; every inbox reconstructs all candidates, including dismissed ones, with no page cursor. Evidence summaries are truncated to 4,096 bytes. SQLite uses a five-second busy timeout. Explicit evaluation serializes all launches, reads/parses the entire target Cargo.toml, queues each evidence source sequentially and ends its directive with 'Use the normal bounded run budget.'
- Consequence: growth increases synchronous collection/projection work and can hide detailed original failure evidence. The SQLite wait is a storage contention policy, not provider context lifetime, but its failure surfaces through a generic inbox internal error. The prompt retains a synthetic budget expectation even though current execution defaults may have removed that budget. Failure/cycle>=3 collection only suggests investigation; it does not stop work.
- Repair direction: page and incrementally backfill verified observations, retain complete source evidence references, expose cancellable contention recovery and remove obsolete budget instructions consistently with actual run policy. Keep evaluation explicitly authorized and untrusted observations inert. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

c2019885-ab0a-595f-8d57-591f57e8a081.title: [L740] Model discovery freshness can gate start and uses an independent cancellation token

A stalled discovery holds its slot until its future resolves or is dropped. Lost selection causes can obscure mixed-protocol metadata/capability failures. Interactive selections correctly disallow silent model failover.
- Repair direction: keep an explicit cancellable, resumable discovery operation and durable metadata revision; separate refresh pressure from admission of a previously verified selection. Preserve explicit model choice and detailed failure ownership. No tests run.

- Repair direction: derive native admission from explicit configured resource policy and account for the pending accept instance; expose pressure and recovery without discarding an authenticated resumable owner. Preserve principal authentication and native buffer validation. No tests run.

c37c52c7-744c-5a42-9152-ac7538593220.title: [L550] Credential-store availability probing hides causes and blocks synchronously
c37c52c7-744c-5a42-9152-ac7538593220.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L550.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-secrets/src/store.rs:60-80`, `src/store.rs:95-146`, `src/store.rs:151-160`, `src/store.rs:226-232`, `src/reference.rs:1-86`.
- Behavior: Platform-store operations perform a synchronous availability probe using `store_status().is_ok()` before access. Probe failures collapse to unavailable/retry instead of retaining locked or denied causes, even though later keyring errors have more specific recovery classifications. Lookup retrieves and hashes all returned bytes before material-size validation. References bind a resource/version digest, but the persistent namespace is configured outside the reference. A repeated remove of a missing entry reports missing rather than completed cleanup.
- Consequence: A locked store can be presented as retryable unavailability, and a blocked native probe has no cancellation path in this crate. Namespace drift and late size rejection can prevent otherwise authorized credential access. Version-digest and owner checks are integrity controls rather than synthetic session deadlines.
- Repair direction: Preserve native failure causes, make host calls cancellable, validate admitted sizes before expensive processing where the backend permits, persist the effective namespace binding, and reconcile already-completed removal explicitly.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

c443a582-368f-5293-b116-89ed5e305cb0.description:

c5c3ab46-97f1-52ef-a346-c27c6eaf1436.title: [L425] E2 analysis and validation repeatedly scan complete evidence before checking most output caps
c5c3ab46-97f1-52ef-a346-c27c6eaf1436.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L425.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-debugger/src/timeline/builder.rs:172-270`, `src/causal/analyzer.rs:112-138,223-345`, `src/causal/candidate.rs:116-164,255-311`, `src/clustering/fingerprint.rs:12-43,65-87`, `src/clustering/engine.rs:146-242`, `src/component/mapping.rs:120-228`, `src/report/validation.rs:159-325`, `src/report/canonical.rs:7-35`, `src/durability/replay.rs:73-126`, `src/wire/event.rs:55-71` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Timeline construction scans the full manifest for each subject and validates each citation through the manifest lookup. Analyzers construct/copy/validate every cause before final dedup/count checks; each diagnostic group copies all successful citations for that subject. Fingerprinting repeatedly looks up cited events and their causal predecessors. Agglomeration uses pairwise group comparison/removal. Component mapping repeats revision/declaration and successful-subject scans. Report validation revalidates the citations again and linearly finds each recommendation parent, then allocates the whole canonical report before the byte cap. Durable loading reduces each event in frame checking and again in loading; rebuild replays the prefix again.
- Consequence: The read functions have input-sized nested scans, repeated byte/citation copies, and late rejection despite positive compiled limits. With linear manifest lookup, a complete timeline alone can require quadratic lookup work in event count; recommendations can require quadratic claim comparisons. These synchronous APIs expose no cancellation/progress parameter. This is a performance/blocking risk inferred from source, not a benchmark or attribution of a live hang; model history/replay in this aggregate is separately limited to 32 attempts and does not have an unbounded attempt-history growth claim.
- Repair direction: Use verified indexes and incremental validation/canonical hashing, admit output capacity before allocation, and expose resumable work/progress/cancellation without discarding the analysis or model context. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

c734e806-1d34-5276-bd31-70a8d629f5df.title: [L539] Upstream credentials require expiry and use counts, but exhaustion is silently omitted
c734e806-1d34-5276-bd31-70a8d629f5df.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L539.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-network/src/credential.rs:103-183`, `src/credential.rs:250-272`, `src/credential.rs:301-317`, `src/proxy/worker.rs:142-160`.
- Behavior: CredentialLease requires positive uses and a nonzero wall-clock expiry, with no renewal or unlimited mode. It binds owner, plan, transport, port and host matcher and decrements before material acquisition or request encoding/write. The worker catches every consume error, including expiry/exhaustion/revocation/mismatch, and returns Ok(None), forwarding the request without the configured injection. Provider acquisition failure still consumes the use. Header names are at most 128 bytes and material at most 16 KiB, with injection-safe characters required.
- Consequence: An exhausted or expired proxy credential can appear to clients as an upstream authentication failure rather than the actionable ReacquireCredential error defined by the lease. Failed acquisition can exhaust all uses before any successful authenticated request. These leases are credential authority, not provider context/session TTL; their expiry must not be casually equated with context deletion.
- Repair direction: Make optional versus required credential injection explicit, propagate reacquisition state and retain exact pending use resolution. Keep host/owner/plan and header-injection protections. Define intentional authority renewal independently of synthetic transport lifetime. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ca474a45-8ae6-5e77-bc26-70a3d2a619cf.title: [L234] A rolled-back migration can require operator restore, after which daemon retry reuses a forbidden identity
ca474a45-8ae6-5e77-bc26-70a3d2a619cf.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L234.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-migrations/src/engine/apply.rs:24-47`; `src/engine.rs:235-249,273-298,319-330`; `src/engine/restart.rs:28-67,80-116`; `src/catalog.rs:155-193,268-299`; `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/startup/migration.rs:27-58`.
- Every BeforeCommit failure on a backup-required plan becomes **RestoreRequired**, including failure to acquire the exclusive SQLite transaction before any migration SQL executes. Restart also maps Applying with the original schema version to RestoreBackup when backup was required. The daemon refuses to start until explicit operator restoration, although some of these cases represent no accepted schema effect or a rolled-back transaction.
- After successful restore, the engine records **Restored**, excludes it from pending reconciliation, and rejects apply with that operation ID with “a new identity” required. The daemon always derives its migration operation ID from the same compiled registry digest. On the next startup with the restored old schema, it plans the same migration with the same ID and hits that rejection. This is a source-proven recovery dead end for that production path; the restore test stops after checking the restored version and does not exercise daemon restart/retry.
- The API's Applied/idempotent return is also preceded by validate_plan requiring the old source version to equal the now-current schema, so reusing the original successful plan fails before reaching Applied. Replanning to the target changes from-version/backup policy and fails exact operation-plan reuse. Daemon normal current-schema startup skips apply, so that API defect is not itself evidence of every ordinary restart failing.
- Pending operations are loaded as a whole vector; one malformed retained pending row fails the entire recovery scan. Exact registry/backup digest and accepted-effect reconciliation are necessary, but known nonacceptance, rolled-back work and restored attempts need distinct resumable states and stable lineage with a new attempt identity. **Entire recovery/catalog/apply sources and fault tests read; no tests executed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

cccb9c35-3cf9-51cb-993a-e24360586ca1.title: [L228] Recovery layers use incompatible retry classifications and can discard provider delay/acceptance facts
cccb9c35-3cf9-51cb-993a-e24360586ca1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L228.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/recovery.rs:71-100,105-165`; `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/developer/retry.rs:61-80,92-109,129-157`; `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/failover.rs:12-30,168-193`; protocol `retry.rs:124-178`.
- The developer in-turn planner selects no elapsed horizon but has a fixed **30-second maximum delay**, and refuses Retry-After above that value. It admits both SafeNewRequest **and CallerDecision** as SafeNewRequest; generic Transport/MalformedStream core errors also become SafeNewRequest without acceptance-phase facts in that decision. The pure protocol planner itself protects ambiguous/partial submissions when those causes are supplied; relabeling them bypasses that distinction. Native tools are disabled, but provider cost and duplicated inference remain effects needing exact reconciliation.
- Native Claude capacity failure is Never in the in-turn path (L213), so no in-turn retry occurs. The outer role loop separately permits TransientProvider by category and can make **three role invocations** (L051), before considering authorized fallbacks. Thus Never here does not mean immediate global stop. The outer error representation/recovery classification does not preserve the same certainty/retryability/delay decision; layered policies can disagree or restart promptly after the inner delay bound stopped recovery.
- The shared ProviderTerminal classifier has yet another disposition table: capacity/transient means authorized fallback, malformed/incomplete means same-route retry, and fixed diagnostic substrings for capacity/overloaded/context take precedence over category. That helper alone does not establish the production developer path's behavior; its callers remain pending. Finite retry ceilings are distinct from necessary refusal to duplicate ambiguously accepted work.

Its changed paths cannot satisfy product coverage through this planner unless a separate recognized/explicit contract exists. Treating code as a generic artifact merely to bypass the missing build contract would lose the intended validation. Removal of the nearest manifest can also change discovery rather than reconstructing its historical contract.
- **Repair direction:** Admit host-owned, explicit project contracts and supported toolchain adapters independent of naming heuristics. Preserve complete candidate coverage while representing unavailable discovery as recoverable configuration work rather than another code-fixing loop.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete production planner/commands/report and all planner tests read. Existing fixtures exercise the recognized families; no CMake or other unsupported-family fixture was run.

d056ad9c-597a-52c8-976e-031fe6f23b75.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L165.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/developer_tools/receipt.rs:21-23,181-221`; `receipt/storage.rs:44-88,96-105`.
- The ledger rejects a serialized record above **2 MiB** and refuses appends that would take the entire journal above **128 MiB**. Applied and Completed records each retain the complete result, so successful effects consume result storage twice. The encoded envelope consumes part of the 2 MiB allowance; a tool result at that size cannot fit a receipt at the same ceiling.
- Starting a new effect requires appending Started first. Applied and Completed persistence can fail after execution. The ceiling therefore affects both admission and recording already performed work, including command-control tools routed through the ledger. Out-of-band control paths remain to be traced; this does not establish that every cancellation mechanism is blocked.
- Loading allocates the entire file before checking its 128 MiB size. There is no compaction, retirement, segmented storage, or configurable lifetime allowance in these files. **Source-confirmed; live journal size and full caller recovery remain unverified.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

d18d347b-81e5-527f-b124-3e4b9778b9ae.title: [L685] Exact command retries require original request and correlation identities, which a fresh CLI invocation cannot supply
d18d347b-81e5-527f-b124-3e4b9778b9ae.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L685.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/command/binding.rs:138-190,236-269`; `src/command/idempotency.rs:114-135,146-172`; `src/command/result.rs:99-105,148-165` in that crate; `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/operation.rs:190-205`; `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/id.rs:37-53`.
- Behavior: Command digest includes actor, durable session, application request ID, correlation ID, idempotency key, expected revision, and exact frame bytes. Matching session/actor/key with a different digest is a conflict. A new CLI invocation generates fresh request/correlation identities even if the user supplies identical command files, session, and idempotency key; its grammar offers no original request/correlation option. Result replay preserves the original request ID; this result is explicitly not a durable C0 receipt.
- Consequence: Repeating the same visible CLI command after an uncertain reply cannot perform exact replay through this binding. Preserving only session and key is insufficient. The binding protects effect integrity, but lack of a durable complete request receipt makes the protection a practical reconnect blocker.
- Repair direction: Retain and reopen the full original bound request/operation identity, then reconcile/replay its final receipt. Separate durable operation identity from transient connection correlation if the revised contract deliberately permits that, without weakening duplicate-effect protection. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Systemic repair plan for L004: Checkpoint coverage omits partial selections and empty directories.

Owning contract and implementation boundary: capture.rs:30-50; checkpoints.rs:42-45. Apply the change through the constructors, live callers, durable writer and restart reader for this boundary, not as an isolated constant increase.

Make checkpoint coverage a typed capability manifest: whole files, selected ranges, absent paths and empty directories have distinct restore operations. Record what is covered and why anything is excluded before promising a writable fork. Restore directory identity and range preimages through the same transaction and conflict rules as files; keep credentials, approvals and external effects outside workspace rewind.

Preserve: exact snapshot/preimage identity, protected paths, ancestor and symlink safety, writable-fork coverage, conflict detection, one logical restore transaction and exact effect receipts. Separate a physical allocation/page limit and a genuine authority or integrity check from a cumulative work allowance. Keep transient contention/capacity observable and recoverable under the existing logical task; do not discard accepted state or substitute a fresh session to get around it.

Compatibility/migration: retain decoders and exact receipts for previously accepted records. If representation or lifecycle semantics change, introduce a versioned migration under exclusive ownership; verify a complete replacement frontier before atomic publication and keep the old recovery root until adoption is durable. Rebuild derived projections from authoritative evidence. Update all producers, consumers and invariants together; a rejected new operation must leave the predecessor usable and already owned effects reconcilable.

Acceptance and nonregression: large-file and many-path capture/restore, divergent preimage rejection, interrupted staging/publication/restore, then reopen and continue the same conversation with an exact restored workspace. Exercise the precise source-described failure path and the relevant byte/count/elapsed boundaries listed in this finding, plus ordinary small inputs. Check that legitimate work progresses after the former blocker while malformed input, conflicting identity, stale preimages and unauthorized scope still reject. Add fault injection at the affected acceptance/publication/recovery boundary and run the affected integration and formal checks on the final implementation. Source-derived risks remain distinct from executed reproductions; completion requires this evidence, not a promise that a plan alone cannot break anything.

d263553e-294b-5dff-a6f0-289a230790e7.title: [L280] Partial artifact transfer progress is ephemeral even though ownership and publication identity are durable
d263553e-294b-5dff-a6f0-289a230790e7.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L280.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/artifact/service.rs:33-57,167-183,204-241,293-332`; `artifact/publication.rs`; `artifact/service/scoped.rs`; disconnect cleanup in L236.
- Active reader/writer/ordinal/offset state lives only in the authority's BTreeMap. Cancel/abandon/disconnect or daemon restart drops it. The exact scoped claim and artifact catalog remain durable, but this service has no offset-based restart/resume API; recovery begins a new transfer and sends/verifies all bytes again.
- complete_upload checks foreign ownership first, then removes the owned transfer **before** validating completion metadata, committing acceptance, finalizing the content object, and publishing catalog availability. Any later error loses that transfer's in-memory writer/progress and can leave intermediate durable facts. d2da3470-e795-5abc-b7d5-14f0290b75ab.description:

d3d14313-5879-58eb-9428-6fc375073044.title: [L486] Google gateway routing accepts an Interactions configuration that loses its gateway prefix, and discovery uses beta despite stable-only documentation
d3d14313-5879-58eb-9428-6fc375073044.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L486.

- Evidence: `crates/model/peritus-provider-google/src/config.rs:57-78`, `src/request.rs:67-75`, `src/client.rs:205-231`, `src/client_tests.rs:176-211`, `README.md:3-12`; `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/endpoint.rs:76-89`, `src/catalog/http.rs:12-14`, `src/catalog/http.rs:61-149`.
- Behavior: the gateway constructor accepts either Google dialect at the two exact OpenCode prefixes. Generate concatenates that prefix, while Interactions calls with_path, which replaces it with /v1/interactions. Only Generate gateway routing is tested. Discovery calls /v1beta/models?pageSize=1000 despite the README saying beta is never used. Shared discovery paginates but fails the whole inventory above 16 pages, 4 MiB per page, 16 MiB total or the catalog entry bound; it exposes no resumable partial inventory.

d44d5207-b2e1-51c5-afda-0369422ee4d5.title: [L675] CLI terminal stdin buffers until EOF and terminal following has no reconnect state
d44d5207-b2e1-51c5-afda-0369422ee4d5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L675.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/terminal.rs:21-82,83-159,162-198,210-236,239-250,353-360`; `src/output.rs:35-47,74-110` in the same crate.
- Behavior: File terminal input streams negotiated chunks, but stdin is read to EOF into one unbounded Vec in a blocking task before any bytes are transmitted. An open stdin producer therefore prevents initial input indefinitely. Output follow stores stream state only in memory and exits on disconnect, unavailable output, or sequence validation failure. Ctrl-C exits without issuing an explicit detach/cancel. Attachment IDs are printed, but there is no cursor resume command or durable receipt here. A single sanitizer spans all streams, removes control strings until their terminator, and decodes each safe chunk lossily; split UTF8 and an unterminated control string can distort/suppress human output. Resize accepts the full u16 range even where native backends later narrow dimensions.
- Consequence: Input can appear frozen despite no execution deadline, and a live process cannot automatically restore its original output observation after connection loss through this CLI path. It correctly warns that unavailable output does not prove termination. Native ownership recovery and output replay must be established separately.
- Repair direction: Stream stdin in bounded chunks while serving heartbeat/cancel control, retain attachment/offset/sequence receipts, and reconnect against an authoritative stream disposition. Preserve incremental UTF8 and independent stream sanitizer state. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

d6317395-0c32-52c7-bc70-949291777461.title: [L107] Shell finalization consumes recovery ownership before fallible result construction
d6317395-0c32-52c7-bc70-949291777461.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L107.

- `crates/tools/peritus-tools-shell/src/execution/active.rs:123-144` takes the owned process out of the active invocation before waiting for publication and building the terminal tool result. If result construction fails (including L106), the execution has neither its owner nor a stored terminal result.
- A subsequent poll sees the underlying terminal state and attempts finalization again, which fails with `shell-owner-missing`. The adapter's `recover` path only polls this same object (`active.rs:203-213`); it does not reconstruct the result or adopt the process. This blocks recovery within this execution object after an envelope failure. In ordinary router polling, the first error is normalized to a terminal failed result and the execution object is dropped (L106), so the second finalization is not normally reached. Router recovery instead marks the outcome indeterminate and removes the active owner (`router.rs:228-268`). Higher-level durable recovery remains under examination.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Detached foreground observation transfers an exact deduplicated reconciliation obligation; background completion persists a deferred authoritative reconnect projection before publishing replay, without fabricated stdout/stderr or full artifact rerendering. Foreground materializes the exact retained artifact references. Projection writes are serialized and cannot downgrade a materialized completed projection. Persistent postimages/checksums use .crosslink/code-batch-recovery/issue206-retained-settlement.postimage.*. No runners or test edits; this is source review, not compiled/runtime verification. 7b1ef59a-6ee0-4a23-bd78-5a7f25764ac2.content:
Systemic repair plan for L107: Shell finalization consumes recovery ownership before fallible result construction.

Owning contract and implementation boundary: crates/tools/peritus-tools-shell/src/execution/active.rs:123-144; active.rs:203-213; router.rs:228-268. Apply the change through the constructors, live callers, durable writer and restart reader for this boundary, not as an isolated constant increase.

Persist terminal process evidence and publication receipts before consuming active ownership. Make result construction an idempotent projection from that evidence, retaining the owner or reconciliation obligation until all fallible settlement steps complete. A rendering failure must be retryable without polling a missing owner or losing the original successful process outcome.

Preserve: exact process birth/tree identity, confined authority, one-use dispatch receipts, monotonic cancel intent, truthful terminal/ownership settlement, complete output accounting and platform OS constraints. Separate a physical allocation/page limit and a genuine authority or integrity check from a cumulative work allowance. Keep transient contention/capacity observable and recoverable under the existing logical task; do not discard accepted state or substitute a fresh session to get around it.

Compatibility/migration: retain decoders and exact receipts for previously accepted records. If representation or lifecycle semantics change, introduce a versioned migration under exclusive ownership; verify a complete replacement frontier before atomic publication and keep the old recovery root until adoption is durable. Rebuild derived projections from authoritative evidence. Update all producers, consumers and invariants together; a rejected new operation must leave the predecessor usable and already owned effects reconcilable.

Acceptance and nonregression: long-running commands, output and stdin pressure, stalled helper/input readers, control-queue saturation, late start/exit races, parent loss and restart, proving cancellation responsiveness, no PID-reuse adoption and no duplicate process dispatch. Exercise the precise source-described failure path and the relevant byte/count/elapsed boundaries listed in this finding, plus ordinary small inputs. Check that legitimate work progresses after the former blocker while malformed input, conflicting identity, stale preimages and unauthorized scope still reject. Add fault injection at the affected acceptance/publication/recovery boundary and run the affected integration and formal checks on the final implementation. Source-derived risks remain distinct from executed reproductions; completion requires this evidence, not a promise that a plan alone cannot break anything.

d793a029-b248-5ba5-b6c2-843e7fb6b247.title: [L289] Scheduler replay repeatedly clones and hashes retained state, and estimated size is an additional admission gate
d793a029-b248-5ba5-b6c2-843e7fb6b247.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L289.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-scheduler/src/reducer.rs:63-82,89-116`; `state.rs:308-322`.
- Each command clones the full state, applies the command, refreshes it, checks estimated_encoded_bytes, appends its identity and hashes the complete successor. Replay invokes that reduction for every historical event, with retained event/command ID sets. As state grows, reconstructing all prefixes can accumulate quadratic copying/hashing work; no latency measurement was performed.
- The estimate starts at **1,024 bytes**, adds **512 per worker**, **512 per work plus 16 per dependency/resource entry**, **384 per reservation**, and **16 per historical command/dispatch identity**. It can reject before exact encoding even if the actual frame would fit; exact encoding still enforces its own cap afterward. The estimate is tested before appending the next command ID.
- This is a state-size/performance blocker, not an elapsed timeout. Integrity checking must remain grounded in exact durable facts while checkpoints and bounded frontier state avoid repeated whole-history rebuilding. Canonical hashing has now been fully read: it streams SHA256 while traversing every retained state field, rather than constructing a separate complete hash buffer. Worker refresh scans all retained workers and counts reservations after each event. **Complete reducer, estimator, canonical hashing and outer refresh/worker refresh read; wire encoding and inner dependency rounds pending.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

d7c8a273-96c5-58bb-8cd5-f07535e6a3e8.title: [L434] E3 retry retention acknowledges the only execution directive without scheduling the next attempt
d7c8a273-96c5-58bb-8cd5-f07535e6a3e8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L434.

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/aggregate/reducer.rs:252-273`, `src/durability/commit.rs:158-167,170-211,295-302`, `src/durability/directive.rs:225-239`, `src/runtime/recovery.rs:66-90`, `src/runtime/mod.rs:75-105` in the same crate.
- Behavior: RetainRetryableAttempt changes Running to Scheduled and retains the attempt number. Its required settlement acknowledges the execution claim. transition_outbox emits no directive for this command; execution identity depends on campaign, rollout and request digest, with no attempt identity. With no other pending rows, recovery sees neither Running nor complete counts and returns Continue. RequestSchedule requires Planned and RecordSchedule requires Scheduling, so neither normal scheduling command accepts this retained Scheduled state.
- Consequence: The durable E3 retry path has no newly outstanding execution delivery after the retryable settlement. The runtime facade exposes commits and the journal rather than a retry driver. External code could provide another mechanism, but none is provided by this crate's normal transition/outbox path. This is a source-derived progress gap, not a reproduced installed loop. Raw aggregate retry/start admission also has no frozen maximum/backoff policy in state; the separately bounded accounting ledger is not an aggregate retry controller.
- Repair direction: Commit retry intent, exact next-attempt identity and a deliverable execution directive atomically with retention. Recovery must select the retained attempt's actual outstanding work; preserve the same logical rollout and any continuation instead of reconstructing it from a generic Scheduled flag. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

It deliberately has no --max-time/--connect-timeout; run_command polls indefinitely at 100 ms. The README still claims download time limits. Installation uses a temporary script and ordinary child process with no durable adoption/cancellation state; on try_wait error it kills/waits that child, ignoring cleanup results. Direct credential publication precedes final non-secret profile validation; failed validation discards credential removal errors and returns the profile error.
- Consequence: The installer timer was already removed in actual code. Size rejection remains, and interruption or cleanup failure has no persistent repair receipt in this crate. Credential cleanup after profile rejection can leave an unpublished resource, distinct from provider authentication or session expiration.
- Repair direction: Align documentation with source; retain user cancellation and exact durable installation/credential-publication reconciliation without reintroducing synthetic time limits. Validate non-secret profile shape before effects and preserve cleanup failures.
