da07f412-753f-5281-90c3-6a20e3c4b90e.title: [L257] Journal recovery categories can turn unrelated resource/identity failures into terminal blockers
da07f412-753f-5281-90c3-6a20e3c4b90e.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L257.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/error.rs:103-117,149-178`.
- Busy and generic Storage failures recommend Retry; CAS/NotFound recommend Reobserve; ambiguous commits require resolution of the same command. MissingArtifact, ReadOnly, IdempotencyConflict, CorruptJournal, UnsupportedSchema and representational overflow are all Terminal. These are categorical gates, not elapsed deadlines, and they have materially different recoverability and scope.
- Display collapses all SQLite failures to “SQLite operation failed”; the original source is retained only through the error chain. DiskFull is separately detectable, but the generic recovery category remains Retry. A caller that drops the source or adopts Terminal as a whole-daemon fence can obscure the real cause or prevent unrelated work. Existing caller-wide fences are documented in L197/L198; no additional production consequence is inferred solely from this enum.
- Repair should preserve exact commit/identity/integrity checks while exposing typed resource conditions and scoped recoverable outcomes. **Whole error implementation read; no new retry count or timeout selected here.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

db1ed7a5-217c-5e7f-9a74-a138bafeffae.title: [L319] D0 commits dispatch intent before local capacity and ownership admission
db1ed7a5-217c-5e7f-9a74-a138bafeffae.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L319.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/runtime/driver/tool_steps.rs:137-153,156-200,255-289`; `src/runtime/tools.rs:394-419,584-600`; `src/reducer.rs:487-497,523-547` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** dispatch_tool_once first commits ToolDispatched and increments pure active_tool_calls, then checks that a process-local coordinator exists and invokes its dispatch. The coordinator only then checks slot state, max_parallel, mutation serialization, and C4 authority. Definite pre-effect failures leave the durable slot Dispatched and the runtime slot AwaitingAuthorization.
- **Consequence:** A valid batch whose pure concurrency ceiling permits a second call but whose runtime parallel allowance is one can commit its second dispatch intent and then receive DispatchCapacity before C4 executes anything. Retrying dispatch_tool_once fails because the pure slot is already Dispatched; record_tool_observation_once rejects the still-awaiting runtime slot. The available lost-tool classifier fabricates an Indeterminate outcome despite the known absence of this dispatch, and later prevents a clean gates/review completion. Missing runtime ownership after restore has the same admission order.
- **Repair direction:** Perform effect-free local capacity/ownership admission before durable dispatch intent, retain the exact admitted dispatch capability, and durably classify definitely unstarted versus uncertain intent. Keep committed intent before actual external dispatch; do not remove serialization safeguards to repair the ordering.
- **Evidence scope:** Source-derived capacity counterexample, with independently configurable pure and runtime ceilings. No dispatcher or journal fixture executed; installed DeveloperLoop use of this driver is not established.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

db4614ac-d53d-51a5-9cd6-b0de3e6c13f0.title: [L247] Global event pages validate every row and reject interior gaps; future cursors are silently empty
db4614ac-d53d-51a5-9cd6-b0de3e6c13f0.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L247.

- Source: `crates/state/peritus-journal/src/sqlite/query/records.rs:27-99,102-188,209-248`; `sqlite/query.rs`; `sqlite/reader.rs`.
- The global query accepts **1..4096 records per page**, computes actual retained MIN/MAX in one transaction, and performs exact frame/digest/hash and contiguous-position validation. No event-retention deletion or age timer exists in this file. Aggregate queries still load the entire aggregate history into a Vec without paging here; one malformed row aborts the whole result.
- A cursor at or beyond latest returns an empty page without rejecting a cursor ahead of the actual journal. Thus an ahead-of-store cursor can leave consumers waiting for positions that no longer exist after a store rollback unless a caller explicitly detects and reconciles it. The TUI/server higher-level validation for this case remains to be traced; no rollback reproduction is claimed.
- JournalReader holds a deferred read snapshot for its lifetime and rejects exact store/schema drift. Fixed-length identities and positive i64-backed sequence values are integrity/representation requirements, not elapsed deadlines. **All three files fully read; append/schema and recovery callers still pending.**

dc244688-96fc-5c4e-a506-b4d39b193f01.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L350.

- Behavior: selection requires positive finite maxima for selected nodes and selected bytes, in addition to the usable model input budget. Required roots are admitted with their entire dependency closure. Crossing either allocation ceiling returns `RequiredNodeLimitExceeded` or `RequiredByteLimitExceeded`, even when tokens fit; optional roots are omitted with their entire closure. There is no partial-range admission or automatic compaction in the selector. The independent certificate executes the same rejection rules.
- Consequence: independently configured collection/byte ceilings can prevent a model turn. The physical model window remains a real capacity constraint; these additional ceilings are separate. This pure API permits constructing a larger policy, but exposes no continuation, paging, or negotiated allocation recovery itself. Installed values and error handling must be connected through callers before attributing the live session stall.
- Repair direction: preserve the durable context inventory and required references separately from the materialized model view; admit ranges and dependency references under recoverable allocation policy. Capacity pressure must produce an actionable continuation or compaction path without dropping task/session identity. No tests or fresh runtime reproduction run.

- Test-source corroboration: `tests/selection_matrix.rs:120-140,190-213` expects required byte/node hard errors and atomic optional capacity omissions; `tests/selection_certificate.rs:198-220` requires exact capacity-failure priority. These tests were read completely, not run.

ddea4a0b-b277-5c86-9192-7e4da59902bf.title: [L183] Unknown command projection blocks retry and delivery controls without native outcome reconciliation
ddea4a0b-b277-5c86-9192-7e4da59902bf.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L183.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/operation.rs:31-65,68-183`; `workbench/run_control.rs:53-87`.
- Public projection reads the entire effect ledger and gives unresolved commands priority over execution and deliverable state. A Started receipt with a nonterminal run phase permits only Cancel. Every other unresolved command permits only Acknowledge; Retry, Export, Commit and Discard are omitted by this early return, even if a separate candidate exists.
- Acknowledgement validates that projection, appends Reviewed, and retains the explicit unknown-outcome mutation freeze. The inactive-owner proof is **the run phase**, not a C2 process/command ownership lookup in these methods. This meets the projection's state contract but leaves the shutdown proof gap in L182 unresolved.
- Each control legality check and diagnostic projection reloads/decodes the receipt history under the run records lock. Oversized/corrupt ledger inspection errors abort the projection and authenticated control before their actions. A valid ledger at its append ceiling can still permit dashboard Cancel, which bypasses receipt append; Acknowledge needs another receipt and remains subject to L165.
- Preserve no-duplicate-effect protection while adding durable command identity/outcome reconciliation and a repair projection. **Full caller/source read; no end-to-end lockup or liveness race reproduced.**

de41e444-863c-515d-b6b2-7e1b22abbb0b.title: [L608] Windows ACL rollback ownership is not durable across owner loss
de41e444-863c-515d-b6b2-7e1b22abbb0b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L608.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-windows/src/filesystem/acl.rs:112-140,167-174`; `src/filesystem/acl/reversal.rs:18-58,91-139,160-201` in the same crate.
- Behavior: ACL backup filenames use only ACL-plan digest and entry index. The list of backup paths and restore parents is retained in the transaction's in-memory reversal vector. Save/apply/restore invoke synchronous `icacls.exe` from PATH with no cancellation. Failed installation attempts restoration but discards that restoration result before returning the original error; `Drop` also ignores restore errors. Explicit restore correctly retains unsuccessful reversals for same-owner retry, while successful backup deletion failures are ignored.
- Consequence: A crash or failed drop can leave modified ACLs and backup files without a reconstructible pending reversal list. Concurrent equal plans share backup filenames without per-operation identity here. Synchronous ACL tooling can block preparation and release indefinitely.
- Repair direction: Persist each exact preimage and reversal obligation under a unique transaction before mutation, serialize conflicting ACL owners, and implement cancellable resumable application/reversal with explicit cleanup outcomes.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

de849c9c-7958-5930-bb88-fbcf38217a32.title: [L354] C6 reducing compaction can fail on the union of individually admissible dependencies
de849c9c-7958-5930-bb88-fbcf38217a32.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L354.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-context/src/compaction/replacement/dependencies.rs:21-62,145-172,214-234`, `src/compaction/replacement/graph.rs:30-34,157-181,339`, `src/node/metadata.rs:191-254` (previously read).
- Behavior: the replacement node receives the canonical union of every replaced source dependency outside the replaced set. Dependency metadata is reconstructed under the original graph's finite dependency-per-node limit. dfd04989-9704-5347-8ba5-3a2ec0fdd9fc.title: [L691] Product controls are not fenced to the observed candidate or operation generation
dfd04989-9704-5347-8ba5-3a2ec0fdd9fc.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L691.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/product/control.rs:55-76`; `src/product/operation.rs:190-221,255-266`; `src/product/snapshot.rs:29-69,134-151`; `src/product/settlement.rs:24-47`; `src/product/phase.rs:72-88` in the same crate; `crates/app/peritus-cli/src/product_run.rs:72-137`.
- Behavior: ProductRunControl transmits only run ID and action. It cannot carry the candidate digest or current operation generation observed during confirmation. Operation identity is a bounded string; the constructor checks text and requires uncertainty for OutcomeUnknown but does not forbid retry/accept flags for that state or reconcile phase/control inconsistency. Phase helpers classify WaitingForUser and RecoveryRequired as terminal until explicit input; retryable is a broad Failed/Cancelled/RecoveryRequired classification. Settlement validates candidate run/workspace/qualification but DTO construction alone does not prove an external owner or side-effect state.
- Consequence: A client-visible legal control and local digest confirmation can become stale before the server admits it. These pure projections cannot be used as authority tokens or generic permission to replay uncertain work. The durable host must independently gate exact operation state, and missing fencing can turn valid user control into a conflict or wrong-candidate action.
- Repair direction: Carry exact expected candidate/operation lineage in mutation requests and validate it at the authoritative owner; make legal controls derive from that owner's typed state. Preserve waiting/recovery within the durable goal rather than treating terminal phase as session disposal. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e141d70a-fa77-5e1c-bf11-0258e25ce9ba.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L221.

Both construct the entire VecDeque before consumption, on top of the already fully buffered native process output. This creates avoidable event allocation and per-event trace/reducer work; a 4 MiB argument would approach 262,144 events before protocol framing. Actual adapter admission is additionally bounded by the 4 MiB raw Codex line limit (L218), so no production million-event overflow is inferred solely from the 16 MiB argument maximum.

The host's outer cancellation checks need separate verification; this is not proof that all cancellation is ignored. The shared reducer has a **1,000,000 event** response ceiling (L017/L223), while native builders use production fragment bounds rather than a negotiated narrower request bound.
- **Both complete native stream implementations read; no allocation, latency or cancellation benchmark run.** Buffering and fixed fragmentation are implementation policies, not native model context limits or elapsed timers.

e170275e-c034-50c5-a38e-4bf8f546d75d.title: [L225] HTTP pulls reject valid bodies based on upstream chunk boundaries, while default transport has no selected timer
e170275e-c034-50c5-a38e-4bf8f546d75d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L225.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-core/src/reqwest_transport.rs:36-66,75-93,147-170,183-231,304-312`; `transport.rs:126-155`; `http/message.rs:71-85,142-153`; `http/header.rs:25-32,178-193`.
- Both ReqwestByteStream and BoundedByteStream reject an upstream chunk larger than **1 MiB**, rather than slicing it into allowed pulls. A response whose total and individual SSE/NDJSON frames are otherwise valid can therefore fail solely because the underlying transport groups bytes differently. At **256 MiB cumulative response**, content-length admission or accumulated streaming bytes also fail; full request body admission is **32 MiB**. This closes enforcement of L209/L217, though no large-chunk case has been reproduced.
- Response header limits are **256 entries / 128 KiB aggregate**; a single name is at most **256 bytes**. Hop-by-hop/proxy/header-injection rejection is a separate integrity/credential boundary, not an arbitrary execution deadline.
- Peritus default ReqwestTransport::new selects None for connect/header/body-idle deadlines; an explicit with_timeouts API still accepts three mandatory positive durations and applies header/idle timeout wrappers. AnthropicClient::new uses the untimed constructor. This audit does not infer dependency-internal defaults from the absence of a Peritus value. Redirects, ambient proxies and implicit HTTP retries are disabled deliberately by the transport contract.
- OwnedModelStream stops after the first normalized terminal and cancels on error/drop, but relies on its inner stream to honor cancellation during pull; native adapters ignore the token (L221). The production developer driver additionally wraps drive in cancel_first and isolates cancellation per attempt, so native draining does not establish a general uncancelable run. **All six HTTP/stream implementations plus developer caller fully read; no new network/cancellation tests run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e1963126-ff5e-50d2-aed9-40870db51283.title: [L323] Model output limiting can hide the control identities and terminal status of an oversized tool result
e1963126-ff5e-50d2-aed9-40870db51283.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L323.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/developer/observation.rs:8-69,72-145`; `src/developer/context_port.rs:89-101,128-154` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** Model-visible output gets a policy budget of one eighth of provider input, clamped to 512..10,000 estimated tokens and three bytes per token. Command projection first removes tool_result and all completed progress, or retains only eight active progress events. If the remaining JSON is still oversized, the generic truncator replaces the entire object with head/tail text and digest metadata; it does not separately preserve command handle, state, success/status, failure or recovery fields.
- **Consequence:** A large result can leave the model without structured control/terminal truth even though the full observation was durably retained. The handle or decisive fields may fall outside both previews. A local-context source reference can enable retrieval and is added afterward, but ports need not provide one; legacy callers receive only the warning to make a narrower request. This can drive repeated inspection or prevent the model from selecting the exact poll/recovery action. Metadata insertion after truncation also increases the already selected view size.

e21c9eff-d890-59bd-ab07-66c8fc017166.title: [L224] Writer follow-ups use a role that enabled local memory rejects, and disabled memory selects another native context
e21c9eff-d890-59bd-ab07-66c8fc017166.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L224.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/execution.rs:72-95`; `turn.rs:53-54,292-310`; `local_context/port.rs:58-67`; `workspace_delivery.rs:103-112`.
- When conversation revision differs from retained execution state, the production loop creates a fresh design and invokes complete_developer_turn with role **writer-follow-up**. That function calls input.working_memory(role) before its loop. With local memory enabled, LocalContextHandle accepts only writer/designer/fixer/reviewer, so writer-follow-up returns unsupported local memory role and the authorized follow-up is rejected **before any model inference**. The daemon default enables local memory (L204).
- If local memory is disabled, the rejection is bypassed, but native_session_directory joins the literal role into trace.context/<role>/provider-sessions. Therefore writer-follow-up selects a different parent directory from writer, even with the same run/profile/revision/model, losing automatic reuse of the original writer thread on this path. The repair should separate stable role identity from invocation purpose and retain the same exact writer ownership/context through follow-ups.
- Ordinary design/writer/fixer/reviewer/conversation requests all explicitly supply Some(native_session_directory); run_live_invocation forwards it, and Developer model request construction preserves it. Their bound namespaces have no ephemeral expiry. SemanticCompaction requests intentionally omit that metadata and do not execute host tools. This closes the main production metadata uncertainty in L215, while daemon run/trace identity persistence remains separately audited in L183-L187.
- **Every named implementation and caller fully read; no follow-up execution test run.** This is a source-confirmed production routing incompatibility, not a claim that it caused the earlier observed live lockup.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e221201b-6640-5b84-a08a-ab0147a5f36b.title: [L229] Approval registry size and exact-successor policy can block the entire daemon at startup
e221201b-6640-5b84-a08a-ab0147a5f36b.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L229.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/startup/registry.rs:27-38,44-110,119-134,160-179`; `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/authentication/credential.rs:15-18,92-126,150-177`; `src/digest.rs` in that crate.
- A credential snapshot is limited to **4 MiB / 4,096 entries / 11 distinct ordered approval roles per credential**. Disabled credentials count toward the entry ceiling. The configured payload must be a regular file at its exact canonical path; symlinks, alias components, absent files, oversized bytes and noncanonical encoding fail startup. Unlike workspace registrations, there is no fallback from a missing configured payload in this path.
- Configuration must exactly match durable revision, generation, digest and bytes, or supply **revision = current + 1** with **greater generation**. The previous durable snapshot is verified before a successor is considered, so corrupt old state cannot be repaired merely by supplying a new good snapshot. Arbitrary reset/rollback would weaken revocation and authority; global startup dependence and lack of an explicit repair path are separate daily-use blockers.
- Decision preimages are capped at **4,096 bytes** and key-ID/signed-message preimages at **256 bytes**; these are canonical encoding limits, not inference deadlines. Exact Ed25519 key/signature lengths are algorithm requirements. **Registry implementation, credential projections and startup tests fully read; tests not run.** No automatic credential expiry duration was inferred from these size bounds.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-kernel/src/aggregate.rs:20-37`, `src/aggregate.rs:241-285`, `src/aggregate/lookup.rs:13-278`, `src/aggregate/validation.rs:18-46`, `src/aggregate/validation.rs:49-230`, `src/reducer.rs:120-131`, `src/reducer.rs:159-160`, `src/reducer.rs:175-201`, `src/reducer.rs:305-328`, `src/reducer/refinement.rs:154-211`, `src/reducer/run.rs:128-178`.
- Behavior: command preflight validates the entire aggregate, including pairwise command/event/child uniqueness and repeated linear parent lookups. The reducer clones every accumulated identity and entity vector, appends identities, audits retained accepted runs, and validates the whole next aggregate again. Terminal entities and accepted command/event IDs remain in the vectors; there is no retirement command. Even a pause/cancel request traverses the complete history. Contract binding is checked again on every command; its separately audited graph validation can add further work (L394).
- Consequence: command/event pairwise validation is quadratic in lifetime event count, producing potentially cubic cumulative validation work across a long session. Child cross-products and full retained-state copies add synchronous CPU/allocation work. No low fixed command-count quota is declared in this core; checked u64 event-sequence overflow is a representation boundary. No latency benchmark, memory exhaustion, or live incident was measured. Ghost proof models are not the executable cost.
- Repair direction: preserve immutable history outside a compact live projection, maintain verified identity/parent indexes and incremental invariants, and assemble checked transitions without cloning and rechecking all prior work. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e2c48096-5cfd-5bd8-ab1b-ea9c07973882.title: [L377] B1 a dirty or indeterminate lease inspection makes quarantine unrecoverable
e2c48096-5cfd-5bd8-ab1b-ea9c07973882.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L377.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-leases/tests/phase_matrix.rs:40-66`, `tests/phase_matrix.rs:241-261`, `tests/transitions.rs:190-232`, `crates/state/peritus-leases/src/transition/reconciliation.rs:44-55`, `src/transition/reconciliation.rs:94-106`, `src/transition/lifecycle.rs:65-71`, `src/transition/fencing.rs:31-37`, `src/transition/fencing.rs:123-129`, `src/transition/fencing/release.rs:28-36`, `src/transition.rs:50-84`, `src/binding/command.rs:18-29`, `src/model.rs:54-119`, `src/model/concrete.rs:171-200`.
- Behavior: reconciliation accepts only `Reconciling`. A correlated `Dirty` or `Indeterminate` inspection moves the aggregate to `Quarantined`. The abstract and concrete reachability models also have no outgoing Quarantined edge. The complete exported reducer families have no quarantine recovery transition: acquisition requires Available; renewal/use/release/expiry/holder-loss/discontinuity/revoke require Active; reconciliation itself rejects Quarantined. A later correlated `SafeToAcquire` observation therefore cannot resolve the same quarantined aggregate.
- Consequence: a temporary inability to inspect safety becomes a permanent same-aggregate availability blocker. Quarantine is a valid protective state; the missing path to establish safety afterward is the blocker. Pure mint can create an unrelated new logical aggregate but does not replace a durable existing aggregate or preserve its generation automatically. Installed persistence/admin recovery remains a separate boundary.
- Repair direction: make quarantine an inspectable recoverable state with explicit correlated reinspection/remediation commands and monotonic fencing. Keep acquisition blocked until current holder-quiescence and resource-safety evidence is validated. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e32f10d2-9599-5413-95aa-cd6300a44dd1.title: [L351] C6 synchronous selection repeats full closure computation and full-plan validation
e32f10d2-9599-5413-95aa-cd6300a44dd1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L351.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-context/src/selection/closure.rs:38-83`, `src/selection/ordering.rs:34-51,65-98`, `src/selection/plan.rs:37-41,65-141,143-229,255-269`, `src/selection/certificate.rs:24-257,264-282`, `src/verified.rs:15-183`.
- Behavior: each dependency closure executes graph-node-count complete passes without exiting when closure stops changing; dependency lookup scans the graph. Required roots recompute closure individually, including already selected roots. Optional ordering and render ordering use insertion sorts; render comparisons perform graph lookup. Production selection then calls an independent executable replay of the complete selection state machine. Production construction, certificate construction, and certificate acceptance each validate the full plan, with linear graph/dependency membership lookups and pairwise uniqueness scans.
- Consequence: growing context can amplify synchronous work even when it is admissible. This is a source-grounded performance/blocking risk, not evidence of an artificial timeout or proof of the installed lockup. Node-count closure passes are a structural termination bound, not a work quota. No scheduling yield or cancellation boundary exists inside these pure calls; callers may isolate execution, which remains to be traced.
- Repair direction: index stable node identities, compute reachability with a work queue or cached closures, exit on a fixed point, and use efficient deterministic sorting. Maintain independent validation using an incremental certificate rather than reproducing the entire constructor on every turn; preserve the checked relation and reject corrupt input. Runtime/optimized-build cost has not been measured.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e3846a2d-582e-54e4-a061-d226928f2e20.title: [L788] Exact control recovery exists only in the retained UI model, and some messages overstate admission
e3846a2d-582e-54e4-a061-d226928f2e20.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L788.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/model/chat/workbench.rs:1-394`, `refresh.rs:1-96`, `receipts.rs:1-341`, `receipts/correlation.rs:1-40`, `receipts/recovery.rs:1-37`, `receipts/rejection.rs:1-54`, and `receipts/error.rs:1-236`, all completely read. Response callers `src/model/protocol/response.rs:1-383` and `response/control.rs:1-187` were fully reread.
- Behavior: An original workbench command and draft are retained in `WorkbenchUi.unresolved`; reconnect queries that exact operation before explicit replay. Receipt matching checks operation, destination, and accepted revision. For ResumeGoal, a read-only recovered receipt deliberately leaves the operation unresolved and requires `/sessions retry` because worker launch is separately persisted. Ordinary review receipts label explanation/revision work as started, although the admission/launch split in L753 can prevent execution. Most panel error state uses only the error code rather than diagnostic/recovery detail. A normal disconnect clears pending request maps but retains this command only in the process-local model.
- Consequence: This is stronger than creating a new operation on reconnect, but it is not a durable client outbox that survives loss of the UI process. A missing launch or receipt may fence later edits indefinitely; a claimed start can obscure that distinction. Exact receipt and consent fencing should remain, while recovery must identify accepted-but-unlaunched work.
- Repair direction: Persist client intents and their settlement state, bind launch reconciliation to the accepted operation, and report admission separately from observed launch. Surface the retained diagnostic/recovery source without replacing uncertain operations by new identities.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e3c8da38-73c1-58d4-9e79-369f57b8b7da.title: [L381] B1 approval waiting and approved use are limited by the earliest of five validity deadlines
e3c8da38-73c1-58d4-9e79-369f57b8b7da.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L381.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-approval/src/request.rs:43-54`, `src/authentication.rs:151-161`, `src/authentication.rs:251-267`, `src/state/resolve_helpers.rs:30-50`, `src/state.rs:172-185`, `src/state/lifecycle.rs:8-48`, `src/state/lifecycle.rs:104-143`, `src/state/use_reducers.rs:111-125`, `src/state/use_reducers.rs:246-258`, `src/failure.rs:224-228`.
- Behavior: requests, challenged policy scope, approval requirements, and credentials carry explicit validity windows; every signed decision also carries an exclusive expiry. Authentication requires all four windows and the decision expiry to contain the observation. Resolution stores their earliest expiry. Pending expiration uses the earliest of request/scope/requirement; resolved but unconsumed action/amendment approval also refuses use at the stored boundary. Expired is classified Terminal. Rejected resolution/use preserves the unchanged aggregate, so an Expired error can leave the phase Pending or ApprovedOnce until a separate expire command is applied.
- Consequence: waiting for the user, delayed dispatch, or a pause can make an otherwise retained request/grant unusable. A fresh signature alone cannot extend the old request/scope/requirement. These are supplied authority deadlines, not internal sleep timers or evidence of provider-context deletion; actual production durations and replacement-request orchestration remain caller concerns. Scope use counts independently support Unlimited.
- Repair direction: keep run/context lifetime separate from optional authority validity and provide a durable refresh/reapproval frontier retaining the exact pending intent. If local authority can be untimed, represent that policy explicitly. Timed expiry must trigger reviewable renewal/replacement rather than terminalizing the whole run. Preserve one-use and exact action/amendment binding. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e411ab54-5113-53b2-b11a-60481bf5a676.title: [L300] Collaboration byte checks charge external payload sizes to small digest-only records
e411ab54-5113-53b2-b11a-60481bf5a676.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L300.

- Source: `crates/orchestration/peritus-collaboration/src/message.rs:10-23`; `reducer.rs:72-77,242-261`; `state.rs:279-293`; `canonical.rs:164-177`; `wire/mod.rs:333-355`; `reducer/apply.rs:196-234,237-254`.
- A message stores a payload **length and digest**, plus causal IDs, media type, optional handoff and revision. Neither semantic encoding nor wire encoding contains payload content. Nevertheless command admission estimates **payload_bytes + 768**, and complete-state admission charges the entire payload_bytes again for every historical message.
- A legal digest-only message referring to a 1 MiB payload can fail a 1 MiB command budget while its actual metadata command is much smaller. Repeated metadata messages can consume the aggregate's state budget based on the sum of external content lengths, even after delivery is acknowledged; acknowledgment changes a boolean and releases no quota.
- This synthetic accounting can block commands and long-lived collaboration far below actual canonical storage size. Repair should distinguish actual encoded-state bytes from any separately justified external-content/storage resource policy, with an explicit recovery model. **Both encodings and every accounting/admission path read completely; no boundary test executed.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e41aee25-f211-5970-9fdb-f07c0613c23f.title: [L097] Native helper admission is bounded, but synchronous startup can stall ownership
e41aee25-f211-5970-9fdb-f07c0613c23f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L097.

- `native.rs:41-42,104-117,143-156` caps helper identity at **256 ASCII bytes**, helper manifest at **4 MiB**, and protected-handle count at **256**. Staged protected payloads are capped at **1 MiB** and their ASCII labels at **256 bytes** (`native/protected_handle.rs:14-15,43-50,146-150`); pre-opened channel handles have no finite staged-payload cap. Duplicate handles/labels and mismatched digests are integrity failures; byte/count ceilings are independent implementation bounds.
- Native startup synchronously reads exact ready/activation records, writes/flushes the manifest, and on Windows reads the target-started record (`platform.rs:117-148`, `platform/pipe.rs:89-128`, `platform/pty.rs:143-163`). There is **no elapsed timeout in these routines**. A helper that stays alive without completing the handshake can hold startup before the active `SpawnedOwner` control-draining loop exists.
- Removing synthetic deadlines alone does not provide a cancellation path through blocking handshake I/O. This is an identified source stall path; backend/helper implementations and selected product launch behavior remain pending before attributing any live symptom to it.
- A native backend preparation error records incomplete cleanup (`gateway/native.rs:47-54`), leaving durable ownership unresolved rather than assuming Rust Drop succeeded. That preserves honest recovery evidence but can contribute to L088's blocked admission until reconciled.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e80c6b4d-26d3-511e-bd19-17f40c3836b5.title: [L742] Public interaction observation writes whole run records and hides pending-input read failures
e80c6b4d-26d3-511e-bd19-17f40c3836b5.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L742.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/product_run/interaction/inputs.rs:8-45`; `src/product_run/interaction.rs:106-128,234-302,308-355`; `src/product_run/interaction/models.rs:7-57` in the same crate.
- Behavior: query_interaction first synchronizes every not-yet-projected input revision; changed observations clone and synchronously write the whole run record while holding the global records write lock. Public activities are a bounded FIFO independent of durable input/reply archives. pending_interactive_input converts record-lock and pending_record_input failures to false. Terminal activity append failures are ignored. Model updates also persist under the records write lock, with rollback on write failure.
- Consequence: an observation can hold other runs' record access during source replay and filesystem I/O. A damaged/unavailable pending-input capture can look like no pending work, leaving a waiting run without a surfaced recovery cause. FIFO activity history can disappear while the actual ledger remains durable; those two forms of persistence must not be conflated.
- Repair direction: use incremental durable projections and publish immutable snapshots after I/O outside shared locks; represent pending-input inspection failure explicitly and keep recovery receipts. Retain no-false-acknowledgment rollback and original input authority. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

e8b8eabd-0cb7-5ba1-a433-54b154b85b24.description:

e8f9f353-9abd-543f-ae64-f30660cace08.title: [L376] B1 mutation leases always have finite expiry and cannot renew after the boundary
e8f9f353-9abd-543f-ae64-f30660cace08.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L376.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-leases/src/scope.rs:88-114`, `src/command.rs:57-91`, `src/claim.rs:15-22`, `src/transition/lifecycle.rs:79-110`, `src/transition/lifecycle.rs:171-215`, `src/transition/lifecycle/deadline.rs:28-43`, `src/transition/validation.rs:189-215`, `src/state/validity.rs:10-35`.
- Behavior: acquisition and renewal require a strictly positive finite `u64` millisecond duration. There is no untimed duration/claim representation. The deadline is observation time plus duration with checked overflow. Renewal requires an exact current claim, an observation strictly before expiry, and a new deadline strictly later than the old one. Observation at the deadline rejects renewal as `ClaimExpired`; requesting a nonextending deadline yields `DeadlineNotExtended`. Renewing also changes claim version, invalidating outstanding old claims.
- Consequence: a long pause or late renewal can leave a holder unable to resume through renewal, even if the holder/session still exists. This is an authority validity deadline, not an internal wall-clock timer or proof that a provider session is deleted. The README expressly requires fencing/reconciliation and says expiry cannot prove holder quiescence; that recovery is being audited separately. No caller-selected production duration is established by these files.
- Repair direction: separate durable holder/session identity from optional timed authority validity. If untimed authority is appropriate for local daily driving, represent it explicitly and preserve generation fencing, quiescence, and authorization checks. Timed configurations need durable recovery/renewal orchestration that reports expiry without discarding run context. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

This preserves against blindly reapplying an effect but leaves successful authorized work without its completion acknowledgment.
- Repair direction: journal the cross-layer initialization intent and reconcile the exact installed C1 manifest into the original C0 operation receipt before any new proposal validation. Preserve owner, revision, action and proposal fingerprints. No tests run.

eb2d9758-514f-5676-be1c-29a59bd61331.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L602.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-macos/src/session/lifecycle.rs:17-46`; `src/session/adapter.rs:47-49`; `src/session/cleanup.rs:24-34` in the same crate. Related status-channel blocking is recorded in L593.
- Behavior: After containment checks, activation releases the protected exec-status handle from the launch, then performs status observation. If that observation fails, the phase remains prepared but the handle has already been removed; an identical activation retry fails with absent ownership. If observation succeeds, phase and recovery are changed before the lifecycle observation is appended.
- Consequence: An interrupted or failed activation handshake cannot be resumed from the same prepared owner. Cleanup may still abandon that owner, but repeating activation cannot restore the consumed status capability.
- Repair direction: Model activation as a durable staged transition with status validation and a committed ownership handoff, retaining enough evidence for exact retry or reconciliation after every fallible boundary.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ec2f90a5-76fe-5897-9650-ecfb584d85bd.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L812.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-web/src/config.rs:174-209`; `src/api.rs:25-41,130-140,224-244,315-350`, `src/files/pdf.rs:6-25`, `src/consoles.rs:53-69` in that crate.
- Behavior: HTTP bodies cap at 4 MiB except the 50 MiB file-save route; operation IDs cap at 80 ASCII characters. Preferences accept font sizes 12–22, explorer widths 180–480, three themes, two densities and at most 100 aliases/shortcuts. Renamed titles cap at 256 bytes although the error says characters; new-session titles are not validated until the later daemon preparation. PDF identification inspects the first 1,024 bytes and downloads remain available. Console display titles/suggestions cap at 120 characters/32,768 bytes.
- Consequence: these are representation/admission bounds, not run TTLs. The inconsistent title validation allows a locally created session that later cannot prepare a daemon conversation; configurable alias count and fixed dimensions can also refuse ordinary customization. Loopback origin/token checks, literal path confinement and invalid command rejection protect authority and should not be removed as timers.
- Repair direction: use one validated title contract at creation/edit/preparation, document actual representation units, and make presentation/storage bounds adaptable without ending owned work. No tests were run during this source audit.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ed1914c5-20d2-54ca-9763-365d172227c1.title: [L600] macOS proxy cleanup failure becomes permanently nonretryable
ed1914c5-20d2-54ca-9763-365d172227c1.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L600.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-macos/src/session/cleanup.rs:20-71,75-95`; `src/session.rs:105-108`; `src/session/adapter.rs:73-109` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Release refuses active/cancelling sessions, removes exact materialized secret destinations idempotently, and retries secret-owner release while retaining that owner. Proxy shutdown instead takes the owner before shutdown, then sets `proxy_cleanup_failed` on failure. Every subsequent release stops at that flag. The generic process adapter replaces `RetryCleanup` and the underlying detail with supervisor/cancel-and-reap. Recovery cleanup updates remain only on the in-memory record until an external caller persists it.
- Consequence: A transient proxy shutdown failure cannot be retried by this session even though the native error advertises retryable cleanup. The resource owner and underlying failure evidence are lost, preventing complete release and a trustworthy clean recovery state.
- Repair direction: Retain proxy cleanup ownership until confirmed completion, preserve typed retry and reconciliation state through the process adapter, and persist each cleanup transition atomically with its outstanding obligation.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ee555b2b-3e7a-5f49-bea4-7bacf5adfed4.title: [L597] macOS helper setup silently tightens inherited limits and can lose secret cleanup evidence
ee555b2b-3e7a-5f49-bea4-7bacf5adfed4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L597.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-macos/src/runner.rs:125-164,192-229`; `src/runner/native.rs:134-186,228-265`; `src/runner/materialized.rs:20-25` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Hard rlimits use the minimum of the requested ceiling and both inherited soft and hard limits, then set both to that value without reporting the effective reduction. Untimed CPU zero is explicitly skipped. Protected payload reads, status writes, secret-file writes, and synchronization are synchronous with no cancellation. A failed secret write removes its file best-effort before returning; only successful materialization is added to rollback ownership. Rollback `Drop` also ignores removal failures. Successful exec replaces the helper and does not run that destructor.
- Consequence: An inherited low soft limit can constrain a request that asked for more, without a negotiation error. Failed cleanup can leave untracked protected material, and the rollback owner cannot persist cleanup evidence across helper replacement or crash. Successful-exec secret-file retirement depends on the surrounding session cleanup, which is being traced separately.
- Repair direction: Report and validate effective inherited resource ceilings before target activation; retain exact durable cleanup obligations for partial file creation and unsuccessful removals, and make staging/status work cancellable without inventing a run timeout.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

eea8385a-e53a-5918-986f-c2c42d81f9bf.title: [L552] Patch preparation can leave a manifestless blocker and quarantine has only 100 names
eea8385a-e53a-5918-986f-c2c42d81f9bf.description:

Successful installation exposes cleanup-pending status, but pre-mutation and restored failures do not expose ignored cleanup failure separately.

eec80d75-0da3-569e-9d2e-e10679d522f0.title: [L212] A pre-spawn Codex started marker can permanently fence a session without a native thread ID
eec80d75-0da3-569e-9d2e-e10679d522f0.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L212.

- Source: `crates/model/peritus-provider-openai/src/runtime/provider/invocation.rs:99-116`; `invocation/sessions.rs:16-27,42-65,69-116`.
- Before transport.run, the initial persistent session creates and synchronizes invocation-started. If spawn or another pre-submission transport step then fails before a thread.started event is journaled, Session::open later rejects the namespace as an interrupted invocation with no recoverable identity. This applies even to an outcome known to be definitely absent at the transport boundary; no such phase distinction or marker repair appears in these files.
- Identity recovery scans every turn directory but examines only the first **64 KiB of each native.jsonl**. It accepts complete newline-delimited thread.started records with an ID of at most **512 bytes** using ASCII alphanumeric/hyphen characters, rejects conflicting IDs, and does not use a global latest-thread fallback. A thread event outside the prefix or in a torn final frame cannot establish continuity. Exact identity/conflict protection is necessary; the fixed prefix and lack of definitely-absent launch recovery are separate barriers.
- Started state without identity remains retained and blocked rather than silently starting a fresh context. Inline tests cover torn trailing output, exact thread recovery, role/model isolation and lost-identity refusal; they do not cover a failed spawn after the marker or late identity beyond the prefix.
- **Complete source/tests read; no failed-spawn reproduction run.** A repair needs durable launch phase/identity reconciliation that distinguishes absent effects from ambiguous effects, while preserving existing threads and preventing duplicate starts.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

ef4b793c-6866-53d8-8daf-8beaedc5395d.title: [L316] D0 requires seven immutable positive limits for a turn's accumulated work
ef4b793c-6866-53d8-8daf-8beaedc5395d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L316.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-agent/src/limits.rs:28-93,172-234,262-276`; `src/identity.rs:145-205`; `src/state.rs:127-146`; `src/reducer.rs:38-79,109-139,251-284,355-379,523-547`; `src/command.rs:231-257` (remaining paths in the agent crate).
- **Blocker:** AgentLimits has no unlimited representation. Every dimension must be positive and is bounded by compiled maxima: tool calls 256, provider events 1,000,000, context cycles 4,096, accumulated provider-output bytes 64 MiB, accumulated model-visible tool-result bytes 64 MiB, concurrent calls 32, and transitions 1,000,000. Limits remain fixed in the aggregate and genesis event; the closed command vocabulary cannot rebind or replenish them.
- **Consequence:** Finishing a batch releases active concurrency but never cumulative tool/result/context/output/transition counters. ResultsRecorded discards current tools and resets ModelState, while these lifetime counters remain. Provider bytes are charged using the complete encoded C5 envelope length in the durable driver, including protocol metadata. Even a duplicate envelope increments provider_events and transitions, although its output-byte charge is zero. A productive long turn or repeated reconnection traffic eventually returns LimitExceeded/Exhausted without a durable continuation under the same binding.
- **Repair direction:** Separate finite in-flight capacity and individual encoding bounds from lifetime execution allowance. Persist an advancing logical turn frontier with paged evidence and durable context/provider identity; admit continued work without mandatory total-work quotas. Keep checked arithmetic and authoritative effect authorization.
- **Evidence scope:** Complete source reads; no exhaustion test executed and no proof that the installed DeveloperLoop dispatches through AgentDriver. These D0 aggregate limits are separate from DeveloperLoopLimits already cataloged in L049.

- **Additional fully read fixture evidence:** tests/runtime_driver.rs:203-292 explicitly expects four charged provider events for a stream cursor of three after one duplicate. tests/budgets.rs:13-38 expects terminal Failed at the transition ceiling rather than continued execution. These tests were read, not run.

ef65e4fd-88b1-5d43-a0e5-92c966d642bf.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L571.

- Evidence: `crates/runtime/peritus-sandbox-linux/src/canonical.rs:5-12`; `src/manifest.rs:62-68,109-144,220-230`; `src/manifest/value.rs:20-30`; `src/filesystem.rs:316-347`; `src/runner.rs:80-88` in the same crate.

efff1a0f-39fb-5e9b-a640-9d04eb0a3a8f.title: [L239] Discovery and subscriptions use fixed concurrency windows, and gap recovery is only admitted before progress
efff1a0f-39fb-5e9b-a640-9d04eb0a3a8f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L239.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/session/request/discovery.rs:13-16,48-70`; `subscription/pump.rs:24,39-78,127-224`; `crates/app/peritus-app-protocol/src/subscription/transitions.rs:19-45,75-99,180-241`; topic grammar in daemon `subscription/registry.rs`.
- Model discovery is limited to **4 connection-owned tasks**, counting completed tasks until they are reaped. A fifth query is Backpressure. There is no discovery elapsed deadline here; disconnect aborts and reaps these tasks. This preserves responsiveness relative to serial request handling, but a permanently stalled catalog can occupy a slot until disconnect.
- Subscription count is bound to the protocol's **max_topics (64 at production defaults)**, and each delivery window is at most **256 in-flight events** by default. A full window produces backpressure; pause and gap-recovery phases stop ordinary delivery. Filters use a closed registry of event families and 18 aggregate labels. These connection windows are not run lifetime quotas.
- Every **2 seconds**, all unacknowledged events are redelivered with preserved event bytes/identity and incremented u32 attempt counts. There is no small retry-count cutoff; arithmetic overflow is a representation failure. Whole-window redelivery and all subscription pumps await socket writes serially (L237).
- The daemon checks for a retention gap only while scanned_cursor equals the original requested cursor, and the pure transition rejects a declared gap after any scan/delivery progress. Thus this implementation cannot report a later gap through that transition. Actual source retention behavior and client snapshot/replacement handling still require their complete caller reads before claiming installed midstream loss. **All subscription implementation/proof files and discovery tests fully read; tests not run.**

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

f0ee41e6-e4d9-551f-9ea4-12f3594edec8.title: [L373] S1 knowledge capacities are finite admission policies without an unlimited mode
f0ee41e6-e4d9-551f-9ea4-12f3594edec8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L373.

- Evidence: `crates/orchestration/peritus-run-knowledge/src/limits.rs:29-64`, `src/source/validation.rs:20-26`, `src/section.rs:127-135`, `src/snapshot.rs:138-190`, `src/binding.rs:98-135`, `src/change.rs:29-68`.
- Behavior: all four caller-selected limits must be positive finite `usize` values: snapshot sections, current catalog sources, sources per section, and dependencies per section. Constructors reject oversized vectors rather than paginate them. This crate imposes no default or compiled maximum: callers can construct a larger policy. A policy with fewer than three sections is accepted even though every snapshot requires the three mandatory inventory/map/requirement sections. Bindings and sections validate their own constructor policy and do not retain it; snapshot admission checks its global section count but does not recheck each section's source/dependency counts against the snapshot policy.
- Consequence: a finite policy can reject otherwise valid knowledge growth. Independently selected policies also make the snapshot policy an incomplete statement of admitted per-section capacity. The admission test permits `usize::MAX`, and `tests/snapshot_admission.rs:152-166` explicitly expects nested policy differences to be accepted. These are immutable snapshots/catalogs that callers can replace, not proven lifetime quotas or mandatory expiry. Writer/Reviewer/Fixer role restrictions are an explicit role contract, not a clock or capacity rule.
- Repair direction: distinguish finite caller resource policies from required structural invariants, support resumable catalog/section paging, validate policy consistency at snapshot admission, and offer an explicit unlimited policy where a host can support it. Preserve source identity/digest binding. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

f2123253-989a-5b55-acb2-aa7a31d9a3d2.title: [L622] Admitted causal history across revisions cannot be represented by the current portable bundle policy
f2123253-989a-5b55-acb2-aa7a31d9a3d2.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L622.

- Evidence: `crates/state/peritus-evidence/src/causality.rs:35-67`; `src/bundle/plan.rs:94-119,206-238`; `src/freshness.rs:35-76`; `tests/admission.rs:137-176`; `tests/freshness.rs:27-89` in the same crate.
- Behavior: Admission requires causal parents to exist and have earlier journal positions; it does not require their revision to equal the child's. Bundle planning requires all records to be current against one supplied revision, every causal parent to be included, and all included records to share the same exact revision tuple. Explicit invalidation is durable and dominates drift; no elapsed-time TTL appears in this freshness implementation.
- Consequence: A valid current record citing an older-revision parent has no successful bundle selection: omitting the parent breaks ancestry, while including it breaks currentness/revision equality. This is a source-derived history/export incompatibility, not proof that the installed run hit this path. The ancestry test only uses one revision.
- Repair direction: Distinguish historical causal provenance from a present-tense authority assertion. Preserve and export historical ancestors with their original bindings while checking current authority only where required. Source review only; no tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

f2b6413c-1297-58f7-8a34-60dd2b82ec07.title: [L264] Outbox delivery has a fixed 30-second lease and configured shutdown abort, with no renewal during delivery

Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L264.

- Source: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/outbox/pump.rs:10-11,31-50,61-107`; `outbox/clock.rs`.
- The sole production pump selects **30-second leases** and an **idle poll every 25 ms**. The poll is a cadence, not a work deadline. router.deliver is awaited without an elapsed work timeout, but the lease is not renewed while it runs. A concurrent claimant or restart must reconcile the exact effect/fence instead of treating elapsed ownership as proof that no effect happened.

An in-progress native/cross-store settlement can therefore be interrupted at the shutdown cutoff; durable recovery must resolve it, not assume completion from task cancellation.

These long representation boundaries are separate from the selected 30-second lease; rollover/shift behavior was not executed or qualified here.
- Production has one sequential pump, so L251's invalidation of a still-active final claim requires another claim operation to overlap it; ordinary single-pump sequential delivery alone does not establish that reproduction. **Complete pump/clock/route implementations read; no concurrent lease test run.** The fully read `peritus-journal/src/sqlite/tests/outbox_tests.rs:10-63` covers reclaim at expiry with max_attempts=3 and accepts an old fence after final acknowledgment. f397a87b-9789-5b27-b8dd-39e375ec2c1a.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L089.

- `supervisor/resource.rs:72-89,109-126,205-214` baselines the entire working directory and resamples disk growth each **1 second**, plus process resources each **20 ms**. These intervals are sampling cadence, not elapsed execution deadlines. Exceeding CPU, memory, disk growth, process count, or descriptors requests resource-limit cancellation (`owner.rs:164-188,244-259`), even when ordinary wall time is absent.
- `supervisor/resource/disk.rs:13-56` recursively enumerates all regular files without the tooling layer's build/cache exclusions. Deleted descendants are tolerated, but unreadable directories, entries, or metadata cause an error. Owner-loop sampling errors become supervisor failure and cleanup (`owner.rs:133-146`), so inability to measure a descendant can terminate otherwise working execution.
- Repeated full-tree scans can delay output/control observation in a large workspace. This is source-derived synchronous work, not a benchmark or diagnosis of the reported live lockup. Symlinks are skipped; growth uses logical file sizes above the baseline, not physical filesystem capacity.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

f3d1bc32-bfea-539f-9cdd-a058eefed2b4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L584.

There is no cancellation or paging in this path. Unrelated entries make the Git workspace dirty; folder recovery rejects any other transaction or unrelated entry before reconciling its exact target. Rolled-back cleanup-pending state is recorded in the digest but does not independently clear the Git transaction-clean flag.

Another outstanding folder transaction can prevent exact-target recovery, and a cleanup obligation may remain while the Git classifier reports clean. Artifact failure overrides even a completed inspection to indeterminate.

f441d325-5bc6-59f3-ac72-981cb3544a55.title: [L507] Plugin payload and frame constructors disagree with fixed deserialization limits
f441d325-5bc6-59f3-ac72-981cb3544a55.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L507.

- Evidence: `crates/extensions/peritus-plugin-sdk/src/payload.rs:21-65,89-105,108-159`; `src/canonical.rs:8-78`; `src/framing.rs:15-54`; `src/protocol/wire.rs:5-58`; `src/protocol/request_wire.rs:41-74`; `src/protocol/response_wire.rs:96-134` in the same crate.
- Behavior: production JSON limits are 1 MiB canonical/input bytes, depth 32, 16384 total members/elements, and 256 KiB per key/string. New/parse accept caller-provided bounds, but every Serde deserialize forces production bounds. All floating-point values are rejected. Payload validation/canonical rendering traverses complete Value trees; protocol serialization converts nested payloads into fresh Value trees and frame encoding allocates the whole JSON before enforcing its positive u32 frame maximum. Duplicate JSON members are already collapsed by Value parsing, so canonicalization cannot establish their original uniqueness.
- Consequence: a payload created under broader bounds can encode successfully but fail on decode despite an enlarged frame quota. Legitimate decimal-valued tool inputs/results fail this plugin representation. Whole-value conversion/canonicalization and escaping can produce a late frame-bound failure after earlier logical admission; widening frame bytes does not widen payload admission.
- Repair direction: bind consistent recursive/payload/frame policies to both encoding and decoding, choose a documented numeric domain suitable for tool results, and enforce duplicate/member/encoded-size correctness at the parser boundary before whole copies. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

f44cccbf-5850-5417-92f8-4bf92dbb4b42.title: [L791] Foreground candidate execution suspends the whole UI reducer without a durable process owner
f44cccbf-5850-5417-92f8-4bf92dbb4b42.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L791.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/runtime/candidate.rs:1-144`, `candidate/foreground.rs:1-152`, and `runtime/terminal.rs:1-221`, all completely read; caller `src/runtime.rs:1-347` fully reread.
- Behavior: Running a candidate checks the exact repository digest, parses a direct executable/argument command, stops the terminal input worker, suspends the full-screen terminal, and awaits a blocking child-status task. That await does not pump `next_effects`, daemon events, subscription acknowledgements, local reads, or model polls. Interrupt signals are consumed while waiting for the foreground command to exit. Unix transfers the terminal to the child's process group, observes stops with waitpid, and waits for shell SIGCONT before foreground restoration; handoff failure kills that group. This child has no durable C2 launch receipt or reconnect/adoption identity here. The 100 ms input poll/park is a scheduling cadence, not a lifetime cap; selection mode deliberately skips all subsequent redraws until release.
- Consequence: A long-running or interrupt-resistant candidate can keep the interface unavailable while its connection event queue stops draining; loss of the owning client cannot adopt this same process through these APIs. Natural command duration and OS job-control waits must not be replaced by a synthetic execution deadline. Candidate digest/foreground ownership checks are integrity boundaries.
- Repair direction: Keep connection/control progress alive during terminal handoff and route candidate launches through a durable process owner with explicit cancel, exit, and adoption receipts. Preserve correct foreground process groups and exact candidate authorization.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Every brief field uses 8,192-byte text, with exactly four semantic field types, and full brief rendering must fit MAX_REQUEST_CONTEXT_BYTES. Complete source metadata and byte/line bounds are limited to 64 MiB even for small selected ranges; each selected version must fit 256 KiB and match its source range/digest. Every refresh stays in immutable history; deselected entries and old versions remain in whole-record serialization, without an independent history compaction mechanism here.

Historical file selections are frozen snapshots, not expired grants. Identity/digest/authority constraints are separate from product-selected text/storage ceilings.

f609f8f9-8cd4-5a63-9686-aca2a053e9f2.title: [L232] A 64 MiB migration reserve gates startup even when the schema needs no migration
f609f8f9-8cd4-5a63-9686-aca2a053e9f2.description:

These operations have no elapsed deadline here but add synchronous work as state grows; duration was not measured. f6a908ad-1218-5d0e-8b2c-4c13f0b31d66.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L439.

Statistical confidence and probability bounds are mathematical preconditions, not execution deadlines.
- Repair direction: Preserve deterministic seed/draw identity while processing resamples in cancellable, durable batches. Expose progress and resumable state; make requested statistical workload explicit instead of relying on a compulsory compiled ceiling to contain blocking computation. No tests run.

Expiry permanently changes its state before owner and execution scope checks, and successful delivery decrements its lifetime use count. There is no unlimited representation or renewal operation. Material lookup occurs before delivery validates the live lease, and a file-staging failure does not return the moved lease for retry.

An incorrectly scoped attempt at or beyond expiry can change lease state. These are source-level behaviors; installed caller values and native recovery integration remain separate questions.

f8b350ca-faa5-51ac-9bae-6b0127f25026.title: [L400] B0 session aggregate cannot advance its revision or acceptance-contract binding
f8b350ca-faa5-51ac-9bae-6b0127f25026.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L400.

- Evidence: `crates/foundation/peritus-kernel/src/aggregate.rs:20-37`, `src/aggregate.rs:138-190`, `src/command.rs:16-103`, `src/reducer.rs:148-160`, `src/reducer.rs:203-246`, `src/reducer.rs:305-322`, `src/aggregate/validation.rs:9-46`, `tests/adversarial.rs:13-47`.
- Behavior: genesis fixes the session aggregate's exact seven-component revision and contract ID/digest. Every command must use that revision and contract; every run must match it. The complete command vocabulary has no revision/contract amendment, rebinding or successor transition, and reduction explicitly preserves the original revision. Creating another aggregate is possible through open(), but no in-place continuation across a workspace revision, harness, policy or provider-profile change exists here.
- Consequence: an ordinary candidate revision or authorized policy/contract update cannot be represented as advancement of this aggregate. A caller must manage a new aggregate and its continuity externally. This does not prove that a new model context or session identity is required: open() accepts caller-supplied identities, and this effect-free crate does not own persistence or provider contexts. Reusing stale revision facts to evade freshness is not a valid repair.
- Repair direction: model durable session identity separately from versioned run authority, with an explicit checked revision/contract successor transition that preserves history, invalidates only affected current evidence, and retains resumable work/context bindings. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

f8e53bb0-2946-5fac-81ca-1386c5e2fd7d.title: [L432] E3 accepts a frozen profile whose component policies disagree with its final limits and provider
f8e53bb0-2946-5fac-81ca-1386c5e2fd7d.description:

- Evidence: `crates/analysis/peritus-eval/src/profile/binding.rs:250-330,407-459`, `src/profile/provider.rs:165-201`, `src/profile/policy.rs:12-69,118-170`, `src/dataset/manifest.rs:24-70`, `src/aggregate/state.rs:185-195`, `src/durability/commit.rs:82-94` in the same crate.
- Behavior: The final profile rechecks selected rollout cardinality, but does not recheck dataset task count, retry maximum, bootstrap count or pass-k count against the final EvaluationLimits. Previously checked components can come from different limits. Model controls incorporate the provider used at construction into a digest, but retain no independently checked provider binding; the final profile accepts a separate provider snapshot without comparing it. Aggregate checkpoint serialization uses CodecLimits::PRODUCTION rather than the frozen profile's state_bytes.

This postpones rejection or permits policies that do not match the purported frozen contract. For example, a two-task dataset can be admitted with final tasks=1 if the independent rollout ceiling accommodates it. These are source-derived constructor/enforcement gaps, not executed examples or proof of an installed provider failure.
- Repair direction: Validate the complete profile as one coherent contract; retain and compare provider bindings and distinguish explicit workload policy from storage limits. Any intentional limit should be enforced at its ownership boundary and remain recoverable. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

Native backend translation may impose additional rules; this is a contract/translation risk, not a confirmed installed failure.

fa1da797-ba30-5a36-aed1-ee134e9d6d0d.title: [L118] Whole conversation is capped at one MiB before a persistent run can execute
fa1da797-ba30-5a36-aed1-ee134e9d6d0d.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L118.

- `crates/orchestration/peritus-obligations/src/limits.rs:67-84` sets production public source to **1 MiB**, each clause to **64 KiB**, **4096 requirements**, **256 paths per requirement**, **1024 schema fields**, and **8192 evidence records**. `PublicTaskSource::from_parts` rejects empty or oversized source (`provenance.rs:31-54`); it has no paged/archive representation.
- The product passes the **entire rendered conversation** into this source on execution preparation (`peritus-product-runner/src/execution/state.rs:41-42`, `execution/obligations.rs:50-70`). Once that transcript exceeds 1 MiB, a resumed pipeline fails `InvalidPrecondition` before design/writer execution. Initial-error settlement treats that category as fatal (L117). This is a source-confirmed total-history admission cap, independent of provider context compaction and selected elapsed budgets.
- Source construction hashes the complete supplied bytes before checking size (`provenance.rs:211-217`). Requirement extraction enforces nonempty/at-most4096 drafts, clause size and path counts (`ledger/validation.rs:85-103,118-124`); Schema requirement and observation constructors enforce the selected schema-field maximum (`schema.rs:107-124,168-187`, `schema_validation.rs:71-86,137-150`); production therefore rejects more than 1,024 fields. Required field sets must also be nonempty, while observed sets may be empty; field-name byte limits are supplied separately to `SchemaField::new`. Qualification enforces the selected evidence-record maximum before ordering and known-identity checks (`qualification/validation.rs:91-160`), confirming the production 8,192 ceiling. However, valid evidence is strictly unique by requirement identity and must belong to the at-most-4,096-entry ledger, so that production evidence ceiling does not independently bind a valid input under these defaults. Conditions have strict ordering/uniqueness but no separate count ceiling here. Evidence-bound observed candidate paths independently use the selected 256-path maximum (`evidence/binding.rs:78-105`). Schema coverage is an actual linear two-cursor subset check (`schema_coverage.rs:236-302`), not a quadratic scan or work deadline. Product segmentation under the 1 MiB source cap normally creates at most 16 full-size clauses, so the 4096 draft ceiling is not its immediate limiting factor.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

faad2d50-2429-5d29-994c-6a9f0510151f.title: [L644] Git mutation can succeed before its terminal envelope is rejected
faad2d50-2429-5d29-994c-6a9f0510151f.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L644.

- Evidence: `crates/tools/peritus-tools-git/src/dispatcher.rs:117-173,185-233`; `src/dispatch_support.rs:23-45`; `src/render.rs:52-78`; `crates/tools/peritus-tool-protocol/src/result.rs:327-351`; workspace restart dependency in L582.
- Behavior: Candidate/rollback dispatch consumes process-local optional mutation/candidate context, performs the workspace operation, renders, retains the resulting outcome, then builds the terminal result. Its preflight accepts 128-byte model/human limits instead of validating the eventual complete rendering. The rollback sentence `Restored {commit} as successor snapshot {snapshot}.` needs 129 ASCII bytes for a valid 64-character commit and 32-character snapshot, so that accepted bound can fail after the effect. Both result text lengths are checked by the protocol. Candidate result/JSON errors can likewise arise after publication.
- Consequence: The effect and successful reply are not atomic. A caller can see a protocol error despite an applied mutation, while continuation depends on the same in-memory context/outcome rather than a durable receipt adoption API. The 129-byte boundary is derived from source; it was not executed against a SHA-256 repository.
- Repair direction: Validate or safely render reply capacity before effect, and persist an exact-action result/reconciliation receipt that a replacement process can adopt without repeating the mutation.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

fac5d399-4c9e-5bab-9459-6df3648b1490.title: [L790] Canceling an attachment panel does not cancel its capacity-one blocking file reader
fac5d399-4c9e-5bab-9459-6df3648b1490.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L790.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-tui/src/runtime/files.rs:1-40`, `runtime/images.rs:1-32`, `runtime/interrupts.rs:1-36`, and `runtime/product.rs:1-190`, completely read; runtime dispatch fully reread as cited in L789.
- Behavior: File and image readers each admit one `spawn_blocking` job until their JoinSet produces a completion. Panel dismissal changes reducer ownership and suppresses late continuation, but these reader APIs have no cancellation operation. A second read reports that another read is still finishing. Thread work uses the existing synchronous whole-source readers (L261) and remains active through a stuck filesystem read. The event loop otherwise selects local job completions alongside input, connection, ticks, and process interrupts. Product launch facts scope run/conversation/latest selection to the caller's workspace; they are not fresh health evidence.
- Consequence: A slow or stuck old read can prevent a new explicit attachment read after its panel was dismissed. It does not by itself stop daemon work, and introducing a timer would not cancel a blocking filesystem thread or make effects recoverable.
- Repair direction: Implement cancellable/chunked reads with independently owned reader generations and explicit completion settlement; permit unrelated requests to progress without falsely claiming the old job stopped.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

fb2c669b-199c-5120-92c2-63421c6d58d4.title: [L306] Collaboration exact retries require the current checkpoint to remain the original successor
fb2c669b-199c-5120-92c2-63421c6d58d4.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L306.
