fc32ec76-2a63-5413-a71d-44679c5ac7a6.title: [L142] Managed workspace image discovery silently drops candidates and can stop the whole traversal on depth
fc32ec76-2a63-5413-a71d-44679c5ac7a6.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L142.

- **Source:** `crates/app/peritus-product-runner/src/workspace_media.rs:17-21,53-69,103-139,150-180,258-282`; caller `workspace_delivery.rs:83-100`.
- **Limits/enforcement:** Discovery retains at most 1,024 image paths, selects only the first 16 sorted matches, excludes six named directory components, and limits traversal depth to 16. Encountering any pending directory deeper than 16 uses `break`, ending the entire traversal rather than skipping that directory. Directory entries are collected and sorted before the image limit helps; there is no directory-entry bound or cancellation inside this synchronous walk.
- **Failure/recovery:** Each candidate must be nonempty, at most 4 MiB or the provider's lower inline limit, with at most 12 MiB aggregate bytes. Oversized candidates silently disappear from the attachment manifest; if every candidate is rejected, the entire operation fails with a Provider error. A content/extension signature mismatch or any directory/read error fails discovery. A visual request with a provider lacking image support is refused. Supported discovery types are PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP, selected through fixed phrase/path heuristics. Explicit-media hosts bypass this legacy discovery.
- **Classification:** Product-selected discovery/attachment ceilings and truncation, separate from provider capacity and integrity checks. No paging, resizing, or continuation is implemented here. The explicit in-place child is now fully read: it accepts only explicit tokens that pass protected-file checks, silently discards invalid paths/errors, and takes 16 candidates BEFORE deduplication; repeated early references can therefore consume the entire selection allowance. Its tests and the managed discovery tests are fully read, not executed. This is source-confirmed behavior, not evidence that it caused the current live run to stall.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.

fcc51810-36c4-5a45-8419-7c3608c15fe8.title: [L307] E0 mandates immutable positive lifetime cycle and retention budgets
fcc51810-36c4-5a45-8419-7c3608c15fe8.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L307.

- **Source:** `crates/orchestration/peritus-orchestrator/src/limits.rs:22-46,116-150`; `src/binding.rs:71-102,151-173,231-247,291-342`; `src/state/counters.rs:21-34,61-81,131-137`; `src/state/mutation.rs:180-203`; `src/reducer.rs:68-95`; `src/reducer/apply/role_cycle.rs:39-45,323-350`; `src/reducer/apply/acceptance.rs:15-51` (all latter paths in the same crate).
- **Limiter:** Twelve dimensions must be positive and stay below compiled maxima: revisions/writer/fixer cycles 256 each; gate/review cycles 1,024 each; handoffs/directives/cancellation reconciliations 4,096 each; retained observations 8,192; artifact references 1,024; event/checkpoint payloads 16 MiB minus the frame header each. Gate/review cycles also use the smaller immutable acceptance-contract ceiling. Genesis already consumes one revision and handoff. Limits participate in the binding digest; no unlimited representation or budget-changing command exists in the closed reducer dispatch.

Counters never reset or release capacity when work finishes. The reducer returns an error rather than automatically committing an Exhausted outcome or creating a durable continuation with the same authority and context.

Persist unbounded logical progress using a versioned history/frontier representation and preserve context/authority across continuation. Any user-selected stopping policy should be explicit and optional.

ff71fb92-0f40-57d1-986d-35bc8e21be35.title: [L727] Terminal observation can overflow an attachment before giving it a delivery opportunity
ff71fb92-0f40-57d1-986d-35bc8e21be35.description:
Source finding: docs/daily-driving-limiters-audit.md — L727.

- Evidence: `crates/app/peritus-daemon/src/terminal/limits.rs:1-80`; `src/terminal/bridge.rs:260-267`; `src/terminal/bridge/observation.rs:35-93`; `src/terminal/attachment.rs:87-115,160-183`; `src/session/connection/terminal_tests/native.rs:1-127` in the same crate.
- Behavior: a poll observes up to eight 256-event process pages before draining at most 128 delivery events. That producer batch exceeds the 1,024-event pending ceiling even before smaller client chunk sizes multiply events. Overflow faults the attachment; its error omits an exact missed byte range. A sequence gap faults the whole bridge.
- Consequence: a burst can trigger loss of an otherwise responsive attachment; slowing the reader is not the only cause. Existing native tests show isolation for a 4 KiB burst and continuation of a sibling, not large-history reconnect or owner restart.
- Repair direction: couple observation to downstream capacity or a durable spool, retain retry offsets and distinguish per-reader pressure from corrupted producer ordering. Preserve exact sequence/stream identity validation. No tests run.

Scope: implement and verify the systemic repair recorded in the decision comment. Source-derived behavior remains distinct from a reproduced live incident.
